# Making the engine safe on the searches that matter most

**Implementation plan — Phases A, B, C and D.** Written 2026-09-04 against
HEAD `528afdd` (`ENGINE_VERSION 0.14.0`, `TOKENIZER_VERSION 1.0.0`,
`SCHEMA_VERSION 9`), in answer to the theological audit of the same date
(`research/audits/2026-09-04-engine-theological-audit.md`).

## Purpose

The audit graded the crisis register **F**: on the highest-stakes searches
the engine receives — a person typing *"I want to kill myself"*, *"my wife
died"*, *"my parents are getting divorced"* — the first result was not merely
unhelpful but harmful. `I want to kill myself` returned Acts 7:28, *"Do you
want to kill me as you killed the Egyptian?"*; `my husband died` returned
*"Husbands, love your wives"* and five more marital-duty texts to a fresh
widow; `i lost my job` returned *"whatever you do, work heartily, as for the
Lord"* (S-A1 §A1.0, S-A2 §A2.0). Almost none of this is a scoring defect.
The packs that should answer these searches already exist, already carry
comfort-first anchors, and were already approved — **the sentence a real
person types never reaches them**, so the query falls through to raw lexical
scoring on whichever unrelated verse happens to share a word (S-A1 §A1.0).
This plan closes that gap: curated vocabulary and anchors so the sentence
reaches the right pack (Phase A), ten engine changes shipped as one version
bump so the ordering and the explanations can be trusted (Phase B), the data
that only becomes safe once the engine changes land (Phase C), and the
measurement that keeps all of it from silently rotting (Phase D). Nothing in
it puts a model at query time, and nothing in it teaches the engine to judge
theology.

---

## What a person will experience afterwards

This is the part to read first. Every "today" and "after" below was measured
by running the real engine against a copy of the real corpus — the before
column is what the engine returns at HEAD today, the after column is what it
returns with the section's changes compiled in. The section that measured
each one is named so any line here can be checked against its own table.

**`i want to kill myself`**
- *Today:* **Acts 7:28** — *"Do you want to kill me as you killed the
  Egyptian?"* — a rebuke of Moses about third-party violence, at 11.17.
- *After:* the despair pack answers at parity — **2 Corinthians 1:8-10**
  40.00, then 1 Kings 19:4-7, Matthew 11:28-29, Psalms 42:5. Acts 7:28 falls
  below the tenth anchor (11.17 against 14.00) and leaves the page.
- *Measured in:* S-A1 §A1.1.

**`my wife died`**
- *Today:* **Ezekiel 24:18** at 40.00 — the passage where God *forbids*
  Ezekiel to mourn, quoted to a man who has just lost his wife.
- *After:* Psalms 34:18 leads, with Revelation 21:3-4 and John 11:25-26
  above it; **Ezekiel 24:18 is #4**. This is the one harm Phase A cannot
  delete — it is an exact-phrase hit, and the plan says so plainly instead of
  promising a ban it cannot hold. A curated anchor is put level with it and
  wins the tie.
- *Measured in:* S-A1 §A1.6 (acceptance).

**`why did god take my husband`**
- *Today:* **Ephesians 5:25**, *"Husbands, love your wives"*, at 12.64,
  explained to her as *Theme: Marriage*.
- *After:* **Psalms 34:18** 50.80 (*Theme: Grief and loss*), Revelation
  21:3-4, John 11:25-26. Ephesians 5:25 is absent from the top 25 on all 61
  queries in that fixture.
- *Measured in:* S-A1 Appendix, *Question-form results*.

**`will i see my baby again`**
- *Today:* **Job 3:16** — *"as a hidden untimely birth I had not been"* — to
  a mother asking about her child.
- *After:* **Psalms 34:18** 45.82 (*Theme: Losing a child*), Revelation 21:4,
  John 11:35.
- *Measured in:* S-A1 Appendix, *Question-form results*.

**`my son passed away`**
- *Today:* **1 Corinthians 7:31**, *"the mode of this world passes away"* —
  the euphemism matched as vocabulary, not as grief.
- *After:* **Psalms 34:18** 50.80, Revelation 21:3-4, John 11:25-26.
- *Measured in:* S-A1 Appendix, *Question-form results*.

**`god has forsaken me`**
- *Today:* **Psalms 71:11** at 50.70, labelled *Exact phrase* — his
  persecutors' sentence *about* him, handed back to him as if it were God's
  word to him.
- *After:* **Hebrews 13:5** 64.00 (*Theme: The presence of God*) — God's own
  *"I will in no way leave you, neither will I in any way forsake you"* —
  with Psalms 71:11 demoted to #2, not suppressed.
- *Measured in:* S-A1 Appendix, *Question-form results*.

**`verses for a funeral`**
- *Today:* **Matthew 11:17** at 1.78 — a rebuke of "this generation",
  reached only through commentary vocabulary, because the word *funeral*
  occurs nowhere in the WEB text.
- *After:* a new `funeral-readings` pack: **John 14:1-3 #1** on all nine
  funeral queries, John 11:25-26 #2, 1 Thessalonians 4:13-18 #3/#5,
  1 Corinthians 15:54-57 #5/#7.
- *Measured in:* S-A1 §A1.11.

**`my mom has dementia`**
- *Today:* **zero results.** The words *dementia* and *alzheimer* do not
  occur anywhere in the WEB text, and no curated lexicon carried them.
- *After:* **2 Corinthians 1:3-4** within the top 3 on all six queries in the
  fixture. (It sits exactly *at* #3, and the plan names that boundary rather
  than rounding it away.)
- *Measured in:* S-A1 §§A1.8-A1.9, and *What is not claimed*.

**`i lost my job`**
- *Today:* **Colossians 3:23**, *"whatever you do, work heartily, as for the
  Lord"* — a work-ethic verse served to someone who has just lost the work.
- *After:* a new `provision-in-hardship` pack: **Matthew 6:25-34 #1 on all
  fourteen** job-and-money queries; Colossians 3:23 drops to #11 and is
  pinned there by a guard.
- *Measured in:* S-A2 §A2.11 and the per-fixture table
  (`job-loss-and-money-fear`).

**`panic attack`**
- *Today:* **2 Samuel 17:9**, a battle report with no comfort content,
  because nothing curated competed for those two words.
- *After:* **Philippians 4:6-7 #1 on all five** queries, Psalms 56:3 at #10;
  2 Samuel 17:9 falls to #16.
- *Measured in:* S-A2 §A2.8 and the per-fixture table (`panic-attack`).

**`my parents are getting divorced`**
- *Today:* the parenting pack fires on the bare word *parent*, so a child
  watching their home come apart is told **"Children, obey your parents in
  all things"** (Colossians 3:20-21, Ephesians 6:4).
- *After:* a new `children-of-divorce` pack: **Psalms 27:10 #1 on all seven**
  queries, Psalms 68:5-6 #2, Mark 10:13-16 #7; Colossians 3:20-21 held at
  #11 and Ephesians 6:4 at #13 by guards.
- *Measured in:* S-A2 §A2.5 and the per-fixture table (`children-of-divorce`).

**`am i going to hell`**
- *Today:* **Mark 9:43-48**, then Matthew 18:8-9, then Matthew 5:22 — three
  hell texts and no gospel, to someone frightened enough to type the
  question.
- *After:* **Acts 16:30-31** (*"Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be
  saved"*), Romans 10:9, Ephesians 2:8. On the neighbouring informational
  forms (`what is hell`, `is there a hell`) Mark 9:43-48 still leads and the
  gospel arrives at #2 and #3 — the plan pins what is true rather than what
  is wished for.
- *Measured in:* S-A3 §A3.0 and Appendix, *Felt-need forms*.

**`will god forgive me`**
- *Today:* **Matthew 18:21-22** — *Theme: Forgiving others*. The person
  asking whether *God* forgives *them* is answered with their duty to forgive
  someone else.
- *After:* **1 John 1:9** (*Theme: Salvation*), Acts 16:30-31, Romans 8:1.
- *Measured in:* S-A3 Appendix, *Felt-need forms*.

**`i dont feel god anymore`**
- *Today:* **Proverbs 23:35** — the drunkard who cannot feel a beating.
- *After:* **Hebrews 13:5** (*Theme: The presence of God*), Psalms 139:7-10,
  Psalms 42:1-5.
- *Measured in:* S-A3 §A3.0 and Appendix, *Felt-need forms*.

A note on how to read these. The before column is not a list of bugs in the
ranking arithmetic; every one of those results is the engine working
correctly on data that had never been asked that question (S-A1 Appendix).
And the after column is deliberately not perfect: `will i go to hell` still
leads with Mark 9:43-48, `my wife died` still returns Ezekiel 24:18 at #4,
and three bereavement registers stay open by measurement rather than by
omission. Each is named in the section that owns it, with what it would take
to close it.

## The covenants this plan holds to

These are `CLAUDE.md`'s six non-negotiables. Each line says how the plan
respects it — and where the plan pays a cost to keep it, the cost is named.

1. **No AI at runtime.** Nothing in Phases A-D adds a model to the query
   path. Every addition is reviewed data — lexicon phrases, anchors with
   weights, alias rows, tokenizer tables — merged by human PR review. The
   Phase B tokenizer tables are derived mechanically from the corpus
   vocabulary and then *signed by a reviewer*, which is the same discipline
   applied to code (S-B §B.0 covenant checklist).
2. **Determinism is the product, and the version bump is not optional.**
   Phase A moves `layerFingerprint` only — it is curated data, so
   `ENGINE_VERSION` must *not* move (S-A1 §A1.0). Phase B moves all three
   identities at once, deliberately: `ENGINE_VERSION 0.14.0 → 0.15.0`,
   `TOKENIZER_VERSION 1.0.0 → 2.0.0`, `SCHEMA_VERSION 9 → 10`, in a single
   baseline commit (S-B §B.0). The plan never signs an A-batch and a B-batch
   under one bump, precisely so a reviewer can tell from the version numbers
   alone whether an ordering change came from curated data or from code
   (S-C §C.6, *Signing convention*).
3. **The engine package does no I/O.** No item adds a file read to
   `engine/`. Phase B's query frames live in `engine/src/config/` as a
   constant, and the one corpus lookup they need goes through
   `ContentQueryPort` like every other read (S-B §B.0, item B3).
4. **One tokenizer.** Phase B1 rewrites the tokenizer as *one* module with
   one call site that the pipeline imports — the covenant is the item's whole
   point. No per-caller option is added anywhere in the plan (S-B §B.0).
5. **Explanations are part of the contract.** Phase A treats a wrong
   explanation as a defect equal to a wrong result: S-A1's procedure requires
   every quoted result to print every reason label the engine returned, and
   that rule is what exposed a widow's #2 result being labelled *"Related
   theme: Betrayed by a companion"* (S-A1 §A1.0d Step 7, §A1.6 Ruling 5).
   Phase B9 makes every chip quote a surface word the searcher actually
   typed.
6. **No theology scores.** Nothing in the plan scores doctrine. The engine
   continues to report only that a named curated source associates a passage
   with a concept, and which source. Phase B8's new `care` flag says "a
   reviewed care list names this concept" and nothing more; B10's alias
   chips name a saying's origin, which is provenance, not a verdict (S-B
   §B.0).

### The doctrinal basis, and what it excludes

`docs/DOCTRINAL-BASIS.md` governs which curated sources may be admitted at
all. Its baseline is the nine points affirmed in common by the three
statements of faith Jesse named; its one named exclusion criterion is
prosperity and seed-faith teaching, citing the Lausanne Movement's Akropong
statement. The criterion judges a source's *framing*, never the verses
themselves — John 14:12 and Job 36:11 are Scripture and may rank honestly
wherever faithful curation puts them; what is excluded is the pairing frame
that recruits them as an achievement formula. The plan honours this
mechanically rather than by intention: the `prosperity-*` fixture family
encodes the exclusion as `mustNotRank` assertions checked on every gate run,
and S-A2's new `provision-in-hardship` pack was deliberately built *outside*
`gods-provision` — whose own header explains that the split is what keeps
watchlisted references and material-frame vocabulary from ever co-occurring
in one concept — so that "I can't pay rent" never recruits Philippians 4:19
at 0.95 (S-A2 §A2.11).

## How the work is phased

**Phase A — data, now.** Four sections of curated data with no engine
change: crisis and bereavement (S-A1), marriage and life events (S-A2),
assurance, doctrine, named passages and occasions (S-A3), and the deferred-
anchor backfill (S-A4). Every edit is ontology YAML plus golden fixtures, so
**`layerFingerprint` moves and `ENGINE_VERSION` does not**. Review cost is
per-PR and ordinary — YAML diffs, fixtures, and the Admission Report — with
one merge-order constraint that matters: three A1 items edit the same grief
pack and must land in a stated order, and the deletion of two lexicon lines
from `godly-marriage.yaml` rides the same commit as the change that needs it
(S-A1 §A1.0e). Signing is once per data batch, not once per fixture (S-C
§C.6). No consumer re-pin is required beyond the artifact descriptor.

**Phase B — the engine bundle, at 0.15.0.** Ten engine changes ship as *one*
version bump, on one branch with one commit per item and a single baseline
commit at the end (S-B §B.0, §B.11). One bundle instead of ten is a review
decision with a price attached: ten bumps would mean ten ordering-snapshot
regenerations, ten probe-baseline regenerations, ten independent reviews
under `docs/governance/probe-baseline-review.md`, and ten consumer re-pins
across Maskil, LH Worship Setlist and Versed. The bundle means **one**
`ENGINE_VERSION` bump, **one** `TOKENIZER_VERSION` bump, one regeneration
each of the ordering snapshot, the probe baseline and the rank-metrics
baseline, **one** independent-review packet and set of approvals, and **one**
consumer re-pin of `(0.15.0, new descriptor)`. Because tokenizer 2.0.0
refuses every 1.0.0 artifact at load, the engine and artifact halves of that
pin move together by construction. Expect G2 to be red on every intermediate
commit of the branch — that is the gate working, not a defect, and the branch
merges only after the baseline commit lands (S-B §B.11).

**Phase C — the data B unlocks.** Two classes of work that are unsafe or
impossible before the bundle lands: the alias files (S-A3 §§A3.24-A3.25 —
misquotes and named passages, both gated on B10 and on their source
manifests existing), and the registers that need tokenizer v2 — the bare
words `hate`, `worthless`, `burden`, `alone`, `cant`, `hurt`, and the
restoration of `cutting myself` once `myself` stops being a stopword (S-A1
Summary; S-B ruling 1, ruling 7). Also here: the Tier-2/Tier-3 anchor
backfill (S-A4 §A4.4). Identity cost is `layerFingerprint` again — but the
alias rows cannot legally ship before B10's manifests exist, so a Phase C PR
merged early fails G1, not review.

**Phase D — measurement.** The gates that keep this from decaying: G13
rebuilt to read the same fixtures G3 already validates plus one new reviewed
register map (`eval/registers.json`), with a mandatory fixed top-10 scan a
fixture's own narrower window cannot weaken; the rank-quality thresholds
flipped from `null` to real numbers, which is blocked behind closing the
existing G2/G8 approval debt; the pending-fixture debt burned to zero and
`--pending-debt-ok` removed (S-C §C.4, §C.5). Phase D adds no data and no
ordering change, so it moves no fingerprint — but D2's flip re-opens a
signing cycle of its own, because a rank-metrics threshold needs an approval
whose independence attestation names a reviewer distinct from the author
(S-C §C.5 item 9).

## How every item was verified

No number in this document is an estimate, and none was carried forward from
an earlier draft without being re-run. The method is the same in every
section:

1. **Copy the corpus.** `pipeline/output/fixture.db` — the full WEB, 31,098
   verses — is copied to a scratch directory. The repository is never
   modified and the working tree is never read from.
2. **Compile the proposed data through the real importer.** Two ontology
   trees are built — `git archive HEAD`, and a copy carrying the section's
   edits — and both are compiled with
   `pipeline/src/importers/ontologyImporter.ts`, the same code the build
   uses. The two compiles are *diffed*, and the diff is applied to the copied
   database. Diffing rather than inserting is what makes a **deletion**
   visible: S-A1 removes two lexicon lines, and a harness that only inserted
   would have reported success while measuring the wrong corpus (S-A1
   §A1.0d Step 2).
3. **Rebuild the spelling index**, because it is derived from the lexicon and
   a corpus patched without it ships a mismatched index (S-A1 §A1.0d
   Step 2b).
4. **Run the real gates, unmodified.** `corpusGoldenGate` with the limit-50
   presence engine exactly as the gauntlet constructs it, plus the concept-
   coverage, collision, collapse-inventory, bare-word-inventory and
   doctrinal-pairing checks.
5. **Require zero regressions.** The whole of `eval/golden/` is run against
   the patched corpus and against the unmodified one, and the two reports are
   *diffed, not eyeballed*. S-A1's is byte-identical: 532 hold, the same 14
   pending fixtures failing on the same expectations, 0 regressions — which
   is the load-bearing evidence for its most invasive edit. S-A2 reports the
   same, character-identical to its baseline line.
6. **Sweep the standing exclusions across every query, not just the guarded
   ones.** A gate only checks the guards a fixture writes; the sweep checks
   the references the corpus already treats as dangerous — Psalms 116:15, the
   six suicide narratives, the marital-duty family — across every query the
   section adds, to a depth of 25. This step is what found Psalms 116:15
   inside the served page on thirteen queries against a standing written
   ruling (S-A1 §A1.0d Step 6).

The measured totals, for scale: S-A1 runs **149 queries against 17 fixtures
with 0 findings**; S-A2 runs 27 fixtures with one deliberately-failing
pending fixture that records a structural limit; S-A3 runs 46 fixtures, 32
active and 0 failing.

**Those are per-chapter numbers, each measured against HEAD, and they are not
the plan's numbers.** The data chapters were composed onto one tree and
re-measured after the cross-chapter conflicts were resolved; that run, its
gate output and the corrected totals are **S-C's *Composed verification*
appendix**, which is the figure to quote for anything plan-wide. In short:
**305 concept packs** (289 + 16), **2,017 lexicon rows**, **2,006 compiled
anchor rows** (2,037 once S-A4's three backfill batches land), **840
`related:` edges**, **635 fixture files** (605 active, 30 pending) carrying
**414 asserted queries, 409 distinct**, and a recomputed G4 bare-word census
of **318 admitted / 293 skipped**. Composed, G4's three sub-checks, concept
coverage and the doctrinal-pairing watchlist all pass; the golden gate holds
603 corpus fixtures and fails **one** expectation, which is written up as
KG-C-7 rather than smoothed away.

**What this proves, and what it does not.** It proves that the proposed data,
compiled by the real compiler into the real corpus and judged by the real
gates, produces the stated results and breaks nothing that passes today. It
does **not** prove that the results are pastorally right — that is Jesse's
merge, and the rulings each section raises are addressed to him. It does not
prove anything about queries nobody typed: the fixtures assert what they
assert, which is why S-A1's largest single addition this round was the
sentences a person in pain actually types, and why three registers are listed
as open. And its safety claims are scoped to the gate's window, not the
engine's: the served page is 25 results deep and the fixture format cannot
express a ban at 25, so wherever a banned reference survives between #11 and
#25 the plan prints the position rather than rounding it away (S-A1, *What is
not claimed*).

## A reader's guide

| If you want to know… | Read |
|---|---|
| What a searcher in crisis or bereavement will get, and what they get today | **S-A1** — crisis, suicide, bereavement, child loss, dementia, funerals, widows, pets |
| What changes for marriage, divorce, parenting, job loss, illness, sleeplessness | **S-A2** — with the register-collision table showing who else answers when |
| What changes for assurance, doctrine questions, named passages, weddings, Christmas and misquotes | **S-A3** |
| Why some packs are missing their own proof text, and the conventions every fixture in this plan follows | **S-A4** |
| What the engine itself does differently at 0.15.0, and what that costs in review and re-pinning | **S-B** — ten items, one bundle, seventeen owner rulings applied |
| Whether typing the same need a different way gets the same answer, and how any of this stays true | **S-C** — the search-form matrix and Phase D measurement |
| Every open question addressed to Jesse, in one place | The rulings register (assembled last), plus each section's own *Rulings* blocks |
| Whether a specific number here is real | The Appendix of the section that states it — every one carries its harness and its raw gate output |

**A note on provenance.** The audit's own file could not be opened from this
session (`/mnt/project-files` returned an I/O error), so the audit citations
in the Purpose above are drawn from the sections' own restatements of its
findings and from the audit's grade for the crisis register as reported to
the plan's authors. Before this document ships to review, that opening
paragraph should be read once against
`research/audits/2026-09-04-engine-theological-audit.md` itself. Everything
else in the front matter is sourced to a section and a table in this
document.

# Phase A1 — Crisis and bereavement registers

## A1.0 Why this comes first

The audit found harmful #1 results on the highest-stakes queries the engine
receives. Every number below was **re-measured live for r2** against
`pipeline/output/fixture.db` (full WEB, 31,098 verses) through the built
engine's public `research()` API, and every score is quoted from that run,
not restated from R1/R2.

| query | measured today | score |
|---|---|---|
| `I want to kill myself` | **Acts 7:28** "Do you want to kill me as you killed the Egyptian?" | 11.17 |
| `kill myself` | **1 Samuel 1:25** "They killed **the bull**" | 4.29 |
| `giving up` | **Job 11:20** "the eyes of the **wicked** will fail… their hope will be the giving up of the spirit" | 10.00 |
| `I dont want to live` | **Job 7:16** "I loathe my life… Leave me alone" | 36.53 |
| `end my life` | **Hebrews 7:3** (Melchizedek: "neither beginning of days nor end of life") | 7.92 |
| `I wish I was never born` | **Ephesians 2:8** + the whole `salvation` pack (born-again texts) | 16.16 |
| `god hates me` | **Deuteronomy 16:22** (an idolatry text) | 10.44 |
| `I hate myself` | **John 15:23**, **Psalms 139:22** ("I hate them with perfect hatred") | 7.50 / 6.01 |
| `self hatred` | **Psalms 139:22** #1 | 4.10 |
| `god abandoned me` | **2 Kings 21:22** "he **abandoned** Yahweh" — the reversed direction | 9.54 |
| `im all alone` | **Proverbs 5:17** (marital fidelity, wrong sense of "alone") | 7.50 |
| `my husband died` | **Ephesians 5:25**, 5:22-24, 1 Pet 3:1-6, 5:28, Titus 2:3-5, **Heb 13:4** | 17.20 … 13.22 |
| `lost my husband` | Eph 5:25, 5:22-24, 5:28, **1 Peter 3:7**, 1 Pet 3:1-6, Titus 2:3-5 | 18.53 … 14.92 |
| `I lost my wife` | **Deuteronomy 22:30** #1; **Exodus 20:17** (the Tenth Commandment) #3 | 3.11 / 2.52 |
| `my wife died` | **Ezekiel 24:18** — an `exact_phrase` hit inside the passage where God *forbids* Ezekiel to mourn | **40.00** |
| `my mom died` | **Romans 6:8** "if we died with Christ" | 3.37 |
| `my father died` | **John 8:53** (a hostile taunt) | 11.77 |
| `my sister died` | **2 Samuel 13:1/13:2/13:4** — the Tamar/Amnon rape narrative | 3.11 / 2.88 / 2.73 |
| `stillborn` | **Psalms 58:8** (imprecatory curse-image), **Ecclesiastes 6:3** — the entire result set, 2 rows | 2.73 / 1.58 |
| `my baby was stillborn` | **Numbers 12:12** (Miriam's leprosy), **Job 3:16**, then Ps 58:8 #4 | 6.00 / 6.00 / 1.47 |
| `my mom has dementia` | **0 results** | — |
| `widower` | **1 Corinthians 7:8**, one row, matched only through commentary vocabulary | 2.05 |
| `verses for a funeral` | **Matthew 11:17**, then Deut 14:1, Matt 11:16, **Leviticus 19:27** | 1.78 … 1.50 |
| `my pet died` | **Romans 6:8** again | 3.37 |

Two r1 claims are corrected here by measurement: Exodus 20:17 is **#3** for
"I lost my wife" (Deuteronomy 22:30 leads), and "I feel like a burden"
leads with **Psalms 73:5**, not Galatians 6:5.

Almost every one of these is a **lexicon gap**, not a missing-concept
problem: the packs that should answer already exist, already carry
comfort-first anchors, and are already Jesse-approved — the phrase a real
person types never reaches them, so the query falls through to raw lexical
scoring on whichever unrelated verse shares a token. This phase closes that
gap with lexicon and anchor extensions to existing packs, two new packs, and
golden fixtures.

**The one exception, named up front.** `"my wife died"` → Ezekiel 24:18 is
**not** a lexicon gap. It is a 40.00-point `exact_phrase` hit, an
authoritative family, and nothing in Phase A or Phase B lowers it (see
A1.6's arithmetic and §A1.0c). Phase A can only put a curated anchor above
it. That is what this section does, and the fixture says so honestly rather
than banning a verse it cannot ban.

**No engine code changes.** Every edit in A1.1–A1.13 is ontology data plus
golden fixtures, so `layerFingerprint` moves and `ENGINE_VERSION` does not
(CLAUDE.md non-negotiable #2's three identities: engine code, scripture
text, curated layers — this section touches only the third).

## A1.0a Method, and four invariants r2 adopts

**Tokenizer.** Every phrase, every fixture `query` and every
`additionalQuery` in this section was run through the live
`significantWords()` (`engine/src/tokenizer/index.ts`, via `npx tsx`) and the
output is quoted verbatim in each item's Tokenizer-hazards block. Nothing is
restated from R1/R2.

**Invariant 1 — phrase coverage.** Every lexicon phrase an item adds appears
in that item's fixture as the `query` or an `additionalQuery`, *unless* the
item shows the tokenizer output proving its token set is identical to one
already tested. Matching is set-containment over normalized tokens
(`ConceptRepository.matchConcepts`, `repository.ts:693-724`), so two phrases
with the same token set in any order are one entry's worth of behaviour —
r1 shipped several such pairs as if they were two.

**Invariant 2 — the Guards table IS the `mustNotRank`.** Every ref named in
an item's prose Guards table appears verbatim in that item's fixture, at the
same range, and the item shows the arithmetic that the guard will actually
hold. Where the arithmetic says a total ban will *not* hold, the guard is
written as `mustNotLead` with the measured position, and the item says so.
A guard that cannot hold is worse than no guard (CLAUDE.md gate discipline).

**Invariant 3 — every fixture that claims a concept proves it.**
`conceptCoverageGate` (`corpusGolden.ts:833-877`) counts a fixture toward a
concept's coverage only when `status: "active"`, the `query` is non-empty,
**and** some `expectedTop` entry carries both
`requiredReasonFamily: "concept_anchor"` and `requiredReasonLabel` equal to
`"Theme: " + <the pack's own label:>`. Every fixture below satisfies that
for every id in its `coversConcepts`, and no fixture declares a concept its
item does not build. The exact labels used, read from the packs:
`Hope in despair`, `Identity in Christ`, `The love of God`, `Loneliness`,
`God's forgiveness`, `Grief and loss`, `Losing a child`,
`Caring for aging parents`, `God in the valley`, `Care for widows`,
`Funeral and memorial readings`, `Losing a pet`.

**Invariant 4 — one worked inventory example, reused by reference.**
`ontology/lexicon-inventory.yaml` has two independent sections and r1
confused them in five items:

- **`collapses:`** acknowledges a *multi-word phrase whose significant width
  is one token*. `singleTokenCollapses` (`collision.ts:167-190`) records one
  only when `tokens.length === 1 && phrase.trim().split(/\s+/).length > 1`.
  **A one-word phrase is not a collapse**, and a row for one is a *stale
  acknowledgment* that fails G4.
- **`concepts:`** records, per compiled concept id, which bare single words
  must fire it (`admitted:`) and which must not (`skipped:`, with a
  reason). A bare word that fires with no `admitted:` entry is reported
  (report-only) as "behaviour without a recorded decision"
  (`lexiconInventory.ts:209-224`).

So: **a bare word needs an `admitted:` entry and no `collapses:` row; a
multi-word phrase that collapses needs both.** This section adds exactly two
`collapses:` rows (A1.1's `kill myself` → `kill` and `giving up` →
`giving`), and `admitted:` entries everywhere else.

Worked example, the one every other item points at (A1.1):

```yaml
# ontology/lexicon-inventory.yaml — collapses: section, APPEND
  - conceptId: hope-in-despair
    phrase: "kill myself"
    token: kill
    intended: true
    reviewedBy: pending-J12
    date: "2026-09-04"
    note: >-
      "myself" is a stopword, so the phrase IS the bare token `kill`.
      Admitted deliberately (A1.1 Ruling 1): the lone query "kill myself"
      must reach hope-in-despair, and the fixture bans the WEB kill-
      narratives it competes with.

# ontology/lexicon-inventory.yaml — concepts: section, EDIT the existing row
# (D1, cross-section): this section adds `kill` and `giving` to that row's
# admitted: list, and it deliberately does NOT print the row. S-A2 A2.10 adds
# `numb` to the SAME row and is the `apply=ops` chapter a parser reads, so
# A2.10 prints the one merged listing —
#   admitted: [suicide, suicidal, depression, depressed, cutting, kill, giving, numb]
# — and this section states its two additions in prose instead. Two chapters
# printing one row is how the row ends up with two incompatible listings.
```

**Both halves were executed, not asserted.** A scratch copy of the whole
ontology with every A1 lexicon edit applied, plus a scratch copy of
`lexicon-inventory.yaml` with every row below, was compiled with
`compileOntology` and run through all three G4 sub-checks
(`collisionGate`, `collision.ts`'s `lexiconInventoryCheck` collapse
deny-list, and `gates/lexiconInventory.ts`'s `lexiconInventoryCheck`
bare-word inventory):

```
compile errors: none        concepts: 291
G4 collision                     pass | 291 concept(s) are mutually distinct
G4 collapse deny-list            pass | 70 single-token collapse(s), all acknowledged
G4 bare-word inventory           pass | 291 concept(s) carry an explicit bare-word
                                        decision (293 admitted, 244 skipped)
```

The bare-word result carries **no** `firing-token-undecided` findings, which
is the report-only line r1's rows would have produced.

**Correction to r2 (critique obj 22), carried through r4.** r2 printed
"294 admitted, **243** skipped" as literal tool output. Re-run, the r2 edit
set gives **294 admitted, 242 skipped**; the r3 edit set added one admission
(`widow` on `grief-and-loss`, A1.10 Ruling 3) and gave **295 / 242**. The r4
edit set **moves two admissions to skips** — `husbands` and `wives` leave
`godly-marriage`'s `admitted:` list and become `skipped:` rows carrying their
reason, in the same commit that removes the two lexicon entries (A1.6
Ruling 5) — so the r4 numbers are the **293 / 244** above. The block is the
run's own text, and §A1.0d says how to reproduce it.

## A1.0b The scoring arithmetic every item below uses — and its limits

Anchor points are a closed formula. **A row's score is not.** r2 quoted the
formula as if it were the score, and that single error produced every one of
the 49 gate failures the r2 critique measured. r3 states the boundary first,
then the formula.

```
anchorPoints = clamp01(anchorWeight)
             × (parity ? 1 : min(1, 0.55 + 0.15 × (m − 1)))   # conceptSpecificity
             × sqrt(min(1, m / q))                            # conceptCoverage
             × 40                                             # concept_anchor maxPoints
  where m = matched phrase's token count, q = query's token count,
        parity = (m >= 2 && m === q)
```
`engine/src/intents/concept.ts:23-68`; `40` is
`DEFAULT_BUDGETS.families.concept_anchor.maxPoints`
(`engine/src/ranking/budgets.ts:66`).

**`anchorPoints` is one component of one row.** The same target also collects,
and every one of these can and does reorder an anchor ladder:

| family | budget | seen in this section |
|---|---|---|
| `concept_lexicon` (a `related:` theme) | 12, `maxReasons: 2` → up to **12.00** | Ps 34:18 carries 12.00 on every `grief-and-loss` query (from `pregnancy-and-child-loss` + `near-to-the-brokenhearted`), which is why it leads the whole register |
| `translation_variant` | **14** | Heb 13:5 on `"god abandoned me"` (14.00, and it takes #1); 1 Thess 4:13-14 on `"my sister died"` |
| `token_overlap` | 10 | 1 Tim 5:3-8 +6.00 on `"widow"` |
| `passage_terms` | 8 | Isa 54:4-6 +1.56 on `"my husband died"` |
| `proximity` | ~6 | the reversal texts on `"god abandoned me"` |

`soleEvidenceMaxPoints` (6) **cannot** trim any of these when a
`concept_anchor` survives on the row — `budgets.ts:205-207` applies the
sole-evidence cap only when no authoritative reason remains. r2's CR-2 read
the 6 as `translation_variant`'s budget; it is 14 (critique obj 21, accepted
and corrected in the appendix).

Three corollaries, each now quoted **as the row score the engine returned**,
not as the anchor component:

1. **Parity (the query IS the phrase): `anchorPoints = 40 × weight`.**
   Measured, `"god is angry with me"` → Gen 32:24-30 **40.71**
   (`concept_anchor` 40.00 + `token_overlap: god` 0.71), Ps 13:1-2 **36.00**,
   Ps 73:16-17 **34.00**, Hos 12:3-4 **32.00**, Job 23:3-4 **30.00**. r2
   printed 40.00 for the first row and quoted 40.71 for the same row four
   hundred lines later.
2. **A bare single-token query: `anchorPoints = 22 × weight`.** Measured,
   `"miscarriage"` → Ps 34:18 **27.10** (22.00 + `Related theme: Grief and
   loss` 5.10), not 22.00; `"suicide"` → 2 Cor 1:8-10 **22.00** (no add-on on
   that target, so here the two coincide).
3. **A bare cue inside a longer query: `anchorPoints = 22 × weight × sqrt(1/q)`.**
   Measured, `"death of a spouse"` (q = 2) → Ps 23:4 anchor component
   **15.56**, row **16.31**, at **#3** behind 2 Cor 12:9-10 (19.22) and
   Ps 73:26 (16.47). r2 quoted 15.56 as the row and implied #1.

**The rule r3 adopts, and §A1.0d enforces.** No item below predicts a
*position* from a weight ladder. Every position, every window and every guard
in this section is quoted from a run of the real engine against a corpus with
the section's own edits applied, and every fixture is run through the real
`corpusGoldenGate` before it is written down. Weight ladders still appear —
they explain *why* a number is what it is — but they are never the evidence
for a fixture assertion.

**Which window the safety claims are scoped to (critique obj 18).** Every
`mustNotRank` in this section is a ban *from the fixture's measured window*,
and `measuredWindow` here is **10** (`corpusGolden.ts:798-806`). The engine's
own default page is **25** — `DEFAULT_LIMIT = 25`, `engine/src/ranking/rank.ts:46`
— and the three consumer apps take that default unless they pass
`rankOptions.limit`. So "absent from the top 10" is a true, machine-checked
claim about a window that is **not** the page the searcher sees, and this
section says so wherever the gap matters:

- The gate cannot express a ban at 25. `withinTop` accepts 1, 3, 5 and 10
  (`corpusGolden.ts:616-624`), and `expectedWithinTop` sets the ban window.
  Writing "ban it from 25" is not available in Phase A.
- Where a guarded ref measures between #11 and #25, the item **prints the
  position** rather than resting on "absent from the top 10". Every one that
  does is named, here and in the Appendix's standing-exclusions matrix:
  **Psalms 116:15** at #11-#12 on `pastoral-spouse-dying`, #18 on the
  dementia and `death of a child` queries, #21/#24 on two
  `pastoral-spouse-death` queries (A1.9 Ruling 3, A1.6, A1.7, A1.8);
  **Matthew 27:5** at #22/#24 on two child question forms (A1.6);
  **2 Samuel 17:23** at #17-#23 on the pet queries and `my father died`
  (A1.6, A1.12); **Deuteronomy 22:3** at #14 and **Deuteronomy 22:30** at
  #13 (A1.6); the **euphemism family** at #13-#20 on the `passed away`
  queries (A1.6); **Romans 6:8** at #21 on `my baby died` (A1.7); and the
  three reversal texts at #17-#19 on `god has forsaken me` (A1.4).
- Where the residue could be removed by design rather than demoted, r4
  removes it. The whole marital-duty family sat at **#12-#19** for a widow in
  r3 — inside the served page — and r4's A1.6 Ruling 5 takes it off the page
  entirely by removing `godly-marriage`'s bare `husbands`/`wives` cues.
  Measured: Ephesians 5:25, 5:22-24, 5:28, 1 Peter 3:1-6, 1 Peter 3:7,
  Titus 2:3-5, 1 Corinthians 7:3 and Hebrews 13:4 are **absent from the top
  25** on all 61 `pastoral-spouse-death` queries, where r3 had them at
  #12-#19 on three of them.

**Ties.** `compareResults` (`engine/src/ranking/rank.ts:57-77`) breaks an exact
score tie between two authoritative results in favour of the one carrying a
`concept_anchor` reason, then by `targetId`. This is load-bearing in A1.6 and
is the only reason the Ezekiel 24:18 guard is assertable at all — verified in
the run: `"my wife died"` returns John 11:25-26 **40.00 #3** and Ezekiel 24:18
**40.00 #4**.

## A1.0c What Phase B does and does not fix here

r1 and the r2 owner brief both assumed Phase B's **B2 sole-evidence
ceiling** would eventually cap Job 7:16 and Ezekiel 24:18. Read against
S-B §B.2, it will not, and this section must not promise it.

B2's predicate is *"no surviving reason is authoritative"*
(S-B §B.2 design block: `reasons.length > 0 && !reasons.some(r => isAuthoritative(r.family))`),
and `isAuthoritative` covers `reference`, `exact_phrase`, `concept_anchor`.
Both verses lead on `exact_phrase`:

- **Job 7:16** = `exact_phrase 26.67` + `proximity 5.70` + `token_overlap 4.17` = 36.53
- **Ezekiel 24:18** = `exact_phrase 40.00`, sole reason

B2 never fires on either. B6 (curated-order guard) scales *add-ons on
anchored results* and does not touch a lexical-only row either. So the
mechanism that holds the line for both is the one available **today**:
parity competition from a curated anchor, plus `rank.ts`'s
curated-anchor tie-break. Each item below shows that arithmetic instead of
deferring to a Phase B item that cannot deliver it.

## A1.0d The acceptance procedure — how every number below was produced

This is the section's acceptance procedure, written out so a Phase C author
can repeat it without inventing it. It is the difference between "the
arithmetic shows the guard holds" and "the gate says it holds", and it is why
r3 exists: run against the r2 text, it returned
`STATUS fail | 49 corpus fixture expectation(s) failed`.

**Step 1 — copy the corpus.** `cp pipeline/output/fixture.db $SIM/post.db`
(full WEB, 31,098 verses). Never edit in place; never write inside the repo.

**Step 2 — compile the YAML with the real importer, diff, and apply the
diff.** r3 prescribed hand-written `INSERT` statements here, which
reimplements `ontologyImporter.ts` — the verse-id arithmetic, the
`normalized` convention, the `sources`/duplicate-range rules — for no gain
(critique obj 14). Do this instead, which is strictly safer and no harder:

```ts
// 1. two trees: HEAD's ontology/concepts, and a copy with the section's edits
import { compileOntology } from 'pipeline/src/importers/ontologyImporter.ts';
const before = compileOntology(readYamlDir('onto-base')).ontology;
const after  = compileOntology(readYamlDir('onto-r4')).ontology;   // errors MUST be 0

// 2. diff the four row sets (concepts, lexicon, anchors, related) by value,
//    then apply the adds and removes to the copied DB. A weight EDIT shows up
//    as one anchor removal plus one anchor insert, which is what it is.
```

Compiling both trees is also the only way a **removal** is caught: r4 removes
two `godly-marriage` lexicon rows, and a script that only inserts would have
reported success while measuring the wrong corpus. The diff for this section
is `concepts +2, lexicon +144 -2, anchors +25, related +3`, printed by the
harness before it writes anything.

**Step 2b — rebuild the spelling index.** `pipeline/src/buildSpellingIndex.ts`
reads `SELECT DISTINCT normalized FROM concept_lexicon`
(`buildSpellingIndex.ts:108`), so a corpus built by step 2 alone has a
spelling index that no longer matches its lexicon. This section adds five
terms that reach it — `alzheimer`, `cat`, `dad`, `dementia`, `mom` — and r3's
procedure never mentioned the rebuild (critique obj 14). Run it:

```ts
import { buildSpellingIndex } from 'pipeline/src/buildSpellingIndex.ts';
buildSpellingIndex(db);   // r4 run: terms 18428, deletes 400505
```

Verified: every assertion in this section holds identically with and without
the rebuild, so nothing here depends on it. The procedure is still wrong
without it, and a Phase C author following it would ship a mismatched index.

**Step 3 — run the section's own fixtures through the real gate.** Transcribe
every fixture in the section to JSON, then, exactly as
`eval/src/gauntlet.ts:847-852` does:

```ts
const engine = await createEngine(openCorpus(post));
const presenceEngine = await createEngine(openCorpus(post), { rankOptions: { limit: 50 } });
const result = await corpusGoldenGate(engine, fixtures, { presenceEngine });
```

The limit-50 `presenceEngine` is not optional: a `presenceOnly` expectation
without it reports `G3_PRESENCE_NOT_MEASURED` and fails closed
(`corpusGolden.ts:1194-1215`).

**Step 4 — run the whole existing golden corpus against the same DB.** The
number that matters is the regression count, and it must be **0**.

**Step 5 — run the structural halves.** `conceptCoverageGate` over the
compiled concept list plus the merged fixture set (section fixtures override
repo fixtures by id), and all three G4 sub-checks — `collisionGate`,
`collision.ts`'s collapse deny-list, `gates/lexiconInventory.ts`'s bare-word
inventory — over a scratch `lexicon-inventory.yaml` carrying every row the
section prescribes. Thresholds come from `eval/budgets.json`, never from a
guess.

**Step 6 — sweep the standing exclusions across every query.** New in r4, and
it is the step that found this round's worst defect. The gate only checks the
guards a fixture writes. Take the refs the *existing* corpus already bans —
Psalms 116:15, the six suicide narratives (Matt 27:5, 2 Sam 17:23,
1 Sam 31:4-5, Judges 16:30, 1 Kings 16:18), Philippians 1:21-23, and the
marital-duty family — and search for each of them in the top **25** of every
query the section adds. The r4 matrix is in the appendix. It found
Psalms 116:15 inside the served page on 13 queries against a dated written
ruling that excludes it (A1.9 Ruling 3), and Matthew 27:5 at #22/#24 on two
child question forms; it also *cleared* twenty other rows, which is the other
half of the point.

**Step 7 — print every reason label on every row you quote.** Also new in r4.
r3 printed one add-on as `+ 5.10` instead of by name, and the name was
`Related theme: Betrayed by a companion` on a widow's #2 result (critique
obj 2). CLAUDE.md non-negotiable #5 makes the explanation part of the
contract, so a document that quotes scores without labels cannot see its own
worst defect. **Rule: every result row quoted anywhere in this section shows
every reason label the engine returned for it.** Where a chip must never
appear at all, the fixture says so with `forbiddenReasonLabelSubstrings`,
which scans every returned result rather than a window
(`corpusGolden.ts:1279-1297`).

**Step 8 — write the fixture only then.** If a window fails, the fixture is
wrong until proven otherwise: widen it to what the run supports and say why,
or change the design. Raising a weight to win an assertion is weight-shopping;
adding a `related:` edge to fill a ban window is guard-shopping. Both are
refused below, by name.

**What each finding means when it fires** (so the next author does not
misread one):

- `G3_EXPECTED_TOP_ABSENT` — the window is wrong or the anchor is too light.
- `G3_MUST_NOT_RANK` — the ban's window is `measuredWindow` =
  `max(expectedWithinTop, largest non-presenceOnly expectedTop.withinTop)`
  (`corpusGolden.ts:798-806`). A pack with two anchors cannot clear a
  window-10 ban; that is arithmetic, not a fixable defect (A1.12).
- `G3_MUST_NOT_LEAD` — windows may be **1 or 3 only** (`corpusGolden.ts:616-624`).
- `G3_PREFERRED_ORDER` — **absence is not a failure**
  (`corpusGolden.ts:1299-1310`). A pin whose `below` ref never enters the
  window never fires and is decoration; both pins in this section are
  measured with both refs inside the window (A1.4, A1.9).

## A1.0e Merge order, phase, and cross-section coordination

Six things r2 and r3 left an engineer to guess. The critique executed A1.6
end-to-end from this text alone and had to decide four of them unaided
(critique obj 15); all four are answered below, in the file, not in prose
about the file.

**Merge order.** A1.6, A1.7 and A1.10 all edit
`ontology/concepts/pastoral-grief-and-loss.yaml`. Land them in this order, in
one PR train:

1. **A1.6** first — it adds the 61 phrases, the Isaiah 54:4-6 and John 14:1-3
   anchors, the Ps 34:18 weight edit, **and the two-line deletion in
   `ontology/concepts/godly-marriage.yaml` (A1.6 Ruling 5)**, all of which
   A1.7's and A1.10's measured tables assume. The godly-marriage deletion and
   its two `lexicon-inventory.yaml` row moves are part of **this** commit, not
   a follow-up: leaving them apart for even one commit leaves a widow's #2
   result labelled "Related theme: Betrayed by a companion".
2. **A1.7** second — appends four phrases (`my son died`, `my daughter died`,
   `lost my son`, `lost my daughter`) to the same `lexicon:` block, and four
   reunion phrases plus one weight edit to `pastoral-pregnancy-and-child-loss.yaml`.
3. **A1.10** third — appends `widower` and `widow` to the same block and edits
   the file's TOKENIZER NOTE.

A1.13 also touches `caring-for-aging-parents.yaml`, which A1.8 edits; land
A1.8 before A1.13 (A1.13's measured ladder assumes A1.8's phrases and A1.9's
bare `dementia`).

**Where lexicon entries go (guess 1a).** `ontology/concepts/*.yaml` `lexicon:`
blocks are flat lists with no section comments. The "Family 1…9" headings in
A1.1 and the "Family A/B/D/E/F/G" headings in A1.6 are **reading aids in this
document only** — append the phrases to the end of the existing list, in the
order given, with no new comment structure.

**Where anchors go, and what happens to a re-weighted one (guess 1b —
critique obj 15.1).** `pastoral-grief-and-loss.yaml` orders its `anchors:`
list by weight descending, with a per-anchor comment on the ones that need
one. **Keep that convention**: insert Isaiah 54:4-6 (0.9) after Revelation
21:3-4 (0.95) and before 1 Corinthians 15:54-57 (0.85), insert John 14:1-3
(0.9) immediately after it, and **move** the re-weighted `Psalms 34:18`
entry from its current position to directly below John 11:25-26 (1.0), which
is where 0.97 belongs. Moving it is a whitespace-level diff with no
behavioural effect — compiled anchors are keyed by ref, and
`compileConcepts` does not read list order — but a file whose stated
convention is "weight descending" and whose 0.97 anchor sits below two 0.95s
invites the next author to guess again. The same rule applies wherever this
section adds an anchor: **weight-descending, with the comment attached
above the entry.** Packs whose files are not weight-ordered (checked:
`loneliness.yaml`, `pet-loss.yaml` as newly minted) take the append
convention instead.

**Where the new inventory rows go (guess 4 — critique obj 15.4).** The
`concepts:` list in `ontology/lexicon-inventory.yaml` is **alphabetical by
compiled concept id**, and the parser does not care. Keep it alphabetical
anyway: `funeral-readings` goes between `friendship` and `generosity`,
`pet-loss` between `persecution` and `power-of-god`. The `collapses:` section
is also alphabetical by collapsed phrase. Rows are keyed by **compiled
concept id, never by filename** (`lexiconInventory.ts:109-113` fails a row
whose id does not compile), which is why `pastoral-grief-and-loss.yaml`'s row
is `grief-and-loss`.

**New pack filenames (guess 2 — critique obj 15.2).** The directory's
convention is genuinely inconsistent (`pastoral-grief-and-loss.yaml` for id
`grief-and-loss`, `care-for-widows.yaml` for id `care-for-widows`), so this
section states both paths rather than leaving the reader to pick:

| item | file path | compiled id |
|---|---|---|
| A1.11 | **`ontology/concepts/funeral-readings.yaml`** | `funeral-readings` |
| A1.12 | **`ontology/concepts/pet-loss.yaml`** | `pet-loss` |

The `pastoral-` prefix is used in this directory only for the 2026-07-31
pastoral-care wave and its later additions to those same files; a new pack
minted in this phase takes the bare id as its filename. Nothing in the
pipeline reads the filename — `compileConcepts` keys everything off the `id:`
field — so this is a readability convention and is recorded as one.

**The standing exclusions, and the rule that keeps them standing.**
`Psalms 116:15` ("Precious in the LORD's sight is the death of his saints")
carries a **standing global exclusion from illness, grief and despair
queries** — a 2026-08-15 ruling, recorded in
`pastoral-grief-and-loss.yaml`'s own header ("REJECTED from this pack and
globally gated"), in `caring-for-aging-parents.yaml`'s header ("STAYS OUT per
its standing global gate"), and carried as `mustNotRank` on six existing
fixtures. r3 extended two registers into packs that neighbour it and never
measured it; it was measured on **thirteen** of this section's own new
queries (critique obj 1). The rule, from here on:

> **Every new or extended fixture in a grief, bereavement, illness, dying or
> despair register carries `Psalms 116:15` in `mustNotRank`, with the measured
> position in its `why` — whether or not the ref currently surfaces.** A
> defensive ban costs one line and one assertion; discovering the breach in
> review costs a round. The same rule applies to the six suicide-narrative
> refs already banned elsewhere in the corpus (1 Sam 31:4, Judges 16:30,
> 1 Kings 16:18, 2 Sam 17:23, Matt 27:5, and Ahithophel's parallel) whenever
> the register can reach a death word.

§A1.0d Step 6 is the mechanical half of this rule: sweep the standing
exclusions across every query in the section before writing a guard table.
The **standing-exclusions matrix** in the Appendix is that sweep's output for
all 149 queries, and it is what a reviewer should read first.

**A `related:` edge makes an anchor addition someone else's problem (new in
r4 — finding r4-a).** `relatedConceptEvidence` pays an add-on to every anchor
a *related* pack also anchors, so **adding one anchor to pack P re-orders the
returned results of every pack that carries `related: P`** — including packs
no item in the PR train touches. This round measured it: A1.6 anchors
John 14:1-3 into `grief-and-loss` for the reunion question, and
`funeral-readings` — which carries `related: grief-and-loss` and anchors the
same verse at 1.0 — moved that verse from **#3 / #5** to **#1 on all nine**
of its queries, invalidating three printed ladders and one carefully-argued
boundary case in an item that changed nothing. The rule, from here on:

> **An item that adds, removes or re-weights an anchor must re-measure every
> pack with a `related:` edge *into* the pack it edited, in the same run, and
> print the after-ladder for each.** A fixture passing is **not** evidence
> this was done: a window of 5 cannot tell #5 from #1.

Compiled from the r4 tree, **nine** packs carry `related: grief-and-loss` and
are therefore in this section's blast radius every time A1.6 or A1.7 touches
an anchor: `care-for-widows`, `caring-for-aging-parents`, `comforting-others`,
`death-and-burial`, `funeral-readings`, `god-of-all-comfort`, `lament`,
`mortality` and `pregnancy-and-child-loss`. Three of them own fixtures this
section already runs (`care-for-widows`, `caring-for-aging-parents`,
`funeral-readings`); the other six are covered by the byte-identical
549-fixture regression in the Appendix, which is the evidence that the John
14:1-3 addition moved nothing they assert. Note that `pet-loss` is **not** on
this list — A1.12's `RELATED EDGE (r3)` decision replaced its
`grief-and-loss` edge with `near-to-the-brokenhearted`, which is why the pet
register was unaffected by A1.6's new anchor.

**Phase.** Every window asserted in this section is measured in **Phase A**,
against a corpus carrying only this section's data edits. No fixture here
waits on S-B §B.6 or any other engine change. Each item carries a
`**Phase.**` line saying so, and naming what B6 would change if it lands
later (B6 scales non-authoritative add-ons on anchored rows; it would tighten
several windows, and none of the assertions below depend on it).

**Cross-section coordination, open.**

| with | what | owner |
|---|---|---|
| **A2.14** | `giving up` / `feel like giving up` must be *removed* from `do-not-lose-heart` in the same merge, or both packs fire on `{giving}` and the two inventory rows contradict each other. If A2 lands first, A1.1's merge removes them; if A1 lands first, A2's merge must not add them. **A1.1's author owns the check either way.** Note also the pre-existing `{give, want}` dual-fire between the same two packs, which is unchanged by either item. | A1.1 |
| **A2.14b** | `im a failure` → `{failure}`: one owner only. Recommendation `identity-in-christ` (A1.2 Ruling 3). **Settled before assembly (C1):** A2.14b drops the bare-word admission (`failure` leaves `shame`'s `admitted:` list), drops the `shame` / `im a failure` collapse row, and removes `im a failure` from its `feel-like-a-failure` fixture, keeping `feel like a failure` and the Psalms 103:13-14 anchor. `identity-in-christ` owns `{failure}`; `pastoral-self-worth-failure` is the only fixture that asserts the query. The alternative — moving the token to `shame` instead — is rulings-register row 43, with what each choice costs. | A1.2 |
| **A3.4** | `{god, punish}` is A3.4's, not A1.3's — measured, and A1.3 adds no phrase for it. A3.4's fixture gains two guards this section measured. See A1.3 Ruling 4. | A1.3 |
| **A2 (`godly-marriage`)** | **A1.6 Ruling 5 deletes `husbands` and `wives` from `godly-marriage.yaml`'s lexicon and moves both tokens from `admitted:` to `skipped:` in `lexicon-inventory.yaml`.** Any A2 item that prints a measured position for a `{husband}`- or `{wive}`-only query must be re-measured after this lands. Measured, the only A2-relevant number that moves is **`my husband doesnt love me`: Eph 5:25 23.83 #1 → Romans 5:8 16.83 #1** (`Theme: The love of God`), with Titus 2:3-5 and Eph 5:28 leaving the top 4 — arguably an improvement for that query, but it is A2's call, not A1's. `my wife left me` is **unchanged** (`{wife, left}` never fired the pack). Every phrase-length godly-marriage query (`marriage`, `biblical marriage`, `godly husband`, `godly wife`, `prayer for my husband`, `husbands love your wives`) is **byte-identical before and after** — verified, and `eval/golden/godly-marriage.json` passes unchanged. **A1.6 owns the deletion; A2 owns re-printing any affected number.** | A1.6 |

A1.6 Ruling 6 claims them for `grief-and-loss` and gives the reason: the person typing them has had a death, and comfort is the answer that is true for every one of them, where a providence answer is true for only some. **A3.4 must not add a competing phrase for the same token sets.** If A3.4 wants the theodicy register, the phrasing that does not collide is the one without a relation noun (`why does god allow suffering`, `why did god let this happen`), which A1.6 deliberately does not claim. | A1.6 |

### A1.1 Extend `hope-in-despair` (`ontology/concepts/pastoral-hope-in-despair.yaml`)

**Measured gap (live, r2).** `"I want to kill myself"` → Acts 7:28 (11.17),
Ex 4:24 (9.70), Luke 13:31 (9.34), Luke 19:27 (8.90) — bare `{want, kill}`
scatter. `"kill myself"` → `{kill}` scatter: 1 Sam 1:25 (4.29, "They killed
the bull"), 1 Sam 31:2, Gen 38:7/38:10, Ex 4:23, then eight more sacrifice
and slaughter verses. `"end my life"` → Heb 7:3 (7.92, Melchizedek
typology). `"ending my life"` and `"want to end it all"` → noise.
`"dont want to be here anymore"` → Job 21:14 (8.06, the wicked telling God
"depart from us"). `"cant do this anymore"` → Job 23:8 (1.66) `cant` noise.
`"self injury"` → Galatians 5:23 (3.97, the fruit of the Spirit's
"self-control"). `"nobody would miss me"` → John 13:28 (2.14, the
disciples' confusion at Judas's exit). `"i feel like a burden"` →
**Psalms 73:5** (6.83, "They are free from burdens of men" — the *prospering
wicked*). `"burden to everyone"` → Nehemiah 4:17 (8.48, wall-builders
carrying loads). `"im a burden to my family"` → Numbers 4:24 (8.60, the
Gershonites' service loads). `"i want to disappear"` → 2 Sam 14:7 (6.00).
**`"i wish i was never born"` → the entire `salvation` pack** (Eph 2:8
16.16, Acts 16:30-31, Rom 10:9, John 3:3) because `born` reaches
born-again texts — a new finding, and a bad one: the register asking for
non-existence is answered with the new-birth. `"life is meaningless"` fires
only `vanity-of-life`. `"tired of living"` fires only `rest-for-the-weary`
(Isa 40:31 18.62), whose header scopes itself to burnout. `"giving up"` →
**Job 11:20** (10.00, `token_overlap: Exact phrase`) — "the eyes of the
**wicked** will fail… their hope will be the giving up of the spirit," the
one WEB occurrence of the string, and it is a description of the death of
the wicked. `"i dont want to live"` → **Job 7:16 at 36.53** (see Guards).

**contained in** `dont want to go to church anymore`
(`{dont, want, church, anymore}`) — an `additionalQuery` of S-A2 A2.18's

Under containment matching this pack therefore fires on that church query at

The church register wins the query **on its own parity**: it matches 4-of-4

**Narrowing this entry is not an available fix**: `dont want to be here`
normalizes to `{dont, want}`, a *smaller* set that fires on strictly more

```
                                    query "dont want to go to church anymore"
```

Coverage notes, each with the tokenizer output that justifies it:

- `cant do this anymore` also serves `"cant go on anymore"` →
  `{cant, anymore}`, identical. It does **not** serve
  `"cannot go on anymore"` → `{cannot, anymore}` — a different set, and
  r1 claimed otherwise. That phrasing is already in the pack's lexicon and
  already returns 2 Cor 1:8-10 at 40.00; it stays in `additionalQueries` as
  a regression check.
- `tired of living` also serves `"im so tired of living"` →
  `{tired, living}`.
- `what is the point of living` also serves `"whats the point of living"`
  and `"no point in living"` → `{point, living}` for all three.
- `i wish i was never born` also serves `"i wish i had never been born"` →
  `{wish, never, born}`.
- `end my life` `{end, life}` and `ending my life` `{ending, life}` are
  **distinct** (`ending` is 6 chars, 6−3 = 3 < 4, below the stemmer's
  floor); both entries are needed and both are tested.

Three phrasings are unreachable at any safe width and are **not** added:
`i cant go on` → `{cant}`; `im a burden` / `i am a burden` / `such a
burden` → `{burden}`; `im all alone` → `{alone}`. `i feel like a burden`
and `im a burden to my family` are the substitutes for the second.

`"better off without me"` → `{better, without}` is safe by width and is
still **declined**: the identical token set is produced by
`"im better off without him"` / `"…without her"`, an ordinary
breakup/divorce query, so the entry would serve the crisis pack's whole
anchor set to that searcher. Measured today the register is genuinely
unserved (`"better off without me"` → Eccl 10:11, 1 Cor 9:15, 2 Cor 11:23
at 6.00, pure `translation_variant`), but the pack's own existing 3-token
`everyone would be better off without me` covers the unambiguous phrasing
and returns 2 Cor 1:8-10 at **40.00** today. Same reasoning as the deferred
bare `cant`: a phrase that fires this pack far outside its register is a
harm, not a gap closure.

**Deferred to Phase C** (needs tokenizer v2 / S-B §B.1). All counts are
`select count(distinct verse_row_id) from verse_tokens where token = ?`
against `fixture.db`, so they are verse counts and comparable with one
another: bare `hate` (**118 verses**; see A1.2, which ships two safe phrasal
substitutes); bare `burden` (**90 verses**, overwhelmingly slave-labour /
priestly-service / prophetic-oracle senses — r2 said 91, which was the
occurrence count, not the verse count); bare `cant` (**187 verses** — r2 wrote
"0 native occurrences", which reads as a corpus count and is wrong: WEB's own
contractions put `cant` in 187 verses, in as many unrelated senses, which
makes the refusal *more* justified, not less); bare `hurt`; bare `alone`
(**116 verses**; see A1.4, and the corrected disclosure in the Summary).

**Cross-item hazard (obj 35).** `funeral-readings` (A1.11) anchors
Ecclesiastes 3:1-4, whose v3 is "a time to **kill**, and a time to heal."
Measured: Eccl 3:3 does not appear in the top 12 for `"kill myself"` today,
and `funeral-readings` carries no phrase normalizing to `{kill}` (see its
token list), so the bare `kill` admission cannot fire it. After this item
lands, ten anchors at 22.00→7.70 sit above every `kill` token-overlap row.
No guard needed; recorded so the interaction is on the record.

**Guards.**

1. **Bare `kill` (via `kill myself`): admit now**, with the guards above and
   the `collapses:` + `admitted:` rows of §A1.0a. Unlike `funeral`/`widower`,
   `kill` **is** WEB-native, so this is a risk-accepted policy call, not a
   zero-occurrence freebie — recommended because the harm is live today and
   the discount mechanism is identical to the already-approved `suicide` /
   `suicidal` / `cutting` admissions in this same file.
2. **Bare `giving` (via `giving up`): admit now.** Moved here from A2.14 by
   owner decision. `giving` does not stem to `give`, so the pack's existing
   `want to give up` / `ready to give up` never reached it — measured, the
   query returns Job 11:20 (the death of the wicked) at #1. **Merge
   coordination:** `giving up` and `feel like giving up` must be *removed*
   from A2.14's `do-not-lose-heart` edit in the same merge, or both packs
   fire on `{giving}` and the two inventory rows contradict each other.
3. **Job 7:16 anchor: do NOT add** (reverses r1's "apply as given"). The
   stated warrant — "direct textual match for 'I don't want to live'" — does
   not survive the WEB text, which reads "I don't want to live **forever**"
   and continues "Leave me alone," one verse after "my soul chooses

   its own `mustNotLead` in mechanical tension. It is guarded instead, and

   validation. If lament validation is wanted with a stronger voice,
   **Job 7:11** ("I will not keep silent. I will speak in the anguish of my
   spirit") is the verse to consider — recorded, not proposed.
4. **Bare `cant`, `burden`, `alone`, `hate`: do not admit in Phase A.**
   Revisit with S-B §B.1 tokenizer v2.
5. **`better off without me`: declined**, with the token-set collision
   measurement above. A decision, not an omission.

`self hatred` and `i hate my life` are genuinely distinct entry points:

1:21, Psalms 56:12, Deuteronomy 13:12)". Re-measured:

```
== "god is angry with me"                     == "angry at god"
  1. Genesis 32:24-30  40.71  Wrestling with God     identical, row for row
  2. Psalms 13:1-2     36.00  Wrestling with God
  3. Psalms 73:16-17   34.00  Wrestling with God
  4. Hosea 12:3-4      32.00  Wrestling with God
  5. Job 23:3-4        30.00  Wrestling with God
```

The cited noise triple is `"god gave up on me"`'s measurement
(Ex 1:21 11.41, Ps 56:12 11.11, Deut 13:12 11.00), mis-attributed. The
cause is checkable and decides this item:

```
"angry at god"          -> {angry, god}    (wrestling-with-god's existing phrase)
"god is angry with me"  -> {god, angry}    SAME SET
"is god angry with me"  -> {god, angry}    SAME SET
```

Concept matching is set-containment (`repository.ts:705-707`), so a second
`{angry, god}` phrase in `gods-love` would fire **both** packs for **both**
phrasings, identically, in both directions of the felt need — the searcher
angry *at* God and the searcher afraid God is angry *at them*. G4 would not
flag it, because `collisionGate` compares the joined normalized string
(`"angry god"` vs `"god angry"`, `collision.ts:82-84`) — so r1's "G4 green"
claim was not evidence of no overlap.

The remaining registers **are** broken and are what this item fixes:
`"god hates me"` → Deut 16:22 (10.44, a sacred-stone/idolatry text),
Mal 2:16 (7.22, marital treachery), Deut 30:7, Deut 12:31, Ps 68:1 — all
wrong-sense `hate`. `"god gave up on me"` → Ex 1:21 (11.41), Ps 56:12,
Deut 13:12 — pure `{god, give}` noise. `"god is mad at me"` →
`{god, mad}` → Jeremiah 29:26 (1.87, "every man who is crazy and makes
himself a prophet") — the register with a *distinguishing* token, and it
reaches nothing.

**Change.**

```yaml
lexicon:
  - god hates me
  - god gave up on me
  - god is mad at me     # {god, mad} — the distinguishing token; deliberately
                          # NOT "god is angry with me" ({god, angry}, which
                          # wrestling-with-god already owns). Ruling 1.
```

**No new anchor.** r1 proposed Ps 86:15 at 0.7. Arithmetic (Ruling 2): at
parity this pack's ladder is 40.00 (John 3:16 1.0), 38.00 (Rom 8:38-39
0.95), 36.00 (Rom 5:8 0.9), 34.00 (Rom 8:31-32 0.85), then **five** anchors
at 32.00 (1 Jn 4:9-10, Rom 8:35, Eph 2:4-5, 1 Jn 4:16, Zeph 3:17 — the last
verified present and scoring live at 35.33 for `"god loves you"`), then four
at 30.00. A 0.7 anchor scores **28.00 and lands #14-#16**. It would change
nothing a searcher sees: `NO MEASURABLE EFFECT`, which CLAUDE.md says means
do not merge.

**Tokenizer hazards.**

```
"god hates me"         -> {god, hate}    fires on the phrase, not bare `hate`
"god gave up on me"    -> {god, give}    `gave` → `give` via the irregular table
"god is mad at me"     -> {god, mad}
"god is angry with me" -> {god, angry}   NOT ADDED — see Ruling 1
```

**Guards.** At parity this pack's 10th anchor scores **30.00**, so every
measured harm below (max 11.41) leaves the window-10 ban comfortably.

**Pastoral caution (PR body, not a guard).** Per DOCTRINAL-BASIS §1's
"reports, never adjudicates" boundary, this register must never sound like
the engine is deciding *whether the searcher's sin justifies the feeling*.
Every anchor it reaches states who God is; none renders a verdict.

**Rulings for Jesse.** Both were hidden decisions in r1.
1. **`{angry, god}` stays with `wrestling-with-god`; `gods-love` takes
   `{god, mad}` instead.** Measured basis: the token set is already owned,
   and what it returns — Ps 13:1-2 "How long, LORD? Will you forget me
   forever?", Job 23:3-4 "Oh that I knew where I might find him!" — is a
   defensible pastoral answer to *both* directions of the felt need, while a
   second pack on the same set would be an unresolvable dual-fire the
   tokenizer cannot arbitrate. The honest cost, recorded: a searcher who
   types the exact words "God is angry with me" gets lament anchors, not
   "slow to anger" — and only a phrase carrying a distinguishing token
   (`mad`), or S-B §B.5 ordered phrases, changes that.
2. **Ps 86:15 anchor: do not add at 0.7** (reverses r1). Two honest options
   were costed: (a) 0.7 → 28.00, position #14-#16, no measurable effect;
   (b) ≥0.9 → 36.00, position #3-#4, measurable — but 0.9 also reorders
   *every* `gods-love` query, putting a slow-to-anger confession above
   Rom 8:31-32 and Rom 8:35 for "God loves you". Recommendation: neither;
   ship the item lexicon-only. The measurable effect this item claims is the
   whole pack becoming reachable from a query that today returns an idolatry
   text at #1 — which is a large one.
3. **Routing "God hates me" to `gods-love` rather than `shame`**: named, not
   silent. "God hates me" is a claim about *God's* disposition, which is
   this pack's subject; `shame` answers a claim about the searcher's own
   standing. Recorded so the next assessor can reverse it deliberately.

4. **`"God is punishing me"`: the register is real and this item does not
   own it** (critique obj 12, measured and coordinated). The critique is
   right that the register is live and harmful — measured on the base corpus,
   `"god is punishing me"` returns **Job 31:28 9.71 #1** ("this also would be
   an iniquity to be punished by the judges") and **2 Thessalonians 1:8 8.44
   #2** ("giving vengeance to those who don't know God"), a judgment oracle
   handed to a person asking whether God is punishing them. It is wrong
   about ownership, and one run settles it:

   ```
   "god is punishing me"     -> {god, punish}
   "why is god punishing me" -> {god, punish}
   "is god punishing me"     -> {god, punish}        <- S-A3 §A3.4's phrase
   ```

   All three are the same token set, and **S-A3 §A3.4 already adds
   `is god punishing me` to `why-god-allows-suffering`**. Adding a second
   `{god, punish}` phrase here would be the identical unresolvable dual-fire
   Ruling 1 refuses for `{angry, god}` — and would break invariant 1 across
   sections. So `gods-love` adds nothing, and the fix is in A3.4's own pack.

   Simulated with A3.4's four phrases applied, `"god is punishing me"` and
   `"why is god punishing me"` return, identically:

   ```
   1. Job 1:21          40.00  [concept_anchor:Theme: Why God allows suffering]
   2. Genesis 50:20     36.61  3. Romans 8:18        36.00
   4. 2 Cor 4:17-18     34.00  5. Job 42:5           32.00
   6. Luke 13:2-5       32.00  7. John 9:2-3         32.00
   8. 1 Peter 4:19      30.00  9. Job 1:8            10.50
  10. Job 31:28          9.71 11. 2 Thessalonians 1:8  8.44
   ```

   **Two guards A3.4 must carry, measured here so its author does not have to
   re-derive them** (`eval/golden/why-do-i-suffer-plain-language.json`):

   ```json
   "mustNotRank": [
     { "ref": "2 Thessalonians 1:8", "why": "'Giving vengeance to those who don't know God' — a judgment oracle, measured 8.44 #2 for 'god is punishing me' before A3.4, #11 (outside the window) after." }
   ],
   "mustNotLead": [
     { "ref": "Job 31:28", "withinTop": 3, "why": "'An iniquity to be punished by the judges' — measured 9.71 #1 for 'god is punishing me' before A3.4, #10 after. It cannot be a mustNotRank: the window is 10 and it sits exactly at 10." }
   ]
   ```

   Both were run against the simulated corpus and **pass**; the ban is a ban
   because 2 Thess 1:8 leaves the window, and the leadership guard is a
   leadership guard because Job 31:28 does not. No phrase is duplicated across
   packs. Recorded in §A1.0e as an open cross-section item.

### A1.4 Extend `loneliness` (`ontology/concepts/loneliness.yaml`)

**Measured gap (live, r2).** `"God abandoned me"` → 2 Kings 21:22 (9.54,
"he **abandoned** Yahweh, the God of his fathers" — Amon), Deut 32:15
(8.50, "he **abandoned** God who made him"), Jer 22:9 (8.20), Judges 2:12
(7.60), 1 Kings 9:9 (7.60). **Every hit has the subject and object
reversed**: Scripture uses "abandon" almost exclusively for Israel and its
kings forsaking God, never God forsaking a person. `"im all alone"` →
**Proverbs 5:17** (7.50, "Let them be for yourself **alone**, not for
strangers with you" — marital fidelity), Job 31:17, Lam 3:28.

**Change.**

```yaml
# ontology/concepts/loneliness.yaml
lexicon:
  - god abandoned me       # also serves "has god abandoned me" — identical
                            # token set {god, abandon}
  - i feel abandoned by god
  - god has forsaken me    # NEW in r4 — {god, forsaken}, a DISTINCT token
                           # set from {god, abandon}; see Ruling 5
anchors:
  - ref: Psalms 22:1
    sources: [editorial]
    weight: 0.5
  - ref: Matthew 27:46
    sources: [editorial]
    weight: 0.5
  - ref: Psalms 22:24        # NEW in r2 — the psalm's own answer
    sources: [editorial]
    weight: 0.65
  - ref: Isaiah 49:15-16     # NEW in r3 — Ruling 4; the tenth anchor, and
    sources: [editorial]     # the reason the five reversal bans hold
    weight: 0.6
```

```yaml
# ontology/concepts/presence-of-god.yaml — ONE lexicon entry, no anchors,
# no weight change (r4, Ruling 5). This is the half of the fix that works:
# the pack already anchors Hebrews 13:5 at 0.9, and Hebrews 13:5 is God
# saying "I will in no way ... forsake you" in the searcher's own word.
lexicon:
  - god has forsaken me
```

**Tokenizer hazards.** Live output:

```
"god abandoned me"        -> {god, abandon}
"has god abandoned me"    -> {god, abandon}   identical; one entry serves both
"i feel abandoned by god" -> {feel, abandon, god}
"god has forsaken me"     -> {god, forsaken}  NEW in r4 — a DISTINCT set
"why has god forsaken me" -> {god, forsaken}  identical set, different result
"has god forsaken me"     -> {god, forsaken}  (exact_phrase reads the string)
"feeling alone"           -> {feel, alone}    the pack's EXISTING phrase
"im all alone"            -> {alone}          BARE — unreachable, not added
```

`forsaken` is **8 characters** and does not stem to `forsake`; `forsook`
is a fourth token again. The register has four verbs in the corpus
(`abandon`, `forsake`, `forsaken`, `forsook`) and the pack now reaches two of
them by lexicon. The other two get no phrase, because this section adds no
lexicon entry it does not also exercise with a fixture query (invariant 1),
and no query below uses them. If a later measurement finds real traffic on
`forsook`, it is one entry and one query, not a redesign.

Correction to r1: the existing phrase is `feeling alone` → **`{feel, alone}`**,
not `{feeling, alone}` (`feeling` is 7 chars, 7−3 = 4 ≥ 4, so it stems).
That is good news r1 did not claim: `"i feel so alone"` and
`"feeling all alone"` also reach the pack. It does **not** rescue
`"im all alone"`, which collapses to bare `{alone}` (`im` is 2 characters,
dropped by the length floor; `all` is a stopword).

Direct WEB check on bare `alone`: **116 occurrences**, overwhelmingly
unrelated senses — "It is not good for the man to be alone" (Gen 2:18),
"Leave me alone" as dismissal (Ex 32:10, Num 11:14), "the LORD alone led
him" (Deut 32:12), "I am not able to bear… myself alone" (Deut 1:9, 1:12).
Not a safe bare admission; deferred to Phase C with `hate` / `worthless` /
`burden`.

**Anchors.**

| ref | WEB opening words (verified in `fixture.db`) | weight | why this is how God's word answers this search | sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Psalms 22:1 | "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? Why are you so far from helping me…?" | 0.5 | Not a doctrinal claim about the Trinity — a pastoral one: these are Christ's own words on the cross. A person crying "God has abandoned me" is not saying anything Christ himself did not say; the value is companionship in the very words, not resolution. | editorial; GotQuestions; Ligonier ("The Suffering and the Glory of Psalm 22") |
| Matthew 27:46 | "About the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice… 'My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?'" | 0.5 | The Gospel's own record of the same cry, cited separately per the schema's no-duplicate-range rule. | editorial; same sources |
| **Psalms 22:24** | "For he has not despised nor abhorred the affliction of the afflicted, neither has he hidden his face from him; but when he cried to him, he heard." | 0.65 | **New in r2.** r1 argued Ps 22:1 must not lead *because the psalm resolves later*, then anchored nothing from later. This is that resolution, in the same psalm, a separate range — so the answer travels with the cry instead of being asserted about it. At 0.65 it scores 26.00 and sits above both cries (20.00), which is the ordering the argument requires. | editorial; the psalm's own structure |
| **Isaiah 49:15-16** | "Can a woman forget her nursing child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb? Yes, these may forget, yet I will not forget you! Behold, I have engraved you on the palms of my hands." | 0.6 | **New in r3, and it does two jobs.** Pastorally it is the canon's most direct answer to "God abandoned me": not *he has not left*, but *he could not forget you if he tried*. Mechanically it is the pack's **tenth** anchor, and the r2 guard table was wrong without it — see the Guards block. r2 declined it under "fewer, stronger" on the reasoning that Deut 31:8 and Heb 13:5 already carry the never-forsake promise; they carry the promise, and this carries the *tenderness*, which is the register's actual felt need. **Context disclosed (critique obj 13),** on the same standard this section applies to Jeremiah 31:15 (A1.7 Ruling 3), Isaiah 54:4-6 (A1.6) and Job 1:21 (A1.11): the oracle's addressee is **Zion**, and v14 — one verse above the anchor — is "But Zion said, 'The LORD has forsaken me, and the Lord has forgotten me.'" The anchor range **starts at v15**, so nothing the searcher reads carries a corporate referent, and the appropriation is the *strongest* of the section's three: the verse is literally God's answer to the sentence the searcher just typed. r3 exempted it from its own disclosure test on the grounds that the reading was obvious; a disclosure that is only written down when the case is weak is not a standard. | editorial; the verse's standing in every pastoral source surveyed for this register |

r2 considered and declined this anchor. The r2 critique's simulated gate then
returned three failures caused by its absence, on this item's own headline
harm. Both halves of that are recorded in Ruling 4.

**Guards.**

**Measured, after the change** — the full returned rows for the fixture's own
query, not a weight ladder. r2 printed the ladder above as if it were the
result set; it is the anchor component only, and it hid two things: Hebrews
13:5 collects a **14.00 `translation_variant`** add-on on this query and takes


**Why r2's guard table was exactly backwards (critique obj 2).** r2 wrote
"max measured harm 9.54, **9th anchor 20.00 — all clear**". With nine anchors,
positions 1-9 are the anchors and position **10** is the highest remaining
row — which is 2 Kings 21:22 at 9.54, *inside* the fixture's measured window
of 10. All three of this fixture's queries failed the real gate on that one
ref. The arithmetic that matters is not "is the harm below the last anchor"
but "does the anchor set fill the window": a window-10 ban needs **ten**
rows above the harm. Isaiah 49:15-16 is the tenth, and with it 2 Kings 21:22
lands **#11** and all five reversal bans hold.

mustNotRank (window 10; measured positions after the change):

| ref | why | before → after |

| 2 Kings 21:22 | "he **abandoned** Yahweh, the God of his fathers" (Amon) — reversed direction. | 9.54 **#1** → **#11** |
| Deuteronomy 32:15 | "he **abandoned** God who made him" — same reversal. | 8.50 #2 → **#12** |
