| 1 Kings 9:9 | "because they **abandoned** the LORD their God" — same. | 7.60 #5 → below #14 |

mustNotLead (measured):

| ref | withinTop | why REQUIRED | measured after |
|---|---|---|---|
| Psalms 22:1 | 3 | Lament may accompany this register; leading with the cry alone risks compounding despair rather than companioning it. r1 asked for window 1; r2 raised it to 3, which the run supports. | **#10** |
| Matthew 27:46 | 3 | Same ruling, same reasoning — the Gospel narrative continues past this verse. | **#9** (21.34 — it picks up a 1.34 `passage_terms: abandon` chip Ps 22:1 does not) |

`preferredOrder` Ps 22:24 above Ps 22:1, window 10: **both refs are inside the
window** (#7 and #10), so the pin is evaluated and passes. That is the test
A1.9's r2 pin failed (obj 11) and the reason this one is written at 10.

**Proverbs 5:17 is removed from this item's guards.** r1's Guards table
listed it and the fixture did not, which is the exact "guard that exists in
prose and nowhere in the fixture" failure. It cannot be fixed either way
round: Prov 5:17 is measured **#1 at 7.50** for `"im all alone"`, that query
collapses to bare `{alone}`, bare `{alone}` is deferred, and no phrase in
this pack can reach it — so a `mustNotRank` would fail the build and a
fixture query for it would fail too. **Stated plainly: the bare-`{alone}`
phrasings carry no machine-checkable guard until Phase C (S-B §B.1).**

**And the exact scope of that, measured (critique obj 24).** r2's Summary
called the `alone` register "genuinely unserved", which overstates. The
register splits cleanly on one token:

```
"i feel so alone"    -> {feel, alone}    "feeling all alone" -> {feel, alone}
"im all alone"       -> {alone}          "all alone"         -> {alone}
```

The `{feel, alone}` half is **served today** by the pack's existing
`feeling alone` phrase — measured, both phrasings return Ps 27:10 **44.50 #1**,
Deut 31:8 36.00, John 14:18 34.00, Heb 13:5 33.40, and after this item
Ps 22:24 #7 and Isa 49:15-16 #8. The bare `{alone}` half is not, and returns
Prov 5:17 at 7.50 #1 unchanged. **That** is the unserved register, it is one
phrasing family and not the whole of `alone`, and the Summary is corrected to
say so.

**The register's other half, which r3 never typed: `"god has forsaken me"`
(critique obj 6).** The item anchors two verses whose own words are *"why
have you forsaken me"* and never measures the sentence a person actually
types with that verb. Measured on the base corpus:

```
== "god has forsaken me"                (base, before this item)
   1. Psalms 71:11        50.70  [Exact phrase 40.00 | proximity 5.70 | Shared words: forsaken, god 5.00]
   2. Jeremiah 2:17        9.54    3. Ezra 9:10            9.01
   4. Matthew 27:46        8.87    5. Judges 10:10         8.56
   6. 2 Chronicles 13:10   8.44    7. 2 Chronicles 21:10   8.18
```

**Psalms 71:11 is the persecutors' taunt**, spoken *about* the psalmist by
the people hunting him: "saying, 'God has forsaken him. Pursue and take him,
for there is no one to deliver him.'" A person who types "God has forsaken
me" is served, at #1, the sentence his enemies say about him — presented as
`Exact phrase`, the engine's most confident-sounding reason label. Rows 2, 3,
5, 6 and 7 are the same subject/object reversal this item already documents
for `abandon` (Israel forsaking God), and row 4 is the dereliction cry the
item deliberately demotes.

**Why the pack's existing phrases do not reach it.** `god abandoned me` →
`{god, abandon}`; `god has forsaken me` → **`{god, forsaken}`** (`has` and
`me` are stopwords; `forsaken` is 8 characters and does **not** stem to
`forsake`, so it is a fourth distinct token beside `abandon`, `forsake` and
`forsook`). Containment cannot bridge them. The register has two verbs and
the pack carried one.

**The fix, and why one pack was not enough.** Adding `god has forsaken me` to
`loneliness` alone is measurably insufficient: `Psalms 27:10` at weight 1.0
takes parity 40.00 and collects 6.21 of add-ons for **46.21** — still below
Ps 71:11's 50.70, so the taunt keeps #1 and the guard fails. Nothing inside
`loneliness` can beat 50.70: its top anchor is Ps 27:10, and raising a weight
to out-score an `exact_phrase` hit is weight-shopping to win a fixture, which
A1.5 and A1.6 both refuse by name.

**So the phrase is added to two packs, and the second one is the answer.**
`presence-of-god` anchors **Hebrews 13:5** at 0.9 — *"for he has said, 'I
will in no way leave you, neither will I in any way forsake you'"* — which is
God's own use of the searcher's own word, in the negative. `loneliness`
anchors the same verse at 0.7. Both fire, the two `concept_anchor`
components are additive, and Hebrews 13:5 scores **64.00**:

```
== "god has forsaken me"                 (after; identical top rows on
   1. Hebrews 13:5      64.00  [Theme: The presence of God 36.00 | Theme: Loneliness 28.00]
   2. Psalms 71:11      50.70  [Exact phrase 40.00 | proximity 5.70 | Shared words: forsaken, god 5.00]
   3. Psalms 27:10      46.21  [Theme: Loneliness 40.00 | Related theme: The God who sees 4.50 | Preached vocabulary: forsaken 1.71]
   4. Psalms 139:7-10   40.00     5. James 4:8         38.00
   6. Deuteronomy 31:8  36.00     7. John 14:18        34.00
   8. Psalms 68:6       32.00     9. Matthew 28:20     30.00
  10. John 14:23        30.00
```

That is the ordering a pastor would choose without knowing the arithmetic:
the searcher's sentence is *"God has forsaken me"*, and the first thing the
engine says back is God's own *"I will never forsake you."* The taunt is not
suppressed — it is at #2, where a person who wants the psalm can find it, and
where it reads as the psalm's setting rather than as the engine's answer.

**Dual-homing is deliberate, and it is not a G4 collision.** The two packs
share exactly this one phrase; measured, `loneliness` and `presence-of-god`
share **1 lexicon phrase and 2 vocabulary tokens**, far under
`maxSharedPhraseRatio` 0.34 and `maxSharedTokenRatio` 0.60. G4 collision
passes with 291 concepts mutually distinct. The precedent is the pack
header's own: `overdose` is deliberately in both `grief-and-loss` and
`freedom-from-bondage` because "the same word is an addict's fear and a
survivor's grief". `God has forsaken me` is both a lonely person's sentence
and a question about whether God is there; both packs answer it, and their
answers add.

**Two phrasings, one token set, two different results — and the fixture tests
both.** `why has god forsaken me` and `has god forsaken me` both tokenize to
`{god, forsaken}`, identical to the entry. They are still worth asserting
separately, because `exact_phrase` matches the **query string**, not the
token set: on those two phrasings Ps 71:11 loses its 40.00 and drops out of
the top 10 entirely — measured **#16 at 10.70** — while Hebrews 13:5 stays
at 64.00 #1. The
fixture carries `why has god forsaken me` as an `additionalQuery` for exactly
that reason, and the note says so — this is the one place in the section
where two queries with the same token set are not redundant.

**A separate fixture, not an extra query on `pastoral-god-abandoned-me`.**
Measured: on `god has forsaken me`, `Deuteronomy 31:8` is **#6**, and that
fixture asserts it `withinTop: 3`. Adding the query there would fail the
build on an assertion that is correct for the `abandon` half of the register.
Two verbs, two result shapes, two fixtures.

5. **Lamentations 3:31-33 in `loneliness`: DECLINED in r4, and the reason is
   a measurement, not a preference** (the critique's must-add list). "For the

   the children of men" is the doctrinal answer this register lacks, and the
   critique is right that it belongs beside Isaiah 49's tenderness. It was

   ```

     7. Psalms 22:24  26.00    8. Isaiah 49:15-16  24.00
     9. Lamentations 3:31-33  24.00   10. Matthew 27:46  21.34
    11. Psalms 22:1  20.00    <- pushed OUT of the window
   ```

   The pack would then have **eleven** anchors against a fixture window of
   **10**, and Psalms 22:1 falls to #11. This item's `preferredOrder` pin —
   Ps 22:24 above Ps 22:1, the mechanism that makes *the psalm's own
   resolution outrank the psalm's cry* — then stops being evaluated at all.
   **Proved by reversal, not assumed:** with the eleventh anchor in place, a
   *deliberately inverted* pin (Ps 22:1 above Ps 22:24) **also passes**;
   without it, the inverted pin fails with `found them at positions 10 and 7`.
   That is precisely the "guardrail becomes decoration" class this item was
   corrected for in r3 (critique obj 11), reintroduced by a good verse.

   **`withinTop` accepts only 1, 3, 5 and 10**, so there is no window of 11
   to widen to. The options are therefore: **(a) decline the anchor** — what
   r4 does; **(b) add it and delete the pin**, accepting that "resolution
   above cry" becomes a claim in prose that nothing checks; **(c)** find it
   another home, which is a separate item's work and not this one's.
   **Recommendation: (a) for now, and (b) is a defensible reversal if Jesse
   values the verse above the pin** — but it must be taken deliberately,
   because the cost is an unrun check, and this section's own gate discipline
   says an unrun check must never report `pass`.
6. **`god has forsaken me` in BOTH `loneliness` and `presence-of-god`: new
   in r4, recommended, and this is a real decision.** Dual-homing one phrase
   is a departure from the section's own "one home only" rule (A1.6 Ruling 1,
   A1.7 Ruling 2), and it is taken deliberately, on the precedent this pack's
   neighbour already set for `overdose`. The measured cost of the alternatives
   is stated rather than argued: **(a)** `loneliness` only — Ps 71:11 keeps
   #1 at 50.70 and the item's own headline harm survives, so this fails;
   **(b)** raise a `loneliness` weight until something beats 50.70 — this is
   weight-shopping to win a fixture, refused by name in A1.5 and A1.6, and it
   would move that anchor for every other query in the pack; **(c)** anchor
   Hebrews 13:5 higher inside `loneliness` — same objection, and it would
   demote Ps 27:10 for `feeling alone`, which is measured and correct today;
   **(d)** the recommended route — one lexicon line in the pack that already
   anchors the right verse at the right weight, changing no weight anywhere.
   The cost of (d) is that `presence-of-god` now fires on a lament phrasing,
   which is visible in the result set as a second `Theme:` label on the
   leading row and is, on inspection, the correct explanation: the searcher
   asked whether God is there. **If Jesse prefers strict one-home, the honest
   consequence is that Ps 71:11 stays at #1 and this objection is not fixed**
   — that is the trade, and the recommendation is (d).

### A1.5 Extend `forgiveness-of-sins` (`ontology/concepts/forgiveness-of-sins.yaml`)

**Measured gap (live, r2).** `"im too far gone"` → Romans 13:12 (10.00,
"The night is far gone, and the day is near"), Jeremiah 2:5 (9.08), Numbers
16:7 (8.56), Genesis 44:4 — pure `{far, gone}` proximity noise.
`"cant be forgiven"` reaches real forgiveness texts only through the bare
token `forgiven`, which R1 documents as an orphan: `forgive` / `forgiv` /
`forgiveness` are all carried by existing lexicon entries and `forgiven` is
carried by none, so the pack's own curated anchors (Ps 103:12, Isa 1:18,
1 John 1:9) never appear with a chip.

**Change.**

```yaml
lexicon:
  - too far gone
  - cant be forgiven       # {cant, forgiven}
  - cannot be forgiven     # {cannot, forgiven} — a DISTINCT set; r1 shipped
                            # only the contracted form
  - beyond forgiveness
anchors:
  - ref: 1 Timothy 1:15-16
    sources: [editorial]
    weight: 0.8
  - ref: Luke 23:42-43
    sources: [editorial]
    weight: 0.75
```

**Tokenizer hazards.**

```
"too far gone"        -> {far, gone}          also serves "im too far gone"
"cant be forgiven"    -> {cant, forgiven}
"cannot be forgiven"  -> {cannot, forgiven}   DISTINCT — both entries needed
"beyond forgiveness"  -> {beyond, forgiveness}
```

`too far gone` is **not** an `additionalQuery`: `{far, gone}` is identical to
the fixture's own query `"im too far gone"`, so listing it would break the
section's invariant 1, which A1.2 and A1.10 apply explicitly and r2 broke here
and in A1.4 (critique obj 18). Both are fixed.

Two of those are the audit's own flagship harms returned **verbatim** to a
question form the section shipped without: `Husbands, love your wives` to a
widow and `A man shall not take his father's wife` to a widower. One is the
euphemism harm this item already bans for nine relations and left open for
five. One is a suicide narrative. That is what "type the query the way a
person in pain types it" found, and it is why §A1.0d now has a step for it.

An unbroken run of marital-submission texts for a fresh widow, via
`godly-marriage.yaml`'s bare `husbands` / `wives` cues; the Tenth
Commandment for a widower; dying-to-sin theology and genealogical formulas
for a bereaved child; "the world is **passing away**" for the euphemism
family; and the Tamar/Amnon rape narrative for a bereaved sister.

**The one harm Phase A cannot remove.** `"my wife died"` → **Ezekiel 24:18
at 40.00**, a bare `exact_phrase` hit inside the passage where God
*forbids* Ezekiel to mourn as a prophetic sign-act. `exact_phrase` is an
authoritative family, so S-B §B.2's sole-evidence ceiling never fires on it
(§A1.0c) and no Phase A data change lowers it. What Phase A *can* do is put
a curated anchor level with it and win the tie: `compareResults`
(`rank.ts:57-77`) breaks an exact tie between two authoritative results in
favour of the `concept_anchor` one. John 11:25-26 at parity scores exactly
**40.00**, so it takes #1 and Ezekiel 24:18 becomes **#2**. The fixture
therefore guards it as `mustNotLead withinTop 1` — the strongest claim that
is true. r1's `mustNotRank` on it would have failed the build.

Three tokenizer facts do real work here and are worth stating, because each
one refutes a plausible assumption:

- **`did` → `do`, and `let` and `why` vanish.** `why did god let my husband
  die` is **`{do, god, husband, die}`** — four tokens, not six. `let` is a
  stopword and `why` is dropped; `did` stems to `do`, which is a *generic*
  token that the pack now carries in sixteen entries. That is safe only
  because matching is containment over the **whole** set: `{do, god, husband,
  die}` requires all four.
- **`will`, `i` and `again` all vanish.** `will i see my husband again` is
  **`{see, husband}`** — two tokens. There is no phrasing of the reunion
  question that survives the tokenizer with more than the verb and the
  relation. Ruling 7 costs what that means.
- **`take` and `die` are what separate Family G from Family H**, so the two
  families never collapse into each other; and `{do, god, take, son}` is
  disjoint from `{do, god, son, die}`, so both phrasings need their own entry.
  Sixteen entries is not padding.

`died` / `dies` / `dying` / `death` are four separate tokens (none stems
below the 4-character floor), so each family needs its own past-tense entry
and its own present-progressive entry; this item carries the past tense and
A1.8/A1.9 carry "is dying". `{lost, mother}` is a **distinct** set from
`{mother, died}` — and `{lost, mom}` is distinct from **both** (critique obj
8: r3 shipped `lost my mother` and `lost my father` and left the two words
people actually type uncovered, where they returned Matthew 18:11 at 3.35 on
a bare `lost` chip, and `lost my brother` returned Deuteronomy 22:3, "every
lost thing of your brother's"). The tested query never stands in for an
untested set, which is why all **61** sets are tested below: 1 `query` + 60
`additionalQueries`. (r2's Change block, hazards block and fixture all
carried 29 while two sentences said 28 — critique obj 14, corrected in r3;
r4 raises the count to 61.)

  honest cost is stated rather than hidden:
  the weight is pack-wide, so a widow-specific text will also appear around
  #5 for "my brother died". That is a mis-fit, not a harm. The alternative
  — routing the spouse-death phrases into `care-for-widows` instead — was
  measured and rejected: that pack's own top anchors are Ps 146:9 (1.0),
  James 1:27 (0.95, "**visit** the fatherless and widows in their
  affliction") and Exodus 22:22-24 (0.9, whose punchline is "**your wives
  shall be widows**"), so it would lead a fresh widow with the assembly's
  duty toward her and a threat oracle. One home only, per the owner's
  no-duplicates rule: `grief-and-loss`.
- **Psalms 34:18 from 0.85 to 0.97 — and Psalms 34:18 leads 60 of the 61
  queries, not all 61. That is the decision, and the exception is stated.**
  The pack's own header says "John 11 leads because it holds resurrection
  hope and Jesus' tears together — grief answered with **presence before
  doctrine**". r2 wrote that 0.97 "makes the weights say what the header
  says, keeping John 11:25-26 first". Measured, it does not: **John 11:25-26
  is #3 or #4 everywhere and Psalms 34:18 leads at 50.80**, and it would have
  led at 0.85 too (46.00), because the 12.00 of related-theme points is what
  decides it, not the 0.12 of weight.

  **The one exception, measured (critique obj 5).** r3 wrote "leads all 29"
  in the ruling, in the pack-header replacement and in the fixture note; the
  critique found it leads **28 of 29**, and r4's own run over the enlarged
  set makes it **60 of 61**. The exception is `"my sister died"`, where
  **1 Thessalonians 4:13-14 leads at 52.00** — `Theme: Grief and loss`
  38.00 plus `Worded this way in another translation: died, sister` **14.00**,
  because the WEB's "concerning those who have fallen asleep" is rendered
  with `died` and `sister` in another translation keyed to that anchor's own
  target. Ps 34:18 is #2 at 50.80.

  **Decision: accept it; do not re-weight.** "But we don't want you to be
  ignorant, brothers, concerning those who have fallen asleep, so that you
  don't grieve like the rest, who have no hope. For if we believe that Jesus
  died and rose again, even so God will bring with him those who have fallen
  asleep in Jesus" is a *fitting* lead for a sibling's death, and it arrives
  with the right reason label. The alternatives were costed and both are
  worse: raising Ps 34:18 above 1.0 is out of range and would still lose (it
  needs +13.2 points, and weight caps at 40.00 parity); adding a
  `preferredOrder` pin fails the build for the reason A1.6 Ruling 4 already
  records. **Nothing is changed to win this row.** What changes is every
  sentence in this section that said "all 29" — the ruling, the header text
  and the fixture note now say **60 of 61, and name the exception**, which is
  the claim the run supports.

  r3 does not try to reverse the general ordering with a pin or a weight
  either. **"The LORD is near to those who have a broken heart, and saves
  those who have a crushed spirit" leading a bereavement query IS presence
  before doctrine** — it is the better reading of the header's own rule, and
  the one a pastor would defend. What changes is the header, in the same
  commit (see below), so no comment in the repo describes a world that no
  longer exists.
- **The pack header is rewritten in the same commit — and here is exactly
  which lines (critique obj 7).** Required, not optional: leaving "John 11
  leads" standing is the stale-acknowledgment class A1.11 polices for

  over lines 15-22 would have deleted the standing exclusion from the file
  that carries it, in the same section that breaches it (objection 1).

**Rulings for Jesse.**
1. **Register scope.** A distinct `losing-a-spouse` pack was considered (R2)
   and is still not recommended: `grief-and-loss` now answers the register
   honestly with one added anchor, and a near-duplicate comfort pack is what
   G4 exists to prevent.
2. **Isaiah 54:4-6 at 0.9 in `grief-and-loss` only** (owner brief said
   "~0.6"; the arithmetic above shows 0.6 is invisible). Accepts a
   widow-specific text appearing around #5 for non-spouse bereavement, and
   refuses the alternative that would lead a widow with Exodus 22:24.
3. **Psalms 34:18 0.85 → 0.97, and Ps 34:18 leads the register.** A
   reviewed-data ordering change inside one pack; `layerFingerprint` moves,
   `ENGINE_VERSION` does not. The pack header is rewritten in the same commit
   to describe the measured order — r2 claimed John 11:25-26 stayed first and
   the run refuses it (critique obj 5). If Jesse wants John 11:25-26 first,
   the honest route is S-B §B.6 plus a `preferredOrder` pin landed *after* it,
   not a weight; that is recorded, not proposed.
4. **No `preferredOrder` here** — the measured `translation_variant` add-on
   on 1 Thess 4:13 is **14.00**, not 6.00, so the merged row is **52.00** and
   the pin fails harder than r2 costed. It belongs with S-B §B.6.
5. **Delete `husbands` and `wives` from `godly-marriage.yaml`'s lexicon, and
   move both tokens to `skipped:` in the inventory — NEW in r4, and this is
   the ruling r3 took silently** (critique obj 2, obj 18, rulings-list item
   2). r3's fixture note said "`godly-marriage.yaml` is untouched" as though
   it were a design fact. It is a decision, it was never costed, and it is the
   single cause of three separate findings:

   | what the untouched bare cue produced | measured (r3 tree) |
   |---|---|
   | `Related theme: Betrayed by a companion` on a widow's Isaiah 54:4-6 row | **#3** on `my husband died`, **#2** on `i lost my husband` |
   | Ephesians 5:25 / 5:22-24 / 1 Pet 3:1-6 / Titus 2:3-5 / Heb 13:4 inside `DEFAULT_LIMIT` 25 for a widow | **#12, #13, #14, #16, #17** |
   | `Theme: Marriage` at **#1** for every question form | `why did god take my husband` → Eph 5:25 12.64; `will i see my husband again` → Eph 5:25 17.20 |

   **Where the wrong label came from — proved, not guessed.** The chip is
   `relatedConceptEvidence` (`intents/concept.ts:287`), which fires **only**
   from an *authoritative* matched concept and emits
   `Related theme: <label>` at `weight × 0.5`. For the query `{husband,
   died}` exactly two concepts fire: `grief-and-loss` (via `my husband
   died`) and `godly-marriage` (via the bare `husbands` cue). `godly-marriage`
   carries `related: [marriage-divorce-teaching, betrayal-and-marriage-crisis,
   loving-others, parenting]`, and `betrayal-and-marriage-crisis` anchors
   **Isaiah 54:5-6**, whose presented span merges into grief's Isaiah 54:4-6.
   The chip therefore lands on that row and nowhere else. The same cue also
   produced `Related theme: Marriage and divorce`, `Related theme: Raising
   children` and `Related theme: Loving one another` on other rows in the same
   register. **Remove the cue and every one of them disappears** — verified:
   Eph 5:25, 5:22-24, 5:28, 1 Pet 3:1-6, 1 Pet 3:7, Titus 2:3-5, 1 Cor 7:3
   and Heb 13:4 are **absent from the top 25 on all 61 grief queries**, and
   no reason label containing "Betrayed" appears anywhere in any of them.

   **Three alternatives were measured, and two are refused.**
   **(a) Non-overlapping span** — re-anchor grief's Isaiah 54 to **54:4
   alone** so the spans stop colliding. *Refused on the text.* Isaiah 54:4 is
   "Don't be afraid, for you will not be ashamed… you will forget the shame of
   your youth"; the line the anchor exists for — **"For your Maker is your
   husband"** — is **v5**, and v5-6 is precisely what
   `betrayal-and-marriage-crisis` anchors. Narrowing to v4 removes the chip by
   removing the verse, which is fixing the label by deleting the answer.
   **(b) Label ban only** — `forbiddenReasonLabelSubstrings: ["Betrayed"]` on
   the widow fixtures and nothing else. *Refused as sufficient:* it makes the
   defect a build failure, which is right, but it leaves nothing that could
   make the build pass — the label is produced by data the section declines to
   change, so the gate would simply be red. It is adopted as the **check**,
   not the fix, and it is on all three widow-facing fixtures.
   **(c) Accept the dual home with disclosure.** *Refused:* the disclosure
   standard this section applies (Isa 54:4-6, Isa 49:15-16, Jer 31:15) covers
   a reading that is *true but partial*. "Betrayed by a companion" is not
   partial for a widow; it is false. CLAUDE.md #5 does not have a disclosure
   escape hatch.
   **(d) Delete the two bare cues — recommended.** Two lines, one commit.

   **The cost, measured and disclosed.** Bare `husbands` and `wives` stop
   reaching the pack, and return lexical noise instead: `husbands` →
   Eph 5:22 6.66 (`Shared word: husband`), Col 3:18 5.91; `wives` →
   Eph 5:22 6.67 (`Shared word: wive`), Col 3:18-19 6.01. That is a real
   regression for two one-word queries, and it is the honest price. Against
   it: **every phrase-length marriage query is byte-identical before and
   after** — `marriage`, `biblical marriage`, `godly husband`, `godly wife`,
   `prayer for my husband`, `husbands love your wives` all return the same
   rows at the same scores, because `marriage` stays admitted and the longer
   phrases carry their own entries. `eval/golden/godly-marriage.json` (query
   `marriage` + five additional queries, `expectedTop` Eph 5:25 `withinTop`
   5) passes unchanged — **0 regressions across all 532 existing fixtures,
   byte-identical gate output**. And note the second row of the inventory
   change: the token is **`wive`**, not `wife`, so that entry never served
   `my wife died` in the first place. One of the two cues this section is
   deleting was never doing the job its own inventory row claimed.
   **If Jesse wants bare `husbands`/`wives` to keep firing the marriage pack,
   the consequence is that objection 2 is not fixed** — the widow keeps the
   label and the duty texts keep #12-#17. That is the trade; the
   recommendation is (d).
6. **One home for the question and euphemism registers, and the split is
   forced by G4, not chosen — NEW in r4** (critique obj 3, rulings-list item
   3). Sixteen `why did god take/let my <relation>` phrases, five `passed
   away` completions and eight reunion phrases have to live somewhere.
   Dual-homing all of them in both `grief-and-loss` and
   `pregnancy-and-child-loss` was the first attempt and **fails G4 collision
   outright**: "share 16 lexicon phrase(s) (52% of the smaller lexicon; limit
   34%)". Putting all the child-relation forms in `pregnancy-and-child-loss`
   fails the other half: "share 65% of their vocabulary (limit 60%): away,
   child, daughter, death, die, died, do, god, lost, pass, see, son, take".

   There are four phrase families whose child forms could go either way, so
   sixteen assignments. **Three of the sixteen pass G4**, measured with the
   gate's own ratio (`collision.ts:98-123`; shared ÷ the *smaller* vocabulary):

   | assignment | tokenRatio (limit 0.60) | phraseRatio (limit 0.34) | |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | everything → `grief-and-loss` | **0.538** (7/13) | 0.267 | passes, most margin |
   | euphemism + both question families → `grief-and-loss`, **reunion → `pregnancy-and-child-loss`** | **0.571** (8/14) | 0.211 | **chosen** |
   | euphemism → `pregnancy-and-child-loss`, the rest → `grief-and-loss` | **0.600** (9/15) | 0.211 | passes by exactly 0.000 |
   | the other thirteen | 0.625 – 0.684 | — | **fail** |

   **Chosen: the middle row, and the 0.033 of margin it gives up buys one
   thing.** The four child reunion phrases (`will i see my son/daughter/
   child/baby again`) are the only route by which a bereaved parent reaches
   **2 Samuel 12:22-23** — David on his dead child, *"I shall go to him, but
   he will not return to me"*, which A1.7 Ruling 4 raises from 0.5 to 0.8 for
   exactly this. Route them to `grief-and-loss` with everything else and the
   parent gets the general reunion answer and never David's. The third row
   was refused for a mechanical reason: **0.600 against a limit of 0.600 is
   zero margin** — `collision.ts:118` fails on `>`, so it passes today and
   fails the next time anyone adds one word to either pack. A threshold met
   exactly is not protection.

   **The asymmetry this creates, disclosed.** `my son died` fires **both**
   packs (A1.7 Ruling 2's dual-fire) and returns Ps 34:18 at **84.80** with
   two `concept_anchor` labels, Jer 31:15 and the child pack's own anchors.
   `my son passed away` and `why did god take my son` fire **only**
   `grief-and-loss` and return Ps 34:18 at 50.80 with one label. Both answers
   are right for a bereaved parent — the second is simply the general
   bereavement answer rather than the child-specific one. Making them
   symmetric means dual-homing five more phrase families, which is the
   assignment G4 rejects at 52% shared phrases. **The asymmetry is a cost of
   the G4 threshold, it is stated rather than hidden, and the query that most
   needs the child pack — the reunion question — is the one routed there.**

   **Why `grief-and-loss` and not a theodicy pack** (the A3.4 coordination
   row in §A1.0e): `why did god take my husband` is a theodicy sentence typed
   by a person who has had a death. Comfort is true for every person who
   types it; a providence answer is true for some of them and is an argument
   with the rest. The engine reports what a curated source names for a
   concept and never adjudicates (CLAUDE.md #6), so the register it can serve
   honestly is the bereavement one.
7. **The reunion family's containment cost — accepted, and this is the ruling
   the critique's own CR-1 test demands.** `will i see my husband again`
   tokenizes to **`{see, husband}`** — the tokenizer drops `will`, `i` and
   `again`, and no phrasing survives with more. That set is contained in
   ordinary living-person queries: measured, `when can i see my husband` now
   returns Ps 34:18 50.80, Rev 21:3-4 43.10, John 11:25-26 40.00, and
   `i want to see my mom` returns Ps 34:18 34.18 (a partial match, m=2 of
   q=3). **This is exactly the shape of the argument CR-1 used to decline
   `better off without me`, and it comes out the other way, for a stated
   reason.** There, `{better, without}` on "im better off without him" would
   hand an ordinary breakup query the *suicide-crisis pack's entire anchor
   set* — a register that is dangerous when it is wrong. Here the false
   positive receives "The LORD is near to those who have a broken heart",
   "he will wipe away every tear" and "I go to prepare a place for you". A
   person asking when they can visit their husband gets comfort texts that do
   not fit; nobody gets handed a crisis. **A mis-fit, not a harm** — the same
   standard Ruling 2 uses for a widow-specific text appearing at #6 for
   "my brother died". If Jesse disagrees, the cost of declining is that the
   reunion question — one of the four sentences a bereaved person most
   reliably types — returns Ephesians 5:25 for a widow and Luke 6:36 at 1.63
   for a bereaved child, which is where r3 left it.
8. **The grandparent register and the British spelling — new, and cheap.**
   `my grandma/grandpa/grandmother/grandfather died` and `my mum died` all
   returned **Romans 6:8 at 3.37** ("if we died with Christ") on a bare
   `died` chip — the same dying-to-sin family this item bans for `my mom
   died`. Five phrases close it; all five now lead with Ps 34:18 50.80. No
   new anchor, no weight change. **`where is my <relation>` and
   `where is my <relation> now` are DECLINED, with proof** (the owner brief
   listed them): `where is my mom now` tokenizes to **`{mom, now}`**, which
   is contained in `my mom now has cancer` (`{mom, now, cancer}`) and
   `where is my wife now` → `{wife, now}` in `my wife now wants a divorce`.
   Adding them would fire the bereavement anchor set for a living mother
   with cancer and for a marriage in crisis — the CR-1 class, and on the
   dangerous side of it. Recorded as declined by name rather than omitted, so
   the next round does not re-propose it.
9. **2 Corinthians 1:3-4 stays out of `grief-and-loss` — declined, recorded**
   (the critique's own must-add list). "The Father of mercies and God of all
   comfort, who comforts us in all our affliction" is arguably the NT's
   bereavement text, and it does not appear in this register's top 12. It is
   left where it is — `caring-for-aging-parents`' 1.0 lead, measured 46.00
   #1 — for the reason the critique itself supplies: the verse **turns within
   a verse** to "that we may be able to comfort those who are in any
   affliction, through the comfort with which we ourselves are comforted by
   God". That is the caregiver's charge. Handed to a widow at #2 it tells her,
   six days in, what her grief is *for*. The placement is exclusive on
   purpose, and this ruling says so rather than leaving the absence to look
   like an oversight.

**Phase.** Holds in Phase A. Simulated gate: `pastoral-spouse-death` **pass**,
0 findings across **61 queries × 31 assertions** (4 expectedTop,
26 mustNotRank, 1 mustNotLead) = **1,891 assertion-instances**, plus a
`forbiddenReasonLabelSubstrings: ["Betrayed"]` scan over **every returned
row** of all 61 queries (`corpusGolden.ts:1279-1297` scans the whole result
set, not a window — the one assertion in the fixture format that is not
window-scoped, which is why it is the right check for a label defect). If S-B §B.6 lands later it scales
the non-authoritative add-ons on anchored rows and the order becomes
Ps 34:18 40.00 / John 11:25-26 40.00 / Rev 21:3-4 38.51 / Isa 54 36.57 —
every window here still holds, tighter. (That B6 ordering is the r2 critique's
own simulation, quoted; it is not re-measured here, because nothing in this
item depends on it.) **No assertion in this item waits on B6.**

**Acceptance.** `pastoral-spouse-death.json` shows John 11:25-26 within top
5, Ps 34:18 within top 5, Isa 54:4-6 within top 10 and John 14:1-3 within
top 10 by `concept_anchor` for all **61** queries; Ezekiel 24:18 never at #1
(measured **#4** on `"my wife died"`, behind Ps 34:18, Rev 21:3-4 and
John 11:25-26 — the 40.00 tie against John 11:25-26 resolves to the anchor by
`rank.ts:71-75`); all **26** banned refs absent from the top 10 everywhere;
**no reason label anywhere in any returned row contains "Betrayed"**.
Gauntlet reports a measurable effect. G4 green — and note that G4 is *load-
bearing* in this item for the first time: the routing in Ruling 6 was chosen
because thirteen of sixteen alternatives fail `collisionGate`, and the two
inventory rows moved in Ruling 5 are what keep `lexiconInventoryCheck` from
failing with "admitted 'husbands' does not fire".

**Effort.** M-L (61 lexicon phrases, 2 new anchors, 1 weight edit, 1
pack-header rewrite scoped to two lines, **2 lexicon deletions and 2
inventory row moves in `godly-marriage`**, 1 fixture with 26 bans and a
label ban). No dependency; merge **first** of the three items that edit this
file, and the `godly-marriage` edit rides the same commit (§A1.0e).

### A1.7 Extend `pregnancy-and-child-loss` (`ontology/concepts/pastoral-pregnancy-and-child-loss.yaml`)

**Measured gap (live, r2).** **`"stillborn"` returns exactly two rows, and
both are the harm**:

```
== "stillborn"  (2 results, the entire result set)
  1. Psalms 58:8       2.73  [token_overlap: stillborn]
  2. Ecclesiastes 6:3  1.58  [token_overlap: stillborn]
```

> **Psalms 58:8** — "Let them be like a snail which melts and passes away,
> like the **stillborn** child, who has not seen the sun." (an imprecatory
> curse against the wicked)
> **Ecclesiastes 6:3** — "…I say that a **stillborn** child is better than
> he." (Qoheleth's vanity argument)

`"my baby was stillborn"` → **Numbers 12:12** (6.00, Miriam's leprosy: "Let
her not be as one dead, of whom the flesh is half consumed when he comes
out of his mother's womb"), **Job 3:16** (6.00, "as a hidden untimely birth
I had not been"), Heb 5:13, then Ps 58:8 at #4. `"my son died"` → Judges
3:11 (9.40), 1 Chr 19:1 (9.40), Gen 36:33, 2 Sam 10:1 — chronicle formulas
("X reigned in his place after Y died"). `"my daughter died"` → 1 Chr 23:22
(8.50, "Eleazar died, and had no sons, but daughters only"), Matt 9:18,
Gen 38:12. `"my baby died"` → 1 Sam 4:20, then bare `died` noise.
`"death of a child"` / `"loss of a child"` miss the pack entirely.

**Change.**

```yaml
lexicon:
  - my baby died
  - my baby was stillborn     # also serves "stillborn baby" — SAME token set
                               # {baby, stillborn}; matching is containment,
                               # so surface order is irrelevant and r1's two
                               # entries were one entry's worth of behaviour
  - stillborn                 # bare: admitted: [stillborn] on the concepts:
                               # row, NO collapses: row. Ruling 1.
  - death of a child
  - loss of a child
  - my son died               # these four ALSO go to grief-and-loss
  - my daughter died          # (Ruling 2, dual-fire)
  - lost my son
  - lost my daughter
  # NEW in r4 — the reunion question, CHILD relations only (Ruling 4).
  # The husband/wife/mom/dad forms are grief-and-loss's; the split is a
  # measured G4 collision requirement (A1.6 Ruling 6), not a preference.
  - will i see my son again
  - will i see my daughter again
  - will i see my child again
  - will i see my baby again
anchors:
  - ref: Jeremiah 31:15       # NOT 31:15-17 — see Ruling 3
    sources: [editorial]
    weight: 0.6

# EDIT an existing anchor weight (NEW in r4, Ruling 4):
#   2 Samuel 12:22-23   0.5 -> 0.8

# ontology/concepts/pastoral-grief-and-loss.yaml — ALSO add (Ruling 2):
#   - my son died
#   - my daughter died
#   - lost my son
#   - lost my daughter
```

**Tokenizer hazards.** Live output:

```
"my baby died"          -> {baby, died}
"my baby was stillborn" -> {baby, stillborn}
"stillborn baby"        -> {stillborn, baby}   SAME SET — one entry serves both
"stillborn"             -> {stillborn}         BARE
"death of a child"      -> {death, child}
"loss of a child"       -> {loss, child}
"my son died"           -> {son, died}      "my daughter died" -> {daughter, died}
"lost my son"           -> {lost, son}      "lost my daughter" -> {lost, daughter}
"will i see my son again"    -> {see, son}       NEW in r4 — 2 tokens; `will`,
"will i see my daughter again" -> {see, daughter}   `i` and `again` all vanish
"will i see my child again"  -> {see, child}
"will i see my baby again"   -> {see, baby}
```

The four reunion sets are disjoint from everything else in either pack, and
their containment cost is ruled on in A1.6 Ruling 7 (`{see, child}` is
contained in "i want to see my child"; the false positive receives comfort
texts, which is a mis-fit and not a harm).

**Ruling 1's arithmetic — the bare `stillborn` admission.** The formula is
§A1.0b corollary 2: a bare single-token query gives `22 × weight`, verified
live on this pack's own existing bare admission:

```
== "miscarriage"   (BASE corpus, before this section — the point is the
                    22 x w identity, which is why the base build is the
                    right one to check it against; A1.7 Ruling 4 then
                    raises 2 Samuel 12:22-23 to 0.8, i.e. 17.60)
                                                    weight   22 x w
  1. Psalms 34:18        27.10 (22.00 + related 5.10)  1.00    22.00 ✓
  4. Romans 8:26         19.80                          0.90    19.80 ✓
  5. Psalms 139:13-14    19.36                          0.88    19.36 ✓
  3. John 11:35          23.68 (18.70 + related 4.98)   0.85    18.70 ✓
  2. Revelation 21:4     24.40 (18.70 + related 5.70)   0.85    18.70 ✓
  6. Matthew 19:14       13.20                          0.60    13.20 ✓
  7. 2 Samuel 12:22-23   11.00                          0.50    11.00 ✓
  8-12. Related theme: Grief and loss rows at 6.00, 5.70, 5.70, 5.10, 4.80
```

So after admitting `stillborn`, the query returns **Psalms 34:18 at 22.00
#1**, seven anchors down to 11.00 (plus the new Jer 31:15 at 13.20), then
five-plus `Related theme: Grief and loss` rows from 6.00 down — and
**Psalms 58:8 at 2.73 lands #20 and Ecclesiastes 6:3 at 1.58 lands #21**
(measured on the r4 corpus at limit 25; r3 wrote "about #14" and "about #16",
which was an estimate read off the ladder and not the run — critique
obj 11).
Nothing in Phase A raises either: both carry a single `token_overlap`
reason, and no lexicon change adds points to a verse.

**The guard is therefore `mustNotLead withinTop 1`, per the owner's ruling,
and that is also the only stable claim.** A `mustNotRank` at window 10 would
pass on today's numbers, but only because ≥ 3 `Related theme` rows from a
*neighbouring* pack sit between this pack's anchors and Ps 58:8 — a fact
about `grief-and-loss`'s weights, not about this item. The leadership guard
depends only on this pack's own ladder, and the gate's own words are that
Scripture is demoted here, never suppressed.

The admission is also strictly safer than the one this section already
recommends: `stillborn` has **2** WEB occurrences, both named in the guards
below, and no competing concept speaks the token; bare `kill` (A1.1) has
hundreds, all in the wrong sense. r1 refused the safer of the two.

**Anchors.**

| ref | WEB text (verified in `fixture.db`) | weight | why this is how God's word answers this search | sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jeremiah 31:15 | "A voice is heard in Ramah, lamentation and bitter weeping, Rachel weeping for her children. She refuses to be comforted for her children, because they are no more." | 0.6 | Canon's own image of inconsolable maternal grief, and the half **Matthew 2:18 actually quotes**. It names no age, so it serves the register whether the child was an infant or grown. Context disclosed: the oracle's own referent is exiled Israel. | editorial; the verse's own re-use in Matthew 2:18 |

**Where Jeremiah 31:15 actually lands, and the fixture split it forces
(critique obj 6).** Measured after the change:

| query | Jer 31:15 | why |
|---|---|---|
| `my baby was stillborn`, `stillborn`, `my baby died`, `death of a child`, `loss of a child` | **inside the top 10** | only `pregnancy-and-child-loss` fires; its eight anchors plus related rows leave room |
| `my son died`, `my daughter died`, `lost my son`, `lost my daughter` | **#14** | Ruling 2's dual-fire: `grief-and-loss` adds **eleven** more anchors to the same window, and Ps 34:18 leads at **84.80** carrying both packs' chips |

r2 called the dual-fire's consequence "pleasant arithmetic" and asserted
`Jeremiah 31:15 withinTop: 10` on all nine queries; the real gate failed it
four times. The arithmetic is pleasant for Ps 34:18 and hostile to every
lighter anchor in the pack, which is the part r2 did not compute.

**The fix is a fixture split, not a window widen.** Widening to 15 is not
available (`withinTop` accepts 1, 3, 5, 10 only) and would in any case widen
this fixture's `mustNotRank` window with it — `measuredWindow` is the max of
`expectedWithinTop` and the largest non-`presenceOnly` `expectedTop.withinTop`
(`corpusGolden.ts:798-806`), so a wider assertion silently makes every ban
stricter. So:

- **`pastoral-stillborn`** keeps the five single-pack queries and keeps
  `Jer 31:15 withinTop: 10`, which the run supports.
- **`pastoral-child-death`** (new) takes the four dual-fire queries and
  asserts **Ps 34:18 `withinTop: 3`** (measured #1, carrying *both* packs'
  `concept_anchor` chips — the thing Ruling 2 exists to produce) and
  **Jer 31:15 `presenceOnly`** with the same required family and label.
  `presenceOnly` asserts presence anywhere in a limit-50 run with the
  provenance pin satisfied, asserts no rank, and never widens the ban window
  (`corpusGolden.ts:1194-1230`, `798-806`). That is the honest claim for a
  verse at #14: *it is reachable and correctly attributed, and this fixture
  does not claim a position it does not have.*

**Ruling 3 — why the range stops at v15.** r1 anchored **31:15-17** and
justified it as "quoted for exactly that in Matthew 2:18". Matthew 2:18
quotes **only v15**. Verses 16-17 continue: "*Refrain your voice from
weeping… for your work will be rewarded… They will come again from the land
of the enemy… Your children will come again to their own territory*" — a
promise of national return from exile. Handed to a woman whose baby was
stillborn it reads either as a promise her child will come back, which will
not happen in this life, or as a resurrection claim about her child that
the text does not make. That is the *pairing-frame* distortion
`docs/DOCTRINAL-BASIS.md` §3's worked example describes: the verses are
Scripture; recruiting them as warrant for a personal outcome is the problem.
It is also the identical objection A1.12 raises to refuse John 11:25-26 for
a pet — applied consistently now.

**Rulings for Jesse.**
1. **Bare `stillborn`: admit** to `pregnancy-and-child-loss`

   Reverses r1's refusal, on the arithmetic above.

   fire BOTH packs** — a stated ruling, not a lexicon-placement footnote.
   The problem r1 created: `my child died` is already in `grief-and-loss`,
   so a parent whose 40-year-old son died would land only in the
   infant/pregnancy pack, whose anchors include Ps 139:13-14 ("you knit me

   children", 0.6) — and r1's premise that "the pack's higher, age-neutral
   anchors already lead" is not what those weights say. Dual-firing is the
   same pattern the section already accepts for `life is meaningless` and
   `overdose`, and its arithmetic consequence is measured, not assumed:
   Psalms 34:18 is an anchor in both packs, carries two `concept_anchor`
   reasons and leads at **84.80** for exactly the query where age is
   ambiguous — **and** the second pack's eleven anchors push this pack's own
   lighter anchors out of the top 10, which is why the four queries now live
   in their own fixture. r2 named only the first half and called it
   "pleasant".
3. **Jeremiah 31:15 alone at 0.6**, not 31:15-17 (see above).

   0.5 → 0.8 — NEW in r4.** `will i see my son again` returned John 6:62
   (12.37, "What then if you would see the Son of Man ascending?"),

   already bans from the top 3 as a harm, and it was the **#1 answer** to a
   bereaved parent asking whether she will see her baby again.

   **Why here and not `grief-and-loss`:** these four are the only route by
   which a bereaved parent reaches **2 Samuel 12:22-23** — David, after the
   child's death: *"But now he is dead… I shall go to him, but he will not
   return to me."* That is the canon's own answer to the reunion question
   asked about a child, in the voice of a father who asked it. It sat at
   weight 0.5 (20.00 at parity), below eight other anchors in the pack, and
   was effectively invisible. **0.8 puts it at 32.00**, and the effect is asserted rather than described:
   the anchor was **absent from the top 25 on all nine** `pastoral-stillborn`
   queries before this change and is **#6 on all nine** after, so the fixture
   carries it as a third `expectedTop` at `withinTop: 10` with the
   `Theme: Losing a child` label. It displaces neither Ps 34:18, Rev 21:4 nor
   John 11:35 — measured, identically on all four reunion queries:

   Note what the reunion forms do *not* fire: `{see, son}` does not contain
   `{son, died}`, so `grief-and-loss` contributes only its related-theme
   chip here. That is deliberate — the parent asking the reunion question is
   answered out of the child pack, which is the pack that holds David's
   answer. **Job 3:16 falls from #1 to #9** on
   `will i see my baby again` and to **#10** on `will i see my child again`,
   and is absent from the top 25 on the other two — still inside the window
   of 10, so it stays governed by this fixture's existing
   `mustNotLead withinTop 3`, which holds. The section states the position
   rather than claiming the ref is gone.

   The alternative — routing all eight reunion phrases to `grief-and-loss` —

   place in the section where a G4 margin is deliberately spent on a
   pastoral judgment, and it is spent knowingly: 0.571 against a limit of

### A1.8 Extend `caring-for-aging-parents` (`ontology/concepts/caring-for-aging-parents.yaml`)

**Measured gap (live, r2).** The pack phrases the formal `"my mother is
dying"` / `"my father is dying"` but not the colloquial register the audit
itself uses. `"my dad is dying"` → **Hebrews 11:21** (2.47, "By faith Jacob,
when he was **dying**, blessed each of the sons of Joseph" — chipless),
2 Cor 4:3, **Mark 5:23** (1.74, Jairus's dying *daughter* — wrong family
member). `"my mom has dementia"` → **0 results**, and `"i have dementia"` →
**0 results**: `dementia` and `alzheimer` are entirely absent from the WEB
vocabulary (0 verse-text occurrences each, and `dementia` has 0 occurrences
in `verse_terms` too), and no lexicon anywhere carries them.

**Change.**

```yaml
lexicon:
  - my dad is dying
  - my mom is dying
  - my mom has dementia
  - my dad has dementia
  - my mom has alzheimers
  - my dad has alzheimers
```

**The bare words move to `serious-illness-and-dying` (Ruling 1)** and are
specified in A1.9. This pack keeps only the two-token *parent* forms, so no
bare word fires it and its inventory row is unchanged (`skipped: [parent]`).

**Tokenizer hazards.**

```
"my dad is dying"        -> {dad, dying}       "my mom is dying"      -> {mom, dying}
"my mom has dementia"    -> {mom, dementia}    "my dad has dementia"  -> {dad, dementia}
"my mom has alzheimers"  -> {mom, alzheimer}   "my dad has alzheimers"-> {dad, alzheimer}
"my dad has alzheimer's" -> {dad, alzheimer}   (apostrophe stripped before tokenizing)
```

`alzheimers` → `{alzheimer}` (length 10, 10−1 = 9 ≥ 4, so the trailing `s`
strips); `widower`/`widowers` in A1.10 follow the identical pattern.

**Anchors.** None new here. The pack's comfort ladder (2 Cor 1:3-4 1.0,
Ps 73:26 0.9, Ps 23:4 0.85, Rom 8:38-39 0.8, 1 Thess 4:13-14 0.7) already
answers "watching my parent's mind and body fail" and is fixture-verified
for the sibling query "watching a parent die" (measured live: 2 Cor 1:3-4
**46.00** #1). The header's stale corpus-deferred claim and the Isaiah 46:4
question are **A1.13**, not a merge-along.

**Where the pack's own anchors land, measured — and the dual-fire this item
creates (critique obj 19).** The pack has eight anchors, so on a parity query
the anchor-component ladder runs 40.00 / 36.00 / 34.00 / 32.00 / 28.00 /
26.00 / 24.00 / 22.00. That ladder predicts 2 Cor 1:3-4 at #1. **It is not
what the run returns on this fixture's own query**, because A1.9's bare
`dementia` admission makes `my mom has dementia` dual-fire, and Ps 23:4 and
Ps 73:26 are anchored in *both* packs:

**2 Cor 1:3-4 holds `withinTop: 3` at exactly #3, with zero margin.** That is
stated, not hidden: the assertion passes today, and what would break it is
one more add-on landing on any row above it — most plausibly a new
`related:` edge into `god-of-all-comfort` or `strength-in-weakness`. The
window is not widened to 5, because #1-#3 being the caregiver's own comfort
ladder *is* the item's claim; if a future edit pushes it to #4, the right
response is to re-measure and decide, not to have pre-widened the window so
that nobody notices. r2 stated the dual-fire and did not compute it.

Both lexical bans clear by more than 19 points; the third is a standing
exclusion and is stated with its margin.

|---|---|---|
| Hebrews 11:21 | "By faith Jacob, when he was **dying**, blessed each of the sons of Joseph" — a patriarchal blessing narrative, chipless; measured #1 for "my dad is dying". | 2.47 #1 |
| Mark 5:23 | Jairus's dying **daughter** — the wrong family member entirely, reached by bare `dying`. | 1.74 #3 |

It is not anchored here — it arrives through the dual fire with `serious-illness-and-dying`, which anchors it at 0.75 (A1.9 Ruling 3). r3 added four `dementia`/`alzheimers` queries to this fixture and never measured it (critique obj 1). | **#18** at 11.67 on all four dementia/alzheimers queries; absent ≤ 25 on `my mom is dying` / `my dad is dying` |

**#18 is outside the window of 10 and inside `DEFAULT_LIMIT` 25**, so the
guard holds and the residue is real. The decision that would remove it
belongs to A1.9 Ruling 3, because the anchor is in that pack, not this one —
which is exactly why the standing-exclusion sweep (§A1.0d Step 6) has to run
across **fixtures**, not packs: a verse this pack refuses arrives anyway
through a dual fire that no single file's header can see.

The pack's existing hijack guards (Col 3:20-21, Eph 6:4) stay where they
are, in `dying-parent-register-guard.json`; this item does not restate them.

Cost: the register loses a Torrey-filed text on the doctrinal question where it is *right*. |

Cost: a man watching his wife die scrolls one screen and reads "Precious in the LORD's sight is the death of his saints." |

   globally gated, one fixture bans it as globally excluded, another pack
   anchors it, and no document says which is true. This section's own first

than a window (`corpusGolden.ts:1279-1297`). A label defect is not a ranking
defect and should not be policed with a ranking window.

**Exodus 22:22-24 at #7 — the ruling r3 replaced with a sentence (critique
obj 16).** r3 justified letting both duty texts rank with one clause: *"they
are `care-for-widows`' own reviewed anchors and the church's care for her is
real."* That is a good argument about **1 Timothy 5:3-8**, whose subject is
genuinely the assembly's care. It is not an argument about this one. The
anchored range's punchline is Exodus 22:24 — *"my wrath will grow hot, and I
will kill you with the sword; **and your wives shall be widows**, and your
children fatherless."* Its stated content is the **making** of widows, and it
sits four rows below "The LORD is near to those who have a broken heart" for
a woman who became one last week. Ruling 4 costs the alternatives; the
section no longer decides it in a subordinate clause.

**The two guards do NOT go on that fixture, and this is the measurement that
decides it.** The critique asked for them there. On `bible verses for widows`
— a query that fixture already runs — `{bible, vers, widow}` is parity with
`care-for-widows`' own three-token phrase, so the pack answers on its own
weight ladder and **Exodus 22:22-24 measures #3**, inside a `withinTop: 3`
leadership window. A guard written there would fail the build on a query
where the verse is arguably apt: someone asking for *verses about widows* is
asking a teaching question, and "You shall not take advantage of any widow"
is one of the Bible's answers to it. The guards belong on the query whose
warrant they carry — a bereaved person typing the bare word — which is
`pastoral-widow`. **Recorded rather than decorated:** on
`bible verses for widows`, Ex 22:22-24 stays at #3 and this section does not
change it.

**Rulings for Jesse.**
1. **Drop the 1 Corinthians 7:8 anchor.** "But I say to the unmarried and to
   widows, it is good for them if they remain even as I am" does not speak
   in a male-widowed voice — Paul addresses the unmarried and widows, and
   "even as I am" means *unmarried*. At 0.5 it would have made
   counsel-not-to-remarry a `concept_anchor` result under a "Theme: Care for
   widows" chip for a man whose wife just died. It stays `alsoAcceptable`.
2. **Route `widower` to `grief-and-loss` as well.** The underlying question
   r1 never asked: does a bereaved man belong in a duty-of-the-assembly pack
   at all? `care-for-widows` is largely the assembly's obligation register
   (James 1:27 "**visit** the fatherless and widows", 1 Tim 5:3-8, Ex
   22:22-24). It should answer him — the church's care for him is real —
   but it should not answer him alone. Both inventory rows gain `widower`.
3. **Route bare `widow` the same way — new in r3, and it is the same
   ruling.** Ruling 2 is the best argument in this item, and r2 applied it to
   the smaller half of the people who type the word. `widower` has **0** WEB
   verse-text occurrences and one commentary hit; `widow` is the far
   higher-volume query and the one where the harm is *leading*, not latent.
   One lexicon line and one fixture take the register from *"Honor widows who
   are widows indeed… he has denied the faith"* at #1 to *"The LORD is near
   to those who have a broken heart"* at #1. `grief-and-loss`'s inventory row
   gains `widow` alongside `widower`; `care-for-widows` already admits it.
   The register is now fixed for both halves, or it is not fixed.
4. **Exodus 22:22-24 at #7 for bare `widow`: what to do about it — NEW in
   r4, and the section takes no option unilaterally** (critique obj 16). Four
   were measured:

   | option | measured consequence |
   |---|---|
   | **(a) Keep the leadership guard only** — r3's position, and what r4 ships | `mustNotLead withinTop 3` holds with four positions of margin (#7). The verse is inside the response a bereaved woman reads. |
   | **(b) Narrow the anchor to Exodus 22:22-23** | Drops v24's "your wives shall be widows" out of the presented span while keeping "You shall not take advantage of any widow or fatherless child… I will surely hear their cry". This is the **recommended** change if one is made: it is a range edit to an existing anchor in a pack this section already edits, it changes no weight, and it removes the sentence rather than the verse's care. Cost: the oracle's teeth go with it, and `care-for-widows`' own author chose the fuller range. |
   | **(c) Lower its weight for the bare query** | Not expressible — weight is pack-wide; lowering it moves the verse for `bible verses for widows` too, where it measures **#3** and where r3 correctly declined to guard it. |
   | **(d) Stop bare `widow` firing `care-for-widows` at all**, now that `grief-and-loss` answers it | Refused. It would take the assembly's genuine duty texts out of a query the assembly also types, and would break `eval/golden/care-for-widows.json`. The register has two readers; the fix was never to delete one. |

   **Recommendation: (b), as a separate one-line PR owned by
   `care-for-widows`, not folded into this item.** A1 ships (a) and states
   the residue. What r4 refuses to do is repeat r3's move of settling it in a
   clause.

**pass**, `pastoral-widow` **pass**, edited `care-for-widows` **pass**, 0

### A1.11 NEW pack: `funeral-readings`

**Measured gap (live, r2) — total miss, confirmed exactly as audited.**

```
== "verses for a funeral"
  1. Matthew 11:17     1.78  [passage_terms: funeral]   3. Deuteronomy 14:1  1.73
  5. Matthew 11:16     1.66                             9. Leviticus 19:27   1.50
== "funeral"  (5 results total)
  1. Matthew 11:17 1.78 | 2. Deut 14:1 1.73 | 3. Matt 11:16 1.66 | 4. Lev 19:27 1.50
== "what to read at a funeral"    2 Cor 1:13 2.69 (pure `read` noise)
== "memorial service verses"      Genesis 50:10 6.00, Exodus 30:16 4.45 — the
                                   literal tabernacle memorial offering
== "celebration of life"          Proverbs 3:18 2.43 — pure `life` noise
```

`funeral` has **0** WEB verse-text occurrences and 11 `verse_terms`
occurrences, which is the whole mechanism: Matthew 11:17 ("We played the
flute for you, and you didn't dance. We mourned for you, and you didn't
lament" — Jesus rebuking "this generation") wins because a commentary
discusses funeral customs on it. No existing pack owns the *occasion*
register (what to read *at* the service), as distinct from `grief-and-loss`
(the feeling) or `death-and-burial` (burial *practice* narrated in
Scripture) — the same three-way split `death-and-burial.yaml`'s own header
uses to justify its existence beside `mortality`.

**Change.**

**File path (critique obj 15.2).**
**`ontology/concepts/funeral-readings.yaml`**, compiled id `funeral-readings`.
r3 gave the id and no path, and the directory's convention is inconsistent
enough that `pastoral-funeral-readings.yaml` was an equally reasonable guess.
Nothing in the pipeline reads the filename — `compileConcepts` keys on `id:`
and `lexicon-inventory.yaml` rows key on the compiled id
(`lexiconInventory.ts:109-113`) — so this is a readability convention, and
§A1.0e now records it for both new packs rather than leaving one of them
stated and one implied.

**Pack file header (required, and r2 gave neither new pack one).** Every file
in `ontology/concepts/` carries a provenance header; a new pack without one is
the only file in the directory that does not say where it came from. Both new
packs in this section ship with one, in the directory's own shape:

r1 listed `funeral verses` and `funeral bible verses` as separate entries
"for readability"; they are the identical token sets to two other entries
(matching is containment, order-free), so they are dropped — nine phrases,
nine distinct token sets, all tested.

**Tokenizer hazards.**

```
"funeral"                          -> {funeral}                    BARE
"verses for a funeral"             -> {vers, funeral}    ("verses" stems to `vers`)
"funeral verses"                   -> {funeral, vers}    SAME SET — one entry
"funeral scripture"                -> {funeral, scripture}
"bible verses for a funeral"       -> {bible, vers, funeral}
"funeral bible verses"             -> {funeral, bible, vers}  SAME SET — one entry
"funeral readings"                 -> {funeral, reading}
"what to read at a funeral"        -> {read, funeral}
"memorial service verses"          -> {memorial, service, vers}
"scripture for a memorial service" -> {scripture, memorial, service}
"celebration of life"              -> {celebration, life}
```

No collapse below 2 tokens except the deliberate bare `funeral`.
`celebration` occurs once in the WEB text and `{celebration, life}` reaches
nothing curated today (measured above).

### A1.12 NEW pack: `pet-loss` — one ruling-gated PR, pack and fixture together

**Measured gap (live, r2).** `"my pet died"` → **Romans 6:8** (3.37), Rom
6:2, John 8:53, Ruth 1:3, Rom 6:10, Gen 5:27 — the identical Romans-6 harm
family as A1.6's parent-death register, because the query collapses to bare
`died` scatter. `"my dog died"` → Rom 6:2 (3.26), John 8:53, Ruth 1:3,
Matt 22:27. `"pet loss"` → 1 Kings 16:34 (1.97), then **2 Samuel 12:3 and
12:1** — Nathan's ewe-lamb parable, reached because `pet` appears twice in
`verse_terms`; a parable told to convict David of adultery and murder.

**What the sources actually say, and why this item is gated.**
GotQuestions.org's dedicated article on pet grief does **not** offer a
death/resurrection-hope anchor set the way it does for human bereavement. It
cites Psalms 34:18 (a claim about the *griever*) and cautions readers to
examine whether "part of the grief we feel may be due to the loss of the
fantasy relationship we pretended we had with our pet." Its companion
doctrinal article states plainly: **"The Bible does not give any explicit
teaching on whether animals have souls or whether our pets will be in
heaven"** — studied agnosticism, not a promise. `docs/DOCTRINAL-BASIS.md`
line 64 reads, in full: *"6. **Humanity in God's image**, with intrinsic
dignity."* (r1 cited this as "humanity *alone* made in God's image"; the
word "alone" is not in the document and is removed. The ruling may still be
right; the citation must not be strengthened in transit.) With CLAUDE.md #6
— the engine adjudicates no theology — anchoring "my pet died" to
John 11:25-26 or 1 Thess 4:13-18 would be an implicit doctrinal claim no
admitted source makes.

**Change (one commit, gated on the ruling — see the shipping note).**

**The `related:` edge is the item's own doctrinal argument, and r2 got it
wrong (critique obj 10).** No resurrection texts (John 11, 1 Thess 4,
Revelation 21) are *anchored*, by design: these two anchors make claims only
about God's character and the griever's own permitted grief, never about the
animal's destiny. But r2 then wrote `related: grief-and-loss`, and a
`related:` edge emits `concept_lexicon` rows for the related pack's own
anchors. Measured on r2's design:

```
== "my pet died"   (r2)

   2. Psalms 145:9            22.00
   3. 1 Thessalonians 4:14     7.19  [Related theme: Grief and loss 5.70 | passage_terms: died 1.49]
   4. John 11:25-26            6.00  [Related theme: Grief and loss 6.00]
```

So the item that argues most carefully against making a resurrection claim
about an animal shipped a pack returning *"I am the resurrection and the
life"* and *"those who have fallen asleep in Jesus"* at #3 and #4 for "my dog
died" — and its own two `mustNotRank` guards failed the real gate on all four
queries. Neither B2 nor B6 helps: those rows carry no `concept_anchor` (B6
does not scale them) and are already at the 6.00 sole-evidence ceiling (B2
does not lower them).

**r3 drops the edge, and replaces it rather than leaving a two-row pack.**
`related: near-to-the-brokenhearted` emits Ps 147:3 ("He heals the broken in
heart, and binds up their wounds"), Isaiah 61:1-3 and Matthew 5:4 ("Blessed
are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted") — the griever's-broken-
heart register, which is *exactly* what this pack's two anchors already claim
and the only claim its sources support. It emits no resurrection text, so the
two doctrinal bans hold. Measured after:

```
== "my pet died"   (r3)                    == "pet loss"   (r3)
   1. Psalms 34:18   30.00  [Losing a pet 24.00 | Related: Near to the brokenhearted 6.00]
   2. Psalms 145:9   22.00                    2. Psalms 145:9    22.00
   3. Psalms 147:3    5.40                    3. Psalms 147:3     5.40
   4. Isaiah 61:1-3   4.80                    4. Isaiah 61:1-3    4.80
   5. Matthew 5:4     4.80                    5. Matthew 5:4      4.80
   6. Romans 6:8      3.37                    6. 1 Kings 16:34    1.97
   7. Romans 6:2      2.99                    7. 2 Samuel 12:3    1.73
```

The substitution is stated as a substitution, not smuggled: it is a
doctrinally different edge, chosen because the first one made a claim the item
forbids, and it is defended on the same ground as the anchors themselves.

**Matthew 10:29-31 is dropped from r1's set (obj 38).**

> "Aren't two sparrows sold for an assarion coin? Not one of them falls to
> the ground apart from your Father's will… **You are of more value than
> many sparrows.**"

Two problems r1's otherwise careful reasoning missed. Its context (v28,
"Don't be afraid of those who kill the body") is *persecution* comfort, not
creature-loss comfort. And its own punchline makes the animal the lesser
term: served to a grieving pet owner it says *the pet was the sparrow and
you are worth more* — not what that person needs to hear about the animal
they are grieving. **Psalms 145:9** ("The LORD is good to all. His tender
mercies are over all his works") carries the providence claim the item wants
without that turn, and it is retained.

**The euphemism family, added in r4.** The critique's search-form matrix
marked this fixture's only gap as *"`my dog passed away`, `losing a pet`
untested — minor, same family as objection 4"*. Measured, it is the same
harm: `my dog passed away` returned **1 Corinthians 7:31 at 10.24 #1** ("the
mode of this world passes away"), 1 John 2:17 #2 and James 1:10 #3 — the
identical trio this section bans for `my son passed away`. Four phrases close
it; after the change the pack's own two anchors lead and the trio sits
**#3-#5**.

Those three are `mustNotLead withinTop 1` and **not** `mustNotRank`, for the
reason the item already states about Romans 6:8: **a two-anchor pack cannot
fill a window of 10**, and anchoring more verses to fill it is the doctrinal
overreach this pack exists to refuse. #3 is the honest claim, and it is made
rather than rounded up.

**Tokenizer hazards.** `my pet died` → `{pet, died}`; `my dog died` →
`{dog, died}`; `my cat died` → `{cat, died}`; `pet loss` → `{pet, loss}`.
All 2 tokens, no collision with any existing pack (G4 collision run: pass).

**Anchors.**

|---|---|---|---|---|

| Psalms 145:9 | "The LORD is good to all. His tender mercies are over all his works." | 0.55 | God's care extends over all his works, without specifying the animal's eternal destiny — the honest limit of what Scripture states. | editorial |

**Guards — and the honest limit of a two-anchor pack.** r2 wrote all five as
`mustNotRank` at window 10, and three of them cannot hold there. The reason is
arithmetic, not a defect to fix: `measuredWindow` is 10, this pack has **two**
anchors by doctrinal design, and three related-theme rows, so positions 6+ are

never have them, and anchoring more verses to fill the window is exactly the

So the two **doctrinal** bans stay bans — they are the ones that matter, and

## Psalms 34:18 — the convergence, counted (critique obj 17)

The critique's sharpest non-blocking observation: *"the engine's answer to
grief, child loss, widowhood, betrayal, pet loss and oppression is converging
on one verse, and nothing in the section counts the convergence."* This
section counts it.

**Before this phase, five packs anchored Psalms 34:18. After it, six.**

| pack | weight | changed by | what the verse is doing there |
|---|---|---|---|
| `near-to-the-brokenhearted` | 1.00 | — | It **is** the pack. The label is the verse. |
| `pregnancy-and-child-loss` | 1.00 | — | pre-existing |
| **`grief-and-loss`** | 0.85 → **0.97** | **A1.6 Ruling 3** | pre-existing anchor, re-weighted |
| `betrayal-and-marriage-crisis` | 0.90 | — | pre-existing |
| `refuge-and-justice-for-the-oppressed` | 0.70 | — | pre-existing |
| **`pet-loss`** | — → **0.60** | **A1.12** | new pack; one of only two anchors, chosen *because* it claims something about the griever and nothing about the animal |

**So this section adds one new anchoring and raises one weight. The
convergence is mostly inherited — and the section still owns it, because the
section is what made it visible.** Measured across this section's own 17
fixtures and 149 queries:

```
Psalms 34:18 leads    0 of 149 queries  (base corpus)
Psalms 34:18 leads   83 of 149 queries  (after this section)
```

Per fixture, after: `pastoral-spouse-death` 60/61, `pastoral-stillborn` 8/9,
`pastoral-pet-loss` 8/8, `pastoral-child-death` 4/4, `pastoral-widow` 1/1,
`pastoral-widower` 1/1, `care-for-widows` 1/3 — and **0 of 62** across the ten
fixtures whose searcher has not lost anyone: `pastoral-kill-myself` (21),
`funeral-readings` (9), `pastoral-dementia` (6), `pastoral-spouse-dying` (6),
`caring-for-aging-parents` (5), `pastoral-self-worth-failure` (4),
`pastoral-too-far-gone` (4), `pastoral-god-hates-me` (3),
`pastoral-god-abandoned-me` (2), `pastoral-god-forsaken-me` (2). That last
number is the one that decides whether this is a defect. (66 of the 149
queries do not get Ps 34:18 at #1 at all; 62 of those 66 are these ten
fixtures, and the other four are named: `does god care for widows`
(James 1:27 44.10) and `bible verses for widows` (Psalms 146:9 40.56) — both
the assembly's register, not a bereaved person's — `my sister died`
(1 Thessalonians 4:13-14 52.00, Ruling 3's stated exception) and
`death of a child` (Romans 8:26-27 48.13).)

**Read as a pastor, is it one? No — and here is the test that would show it
becoming one.** Every query where the verse leads is a query where someone
has lost a person or an animal: "my husband died", "widow", "my son died",
"my dog died". "The LORD is near to those who have a broken heart, and saves
those who have a crushed spirit" is not a *topic* answer that happens to fit
six topics; it is a **condition** answer, and the condition is the same one
in all six. The registers that are about something else — despair, guilt,
abandonment, a dying parent, an occasion — do **not** get it, and that
separation is measured, not asserted.

**What would make it a defect, stated so a later round can check it:**

1. **The verse leading a register whose searcher is not bereaved.** The
   nearest miss today is `betrayal-and-marriage-crisis`, whose anchor
   predates this phase: a person typing "my husband cheated" is crushed but
   not bereaved, and if Ps 34:18 ever leads there **and** the item's own
   betrayal anchors fall below it, that is the first real symptom. It does
   not lead there today. **A2 owns that check**, and §A1.0e now carries the
   coordination row.
2. **A seventh pack.** The threshold this section proposes: **no further pack
   anchors Psalms 34:18 without a ruling that names this table.** Six is
   defensible verse by verse; seven should have to argue against the count,
   not just against the neighbours.
3. **The reason label going generic.** As long as the row arrives labelled
   `Theme: Losing a child` or `Theme: Grief and loss` — the pack that actually
   fired — the searcher is told *why*, and the convergence is invisible to
   them in the way that matters. It is measured: on `my son died` the row
   carries **two** `concept_anchor` labels and both are true.

This is not a defect today. It is now a counted thing with a stated trigger,
which is what the critique asked for.

## Critic responses

Three places where r2 does not do what the critique asked, each with the
measurement that justifies the difference. Everything else in the critique
is accepted and implemented.

### CR-1 — objection 4, `better off without me`: declined, not added

The critique tokenized four phrasings and called them "all safe and all
absent". Three are added (`i want to disappear`, `i wish i was never born`,
`im a burden to my family`). The fourth is declined, and the proof is the
tokenizer:

```
"better off without me"        -> {better, without}
"im better off without him"    -> {better, without}
"im better off without her"    -> {better, without}
```

An entry on `{better, without}` serves the crisis pack's entire anchor set —
2 Cor 1:8-10, 1 Kings 19:4-7, Matt 11:28-29 — to a searcher typing an
ordinary breakup or divorce sentence, because the two queries are the same
query. That is the identical reasoning the section already uses to defer
bare `cant` ("admitting it would fire this concept far more broadly").
The register is not left empty: the pack's existing 3-token
`everyone would be better off without me` returns 2 Cor 1:8-10 at **40.00**
today (measured), and it is now an explicitly tested phrasing.

`i hate everything about me` → `{hate, everyth}` (objection 6's third
suggestion) is declined on the same principle: `everyth` is a generic stem
that would fire the pack from "God is in everything", "I hate everything
about my job", and similar. The two the objection called must-ship —
`i hate my life` and `self hatred` — are shipped.

### CR-2 — objection 20, the `preferredOrder` pin: the fix as written fails

The critique offered two fixes: "Add `preferredOrder` (Ps 34:18 above
1 Thess 4:13-14) or set Ps 34:18 `withinTop: 3`." The first is provably
unsafe today. Measured live:

```
== "my sister died"
  3. 1 Thessalonians 4:13  score=6.00  target=WEB:52004013
     [translation_variant:Worded this way in another translation: died, sister(6.00)]
```

`WEB:52004013` is the *same target* as the `1 Thessalonians 4:13-14` anchor,
so after this item the two reasons merge on one result. **The conclusion is
right and the number was wrong, in the direction that makes the conclusion
stronger (critique obj 21, accepted).** r2 read the 6.00 as
`translation_variant`'s budget and computed 38.00 + 6.00 = 44.00. The 6 is
`soleEvidenceMaxPoints`, which **cannot** apply once the rows merge, because a
`concept_anchor` reason survives on the target (`budgets.ts:205-207`);
`translation_variant`'s budget is **14**. Measured after the change:

```
== "my sister died"
   1. 1 Thessalonians 4:13-14  52.00  [concept_anchor 38.00 | translation_variant: died, sister 14.00]
```

**52.00**, not 44.00 — it leads that query outright. The pin would fail the
build harder than r2 costed, on an `additionalQuery`, for a reason that has
nothing to do with grief ordering.

**r3 also withdraws the replacement r2 offered.** r2 wrote that changing the
weight (Ps 34:18 0.85 → 0.97) was "something stronger and more durable …
keeping John 11:25-26 first". Measured, John 11:25-26 is **#3 or #4 on all 29
queries** and Ps 34:18 leads every one of them; the weight change did not
keep John 11:25-26 first and could not have, because the 12.00 of
related-theme points on Ps 34:18 is a bigger term than the 0.12 of weight.
A1.6 Ruling 3 now states the measured order, defends it as the better reading
of "presence before doctrine", and rewrites the pack header to match. **The
pin stays deferred to S-B §B.6** — that is unchanged, and now for a reason
that is arithmetically correct.

### CR-3 — objection 26, the bonus finding: half of it was already done

The critique is right that r1's recommendation shipped no weights, no
sources and no fixture, that `anchor.weight ?? 1` would have landed all
three anchors at 1.0, that a missing `sources:` is a hard importer error,
and that r1 edited a pack no item owned. All of that is fixed in A1.13.

One factual correction. The critique says the recommendation "adds these
three anchors" to `aging-and-old-age.yaml`. It cannot: that file
**already anchors all three**, at reviewed weights with sources —

```yaml
# ontology/concepts/aging-and-old-age.yaml
  - ref: Psalms 71:9      / sources: [editorial] / weight: 0.9
  - ref: Psalms 71:17-18  / sources: [editorial] / weight: 0.85
  - ref: Isaiah 46:4      / sources: [editorial] / weight: 0.9
```

— even though its header still calls them "corpus-blocked riders". So the
weight-1.0 hazard the critique describes was real only for
`caring-for-aging-parents`, and the substantive work left is one anchor
(Isaiah 46:4, into the caregiver pack) plus two stale header comments. The
critique's register-mismatch point stands and decides the assignment:
Ps 71:9 and 71:17-18 are the aging person's own prayer and stay where they
are; Isa 46:4 fits both voices and is the one that moves.

### Owner-brief premise corrected (not a critic objection)

The r2 brief states that "Phase B2 (sole-evidence ceiling) is what fully
caps" Job 7:16. It does not, and §A1.0c gives the reading: B2 fires only
when **no** surviving reason is authoritative, and Job 7:16 leads on
`exact_phrase` (26.67 of its 36.53), which `isAuthoritative` covers. The
same is true of Ezekiel 24:18 (40.00, sole `exact_phrase`). The owner's
*decision* — drop the anchor, guard with `mustNotLead withinTop 1`, and
require the parity anchors to outscore it — is applied exactly as given, and
the arithmetic showing 2 Cor 1:8-10 at 40.00 > 36.53 is in A1.1. Only the
attribution of the eventual full fix is corrected, so that no one later
merges a Phase B item expecting this to be handled and finds it is not.

weight edits, both new packs, and the `related:` edges. The ontology tree is
built from `git archive HEAD` and the YAML in this document, compiled with
the **real importer** (`compileConcepts`), diffed against the base build and
applied as a diff — so a *removal* is applied, not silently skipped, which
is the §A1.0d Step 2 correction r4 makes. The spelling index is rebuilt
(Step 2b). Every fixture in this section was transcribed to JSON and run
through the real `corpusGoldenGate` (`eval/src/gates/corpusGolden.ts`) with a
limit-50 `presenceEngine`, exactly as `eval/src/gauntlet.ts:847-852` does.

**Every number in this appendix was reproduced end-to-end in r4's final
pass**, from two fresh copies of `pipeline/output/fixture.db` and a fresh
compile of both YAML trees, with the fifteen fixtures **re-extracted from the
JSON blocks printed in this document** rather than from the harness's working
copies — so *printed* and *measured* are the same bytes, and the check is
mechanical rather than a promise. That re-extraction is what caught the four
stale ladders this round corrects (r4-a…r4-d below).
