### Structural halves

```
compile errors: 0   concepts: 291
G4 collision            pass | 291 concept(s) are mutually distinct
G4 collapse deny-list   pass | 70 single-token collapse(s), all acknowledged in ontology/lexicon-inventory.yaml
G4 bare-word inventory  pass | 291 concept(s) carry an explicit bare-word decision (293 admitted, 244 skipped)
COVERAGE                pass | all 291 concept(s) are demonstrated by an active anchor assertion
DOCTRINAL PAIRING       pass | 0 flags — scanned 1847 anchor(s) against 11 watchlist references and 10 material-frame keywords
INVARIANT 1             144 added lexicon rows | 149 fixture queries | 0 uncovered | 0 duplicate token sets
```

`293 admitted / 244 skipped` — r3 measured 295/242, and the two-row
difference is exactly A1.6 Ruling 5 moving `husbands` and `wives` from one
column to the other. G4 was run over a scratch `lexicon-inventory.yaml`
carrying every row this section prescribes, with thresholds read from
`eval/budgets.json` (`maxSharedPhraseRatio` 0.34, `maxSharedTokenRatio` 0.60,
`minLexiconEntries` 2). No `firing-token-undecided` findings.

**G4 collision is load-bearing in r4 and was not in r3.** A1.6 Ruling 6's
routing was chosen by enumerating all sixteen assignments of the four
ambiguous phrase families across `grief-and-loss` and
`pregnancy-and-child-loss` and measuring each with the gate's own ratio:
**thirteen fail**, one passes with zero margin, and two pass. The chosen
assignment measures `tokenRatio` **0.571** (8 shared of 14) and `phraseRatio`
**0.211**. The first attempt — dual-homing all sixteen child phrases — failed
with *"share 16 lexicon phrase(s) (52% of the smaller lexicon; limit 34%)"*,
and the second with *"share 65% of their vocabulary (limit 60%): away, child,
daughter, death, die, died, do, god, lost, pass, see, son, take"*.

### What is *not* claimed

- **No Phase B item is relied on.** Every window above is measured against
  data changes only. S-B §B.6 would tighten several of them; none needs it.
- **Two positions are at their asserted boundary, and are named where they
  occur:** 2 Cor 1:3-4 at **#3** on `my mom has dementia` (asserted
  `withinTop: 3`) and 1 Thess 4:13-18 at **#5** on `bible verses for a
  funeral` (asserted `withinTop: 5`). A third, John 11:25-26 at **#4** on
  `death of a parent`, has one position of margin against `withinTop: 5`.
  r3's fourth boundary case — John 14:1-3 at #5 on bare `funeral` — is gone:
  A1.6's John 14:1-3 anchor lifts it to **#1 on all nine** funeral queries,
  and A1.11 keeps the window at 5 rather than banking the lift (r4-a).
  Each item says what would break it.
- **The safety claims are scoped to the gate's window, not the engine's.**
  `DEFAULT_LIMIT` is **25**; the fixture format cannot express a ban at 25.
  Everywhere a banned ref survives between #11 and #25, this section prints
  the position (§A1.0b, and the matrix above).
- **Three registers stay open by measurement, not by omission:** bare
  `{alone}` (A1.4 / Summary); `bible verses for widows`, where Ex 22:22-24
  stays at #3 and this section deliberately writes no guard (A1.10); and the
  brother/sister/friend question forms (Summary).
- **One anchor was measured and then declined**: Lamentations 3:31-33 in
  `loneliness` (A1.4 Ruling 5) — compiled, run, and rejected because the
  eleventh anchor silently disables that item's `preferredOrder` pin, proved
  by inverting the pin and watching it pass.

## A2.0 Why

The audit found harmful, not merely absent, results.

- `tempted to cheat on my wife` → `{tempt, cheat, wife}` is a superset of the
  existing `wife cheated` → `{cheat, wife}`, so
  `betrayal-and-marriage-crisis`'s comfort-for-the-wounded set fires for the
  man who has not yet sinned — 1 Cor 7:15 included, permission-shaped.
- `my parents are getting divorced` → `{parent, gett, divorc}` carries
  `parenting`'s bare cue `parenting` → `{parent}`, so Eph 6:1 / Col 3:20-21
  ("Children, obey your parents") are served to a child watching the people
  they are commanded to obey fail each other. **Measured, not assumed** — see
  the co-fire table in A2.0b.
- `panic attack` → `{panic, attack}` reaches nothing curated and lands on
  2 Sam 17:9, a battle report.
- `i lost my job` → `{lost, job}` reaches only
  `remembered-work-as-for-the-lord` through its bare `job` cue: Col 3:23,
  "work heartily, as for the Lord", served to a person who has just lost the
  work. Also measured.
- `i cheated on my wife` and `my wife cheated on me` both tokenize to
  `{cheat, wife}`. Containment is order-blind, so the engine cannot tell the
  guilty spouse from the wounded one. This is a **structural limit**, not a
  curation gap; it is disclosed in A2.4 and in **Disclosed residuals**, and it
  is never patched by an assertion the tokenizer cannot honour.

r1 of this section fixed the first three and reproduced the fourth pattern —
one register's vocabulary routed into a neighbouring register's pack — three
more times without noticing. r2 treats it as a class: every register carries
a stated *who is typing this*, and every co-fire is measured before an
assertion is written.

## A2.0b Mechanical gate pre-flight (run, not remembered)

Four rules were read out of the gates and enforced over this section
mechanically. Each is stated with what it actually says, because r1 claimed
"G4 green" nineteen times without running any of them.

1. **`row-missing` (G4, FAIL).** `eval/src/gates/lexiconInventory.ts`
   iterates every compiled concept and fails for any concept with no
   `concepts:` row. This section mints **eight** packs and all eight ship a
   row — `marriage-in-crisis`, `infidelity-and-temptation`,
   `children-of-divorce`, `single-parenting`, `heartbreak-and-breakup`,
   `provision-in-hardship`, `hurt-by-the-church`, `sleep-at-night`. A
   skipped-only row is legal (`aging-and-old-age`, `appointed-feasts`
   precedent). r3 enumerated seven, omitted `marriage-in-crisis`, and failed
   G4 `row-missing` on it (B-1); the missing row is printed in A2.3 and the
   gate is green on the text as printed.
2. **`admitted-does-not-fire` (G4, FAIL).** The gate normalizes the admitted
   string with `significantWords` and requires the result to be a token some
   lexicon phrase collapses to. The rule is *"the admitted string must
   normalize to the firing token"*, **not** "write the surface word" — the
   live `shame: admitted: [shame, asham]` row proves a stem is legal when it
   normalizes to itself. Every admitted token in this section was run:

   ```
   asham -> {asham} OK        diagnosed -> {diagnos} OK    diagnosis -> {diagnosi} OK
   diagnos -> {diagno} FAIL   hyperventilating -> {hyperventilat} OK
   unemployed -> {unemploy} OK  nightmares -> {nightmar} OK   surgery -> {surgery} OK
   chronic -> {chronic} OK    panic -> {panic} OK          numb -> {numb} OK
   weak -> {weak} OK          caregiver -> {caregiver} OK  retirement -> {retirement} OK
   insomnia -> {insomnia} OK  breakthrough -> {breakthrough} OK  failure -> {failure} OK
   mess -> {mess} OK          laid -> {laid} OK            breakup/heartbroken/heartbreak OK
   ```
   r1's `diagnos` is the one that fails; it is written `diagnosed` here.
3. **`lexicon-collapse-unacknowledged` (G4, FAIL).** `singleTokenCollapses`
   (collision.ts:167) flags any phrase of >1 word whose significant width is
   1. Every such phrase in this section has a `collapses:` row: `im weak` →
   `weak`, `im a failure` → `failure`, `messed up` → `mess`. Phrases that
   would have needed one and were **removed** instead: `laid off` → `laid`
   (r3 withdrew the phrase in prose and printed the collapse row anyway;
   applied together those two halves fail G4 with `stale acknowledgment` —
   B-2, fixed in A2.11), `im broke` → `broke`, `my pastor let me down` →
   `pastor`, `before surgery` → `surgery`, `i failed` → `fail`, `giving up`
   → `giving`. The gate confirms it: **71 collapses, all acknowledged, zero
   stale**, on the text exactly as printed.
4. **G3 concept coverage (`conceptCoverageGate`, FAIL).** A fixture counts
   toward a concept's coverage only when `status: "active"`, the `query` is
   non-empty, and some `expectedTop` entry carries BOTH
   `requiredReasonFamily: "concept_anchor"` and `requiredReasonLabel` equal to
   the exact string `Theme: <the pack's label:>`. Consequences applied
   throughout r2:
   - every fixture that declares `coversConcepts` carries that label pin, and
     the label string is copied from the pack's `label:` field verbatim;
   - **the label pin is placed on an anchor no other pack owns**, because the
     displayed reason label is contested when two firing concepts anchor the
     same reference (M19's mechanism). Anchor ownership was checked
     mechanically for every reference asserted below;
   - no fixture declares `coversConcepts` for a concept its item does not
     build;
   - a `pending` fixture cannot cover a concept, which is why the residual
     fixtures below are additions, never replacements.
5. **`alsoAcceptable` asserts nothing.** It is parsed into `FIXTURE_FIELDS`
   and never consulted by any assertion path. No Acceptance criterion in r2
   rests on it; where a claim matters it is an `expectedTop` entry, using
   `presenceOnly: true` (valid only alongside a required reason) when the
   claim is presence rather than rank.

**G4 collision simulation over the proposed set** (thresholds
`eval/budgets.json`: `maxSharedPhraseRatio 0.34`, `maxSharedTokenRatio 0.6`):
zero shared normalized phrases involving any pack this section touches — r1's
two shared phrases (`broken family` with family-reconciliation, `fresh start`
with new-creation) are removed. The tightest token ratio is
`betrayal-and-marriage-crisis ↔ infidelity-and-temptation` at
6/14 = **0.429** (`husband, cheat, wife, spouse, affair, unfaithful`), under
the 0.6 limit and inherent to two packs about the same event from opposite
sides. The one shared phrase in the neighbourhood — `want to give up`,
do-not-lose-heart ↔ hope-in-despair, ratio 0.063 — is the pre-existing,
documented, deliberate share and is untouched here.

**A note on what the phrase check does NOT catch** (corrected in r3 — r2's
statement named the wrong function and used an example the gate *would*
catch). G4 does **not** use the engine's `normalizedPhrase` export. It defines
its own, at `eval/src/gates/collision.ts:36-38`:

```ts apply=none
function normalizePhrase(phrase: string): string {
  return significantWords(phrase).join(' ');
}
```

That **is** a token join, so r2's worked example is one G4 reports:
`significantWords("i was unfaithful to my wife") = ["unfaithful","wife"]` →
`"unfaithful wife"`, identical to `significantWords("unfaithful wife")`. The
pair would surface as a shared phrase.

The blind spot is real, and the hand-check was worth doing, but the mechanism
is **first-occurrence token ORDER**, not surface form. `hurt by my pastor` →
`"hurt pastor"`; `my pastor hurt me` → `"pastor hurt"`. Same token set,
different join, **no G4 finding** — and at match time `matchConcepts` is
order-blind, so both fire the same pack at parity. That is the sentence to
write, and it is the sentence C3 needed: the two phrasings are duplicates at
the token-SET level, which is the level the engine matches at and the level
G4 does not normalize to. Token-set duplicates across packs were therefore
checked by hand-run script over the whole proposed set, and two candidate
entries were dropped for it (Critic responses, C2).

## A2.0b-2 Overlapping-span census (measured)

This section anchors 30 references at spans that **partially overlap** a span
another pack already anchors — Ps 68:5-6 against `single-parenting`'s Ps 68:5,
Rev 21:4 against `grief-and-loss`'s Rev 21:3-4, and so on. Partial overlap is
the one structural hazard the gates do not check: G4 compares lexicon phrases,
not anchor ranges, and `dedupeConceptAnchors` merges duplicates only *within*
one concept, so two packs anchoring overlapping-but-unequal spans of the same
passage produce two independent result rows for what a reader sees as one text.
The failure mode to look for is one span silently displacing the other on a
query the other pack owns.

**The census below was intersected against HEAD, and HEAD is not what ships
(C10).** Every chapter's overlap ledger was built the same way, so no ledger
could see a sibling chapter's additions, and four "anchored by no other pack"
warrants in this section were false the moment S-A1 and S-A3 landed beside it.
They are re-derived against the **composed** tree — A1+A2+A3 applied together
— and named with the sibling pack and weight in their own Why cells:
**Mark 10:6-9** (A2.3 @0.9 vs `wedding-verses` @0.9, a dead tie),
**Mark 10:13-16** (A2.5 @0.7 vs `baby-dedication` @0.85, a loss),
**Isaiah 49:15-16** (A2.5 @0.8 vs `loneliness` @0.6) and
**Psalms 90:12** (A2.17 @0.85 vs `funeral-readings` @0.7, and S-A4's
`stewardship-of-days` row). The two coverage label pins that rested on the
false claim are re-derived from the composed run rather than asserted, in
A2.3 and A2.5. Nothing else in the census moves: sole-anchorship was the
warrant's stated reason, not its mechanism, and the mechanism —
which pack the query reaches — is measured.

Every such pair in this section was enumerated by script and then measured on
the simulated artifact: 30 new anchors stand in 49 partial-overlap relations
with shipped spans. For each pair the script ran a query that should surface
the new span and a query that should surface the other pack's span, and
recorded where each landed.

**Result: no pair displaces the other.** In all 49 relations both spans surface
for their own register, on disjoint query sets. The reason is that the two
spans are reached through different concepts, so each query fires the pack that
owns it and the other span arrives, if at all, several positions lower on weak
evidence.

The one displacing overlap found anywhere in this work was **intra-pack**, not
cross-pack: r2's A2.4b proposed adding Ps 51:1-4 to `forgiveness-of-sins`
*beside* its existing Ps 51:3-4, which put two rows of one pack's own anchors
on one psalm and pushed Rom 8:1 out of #5 in `guilt-and-condemnation.json`.
That is the regression the r2 critique caught, and r3 removes the overlap
rather than managing it — the existing span is widened in place (A2.4b).

| new anchor (pack) | span | other pack(s) with an OVERLAPPING-BUT-DIFFERENT span | measured: the best position each span reaches, and on which query |
|---|---|---|---|

does not own, which is what "no displacement" looks like.

## A2.0c The four routes into the top ten that are not the concept layer

r2's anchor tables modelled only `concept_anchor`, and twelve guards failed
because of it. A verse does **not** need an anchor to reach position 6–10 of a
25-result page. The budgets (`engine/src/ranking/budgets.ts`, reviewed data)
say exactly how loud each alternative route may be:

| family | `maxPoints` | `maxReasons` | what it says | measured in this section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `translation_variant` | **14** | 1 | "another English translation renders this verse with your words" | **Phil 4:13 #8 for `give me strength`** — 14.00 + `passage_terms` 1.48 = 15.48, above six of this pack's seven anchors' tails (A2.13). Also 1 Cor 15:56 #9, 1 Kings 18:46 #10; 1 Pet 3:1-6 #1 for `being a good husband` at 47.53. |
| `token_overlap` | 10 | 1 | shared significant stems with the shipped WEB wording | Mark 12:20 4.00 for `my wife left me` (A2.1); Col 3:20-21 1.11 for the `parent` queries (A2.5) |
| `passage_terms` | 8 | 2 | homiletical term profile | the 1.48 that mattered above; 1.60–3.75 throughout the `parent` tail |
| `proximity` | 6 | 1 | matched words appear close together | 1 Sam 7:8 6.00 for `cant stop crying` (A2.9); Exod 10:5 5.70 (A2.11); Job 7:4 5.70 (A2.19) |

Two properties of the budget code decide most of the tail, and neither is
visible from an anchor table:

1. **The sole-evidence floor.** `soleEvidenceMaxPoints: { translation_variant: 6 }`
   caps a result at 6 points **only when every surviving reason is a hint-only
   family**. One reason from any other family disables the step. So a lone
   `translation_variant` is worth 6 (measured: Ps 55:5 and Jer 2:25 both at
   exactly 6.00 for `cant stop crying`), but a `translation_variant` with a
   1.48-point `passage_terms` chip beside it is worth **15.48** — a 2.6×
   difference produced by the smallest corroborating signal in the system.
   That is the whole of B7, and it is why Phil 4:13 outranked six anchors.
2. **`relatedConceptEvidence` is width-independent.** Strength is
   `anchorWeight × 0.5` under the `concept_lexicon` budget (12 points), with
   **no** specificity or coverage discount. On a one-token query, where a
   pack's own anchors are scaled by `conceptSpecificity(1) = 0.55`, a related
   edge does not shrink with them. Measured: `insomnia` put Ps 127:2 (this
   pack's own 0.9 anchor, 19.80) **above** its 1.0 lead Ps 4:8 (22.00 → the
   0.9 anchor collected a further 3.60 from `sleep-at-night`'s own
   `related: rest-for-the-weary` edge, total 23.40). A pack can defeat its own
   lead with an edge it declares in the same commit; r3 drops that edge
   (A2.19).

**Every `mustNotRank` and `mustNotLead` in this section is now measured
against a real run rather than reasoned against the anchor table.** The census
is in the appendix.

## A2.0d Guard policy (r3)

r2 wrote 74 guards and asserted they held. On the real gate, **18 of the 24
failed expectations were guards**, across ten distinct references (Mark 12:20,
Matt 22:25, 1 Sam 7:8, Col 3:20-21, Phil 4:13, Exod 10:5, 1 Cor 7:15,
Eph 5:21-24, Titus 2:3-5, Job 7:4). The question the critique asked and r2 did
not answer — *what do you do when a guard fails?* — is answered here once,
mechanically, and applied to every guard in the section.

Every guard carries **its measured position** on the simulated artifact (see
the census). Guards fall into four classes — three that are kept, and one
that is deleted:

- **Measured guards.** The reference has a demonstrated route into these
  queries: it is measured somewhere on the served page (top 25). Such a guard
  must be measured **outside** the guarded window, and the item records the
  position. If it measures **inside** the window, the design changes — an
  in-register anchor, a weight, a span, a `related:` edge, or a phrase — or the
  guard narrows to a window the arithmetic supports (`mustNotLead`, which is
  what "must not be the first thing this person is handed" actually means).
  Shrinking `expectedWithinTop` to make a guard pass is not available: that is
  decoration wearing a measurement's name.
- **Standing-contract guards.** The doctrine-negative (flagged-pairings) and
  crisis-floor (suicide / self-harm / abuse-weaponised) lists that the repo's
  own pastoral-care and `prosperity-*` fixtures already keep by convention,
  where **absence is the pass** and the fixture note says so. These are kept
  regardless of measured position and are **labelled as such in the item**, so
  nobody reads them as evidence that a route was found and closed.
- **Ex-ante regression detectors (r4, M-8 — the class r3 used and did not
  name).** The reference has no route *today* and is not on a doctrine or
  crisis list, but its absence is the fixed state of a **specific measured
  defect**, and the guard exists so the defect cannot return silently. **Four**
  in this section are of this kind and r3 filed them wrongly: `panic-attack`'s
  **2 Sam 17:9** (the audit's confirmed wrong result, now #16), A2.11's
  **Exod 10:5** (the locust verse the bare-`laid` admission pulled in, now
  #12) and **Col 3:23** (the work-ethic verse that led a job-loss query in the
  audit, now #11), and `resisting-infidelity`'s **Matt 19:3-9** (the
  divorce-law span the audit measured leading the tempted spouse's page).
  A2.11 already used the phrase "regression detector" for two of them. Such a
  guard is kept, labelled, and carries the defect it detects in its `why`.
- **Decoration — the fourth class, and it is deleted.** A guard that is none
  of the three above — no measured route, no standing contract, no fixed
  defect behind it — is not a check, and it is deleted with the measurement
  recorded in the item instead.

CLAUDE.md: a check that cannot run reports `not-applicable` *with a reason*;
it never reports `pass`. **Thirteen** such guards were deleted in r3 and
**two more in r4** (M-8), each named in its item and listed in the Revision
log's disposition table.
r2's fixtures carried 74 guards. r3 carried 61 and split them 23 measured /
38 standing-contract, then conceded in its own closing pages that four did not
fit either class and kept them anyway. **r4 makes the taxonomy exhaustive and
then applies it** (M-8). Two guards with no route, no doctrine listing and no
fixed defect — `resisting-infidelity`'s 2 Sam 11:2-4 and Prov 7:6-21 — are
**deleted** like r3's other thirteen, so the deletion rule now applies on
identical evidence in both directions. The remaining **59** are classified
mechanically, by whether the guarded reference appears anywhere in the top 50
of any of its own fixture's queries:

```text apply=none
ex-ante regression detectors                                       4
  panic-attack / 2 Samuel 17:9      job-loss-and-money-fear / Exodus 10:5
  job-loss-and-money-fear / Colossians 3:23   resisting-infidelity / Matthew 19:3-9
measured guards (a route exists; the item records the position)   18
  Mark 12:20, Matthew 22:25, Matthew 19:29, 1 Samuel 7:8, Colossians 3:20-21 (x2),
  Ephesians 6:4 (x2), Philippians 4:19, Philippians 4:13, Proverbs 3:9-10,
  Ephesians 5:21-24, 1 Peter 3:1-6, Titus 2:3-5, Malachi 2:16,
  1 Corinthians 7:15, Proverbs 22:6, Job 7:4
standing-contract (absent from the top 50 on every query)         37
                                                            TOTAL 59
```

Two of the eighteen — `failure-and-breakthrough`'s Phil 4:19 (#42) and
`job-loss-and-money-fear`'s Prov 3:9-10 (#16–#36) — are on the flagged-pairings
watchlist **and** have a route, so they satisfy two classes; they are counted
as *measured* because the item records their positions, which is the stricter
obligation. **No guard sits outside the taxonomy.**

One further rule, from M-2: **a guard must measure the harm its `why`
names.** A `mustNotRank` whose `why` describes a harm at the served-page level
while its window is 10 is asserting something its own reason does not mean.
Where the window cannot be widened without an immediate failure, the guard is
deleted and the number is recorded (A2.4's 1 Cor 7:15, measured #18).

### A2.1 Extend betrayal-and-marriage-crisis

**Measured gap.** `my wife/husband left me`, `my spouse/wife/husband wants a
divorce`, `going through a divorce`, `separated from my husband/wife` reach
nothing — only `my spouse left me` exists (`spouse` ≠ `wife`/`husband`).
They fall through to raw retrieval on bare `left`: Mark 12:20 ("left no
offspring"), Matt 22:25, Luke 18:29-30, Mark 10:29-30, Matt 19:29 —
inheritance and voluntary-sacrifice narratives, not abandonment.

**Change.**
```yaml apply=ops
#@ lexicon-add ontology/concepts/pastoral-betrayal-and-marriage-crisis.yaml
  - my wife left me            # {wife, left}
  - my husband left me         # {husband, left}
  - my spouse wants a divorce  # {spouse, want, divorce}
  - my wife wants a divorce    # {wife, want, divorce}
  - my husband wants a divorce # {husband, want, divorce}
  - going through a divorce    # {going, divorce}
  - separated from my husband  # {separat, husband}
  - separated from my wife     # {separat, wife}

  # these two forms are the only suspicion phrasings that do not already
  # reach this pack at parity through `wife cheated` / `husband cheated`.
  - i think my wife is cheating     # {think, wife, cheat}
  - i think my husband is cheating  # {think, husband, cheat}
  # r1's `i want a divorce` is REMOVED from this pack — see B1 / A2.3.
#@ anchors-add ontology/concepts/pastoral-betrayal-and-marriage-crisis.yaml
  # r3, B1 — the design fix, not a guard:
  - ref: Deuteronomy 31:6
    sources: [editorial]
    weight: 0.65
  - ref: Psalms 27:10
    sources: [editorial]
    weight: 0.6
```

**Why two new anchors (r3).** r2 changed nothing but the lexicon and asserted
that the five levirate/renunciation narratives would not rank. Measured, two
of them did: Mark 12:20 #9 and Matt 22:25 #10 for `my wife left me`, on
`proximity` (5.40) + `token_overlap` (4.00) — the routes A2.0c models. The
pack's eight anchors filled exactly positions 1–8 and then stopped, and the
tail is where every failed guard in r2 lived.

The fix is not a stronger assertion, it is a better answer. *"He will not fail
you nor forsake you"* (Deut 31:6) and *"When my father and my mother forsake
me, then the LORD will take me up"* (Ps 27:10) are the two texts in the canon
that answer **"someone left"** most directly, and neither was in this pack.
They fill positions 9–10 with scripture that belongs there, and the five
narratives move to #11–#16 — measured, on the served page, guarded, and out of
the first screen.

**Tokenizer hazards.** All ten entries ≥ 2 tokens (token sets recorded
above); none collapses; no inventory row due. Query reachability, live:

```text apply=none
"my wife left me"           -> {wife, left}            betrayal PARITY
"my husband left me"        -> {husband, left}         betrayal PARITY (+ godly-marriage 1/2, bare `husbands`)
"my spouse wants a divorce" -> {spouse, want, divorce} betrayal PARITY (+ godly-marriage 2/3 via A2.3's `i want a divorce`)
"going through a divorce"   -> {going, divorce}        betrayal PARITY
"separated from my husband" -> {separat, husband}      betrayal PARITY
```

`i want a divorce` → `{want, divorce}` would have matched a same-worded entry
here at **parity**, firing the whole comfort-for-the-abandoned set — 1 Cor
7:15 ("not under bondage") included — for the person contemplating leaving.
That is the register collision this section exists to stop, so the phrase
leaves this pack. It is not left unserved: A2.3 takes it, guarded.

No anchor changes — Luke 15:11-32's father-running-to-the-son scene already
reads correctly for parent↔child estrangement.

**Tokenizer hazards.** All six ≥ 2 tokens; none collapses. Apostrophes are
stripped, so entries are written `wont`, matching this pack's existing `dont`
convention. All six fire this pack at PARITY and nothing else (measured); the
pack's reviewed skips (`family`, `brother`, `estranged`) stay skipped —
`estrang` still never fires bare.

**Anchors.** No new anchors — Luke 15:11-32 @1.0 (owned by this pack alone),
Gen 45:1-15 @0.95, Gen 33:4 @0.9, Gen 50:15-21 @0.9, Matt 5:23-24 @0.85,
Mal 4:5-6 @0.7, Philemon 1:15-18 @0.6.

**Guards — measured, and the honest answer is "none needed" (r3, m9/m-4).**
r1 had no guard, r2 wrote two, and the critique's m-4 was right that a fixture
asserting almost nothing passes for the wrong reason. r3 answers it with a
measurement rather than a third guess.

Two real hazards were checked, both read in WEB and both in corpus:

- Matthew 10:35-36 — *"For I came to set a man at odds against his father,
  and a daughter against her mother… A man's foes will be those of his own
  household."*
- Luke 14:26 — *"If anyone comes to me, and doesn't disregard his own father,
  mother, wife, children…"*

**Both are absent from the top 50 on all six queries.** The reason is
structural and is the useful finding: `research("my son wont talk to me")`
returns **seven results in total**, and all seven are `family-reconciliation`
anchors. There is no tail. `son` is indeed a loaded token, but the containment
matcher only reaches verses through curated phrases or shared *significant*
stems, and `{son, wont, talk}` reaches nothing else above the floor.

Under A2.0d both guards are decoration and are **deleted**. What replaces them
is a stronger positive assertion: three of the seven results are pinned by
position and reason label, so any future change that lets another pack into
this answer set moves a named position and breaks this named file. That is a
tighter contract than two guards that cannot fire.

### A2.3 NEW marriage-in-crisis, and godly-marriage stays a teaching pack

> **This item was rebuilt in r3.** r2 put the five distress phrasings into
> `godly-marriage` as a "crisis sub-register" guarded by `mustNotLead`, and
> wrote in the pack header that the fixture guard was *"the ONLY instrument
> available at this layer"*. That diagnosis was correct and the conclusion was
> invalid: **`mustNotLead` is an assertion, not a suppressor.** Measured on the
> simulated artifact, `i want a divorce` returned nine consecutive
> marriage-duty texts — Eph 5:25, Eph 5:21-24, 1 Cor 13:4-7, Heb 13:4,
> 1 Pet 3:7, Eph 5:28, 1 Pet 3:1-6, Titus 2:3-5, 1 Cor 7:3 — and not one
> pastoral word, with 1 Cor 7:15 at #10. Five of the five guards failed. That
> is a FAIL of the stated bar, produced by the change r2 made in response to
> round 1.

**Measured gap.** `unhappy in my marriage`, `save my marriage`, `my husband
doesnt love me`, `my wife and i keep fighting` reach nothing at parity
(`my husband doesnt love me` reaches godly-marriage today only 1/3, through
the bare cue `husbands`, and `gods-love` 1/3 through bare `love`). And per B1,
`i want a divorce` needs a home that is neither the wounded-spouse pack nor
silence.

**The three structures, measured.** All three were compiled and run. This is
the table the owner asked for; the numbers are top-of-page positions for
`i want a divorce` on the simulated artifact.

| **A** | r2: five distress phrases in **`godly-marriage`**, guarded by `mustNotLead` | Eph 5:25 40.00, **Eph 5:21-24 36.00**, 1 Cor 13:4-7 35.70, Heb 13:4, 1 Pet 3:7, Eph 5:28, 1 Pet 3:1-6, **Titus 2:3-5**, 1 Cor 7:3, 1 Cor 7:15 | **No.** Nine marriage-duty texts. | **#2, #8, #7 — all inside the top 10, two inside the top 3.** 5 `mustNotLead`/`mustNotRank` all FAIL | absent (no route) | none, but the answer is wrong | **FAIL** |

Two of r2's grounds for rejecting a fourth marriage pack were answered by the
compile, not by argument. (i) *"1 Cor 13:4-7 belongs to marriage teaching"* —
a verse can be anchored by two packs; this section already dual-anchors
Ps 34:18 in five and Heb 4:15-16 in four, and the cross-concept sum is
deliberate engine behaviour, not a defect. (ii) *"a fourth marriage pack would
dilute three existing ones"* — dilution is not a mechanism the engine has.
Concepts do not compete for a budget; they compete on anchor weight inside a
query. A distress pack with its own weights is the only thing that **can**
out-rank Eph 5:25 on a distress query, because anchor weights are pack-wide.
The rejected option is the one that works, and it costs one YAML file and no
engine change.

**Change.**
```yaml apply=ops
#@ new-file ontology/concepts/marriage-in-crisis.yaml
# REGISTER: typed from inside a marriage that is failing, by a person who
# asked no teaching question. godly-marriage answers "what does a good
# marriage look like"; marriage-divorce-teaching answers "is it permitted";
# betrayal-and-marriage-crisis answers "my spouse betrayed me". This pack
# answers "we are failing and I do not know what to do", and it is minted
# rather than folded into any of the three because anchor weights are
# PACK-WIDE: a distress query inside a teaching pack can only be answered
# with teaching weights, and a fixture guard cannot demote anything (r2
# measured exactly that; see the structures table above).
# ORDER IS THE ARGUMENT: comfort first (the person is in pain and has not
# asked a question), then God's design and the call to reconciliation, then
# the concrete work of bearing with one another. Malachi 2:16 sits at the
# pack's FLOOR — it belongs here (it is the covenant word about divorce) and
# it must never be the first thing a person in this state reads.
# The pack does NOT promise the marriage survives, and it anchors nothing
# that reads as permission to leave: 1 Cor 7:10-11 is anchored deliberately
# WITHOUT v15, which stays betrayal-and-marriage-crisis's desertion text.

`marriage falling apart` stays `betrayal-and-marriage-crisis`'s: `{marriage,

**The suspecting spouse (r4, B-8) — the harm this round found.** r3 gave
`infidelity-and-temptation` the entry `thinking about cheating` →
`{think, cheat}`. Token-set containment is order-blind, so that two-token set
sits inside `i think my wife is cheating` → `{think, wife, cheat}`, and the
whole resisting-temptation answer set fired for a woman who had just typed
that she suspects her husband. Measured on r3's build, `i think my husband is
cheating`: Heb 4:15-16 #1, Heb 13:4 #2, Jas 1:13-15 #3 (*"drawn away by his
own lust … sin, when full grown, produces death"*), 1 Cor 10:13 #5,
Matt 26:41 #6, 1 Cor 6:18-20 #9 (*"Flee sexual immorality!"*), Job 31:1 #10 —
six of ten addressing the tempted party, with a `Theme: Resisting infidelity`
reason chip, which is a wrong-reason failure under CLAUDE.md #5 on top of the
register error.

**The fix has three parts, and each is measured.** (i) `thinking about
cheating` is **deleted** from `infidelity-and-temptation`. (ii) The two
suspicion forms are added to this pack (above). (iii) The remaining
infidelity entries are checked for the same defect mechanically.

*Enumerated suspicion forms, routed.* Every row below was run against the
text-derived build; "chips" is the set of `concept_anchor` / `related_concept`
labels present anywhere in the served top ten.

Two of the eight are the new entries; the other six already reached this pack

this one. Only the two `i think my …` forms needed new phrases, and they are
the two that were losing.

*Proof that the tempted-party pack can no longer fire on any of them.* The
check is mechanical: for each of the eleven phrases `infidelity-and-temptation`
owns after r4, is its token set a subset of any suspicion form above?

```text apply=none
tempted to cheat                        {tempt, cheat}                 no suspicion form contains `tempt`
tempted to cheat on my wife             {tempt, cheat, wife}           "
tempted to cheat on my husband          {tempt, cheat, husband}        "
tempted to be unfaithful                {tempt, unfaithful}            "
attracted to someone who isnt my spouse {attract, someone, isnt, spouse}  no form contains `attract`
attracted to someone else               {attract, someone, else}       "

RESULT: 11 phrases x 8 suspicion forms = 88 containment tests, 0 fire.
Every remaining entry carries a TEMPTED-PARTY MARKER (`tempt` / `attract` /
`emotional` / `want` / `struggl`) that no suspicion phrasing speaks. That is
the invariant, and it is the thing to preserve: any future entry added to
this pack must carry one of those markers or be re-checked here.

*What ordered phrases would finish.* This fix is a vocabulary fix, and it
holds only because the two registers happen to use disjoint marker words.
The structural defect remains: `i cheated on my wife` and `my wife cheated on
me` are the **same token set**, so no lexicon can separate the spouse who fell
from the spouse who was wounded (that is the residual
`resisting-infidelity-confession-residual.json` records as `pending`). Engine
item **B.5 (ordered phrase matching)** is what closes the *collision* — it is
not by itself what answers the confessing spouse, which needs a Phase-C route
as well (C9). With order significant, `i cheated on my wife` and `my wife
cheated on me` are different
phrases, and `thinking about cheating` would no longer be a match for
`i think my wife is cheating` at all — the marker-word discipline above could
then be relaxed back to natural vocabulary. Until B.5 ships, the markers are
the guard, and they are stated here so the next person adding a phrase to this
pack knows what they are maintaining.

`refuge-and-justice-for-the-oppressed` is **not** reachable from any of these
phrasings (measured: `scared of my husband` → `{scar, husband}`,
`husband hits me` → `{husband, hit}`; neither is a subset of
`{husband, doesnt, love}`). r3 deliberately does **not** add an abuse phrasing
to reach it: the query does not say abuse, and routing a distress query into
the abuse pack would be the same register error in the other direction. The
frightened searcher reaches that pack by naming what is happening, which its
lexicon already covers.

Gender-role note (DOCTRINAL-BASIS §4, an explicit **non-criterion**): nothing
here adjudicates headship or submission. Eph 5:21-24, 1 Pet 3:1-6 and
Titus 2:3-5 belong in `godly-marriage` and lead it — measured #1/#2 for

**pack** a distress query reaches, not what any pack teaches. The three refs
still rank for the distress queries, at #12–#40, through godly-marriage's own
bare cue: scripture is demoted here, never suppressed.

the same anchors — but the instrument is now the pack, not the assertion.

**Rulings for Jesse.**
- **J-A2-1 (ruling, not a recommendation): the Eph 5:22-24 → 5:21-24 span
  widening.** It edits a doctrinally-reviewed pack, rewrites the comment that
  records the reviewed reasoning, and changes a reference **string** that three
  consumer apps can pin (implementation-plan §5). `ENGINE_VERSION` does not
  move — no ordering rule changed — but `layerFingerprint` does. Measured
  effect: six queries in `godly-marriage.json` show `Ephesians 5:21-24` where
  they showed `Ephesians 5:22-24`, at the same positions (#2/#3), plus
  `Ephesians 5:21` newly at #6 for `unequally-yoked.json`'s
  `marrying a non believer`. Nothing else moves. Recommended, but Jesse's.
- **J-A2-13: the pastoral-vs-teaching balance for `i want a divorce`.** Option C
  is adopted because it is the only one that clears the bar, but *how far*
  the pastoral half should lead is genuinely a pastoral judgment, not an
  arithmetic one. As shipped: two comfort anchors, then design and
  reconciliation, then the concrete work, with the covenant word at the floor.
  A reviewer who wants Mark 10:6-9 to lead can have it by swapping the top
  three weights; the measured consequence is that Ps 34:18 falls to #3 and the
  first thing a person in this state reads becomes a statement about creation.
  Recorded so the choice is visible.
- **J-A2-14 (open): does `betrayal-and-marriage-crisis` keep 1 Cor 7:15 at
  0.7?** Not changed here. It is the right text for the deserted spouse and
  the wrong text for three other registers, and it is measured at #18 for
  `tempted to cheat on my wife` (A2.4) and #8 for the pending
  `i cheated on my wife` residual. Per-register anchor scoping is the real
  answer and it is **Phase C** (C8) — no Phase B item provides it; the numbers
  are recorded so the ruling has them in the meantime.

**Existing fixtures re-run (measured, not listed).** `godly-marriage.json` —
six queries move, all pass (see the M17 table); `pastoral-divorce-teaching.json`
— **unchanged, verified** (this is the fixture r2's C4 wrongly claimed does not
exist; see the C4 ruling); `pastoral-betrayal.json` — two positions move,
passes; `unequally-yoked.json` — one position moves, passes;
`gods-love`-family fixtures — unchanged.

**Acceptance (measured on the simulated artifact, not asserted).**
- `i want a divorce`: Ps 34:18 #1, Ps 147:3 #2, Mark 10:6-9 #3,
  1 Cor 7:10-11 #4, Col 3:12-14 #5, Eph 4:2-3 #6, Rom 12:18 #7,
  Phil 2:3-4 #8, 1 Cor 13:4-7 #9, Mal 2:16 #10.
- Ps 34:18 measures #1 on **all five** queries; Mark 10:6-9 #3/#4/#4/#4/#3;
  1 Cor 7:10-11 #4/#3/#3/#3/#4; 1 Cor 13:4-7 #9/#7/#7/#5/#9.
- Eph 5:21-24 ≥ #13 on every query; 1 Pet 3:1-6 ≥ #16; Titus 2:3-5 ≥ #12.
  All three `mustNotLead(3)` guards **pass measured**, not asserted.
- 1 Cor 7:15: absent from the top 50 on five of the six queries, #24 on
  `my husband doesnt love me`.
- Teaching register: Eph 5:25 #1 on `marriage`, `biblical marriage`,
  `godly husband`, `godly wife`, `prayer for my husband`,
  `husbands love your wives`; #2 on `being a good husband`.
- G4: `marriage-in-crisis` ships a `concepts:` row (skipped-only — no bare
  word, no collapse); zero shared normalized phrases with any pack; tightest

**Effort.** M. One new pack (**eleven** anchors — r4 adds Matt 18:15 @0.55,
the first *concrete step* in a pack that anchored four texts about

### A2.4 NEW infidelity-and-temptation (the resisting register only)

**Measured gap.** `tempted to cheat on my wife` → `{tempt, cheat, wife}` is a
superset of `wife cheated` → `{cheat, wife}`, so today the whole
comfort-for-the-wounded set fires — including 1 Cor 7:15 — for someone who
has not sinned. No pack answers the not-yet-fallen, actively-resisting
register at all.

**Change.**

# no row FAILS G4 `row-missing`, regardless of whether it has bare words):
  - id: infidelity-and-temptation
    # A2.4 (r2): every entry keeps >= 2 significant tokens; no bare word

    skipped:

**One entry does not go in this pack (r4, M-5).** `how do i stop lusting` →
`{stop, lust}` reached nothing curated: the served page was Jas 1:14
(*"drawn away by his own lust"*), 1 Cor 10:6, Gal 5:24 — diagnosis without
help. The critique named **this** pack as its home. That is rejected, on
register and measured: the query carries no marriage marker, and this pack is
the *married* tempted party's, so answering a single person's purity question
with Prov 5:15-20 (*"rejoice in the wife of your youth"*) and Heb 13:4 is the
same register error this item exists to fix, one row down. `sexual-purity`
already owns `struggling with lust` → `{struggl, lust}`; the missing form is
the stop-verb one, and it goes there:

```yaml apply=ops
#@ lexicon-add ontology/concepts/pastoral-sexual-purity.yaml
# r4 (M-5). One entry only: "how do i stop lusting", "how to stop lusting"
# and "stop lusting" all normalize to the same {stop, lust}, so a second row
# would be a duplicate span the compile rejects. Neither {stop, lust} nor
# sexual-purity's existing {struggl, lust} is a subset of the other, so the
# two entries do not collide; and `stop` != `stopp`, so this cannot fire
# from "i stopped going to church".
  - stop lusting     # {stop, lust}
```

**Tokenizer hazards.** All nine entries ≥ 2 tokens; none collapses. Live
reachability of every fixture query, and the two the tokenizer forbids:

```text apply=none
"tempted to cheat on my wife" -> {tempt, cheat, wife}
      infidelity-and-temptation PARITY | betrayal-and-marriage-crisis 2/3 ("wife cheated")
      | remembered-a-way-of-escape 1/3 (bare `tempted`)
"im tempted to cheat"         -> {tempt, cheat}          infidelity PARITY
"emotional affair"            -> {emotional, affair}     infidelity PARITY
"struggling not to cheat"     -> {struggl, cheat}        infidelity PARITY
"attracted to someone who isnt my spouse" -> {attract, someone, isnt, spouse}  infidelity PARITY
"i cheated on my wife"        -> {cheat, wife}           ONLY betrayal-and-marriage-crisis (PARITY)
"i had an affair"             -> {affair}                fires NOTHING
```

**The two structural limits, stated rather than patched.**
1. `i cheated on my wife` is token-identical to `my wife cheated on me`. No
   entry of this pack can reach it without also firing for the wounded
   spouse, so it is **not** an `additionalQuery` here (r1 asserted it, and
   `runNormalisedFixture` runs every additionalQuery against the same
   `expectedTop`, so that assertion could only fail). It is filed as a
   `pending` fixture below.
2. The obvious confession phrasings collide head-on:
   `i was unfaithful to my wife` → `{unfaithful, wife}` is the **same token
   set** as this pack's neighbour entry `unfaithful wife`
   (betrayal-and-marriage-crisis), and `i had an affair` → `{affair}` sits
   inside that pack's `my wife had an affair`. Both were tested and dropped.
   The confessing register is served instead by `i committed adultery`
   → `{committ, adultery}`, routed to `forgiveness-of-sins` in **A2.4b** —
   which is also the theologically right home: the answer to a confession is
   1 John 1:9 and Psalm 51, not a resisting-temptation pack whose reason chip
   would read "Theme: Resisting infidelity".

**Anchors.** WEB-verified. The grace half leads, per M1 — as r1 stood, the
highest-weighted thing a resisting husband was told is that his lust, full
grown, produces death.

### A2.4b Extend forgiveness-of-sins (the confessing spouse)

**Measured gap.** The spouse who *did* it has no register at all. The phrasings
that name it collide with the wounded spouse's own vocabulary (A2.4), with one
exception the tokenizer allows: `i committed adultery` → `{committ, adultery}`,
which today fires **nothing**.

**Change.**
```yaml apply=ops

  - i committed adultery      # {committ, adultery} — fires this pack alone (measured)
#@ anchor-respan ontology/concepts/forgiveness-of-sins.yaml Psalms 51:3-4 => Psalms 51:1-4
# EDIT the EXISTING anchor — widen the span, do NOT add a second row (r3, B12).
# Weight stays 0.8. Amend its comment:

#   # carried 51:3-4 ("For I know my transgressions"); widening to v1 puts the
#   # plea for mercy — and the psalm's own superscription, "when Nathan the
#   # prophet came to him, after he had gone in to Bathsheba" — at the head of
#   # what the confessing spouse reads. Weight UNCHANGED at 0.8, deliberately:
#   # see the arithmetic below.
```

**Why a widened span and not a new anchor (r3, B12).** r2 wrote *"ADD to
anchors: Psalms 51:1-4 @0.9"* and never mentioned that `forgiveness-of-sins`
**already anchors Psalms 51:3-4 @0.8**. `compileOntology` errors only on
*identical* ranges, so an overlapping-but-different span in the same pack
compiles clean — and then, at query time, the wider span wins the pericope
group and the existing row **disappears from the result set entirely**.
Measured consequence on the existing suite: Ps 51:1-4 entered
`guilt-and-condemnation.json` at #4 for `guilt` and #5 for `guilty`, pushing
**Romans 8:1 out of that fixture's asserted top 5**. Two expectations, broken
silently, in a pack this item was not looking at.

The arithmetic that decides the weight:

| weight | `i committed adultery` (2-token parity, ×40) | `guilt` (1-token, ×0.55×40 + 1.64 related) | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.9 (r2) | 36.00 → **#5** | 21.44 → **#4**, Rom 8:1 → #6 | **breaks `guilt-and-condemnation`** |
| 0.85 | 34.00 → #5 | 20.34 → #4, Rom 8:1 → #6 | breaks it |
| **0.8 (r3, unchanged)** | **32.00 → #7** | **19.24 → #6, Rom 8:1 stays #5** | **holds** |
| >0.95 (needed for top 3 here) | 38.00+ → #3 | 22.54+ | breaks it worse |

A top-3 assertion for Ps 51 on `i committed adultery` therefore **cannot be
had** without breaking a reviewed existing fixture. r2 asserted top 3 without
the arithmetic; r3 asserts **`withinTop: 10` and measures #7**, and keeps the
weight where the reviewer left it. That is the whole of B3 and B12.

**Tokenizer hazards.** Two tokens, no collapse, no inventory row due. Measured
against every lexicon in the ontology: `{committ, adultery}` fires this pack
and nothing else. Note that `adultery` is *not* admitted bare — the wounded

**Tokenizer hazards.** Live reachability of every fixture query, with the
co-fire that matters printed rather than assumed:

```text apply=none
"my parents are getting divorced" -> {parent, gett, divorc}
        children-of-divorce PARITY | parenting 1/3 (bare `parenting`)
"my parents are divorcing"        -> {parent, divorc}      children-of-divorce PARITY | parenting 1/2
"my parents got divorced"         -> {parent, got, divorc} children-of-divorce PARITY | parenting 1/3
"children of divorce"             -> {children, divorce}   children-of-divorce PARITY (nothing else)
"child of divorce"                -> {child, divorce}      children-of-divorce PARITY (nothing else)
"growing up with divorced parents"-> {grow, divorc, parent} children-of-divorce PARITY | parenting 1/3
"my parents fight all the time"   -> {parent, fight, time}  children-of-divorce PARITY | parenting 1/3
```

`children` ≠ `child` under this tokenizer, so both entries are required (the
`loneliness`/`lonely` pattern). "getting" stems to `gett`, distinct from
`got`, so both surface forms are carried.

**The `parent` co-fire is the flagship harm, and r3 measures it and fixes it
with anchors rather than with an assertion.** Five of the seven queries carry
`{parent}`, so `parenting` co-fires as a bare cue on every one. r2 wrote the
guard and asserted it held; the real gate failed it on all four `parent`
queries:

```text apply=none

   10. Ephesians 6:4       12.98  Theme: Raising children
```

A twelve-year-old typing that her parents are divorcing was handed *"Children,
obey your parents in all things"* at position 8. `mustNotRank` does not demote
anything; the pack's own seven anchors simply stopped at #7 and `parenting`
took the rest of the page.

The question is right and r1 was rightly failed for ignoring it; the
instrument was wrong. Ezek 18:19-20 is worse (it adds *"Why doesn't the son

principle by inference. The alternative — restoring a verse whose first seven
words are "The soul who sins, he shall die" to a frightened child's first
screen — is worse. J-A2-4 is restated below without the false fact in its
favour.

    # HERE, with both chapters' tokens — S-A1 §A1.0a states its two additions
    # in prose and prints no listing, because the row is edited once, in one
    # merge.
    admitted: [suicide, suicidal, depression, depressed, cutting, kill, giving, numb]
```

**Coordination with S-A1.** S-A1 edits this pack and this inventory row in the
same phase (its own admissions, and the `giving up` / `feel like giving up`
phrasings that A2.14 hands over). The row is edited once, in one merge, with
both sets of tokens — not twice, and the printed listing above **is** that one
row (D1): `[suicide, suicidal, depression, depressed, cutting, kill, giving,
numb]`. S-A1 §A1.0a prints no competing listing.

**Tokenizer hazards.** Three ≥2-token entries plus one bare; all four queries
fire this pack at PARITY and nothing else (measured — `do-not-lose-heart`
does **not** fire on `feel numb`, so the Ps 42:5 label contest between the two
packs does not arise for these queries). Bare `numb` measured non-colliding.

**Anchors (M20).** r1's justification was that Ps 42:5 "already speaks to the
flattened, can't-feel-anything experience". It does not: WEB Ps 42:5 is *"Why
are you in despair, my soul? Why are you disturbed within me?"* — a soul in
turmoil arguing with itself, which is the opposite phenomenology to
numbness. Adding lexicon that reaches an anchor which does not answer the
query is the NO MEASURABLE EFFECT shape. So the register gets its own text:

| ref | WEB (verbatim fragment) | weight | why | sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lamentations 3:17-18 | "You have removed my soul far away from peace. I forgot prosperity. I said, 'My strength has perished, along with my expectation from the LORD.'" | 0.3 | The canon's own flat, expectation-gone voice — validation that this prayer is IN the Bible, which is exactly what Psalm 88 does for the crisis register. Owned by no other pack. Weighted below every comfort anchor so it never leads. | editorial |

**Psalm 88 stays at 0.35.** Raising it was considered and rejected: the weight
is a reviewed decision of a Jesse-approved pack (2026-07-31) whose recorded
reasoning is that Ps 88's value is validation and that its weight "keeps it
from ever leading". Re-weighting a reviewed pastoral anchor is a review act,
not a side effect of a lexicon extension — raised as a ruling instead.

**Guards.** The pack's existing crisis guard family
(`pastoral-despair-give-up.json`'s `mustNotRank` set: Matt 27:5, 1 Sam 31:4-5,
Judg 16:30, 1 Kgs 16:18, 2 Sam 17:23, Ps 116:15, Mark 6:25, Phil 1:21-23)
already applies to this pack's queries and is inherited; the numbness fixture
adds **2 Samuel 17:23** explicitly so this file also fails if the floor moves.

**Rulings for Jesse.** (a) Psalm 88's 0.35 weight for the numbness register:

`hope-in-despair`'s existing Lam 3:21-23 (0.85) — two spans of one chapter,

**Existing fixtures re-run.** `pastoral-despair-no-reason.json`,

### A2.11 NEW provision-in-hardship (job loss, rent, bills)

**Measured gap.** `i lost my job` → `{lost, job}` reaches only
`remembered-work-as-for-the-lord` through its bare `job` cue: Col 3:23,
*"whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord"* — a work-ethic verse
served to a person who has just lost the work.
`im afraid we wont be able to pay rent` → `{afraid, wont, able, pay, rent}`
reaches nothing curated and surfaces Exod 10:5, a locust-plague verse.

**Why a new pack and not `gods-provision` (B5, the §3 breach).**
`gods-provision.yaml`'s header states its design in terms:

> its id, label and lexicon speak NO materialFrameKeyword (deliberately —
> "money"/"finances"/"wealth" live in the separate `contentment` concept,
> which anchors no watchlist verse; **the split is what keeps watchlisted refs
> and material-frame vocabulary from ever co-occurring in one concept**…

and that pack anchors **Philippians 4:19 at 0.95** — a
`flagged-pairings.yaml` watchlist reference whose recorded concern is
recruitment "as an unconditional wealth guarantee". r1 put `im broke`,
`cant pay rent`, `unemployed` and `lost my job` into that pack and then listed
Phil 4:19 as acceptable output. Served at 0.95 to a query that is literally
"I can't pay rent", that is the §3 recruitment the watchlist names.

r2 takes the option `gods-provision`'s own header points to: **a separate
pack**, `provision-in-hardship`, that anchors **no watchlist reference at
all**. `gods-provision` is untouched — its lexicon, its anchors and its Phil
4:19 framing all stay exactly as reviewed. Material-frame vocabulary
(`money`, `finances`, `wealth`, `debt`) stays with `contentment`, which
admits those bare words already and anchors no watchlist verse; this pack
takes only the *situation* words (job, rent, bills, unemployed). Measured consequence: **Phil 4:19 is absent from the top 50 of every one of
the eleven money queries.** The reason r2 gave for that — *"no curated path"* —
was wrong, and m-3 was right to say so. A path exists: Phil 4:19 is a
`gods-provision` anchor at 0.95 and this pack declares
`related: gods-provision`, so `relatedConceptEvidence` would carry it at
0.95 × 0.5 × 12 = 5.70 points. What keeps it out of the window is that it
shares pericope 50004010–50004020 with **Phil 4:11-13**, which this pack
anchors at 0.75 and which therefore wins the group. The conclusion holds; the
stated reason did not, and a future pericope change would have silently
invalidated it. It is now stated as what it is: a **grouping** effect, not an
absence of route, and that is why the fixture records the measurement instead
of writing a guard.

**Change.**
```yaml apply=ops

header describes — or the section stops calling them watchlist refs and keeps
them as fixture-local doctrine-negative guards. m-8 asked this about 2 Sam
5:20 alone; it is the same question five times.

**Tokenizer hazards.** Live reachability of every fixture query:

```text apply=none
"im going into surgery tomorrow" -> {going, surgery, tomorrow}  2/3 via "going into surgery"
"surgery"                        -> {surgery}         PARITY
"waiting for a diagnosis"        -> {wait, diagnosi}  PARITY
"terminal diagnosis"             -> {terminal, diagnosi} PARITY
"chronic pain"                   -> {chronic, pain}   PARITY
"test results"                   -> {test, result}    PARITY, and NOTHING else
"afraid of dying"                -> {afraid, dying}   PARITY | fear-not 1/2 (bare `afraid`)
"fear of death"                  -> {fear, death}     PARITY | fear-not 1/2 (bare `fear`)
"im scared of dying"             -> {scar, dying}     fires NOTHING  <-- disclosed residual
```

- `diagnosed` → `{diagnos}` and `diagnosis` → `{diagnosi}` land on different
  stems (a noun/participle spelling accident), so both surface forms are
  required and both are admitted **as surface words**.
- **`test results` → `{test, result}`, analysed (m3/m-7, still owed after r2).**
  It is the thinnest pair this item admits, and the analysis is: `test` is a
  real WEB word (Deut 6:16 "You shall not test the LORD", Ps 26:2 "Examine me,
  LORD, and prove me", Mal 3:10 "test me now in this", Jas 1:3 "the testing of
  your faith"), and `result` is not — it appears in no WEB verse in the corpus
  (verified), so the pair can only match a verse carrying **`test`** plus the
  pack's own phrase. Measured: `test results` fires
  `serious-illness-and-dying` at parity and **nothing else**, and the served
  page is this pack's own anchor set — Ps 23:4 #2, Heb 2:14-15 #7 — with no
  `test`-bearing verse in the top 25. The risk the pair carries is not a
  collision but a *future* one: if any pack ever admits bare `test`, this
  entry becomes a 1-of-2 co-fire on a medical query. Recorded in the inventory
  row's `skipped:` block so a future admission meets the objection.
- `test results` → `{test, result}` was checked against all six existing
  `test` entries across `testing` and `false-prophets` (m3): none is a subset
  of `{test, result}`, so nothing else fires. Verified mechanically, not
  assumed.
- **Never write "scared"**: `scared` → `scar`, the WEB text of Lev 13:23's
  "scar from the boil".
- `im scared of dying` is therefore **removed from the fixture** (B4). r1
  asserted it while the item's own hazard note forbade the only word that
  could reach it, and `runNormalisedFixture` runs every additionalQuery
  against the same `expectedTop` — the assertion could only fail. The query
  is a disclosed residual pending the `dying` ruling.

### A2.14 Extend do-not-lose-heart (discouragement + "breakthrough")

**Measured gap.** "Breakthrough" is confirmed 0 anywhere — the word appears
only in exclusion comments in `blessing`/`generosity`/`providence`/
`tithing.yaml`, deliberately out of scope as a `materialFrameKeyword`. And
`i keep failing` → `{keep, fail}` reaches only `relapse-and-restoration`'s
bare `fail` cue.

**What r1 put here and r2 routes elsewhere.** Three registers were dropped
into this pack because their words had no owner. Each has a right owner, and
two of them already had a *recorded decision* r1 contradicted without naming
it:

| r1 entry | token | r2 routing | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `i failed` | `fail` | **relapse-and-restoration** (already owns it) | `lexicon-inventory.yaml` records `relapse-and-restoration: admitted: [relapse, relapsed, failed]` with the reason *"'I failed' is the pastoral query this pack exists for"*, and the collapses table carries a J12 flag on the same token. Bare `fail` fires exactly one pack today; a second claim would hand a person who failed an exam the sobriety anchor set — and would edit a recorded ruling silently (B8). |
| `messed up` | `mess` | **relapse-and-restoration** (A2.14b) | "I messed up" is a moral-failure confession, not discouragement; Gal 6:9 ("don't be weary in doing good") is the wrong answer to it. The pack whose whole question is "am I finished?" is the right one (M7). |
| `im a failure` | `failure` | **shame** (A2.14b) | An identity claim, not a perseverance one. `shame` anchors Isa 54:4 / Ps 34:5 / Isa 61:7 (M7). |
| `giving up`, `feel like giving up` | `giving`, `{feel, like, giving}` | **hope-in-despair — S-A1 owns it** | `giving` and `give` are different tokens, so these phrasings bypass the documented "want to give up" share and the whole `pastoral-despair-give-up.json` guard family (Matt 27:5, 1 Sam 31:4-5, Judg 16:30, 1 Kgs 16:18, Phil 1:21-23, Ps 116:15, Mark 6:25, 2 Sam 17:23). A person one step from suicide who types the progressive form would have got Gal 6:9 and no crisis floor (B9). S-A1's `hope-in-despair` item takes both phrasings, with the collapses row for `giving up` and the crisis guard list; **this section does not add them here**, and the mirror question — whether do-not-lose-heart should also take them, as it does "want to give up" — is raised there as a ruling so both packs are decided in one commit. |

`{keep, fail}`, `need a breakthrough` → `{need, breakthrough}`,
`waiting for my breakthrough` → `{wait, breakthrough}`,
`spiritual breakthrough` → `{spiritual, breakthrough}`; `breakthrough` is a
deliberate single-word entry with an admitted row. Live:

"need a breakthrough"         -> {need, breakthrough}    PARITY
"waiting for my breakthrough" -> {wait, breakthrough}    PARITY
"spiritual breakthrough"      -> {spiritual, breakthrough} PARITY
"i keep failing"              -> {keep, fail}            PARITY | relapse-and-restoration 1/2 (bare `fail`)
```

**Cross-concept anchor stacking — why r3 does not re-anchor Micah 7:8 or
Phil 1:6 (B8).** r2 added both to `do-not-lose-heart` without checking that
`relapse-and-restoration` already anchors them (Micah 7:8 @1.0, Phil 1:6
@0.85), and `i keep failing` fires **both** packs. `dedupeConceptAnchors`
merges duplicate rows only *within* one concept; across concepts the points
sum, deliberately — two matched concepts naming one verse are two different
claims. Measured, r2's own asserted lead lost to its own addition:

Read, not scanned. Three things leave a served page and each is a different
case. **2 Cor 12:9-10 is fixed, not lost**: r3's anchors displaced *"my grace
is sufficient for you"* to #13, and this round anchors it at 0.5 in the pack
itself, which returns it to #10 with its own reason chip on all three queries
— it now arrives as this pack's claim rather than as a neighbour's 6.00-point
chip. **1 Cor 10:13 leaving `tempted to give up` at #12 is accepted**: the
way-of-escape text belongs to `remembered-a-way-of-escape` and to
`temptation`, both of which the query reaches directly, and what replaces it
is Hab 3:17-19 — the "and if he does not" the breakthrough register needs.

**1 Kings 19:4-6 → #14 on `discouraged` is a real loss and is stated as one.**
The broom-tree narrative — Elijah says *"It is enough. Now, O Yahweh, take
away my life"*, and God's answer is an angel, food and sleep — is arguably the
best single answer in the canon to a bare `discouraged`. It was at #10 on a
5.70-point `hope-in-despair` related chip, i.e. it held the last slot only
because this pack had nothing of its own to put there. **The remedy was tried
and measured and does not work:** anchoring 1 Kgs 19:4-6 here at 0.6 returns
it to #4 on `discouraged` **and breaks a shipped fixture** —
`hope-in-despair` anchors the wider span 1 Kings 19:4-7, the two group into
one pericope run, and on `want to give up` the grouped result scores
38.00 + 24.00 = 62.00 and pushes Gal 6:9 from #3 to #4, failing
`do-not-lose-heart-give-up-phrasings`' `withinTop: 3`. There is no weight
that both restores the `discouraged` page and stays under Gal 6:9's 40.00
there (it would have to be below 0.05). So the trade is: **Elijah under the
broom tree leaves `discouraged`'s first page, and keeps #2–#4 on the
give-up/despair register where it is anchored and where the query is closest
to what the narrative is about.** That is the intended trade, and it is the
one thing in this item a reviewer should push back on if they disagree.

**Acceptance (measured).** All five queries put **Gal 6:9 at #2** and
**Hab 3:17-19 at #3** with this pack's label. Twelve of the thirteen guarded
references are absent from the top 50 on all five; Phil 4:19 is at #42 on one.
G4 green: one bare admission verified to fire, three recorded skips, zero
collapses, zero shared phrases, and the pairing scan runs **in scope** and
returns zero.

**Effort.** M. One bare admission, **four** anchors (Hab 3:17-19,
Ps 37:23-24, Isa 43:18-19, 2 Cor 12:9-10 — r3 said five, counting from the
corrupt block B-4 names; a fifth, 1 Kgs 19:4-6, was tried in r4 and withdrawn
because it breaks a shipped fixture), one anchor refused, one

different ≤3 leads for one string is a contradiction the gate would only

**Tokenizer hazards.** Numerals under three characters are structurally
unreachable ("40"/"50"/"60" drop below the length floor, collapsing
"turning 40" to bare `{turn}`), so every entry spells the number out.
`empty nest` → `{empty, nest}`; `retirement` → `{retirement}`, bare and
measured non-colliding. All five queries fire this pack at PARITY and nothing
else.

**Anchors (M12).** r1 added none, on the reasoning that "Eccl 3:1-8 already
answers every one of these life-stage queries". One eight-verse merism saying
everything has a season is a true frame and the *only* thing that set could
say to five distinct registers — retirement is a vocation-and-identity
transition, empty nest is a loss, turning sixty is mortality. Low risk is not
the bar; whether a wise theologian would recognise the answer is. All three
additions were read in WEB:

|---|---|---|---|---|

Measured on the composed build, neither is reachable from this fixture's queries: `retirement` gives Ps 90:12 #1 (24.10 — `Theme: Seasons of life` 18.70 + `Related theme: Mortality` 5.40) and `turning forty` gives it #2 (39.40), with one `concept_anchor` reason both times. No pin rests on sole ownership. | editorial |
| Psalms 71:17-18 | "Yes, even when I am old and gray-haired, God, don't forsake me, until I have declared your strength to the next generation" | 0.8 | Retirement and empty nest in one voice: what am I *for* now the role has ended — answered with a purpose that outlives the role. DUAL with `aging-and-old-age` (0.85). | editorial |
| Psalms 92:12-14 | "They will still produce fruit in old age. They will be full of sap and green" | 0.7 | Fruitfulness after the working years, said of the righteous planted in God's house. DUAL with `aging-and-old-age` (1.0). | editorial |

**Guard deleted (r3, measured — m6).** r2 put a `mustNotRank` on **Jonah 3:4**
(*"In forty days, Nineveh will be overthrown!"*) on the reasoning that `forty`
saturates the WEB narrative and `turning forty` → `{turn, forty}` reaches it
lexically, so an overthrow oracle could land on a birthday query. m6 objected
that "in corpus, so non-vacuous" is the wrong test, and m6 is right: presence
in the corpus is what `guardVacuityFindings` checks, not what makes a guard
mean anything. The real question is whether there is a **route**, and the
measurement says there is not — Jonah 3:4 is **absent from the top 50 on all
five queries**.

The reason is arithmetic rather than luck, which is why the deletion is safe
to make. `turning forty` reaches `seasons-of-life` at parity, so its four
anchors take 40.00, 34.00, 32.00 and 28.00 points. Jonah 3:4 has no concept
anchor on any of these queries; its only route is `token_overlap`, capped at
**10 points** (A2.0c) and further squeezed by the weak-aggregate cap. A weak
family cannot climb past a parity anchor set, so the guard was never capable
of firing. Under A2.0d it is *decoration* — not doctrine-negative, not a
crisis floor — and is deleted with the measurement recorded in the fixture's
`note`. m6's concern is answered by the number, not by a guard that stands as
reassurance.

neighbourhood) and `caring-for-aging-parents.json` were re-run on the

| query | Eccl 3:1-8 (≤3) | Ps 90:12 (≤10) | Jonah 3:4 |
|---|---|---|---|

Ps 90:12 leading `retirement` is worth saying out loud rather than smoothing
over, because it is the A2.0c mechanism firing exactly as documented.
`retirement` is a **one-token** query, so every anchor is scaled by
`conceptSpecificity(1) = 0.55`: Eccl 3:1-8 at weight 1.0 scores
`1.0 × 0.55 × 40 = 22.00`, Ps 90:12 at 0.85 scores 18.70. But `seasons-of-life`
carries a `related:` edge to `mortality`, and a related edge is
**width-independent** — it does not shrink on a one-token query. Ps 90:12 is
also a `mortality` anchor, so it collects `concept_lexicon: Related theme:
Mortality = 5.40` on top of its 18.70, for **24.10**, and leads. Eccl 3:1-8 is
not a mortality anchor and gets nothing.

This is not a defect to be weighted away. "Teach us to count our days" leading
a retirement query is the right answer; the merism at #2 is the frame behind
it. What matters for the plan's honesty is that the fixture asserts what the
arithmetic produces — Eccl 3:1-8 `withinTop: 3` (measured #2), not the #1 that
r1 asserted and the arithmetic never supported. G4 green given the row edit.

**Effort.** S. One bare admission, three new anchors, no guard.

### A2.19 NEW sleep-at-night

**Measured gap.** No pack owns "can't sleep" or "insomnia", though
`rest-for-the-weary` already anchors Ps 127:2 — a sleep verse lexically
unreachable from this vocabulary.

**Change.**
```yaml apply=ops
#@ new-file ontology/concepts/sleep-at-night.yaml
id: sleep-at-night
label: Sleep and rest at night
lexicon:

  - tossing and turning # {toss, turn}

  # {lying, awake, night} and carries `honesty`'s bare `lying` cue —
  # measured — so an insomniac would meet "Lying lips are an abomination".
anchors:
  - ref: Psalms 4:8
    sources: [editorial]
    weight: 1.0
  - ref: Psalms 127:2
    sources: [editorial]
    weight: 0.9
  - ref: Proverbs 3:24
    sources: [editorial]
    weight: 0.85
  - ref: Psalms 121:3-4
    sources: [editorial]
    weight: 0.75
  - ref: Psalms 3:5
    sources: [editorial]
    weight: 0.7
  - ref: Psalms 63:6
    sources: [editorial]
    weight: 0.6
  # r3 ADDS four (see "Why four more anchors and one fewer edge"):
  - ref: Psalms 130:5-6
    sources: [editorial]
    weight: 0.55
  - ref: Psalms 16:7-8
    sources: [editorial]
    weight: 0.5
  - ref: Psalms 42:8
    sources: [editorial]
    weight: 0.45
  - ref: Psalms 30:5
    sources: [editorial]
    weight: 0.4
related:
  # - rest-for-the-weary   REMOVED (r3, measured) — see below
  - fear-not
  - peace-of-god
#@ inventory-concept sleep-at-night
# ontology/lexicon-inventory.yaml, concepts: section — ADD:
  - id: sleep-at-night
    # A2.19 (r2). Both bare triggers verified to normalize to the token they
    # fire (insomnia -> insomnia; nightmares -> nightmar). `nightmares` is
    # admitted rather than left undecided: a firing bare token with no
    # admitted entry is a `firing-token-undecided` line in the Admission
    # Report — behaviour without a recorded decision (M15).
    admitted: [insomnia, nightmares]
    skipped:
      - token: sleep
        reason: >-
          Generic across the canon (the sleep of death, the disciples
          sleeping in Gethsemane, "he gives sleep to his loved ones"); the
          cant/awake/tossing pairings carry the modern complaint.
      - token: night
        reason: >-
          Saturates the WEB narrative; the paired forms carry it.
```

**Tokenizer hazards.** `cant sleep` → `{cant, sleep}`;
`tossing and turning` → `{toss, turn}` ("and" is a stopword);
`awake at night` → `{awake, night}` ("at" is a stopword). Two bare entries,
both measured non-colliding. `nightmares` → `{nightmar}` is one word as typed,
not a collapse, so it needs an **admitted** row and no collapses row. All five
queries fire this pack at PARITY and nothing else — including
`awake at night`, whose r1 wording did not.

**Anchors.** WEB-verified:

| ref | WEB (verbatim fragment) | weight | why | sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Psalms 4:8 | "In peace I will both lay myself down and sleep, for you alone, LORD, make me live in safety." | 1.0 | The definitive sleep-as-trust psalm. Owned by no other pack — the label pin. | GotQuestions.org |
| Psalms 127:2 | "for he gives sleep to his loved ones" | 0.9 | Answers anxious striving with sleep as gift. DUAL with `rest-for-the-weary` (0.6). | Desiring God |
| Proverbs 3:24 | "When you lie down, you will not be afraid. Yes, you will lie down, and your sleep will be sweet." | 0.85 | Directly answers fear-driven lying awake. | OpenBible.info |
| Psalms 121:3-4 | "he who keeps Israel will neither slumber nor sleep" | 0.75 | God's own sleeplessness on the sleeper's behalf. Verse-scoped inside Ps 121; A2.12 anchors 121:1-2 for a different claim — the two spans are disjoint by design. | GotQuestions.org |
| Psalms 3:5 | "I laid myself down and slept. I awakened, for the LORD sustains me." | 0.7 | Sleep as evidence of trust under real threat. | Crosswalk.com |
| Psalms 63:6 | "when I remember you on my bed, and think about you in the night watches" | 0.6 | Redirects lying awake toward remembering God. | OpenBible.info |

**Why four more anchors and one fewer edge (r3, measured).** r2's pack failed
two things on the simulated artifact, and both failures had the same cause: a
six-anchor pack with a `related:` edge to a pack that shares one of its
anchors.

*Failure 1 — Ps 127:2 outranked Ps 4:8 on `insomnia`, breaking `withinTop: 1`.*
`insomnia` is a **one-token** query, so every anchor is scaled by
`conceptSpecificity(1) = 0.55`: Ps 4:8 at weight 1.0 scored 22.00 and
Ps 127:2 at 0.9 scored 19.80. But Ps 127:2 is also a `rest-for-the-weary`
anchor at 0.6, and a related edge is **width-independent** (A2.0c) — it does
not take the 0.55 discount. So Ps 127:2 collected a flat
`0.6 × 0.5 × 12 = 3.60` on top, for **23.40**, and led. The pack's own defining
verse lost its own register to a chip from a neighbouring pack, and it lost it
only on the short queries, which are the ones people actually type.

*Failure 2 — Job 7:4 measured #7 on `tossing and turning`, inside the window.*
Six anchors do not fill a ten-result page, so positions 7-10 were filled by
whatever weak evidence existed, and the strongest weak candidate for
"tossing and turning" is the verse that says those words.

Both are fixed by design rather than by relaxing the assertions. The
`rest-for-the-weary` edge is **dropped**: it existed to say "rest and sleep are
adjacent", which is true and which the pack did not need, and the only thing it
measurably delivered was demoting Ps 4:8. Ps 127:2 keeps its own 0.9 anchor
here and its 0.6 anchor there — the dual is untouched; only the edge goes. And
four anchors are added, each of them a night text in its own right rather than
padding:

| ref | WEB (verbatim fragment) | weight | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Psalms 130:5-6 | "My soul longs for the Lord more than watchmen long for the morning" | 0.55 | The exact experience of the sleepless hours, named without despair — waiting for morning as an act of hope. |
| Psalms 16:7-8 | "Yes, my heart instructs me in the night seasons." | 0.5 | The night as a place where God still speaks, rather than only a place of absence. |
| Psalms 42:8 | "in the night his song shall be with me: a prayer to the God of my life" | 0.45 | A song in the night, from the psalm whose refrain is "why are you in despair, my soul?" |
| Psalms 30:5 | "Weeping may stay for the night, but joy comes in the morning." | 0.4 | The morning-is-coming word, kept low so it never leads and never sounds like dismissal. |

After both changes: Ps 4:8 measures **#1 on all five queries**, and Job 7:4
falls from #7 to **#11** on `tossing and turning` — outside the measured window
of 10, absent from the top 50 on the other four.

**Guards.** Psalm 91:5 ("terror by night") considered and **not** anchored —
same caution as A2.12's Ps 91/Ps 121 reasoning; it stays `refuge-in-trouble`'s.
`mustNotRank`: **Job 7:4** — *"When I lie down, I say, 'When will I arise, and
the night be gone?' I toss and turn until the dawning of the day"* — the
literal tossing-and-turning verse in the WEB, and it is Job at his most
despairing (eleven verses later: *"my soul chooses strangling, death rather
than my bones"*, Job 7:15). It matches this register's exact words and must not
be served as the answer to insomnia.

This is a **measured** guard under A2.0d, not a decoration one: it has a
demonstrated route (`proximity` 5.70 + `token_overlap` on `toss, turn` 3.64 =
9.34 points), and it measures at **#11** — just outside the window it protects.
It is kept, with that position recorded in the fixture, precisely because it is
close. The four r3 anchors are what put it outside; if a future change removes
one of them the guard fires, which is the guard working.

**Fixture.**
```json apply=fixture

In r2 it measured #7, inside the window; the fix was a design change, not a wider window: sleep-at-night dropped its related edge to rest-for-the-weary and gained four anchors (Ps 130:5-6, Ps 16:7-8, Ps 42:8, Ps 30:5), which fill the ten with the register's own texts.",

## Consolidated regression list (M17) — measured, not predicted

r2 answered M17 with a list of fixtures a reviewer *ought to* re-run. That is
a reading list, not a regression pass. r3 compiled this section's whole
proposed ontology through the real importer
(`pipeline/src/importers/ontologyImporter.ts`), applied the diff to a copy of
the fixture corpus, rebuilt the spelling index, and re-ran **all 549 fixture files in
`eval/golden/`** through the real gate (`eval/src/gates/corpusGolden.ts`),
which classifies 546 of them as corpus fixtures (532 active + 14 pending) and
routes the remaining three — the `ranking-invariants` and reference-grammar
files, which carry `queries` rather than a single `query` — through their own
checks. What follows is the measurement.

**Result: zero breaks, 47 moves.** (r3 measured 55; r4's withdrawals —
1 Cor 15:54-57 under B-9, Lam 3:17-18 from 0.55 to 0.30 under M-2 — took eight
fixtures back to baseline.)

**Three rows in this table are read rather than scanned (r4).** The r3
critique's method was right and its instrument was better than r3's own: a
table that records where a verse *left from* and not where it *went* cannot
show a pastoral regression. Every row below now carries destinations, and the
three that need prose have it.

1 Cor 15:54-57 at 0.85 in `serious-illness-and-dying`. The measured effect was
that *"Death is swallowed up in victory. Death, where is your sting?"* took
**#1 from Psalms 34:18** on `death of a loved one` — the most sensitive query
in the product — and the change was recorded as one line in a 55-row table.

("whether Psalms 34:18 SHOULD lead a grief query is flagged for Jesse's PR-2

**(3) `prosperity-breakthrough` — the whole page is new** and is read in
