**The 47 fixtures whose top ten changed are printed in the appendix, with
destinations (r4).** r3 kept a hand-written copy of this table here and the
generated one in the appendix; they are the same data typed twice, which is
the drift class this round exists to eliminate. The table now lives in exactly
one place — **"The 47 fixture files whose top ten changes, with destinations"**
in the appendix — and it is emitted by the harness from the build this document
generates. Read `in:` as "entered the top ten, from this position at 50" and
`out:` as "left the top ten, to this position at 50"; a `reorder:` row means
the same ten verses in a different order. Three rows are read in prose above:
`pastoral-grief` (reverted), `pastoral-abuse-hitting` (one place, argued) and
`prosperity-breakthrough` (whole page new).

**One invariant, its limits, and three patterns.**

The invariant, recomputed on the r4 build across all **118** individual
displacements: setting aside the span swaps — where the displaced reference is
the *same passage at a narrower span* and the wider span enters at the
**identical** position — **every verse that leaves a top ten leaves from
position 7 or lower**. 91 of the 118 leave from #9 or #10 and 103 from #8 or
lower; exactly two leave from #7 — `gods-surprising-choice`'s Deut 16:7 (→#13)
and `pastoral-god-sees`'s 1 Pet 4:12-16 (→#11) — both displaced by anchors
this section adds to packs those queries already reach. Every displacement
above #7 is a span swap (Ps 51:3-4 → Ps 51:1-4, Eph 5:22-24 → Eph 5:21-24),
where the wider span enters at the exact position the narrower one left and no
ranking changed at all. Nothing this section adds displaces a verse from the
top six of a shipped fixture.

**And the r3 critique was right that this is the wrong measurement, so it is
no longer the only one.** Three of the four pastoral regressions it found were
a *reorder* or an *entry*, not a displacement, and the fourth changed a **#1** —
none of which an exit-position invariant can see. Four rows of this diff are
reorders with no entry or exit at all. So the table now carries destinations,
three rows are read in prose, and the section's real safety argument is not
the invariant but the three instruments together: the gate for the assertions,
the diff for the neighbours, and the untested-form harm search for the queries
nobody has written down.

`prosperity-breakthrough.json` is the one row that needs reading rather than
scanning. Its whole top ten is new, because `breakthrough` previously reached
no concept at all and now reaches `do-not-lose-heart`: Ps 42:5 #1, Gal 6:9 #2,
Hab 3:17-19 #3, then 2 Cor 4:8-10, 2 Cor 4:16-18, Ps 37:23-24, Isa 41:10,
Heb 10:35, Josh 1:9, Isa 43:18-19. That is the *point* of A2.14 — the
prosperity fixture exists to assert that a `breakthrough` query is not answered
with the seed-faith set, and after this change it is answered with perseverance
texts instead of with nothing. All twelve of its `mustNotRank` refs remain
absent from the top 50, so the fixture passes; its `note` is amended in the
same commit because the note recorded the old ordering (B14).

**Three patterns account for the rest**, and each is a deliberate design choice
rather than a side effect:

1. **A shared anchor reaching a pack's own queries** (rows for
   `aging-and-old-age`, `caring-for-aging-parents`,
   `dying-parent-register-guard`, `death-and-burial`, `death-of-a-believer`,
   `vanity-of-life`). A2.15 and A2.17 anchor Isa 46:4, Ps 90:12, Ps 71:17-18
   and Ps 92:12-14 on packs those fixtures' queries already reach, so the
   verses enter at #6-#7 and something leaves from #10. In every case the verse
   that leaves is a passage-terms or token-overlap candidate, not a curated
   anchor.
2. **A span swap** (`confession-of-sin`, `forgiveness-of-sins`,
   `godly-marriage`, `unequally-yoked`). Ps 51:3-4 → Ps 51:1-4 and
   Eph 5:22-24 → Eph 5:21-24 are the same anchor at a wider span, so the old
   reference leaves and the new one enters **at the identical position**. No
   ranking changed; the citation did. `godly-marriage.json`'s `alsoAcceptable`
   entry is amended in the same commit (A2.3), which is why it still passes.
3. **A new or re-weighted anchor reaching a shipped pack's queries, and
   related-theme chips behind it** (`worry-and-stress`, `whatever-is-true`,
   `discouragement`, `do-not-lose-heart-give-up-phrasings`, `trust-in-god-bare`,
   `gods-surprising-choice`, `pastoral-god-sees`, `shame`). Two mechanisms
   combine here: an anchor this section adds to a shipped pack enters at #3-#7,
   and the `related:` edges the new packs carry land a flat 4-6 points
   (width-independent, A2.0c) on verses at #9-#10. Every displacement in this
   class is at position 7 or lower, and in all but two cases at #9 or #10.

**Nothing is owed before merge that was not measured.** r2 ended this section
with two measurements "owed before merge". Both are now taken:

- the thin-cue behaviour of bare `parent` at 2- and 3-token widths (A2.5) — a
  dedicated fixture, `bare-parent-cofire.json`, now measures it on the served
  page: Col 3:20-21 at #1/#7/#11/#13 and Prov 22:6 at #3/#9/#14/#12 across
  `parenting` / `raising children` / `parenting advice` / `how to be a good
  parent`, asserted `presenceOnly` with label pins;
- where 1 Cor 7:15 lands for `tempted to cheat on my wife` (A2.4, m8) — it is
  **#18**, recorded in `resisting-infidelity.json`'s note and in the disclosed
  residuals, and the guard that claimed to protect against it is deleted.

## Deferred registers

Not designed here — fixture-first, per CLAUDE.md's "Adding data" discipline.

- **Blended family / step children / in-laws.** Tokens `{blend, family}` /
  `{step, children}` / `{laws}` (generic, adjacent to
  `the-ten-commandments`/`obedience-to-the-word` vocabulary). No direct
  Scripture teaching on household-blending; "in-laws" as typed is
  valence-ambiguous (conflict or devotion). Do not mint until an audit
  measures a real query pattern.
- **Spouse of a porn-addicted or alcoholic partner.** Verified real gap:
  `{spouse, alcoholic}` matches nothing, and `sexual-purity`'s bare `porn`
  answers "my husband is addicted to porn" by treating the *asker* as the
  struggler — the wrong person's register. The asker needs Gal 6:1-2 plus
  `betrayal-and-marriage-crisis`'s comfort anchors. Its own fixture, next
  after this batch.
- **"I'm pregnant and scared."** Neither `waiting-for-a-child` (pre-conception
  ache) nor `pregnancy-and-child-loss` (grief) fits. Candidate lead anchor:
  **Luke 1:30-38** — "Don't be afraid, Mary… you will conceive"
  (WEB-verified). Never write "scared" in any eventual phrase
  (`{pregnant, scar}`); use "afraid".
- **Bare `dying`, bare `pastor`, bare `unloved`/`rejected`.** Three
  bare-word rulings this section raises and does not decide; each needs a
  fixture-first change of its own.

## Critic responses (round-1 objections contested, with proof)

r2 contested four of the round-1 objections. r3 re-checked all four against
the code and the corpus. **Three stand; one (C4) is withdrawn because r2 was
wrong on a fact it did not check, and C2's verdict stands on a mechanism r2
stated backwards.** Everything else in both critiques was accepted and
applied.

The scoreboard, so a reader does not have to reconstruct it:

| # | r2 said | r3 verdict |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | the critique's stated convention is wrong, its verdict right | **stands** — `shame: admitted: [shame, asham]` is a live counter-example and the rule is normalize-to-firing-token |
| C2 | two of three suggested replacements collide | **verdict stands, mechanism corrected** — G4's `normalizePhrase` *is* a token join; the real blind spot is token order |
| C3 | M13's rewrite duplicates an entry r1 already had | **stands** — `hurt by my pastor` and `my pastor hurt me` are the same token set |
| C4 | `pastoral-divorce-teaching.json` does not exist | **withdrawn** — it exists, it is active, and it is now a measured regression target |

**C1 — B7's stated convention is wrong; its verdict is right.** The critique
says *"The repo's own convention is the surface word, not the stem — see
`relapse-and-restoration: admitted: [relapse, relapsed, failed]`,
`new-creation: admitted: [starting]`"*. The live inventory contains
`shame: admitted: [shame, asham]`, and `asham` is a stem, not a surface word.
Run: `significantWords("asham") = ["asham"]`, and `shame.yaml`'s entry
`ashamed` normalizes to `asham`, so the row passes. The actual rule, read out
of `lexiconInventory.ts:135-160`, is that the admitted string must **normalize
to the firing token**. `diagnos` fails that (`significantWords("diagnos") =
["diagno"]`), so the critique's conclusion stands and r2 writes `diagnosed` /
`diagnosis` — but the rule is stated correctly in A2.0b so the next author
does not reject a legal stem or accept an illegal surface word.

**C2 — B2's suggested replacements collide; only one of the three survives.
The verdict stands; r2's stated mechanism was wrong and is corrected here
(M-1).** The critique offers *"`i was unfaithful` → `{unfaithful}`, `i had an
affair` → `{affair}`, `i committed adultery` → `{commit, adultery}` are
candidates that do not collide, all verifiable"*. Measured:
- `betrayal-and-marriage-crisis` already carries `unfaithful husband` and
  `unfaithful wife`, so `i was unfaithful to my wife` produces the **identical
  token set** `{unfaithful, wife}` as that pack's entry — two packs matching at
  parity on one query.
- `i had an affair` → `{affair}`, and the same pack carries `my wife had an
  affair` / `my husband had an affair`, so a bare `affair` admission fires the
  resisting pack from the wounded spouse's own query.
- `i committed adultery` tokenizes `{committ, adultery}`, not
  `{commit, adultery}` — the stem is `committ`. It is the one candidate that
  fires nothing else, and r2 uses it (routed to `forgiveness-of-sins`, A2.4b,
  which is also the right pastoral home).

**The correction.** r2 explained the first bullet by saying G4 would not report
the duplicate "because `normalizedPhrase` is a surface normalization, not a
token join". That is backwards, and it matters because the wrong statement
would send the next author looking for a defect that is not there. Read
`eval/src/gates/collision.ts:36-38`: the gate's own local helper is

```ts apply=none
function normalizePhrase(phrase: string): string {
  return significantWords(phrase).join(' ');
}
```

— a **token join**, using the same `significantWords` the engine tokenizes
with. So G4 *does* compare at the token level, and `"i was unfaithful to my
wife"` and `"unfaithful wife"` both normalize to `"unfaithful wife"`: the
duplicate **would** be reported. The real blind spot in that helper is
narrower and worth stating exactly, because it is the one this section had to
work around by hand: `join(' ')` preserves **first-occurrence order**, so
`hurt pastor` and `pastor hurt` normalize to different strings and are not
reported as colliding, even though the engine matches them identically as the
set `{hurt, pastor}`. A2.0b states that correctly, and the token-set duplicate
sweep this section ran by hand exists to cover exactly that gap — not the
surface-vs-token gap r2 invented.

**C3 — M13's proposed rewrite is a duplicate of an entry r1 already had.**
The critique proposes replacing `my pastor let me down` with
*"`my pastor hurt me` → `{pastor, hurt}` (2 tokens, no collapse)"*. r1's
lexicon already contained `hurt by my pastor`, which tokenizes to the same
`{hurt, pastor}`; adding the proposed wording would have created an intra-pack
token-set duplicate (the m1 defect) rather than a new reachability. r2 keeps
one entry, `hurt by my pastor`, and the bare-`pastor` refusal is recorded in
the inventory row. The substance of M13 — do not admit bare `pastor` — is
accepted in full.

**C4 — WITHDRAWN. r2 was wrong on the fact, and the critique was right.**
r2 wrote that "`pastoral-divorce-teaching.json` does not exist in
`eval/golden/`". It does. The file is
`eval/golden/pastoral-divorce-teaching.json`, it is `status: "active"`, its
query is `what does God say about divorce`, and it covers
`marriage-divorce-teaching` with Matt 19:3-9 pinned to
`Theme: Marriage and divorce` and Matt 5:31-32 in `alsoAcceptable`. r2 checked
for a filename it guessed at instead of listing the directory, and then used
its own error to dismiss a correct objection. That is the failure mode this
whole revision exists to remove, so it is recorded rather than quietly fixed.

It is also exactly the right instrument for A2.3, because it is the fixture
that would break if a new crisis register bled into the teaching register.
It is restored as a named regression target and measured: on the simulated
artifact its top ten is **unchanged from baseline** — Matt 19:3-9 #1 (42.61),
1 Cor 7:10-16 #2, Matt 5:31-32 #3, Gen 2:24 #4, Mal 2:13-16 #6 — and it does
not appear in the 55-fixture moves table. `marriage-in-crisis` shares no
lexicon entry with this query.

The critique's other named fixture, `contentment-money.json`, is affected by
A2.11 only through the *deliberate non-change* to `gods-provision`, and is in
the consolidated list above as the proof that the money register did **not**
move into the watchlist-anchoring pack. The objection itself was correct and
every item now ends with the fixtures it must re-run, measured rather than
listed.

One further correction, in the critique's favour: **B12 understates the
problem it names.** The `parent` co-fire is not only children-of-divorce's —
measured, it also hits `single parent` / `parenting alone` / `solo parent`
(A2.7) and `my parents are getting old` / `watching my parents age` (A2.15).
r2 guards all three items rather than the one the critique named.

## Simulated-gate results (r4) — printed == measured by construction

Every number in this section was produced by the harness described below, not
by reading the engine and reasoning about it. In r4 the harness changed in one
decisive way, and it is the change the r3 critique asked for: **the build is
generated from this document.** Every fenced block in the file declares in its
info string what it is and where it goes (`apply=ops`, `apply=fixture`,
`apply=fixture-edit`, `apply=fixture-listing`, `apply=none`); a parser reads
them out of the markdown, an applier writes them onto a copy of `git archive
HEAD`, and the compile, the database, the gates and every position table below
run on *that*. Nothing is typed twice. r3's blocking list contained three
anchors missing from a printed block, two weights that contradicted the prose,
two corrupt YAML fences and two fixtures that existed only in prose — a class
of defect this method makes structurally impossible, because a block that is
wrong is a build that is wrong.

The **block inventory** at the end of this appendix lists all 81 fenced blocks
with their targets; it is generated by the same parser.

### The harness

1. `git archive HEAD | tar -x` into a scratch directory (the working tree is
   never read and never touched; `git status --porcelain` is empty).
2. `parse.py` reads every fenced block out of this file and emits an operation
   list plus the block inventory. A block with no `apply=` in its info string
   is a **hard error**, so a block cannot be added without deciding what it is.
3. `apply_ops.py` applies the operations to the copied `ontology/` tree and
   writes the fixture files. The one `apply=fixture-edit` block (the
   `godly-marriage.json` amendment) is applied as a find/replace against the
   shipped file, and the `apply=fixture-listing` block beside it is checked to
   be byte-equal to the result — so the printed listing and the printed edit
   cannot drift from each other:

   ```
   verified: printed listing of eval/golden/godly-marriage.json == result of
             applying the printed edit fragment
   ```
4. Compile with the **real** importer,
   `pipeline/src/importers/ontologyImporter.ts`. Baseline compiles to
   concepts 289 / lexicon 1654 / anchors 1821 / related 787; this section's
   tree compiles to **concepts 297 / lexicon 1795 / anchors 1921 /
   related 815, errors 0**.
5. Apply the compiled diff to a copy of `pipeline/output/fixture.db`. The
   artifact reads **297 concepts / 1795 lexicon rows / 1944 anchor rows /
   815 related rows**. Anchor *rows* exceed compiled anchors by exactly 23 —
   and r3's explanation of that gap ("a multi-verse span expands to one row
   per verse") is **false**, corrected in r4 (M-6/m-4). Measured: the shipped
   db carries `editorial 1521 / torrey 300 / openbible-topics 23`, the compile
   produces `editorial 1521 / torrey 300` and no `openbible-topics` at all,
   and the 781 multi-verse compiled anchors each occupy **one** row. The 23
   extra rows are the `openbible-topics` anchors the ontology compile does not
   produce, verified by set-differencing the compiled JSON against the db
   (`extra rows: 23, all source_id=openbible-topics; missing from db: 0`).
6. **Rebuild the spelling index** with `buildSpellingIndex.ts`
   (**18,438 terms / 401,082 deletes**). Not optional: `concept_lexicon` is
   one of five vocabulary origins feeding the index, and skipping it produced
   eight spurious failures the first time round.
7. Run the **real** gate, `eval/src/gates/corpusGolden.ts`, three times
   (baseline / 549 shipped with this section's two amendments / this section's
   27), the **real** G4 checks (`collision.ts` collision + collapse-inventory,
   `lexiconInventory.ts` bare-word, `doctrinalGuardrail.ts` pairing watchlist,
   `corpusGolden.ts` concept coverage), and a top-10 diff of all 549 shipped
   fixture files with **destination positions**.

### Untested-form results — the harm search, not the regression diff

The r3 critique's sharpest observation: the 549-fixture diff covers the 1,136
queries the repo already asserts, and every harm this section exists to fix
was found **outside** that set. So this table is generated by running forms
nobody has written down — the modal-question axis (`should i …`, `is it ok
to …`) against every register in the section, the suspicion axis, the
first-person axis, and the past-tense axis — and reading what comes back.
Nine of the twelve rows r3's critique measured as MISS or HARM are now served;
the rest are refused with a reason.

**The one query in the owner's serve-list that is refused, with both branches
measured.** `should i move` → `{move}` reaches nothing curated. Serving it
requires admitting bare `move` to `guidance`, because `should` and `i` are
stopwords and there is no longer phrase to hang it on. Built and measured:

```text apply=none
                          WITHOUT bare `move` (shipped)      WITH bare `move`

"i cant move on"          nothing curated                    Ps 32:8 #1, Prov 3:5-6 #9
"move on from my ex"      nothing curated                    Ps 32:8 #1, Prov 3:5-6 #8
"faith to move mountains" Matt 17:20 #2, 1 Cor 13:2 #8       Ps 32:8 #2, Matt 17:20 #3
```

The cost is not hypothetical and it is not small: bare `move` answers
*"i cant move on"* and *"move on from my ex"* — the register
`heartbreak-and-breakup` is built for **in this section** — with *"I will
instruct you and teach you in the way which you shall go"*, and it puts a
guidance chip at #2 on a faith query, displacing Matt 17:20. The tokenizer
does **not** stem `moving` to `move` (verified), so the existing
`move to a new city` / `moving to a new city` entries are unaffected either
way. **Refused**, and the refusal is now a measurement rather than the
inherited preference m12 recorded. It is listed in Known gaps.

### What this measurement can and cannot tell you (corrected, r4, M-6)

It **can** tell you ordering on this corpus: `pipeline/output/fixture.db` is
the same database the gate runs against in CI, so a position measured here is
the position CI will measure.

**r3's stated caveat was wrong and is withdrawn.** r3 said the fixture corpus
is a verse subset and that every "absent from top 50" claim was therefore only
a claim about a subset — and called that re-run "the one item this section
leaves genuinely open". Measured:

```text apply=none
pipeline/output/fixture.db   meta verse_count = 31098 | verses = 31098 | 1 translation (WEB)
pipeline/fixtures/web-subset.json  selection[].why =
  "full-Bible corpus (Jesse 2026-08-26): every chapter ships so any searched word
   surfaces its verses, tagged or not"
```

It is the whole WEB. Raw retrieval, `token_overlap`, `proximity`, concept
anchors and pericope grouping all run against every verse that exists, so
"absent from the top 50" means what it plainly says, and the open item as
stated does not exist.

**The real residual is narrower and sharper.** What *is* partial here is the
Layer-B distillate:

```text apply=none
verse_terms               95,651 rows over  3,275 of 31,098 verses  (10.5%)
verse_translation_tokens 307,923 rows over 30,817 of 31,098 verses  (99.1%)
```

`verse_terms` is the family A2.0c proves can turn a 6.00-point capped hint
into a 15.48-point result by disabling the sole-evidence floor (the Phil 4:13
route). **A verse with no `verse_terms` row here that has one in the full
artifact can gain a corroborating chip and jump.** That is the re-run the PR
landing this section must do before the guard deletions are final, and it is a
claim about ~90% of verses' *distillate rows*, not about the corpus. Every
`translation_variant` and `passage_terms` position in this section — Phil 4:13
#8/#22/#45, Mark 9:17 #8, the `i cant pay my mortgage` page — is in that class
and is the place to look first.

## Revision log (r3)

Round-2 gave 14 blocking, 9 major and 8 minor objections, and set a new
standard: **every fixture in this section must pass the real gate on the
simulated corpus, with zero regressions in the existing fixtures.** It does.
This log records what changed to get there.

### The three failures that changed how the section is written

| # | what r2 got wrong | why it matters beyond the one item |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Twelve guards were written against `concept_anchor` arithmetic alone.** Verses reach positions 6-10 through `translation_variant` (14 pts), `token_overlap` (10), `proximity` (6) and width-independent related-theme chips. Phil 4:13 arrived at #7 on a route r2 did not model. | A new subsection, **A2.0c**, writes the four non-anchor routes and their budgets out once, with a measured example of each, so no later item guesses again. |
| 2 | **Guards were justified by "the verse is in corpus", which is not a route.** Half of r2's guards could never fire; two failed outright. | A new subsection, **A2.0d**, defines two guard classes — *measured* (demonstrated route, position recorded) and *standing-contract* (doctrine-negative flagged pairings and the crisis floor, kept regardless and labelled) — and deletes everything else as decoration, with the measurement recorded where the guard used to be. |
| 3 | **The "regression list" was a reading list.** It named fixtures a reviewer ought to re-run and asserted the result. | The list is replaced by a measurement over all 549 shipped fixtures: zero breaks, 55 moves, each move printed with the verse that entered and the verse that left. |

### One harm neither critique round found

The top-10 diff over all 549 shipped fixtures caught a defect no gate and no
reviewer had: r2's `laid off` lexicon entry collapses to bare `{laid}`, and on
`design-in-creation-job.json`'s query *"where were you when i laid the
foundations of the earth"* it pulled **seven** `provision-in-hardship` anchors
into the top ten, with Matt 6:25-34 at **#2**. G4 was green (the collapse was
declared, the token fires) and G3 did not move (that fixture is pending and
fails identically either way). The admission is withdrawn and replaced by
three paired forms (A2.11); after the fix that query's results are
byte-identical to baseline and the changed-fixture count fell from 56 to 55
on r3's build. (r4's build moves 47 files; the difference is the two
withdrawals under B-9 and M-2.)

This is the argument for the diff itself, not just for the gate: **a gate tells
you whether your assertions still hold; only a diff tells you what you did to
everything you never asserted.**

And r3's critique showed the limit of that argument, which r4 accepts: the
diff covers the 1,136 queries the repo already asserts, and **every harm this
section exists to fix was found outside that set** — including one this
section created. `thinking about cheating` → `{think, cheat}` sat inside
`i think my wife is cheating`, and the resisting-temptation set answered the
suspecting spouse for a whole round, invisibly, because no shipped fixture
asks that question. So the r4 instrument is a third one: a **harm search**
over forms nobody has written down (the untested-form table in the appendix),
run against every register this section touches. **A gate checks your
assertions; a diff checks your neighbours; only a harm search checks the
queries nobody has thought of yet — and that is where this section's harms
have been every round.**

## Revision log (r4)

r3 verdict: FAIL — 9 blocking, 8 major, 9 minor. This is the last revision
round; where an objection is not fully closed it is in **Known gaps** below
rather than described as closed.

**The method changed, and that is the headline.** The r3 critique's third
"wow" item was: *emit the section's change blocks from the harness rather than
typing them beside it, and the entire blocking list except B-7, B-8 and B-9
disappears.* That is what r4 does. `parse.py` reads every fenced block out of
this document, `apply_ops.py` builds from them, and the compile, database,
gates, position tables and diff all run on that build. A block with no
`apply=` declaration is a hard parse error. B-3, B-4, B-5 and B-6 are not
"fixed" so much as **made impossible**: a printed block that omits an anchor,
prints the wrong weight, closes its fence in the wrong place or exists only as
prose is now a build that fails or a measurement that changes.

**cannot see** — a named-passage query answered by the wrong named passage,

harness in this revision, and no register is claimed covered that was not
typed in the form a person types it.**

### The dual rule, made mechanical

r2 disclosed its overlapping anchors and did not measure them, and that gap
is exactly where both of r2's existing-fixture regressions came from. r3
adopted a rule; r4 stops applying it by hand:

> **A new pack's weight on a range another pack already anchors is ≤ the
> owner's weight — unless the owning pack's own golden fixture is re-run on
> the simulated after-state and shown unchanged.**

Overlap is computed by **verse-id range intersection over the compiled HEAD
artifact**, not by `grep`. That is why the ledger finds overlaps r2's greps
could not: `grep "ref: Titus 3:4-7"` cannot see `justification-by-faith`'s
`Titus 3:5-7`. **The exceedance list is now generated** (`ledger.py` diffs
the compiled anchor set and emits every added anchor with every intersecting
owner, then filters to the rows whose weight exceeds an owner's). r3 printed
a hand-written list of eight and two real exceedances were missing from it;
the generated list for r4's 62 added anchors is **eleven**, and every one
names the owner's fixture and its re-run result. The full 62-row table and
the eleven-row exceedance table are in the appendix.

What replaces r2's warranty:

- **Every token set below was produced by running
  `engine/src/tokenizer/index.ts` under `npx tsx`** (`significantWords` /
  `normalizedPhrase`), not by inspection.
- **Every "anchored / unanchored elsewhere" claim below is a range-
  intersection query over the compiled HEAD artifact**, not a grep.
- **Every "Measured gap" and every "Acceptance" line is a live engine run**,
  read-only, over `pipeline/output/fixture.db` (WEB, 66 books) through the
  public API (`createEngine` + a `node:sqlite` `ContentQueryPort`). The
  *after* states were measured too, on a scratch copy; nothing in the
  repository was modified.
- Where a measurement contradicts a proposal, the proposal changed. Four
  items lost their headline claim in r2 that way (A3.9, A3.11, A3.12,
  A3.19's "magnificat"); four more in r3 (A3.3's Isaiah 55:7, A3.10's 0.9,
  A3.14's second fixture, A3.16's Ephesians 5). **In r4 five more did:**
  A3.8 lost its anchor-in-`loving-others` design entirely, A3.7 lost the
  Isaiah 49:25 anchor, A3.19 lost 0.7 for 0.6, A3.16 lost the "whole and
  uncut" claim, and A3.25 lost its "no lexicon phrase" ruling on Romans Road.
- Containment is `phraseTokens.every(t => queryTokens.has(t))`
  (`engine/src/corpus/repository.ts:707`) — **the phrase must be a subset of
  the query**. Every phrase below was re-checked in that direction against
  every query and additionalQuery it must serve.

### The named-passage rule (new in r4)

r3's blocking defect was structural, not local: `loving-others.json` pins
`John 13:34-35` with `expectedWithinTop: 10` and lists `"the golden rule"`
among its `additionalQueries`, and `corpusGolden.ts:867-871` is a `.some()`
over the whole result set — so a 549-fixture suite could not see that the
phrase it asserts had started returning a *different* parable at #1. r4
adopts the rule the critique asked for, and applies it to every named
passage in this section:

> **Every named-passage query pins its own passage's rank explicitly.** An
> alias-backed name pins `withinTop: 1`. A name served only by a lexicon
> phrase pins the rank the harness measures and states in the fixture note
> why it is not 1.

### A3.0 Why — the register-coverage matrix

The unit of work is not "one sentence closed" but "a register covered".
Every row below is a real typed form, tokenized with the shared tokenizer;
`before` and `after` are live top-1 results, re-measured in r4.

**What r3 got wrong here, and what r4 changed.** r3's matrix rows were
accurate as written — the critique verified every one against the compiled
lexicon — but the matrix had no row for two of the commonest phrasings in
the two registers this section leads with: the **verb-fronted interrogative**
(`why wont god answer me`) and the **`anymore` negation** (`i dont feel god

not hand over: Proverbs 23:35 (the drunkard who cannot feel a beating) at #1
for the second, and Job 40:2 ("he who argues with God, let him answer it")

thought of is a coverage claim about the author, not about the register.**

**The uncontracted/contracted axis, applied systematically (r4).** r3 admitted
`god isnt` and `god is not` as a pair and then did not apply the same
reasoning anywhere else. The tokenizer keeps `dont`, `doesnt`, `isnt`,
`cant`, `wont` as distinct tokens — none of them stems to the others and
none is a stopword — so **every contraction is a separate reach**. r4's rule:
when a register admits one contraction, every contraction a person actually
types for that register is measured, and each is either admitted or declined
with its measured result printed beside it. Applied here, that produced
three new `presence-of-god` reaches, two new `unanswered-prayer` reaches,
and one *declined* admission (`why doesnt god answer me` — measured already
covered at HEAD, so a phrase for it would be weight without value).

Two `verses`/`verse` splits the tokenizer forces and r1 missed: `verses` →
`-es` strip → `vers`; `verse` ends in `e`, matches no suffix rule → `verse`.
Every plural-keyed phrase in r1 left the singular form reaching nothing. Every
pack below either carries both forms or a bare word that covers both.

**The one defect no amount of data can close (new finding, r2).** The typed
word `magnificat` is not in `spelling_terms`; the spelling index corrects it
to `magnifical` (distance 1, a `translations`-origin term with
`document_count: 0`), and the corrected token matches no lexicon phrase, so
`research("the magnificat")` returns **zero results even with the lexicon
entry installed** — measured. The curated-alias path is immune: with an alias
row installed the same query returns Luke 1:46-55 at 40.00 with the chip
`(query corrected from "magnificat")`. "The magnificat" is therefore a Phase C
row, not a Phase A lexicon entry (A3.19, A3.25).

### A3.1 Fear of judgment: "am I going to hell", "will God forgive me", "too far gone"

**What the asker is really asking.** Not "give me a list of salvation
verses" — *does God want me?* Two verses answer that sentence directly and
neither was in r1's twelve-anchor extension.

**Measured gap** (live, before):

```
"am i going to hell"   1. Mark 9:43-48  2. Matthew 18:8-9  3. Matthew 5:22
"will god forgive me"  1. Matthew 18:21-22  2. Matthew 6:14-15  3. Ephesians 4:32
"does god forgive me"  1. Isaiah 55:7  2. Matthew 18:21-22  3. Matthew 6:14-15
"too far gone for god" lexical noise only
```

`hell.yaml`'s bare `hell` wins the first by default; `forgiving-others`'
`forgive` collapse wins the next two (A3.2). `assurance-of-salvation.yaml`
is the wrong register by its own design (it answers "am I really saved" for
someone who already professed). `salvation.yaml` (lead Acts 16:30-31, 1.0)
is the correct, too-narrow home.

**Change.**
```yaml
# ontology/concepts/salvation.yaml — lexicon additions
lexicon:
  - am i going to hell
  - have i sinned too much to be forgiven
  - too far gone for god
  - can god forgive me
  - will god forgive me
  - what happens when i die if im not saved
  # ADDED IN r4, ruling R1a (below). Bare, one raw word, so
  # singleTokenCollapses does not fire and no `collapses:` row is needed —
  # only the `concepts:` admission. `hell` is already `hell.yaml`'s admitted
  # word; two concepts may admit one token and both fire.
  - hell
  # ADDED IN r4 under owner ruling 17 (see A3.25). "romans road" ->
  # {roman,road}; 2 raw words, 2 tokens, no collapse. Fixture-first:
  # named-passage-romans-road.json is written against the MEASURED result,
  # which is salvation's own anchor order and not the five-verse sequence.
  - romans road
```
```yaml
# ontology/concepts/salvation.yaml — anchors
anchors:
  # John 3:16 [torrey] @0.7 is LEFT EXACTLY AS IT IS. The extension to
  # v17-18 is LH's judgment, not Torrey's; a widened entry carrying
  # sources: [torrey, editorial] would emit a torrey-sourced row for
  # 43003016-43003018 (John is book 43; r2 wrote 40003016, which is
  # Matthew — right reasoning, wrong book) (ontologyImporter.ts header:
  # collapsing the two is
  # "the single most dishonest thing this pipeline could do").
  # The importer's duplicate check keys on start:end, so a disjoint
  # sibling entry is legal.
  - { ref: John 3:17-18, sources: [editorial], weight: 0.85 }
  - { ref: Ezekiel 33:11, sources: [editorial], weight: 0.9 }
  - { ref: 2 Peter 3:9, sources: [editorial], weight: 0.85 }
```

**Ephesians 2:9 is deliberately NOT added.** r1's critic is right that v9
("not of works, that no one would boast") is the half that answers "have I
sinned too much". But `grace-not-earned.yaml` holds Eph 2:8-9 at **1.0**,
`faith-and-works` holds 2:8-10 at 0.8, `mormon-evangelism` holds 2:8-9 at
0.95, and `salvation.yaml` already lists `grace-not-earned` in `related:`.
Widening salvation's 2:8 would be a fourth claim on one sentence. Span
discipline: cross-reference, do not duplicate. Measured: Ephesians 2:8
already ranks #3 for "am i going to hell" after this change, carrying the
chip `Related theme: Grace, not earned`.

**Tokenizer hazards (run, not inferred).**
`am i going to hell` → `{going,hell}` (`going` does **not** stem to `go`:
`-ing` strips only when the remainder is ≥4 chars, and `go` is 2).
`can/will god forgive me` → `{god,forgive}`.
`does god forgive me` → `{do,god,forgive}` (superset — also matches).
`have i sinned too much to be forgiven` → `{sinn,much,forgiven}` — `sinned`
→ `-ed` strip → **`sinn`, not `sin`**, so the entry fires only on the
inflected form, and `much` is near-generic. Recorded, kept, and the reason
it is safe is that all three tokens must be present.
`too far gone for god` → `{far,gone,god}`.
`what happens when i die if im not saved` → `{happen,die,saved}` (a superset
of `salvation`'s existing bare `saved`, by design).
`is it too late for me` → `{late}` — **rejected**, bare and generic.
`is there any hope for someone like me` → `{hope,someone,like}` — **removed
from the fixture** (r1 asserted it as an additionalQuery). No salvation
phrase is a subset of it; it fires only `hope-in-god`'s bare `hope`, and the
live top-3 is Jer 29:11 / Heb 6:19 / Heb 11:1. Adding `hope for someone like
me` would hijack `hope-in-god`; not proposed.

### A3.2 The `forgive others` collapse — rename, and keep the bare register alive

**Measured gap.** `forgive others` → `{forgive}` (`others` is a stopword),
so bare `forgive` fires interpersonal reconciliation and every
receiving-forgiveness query is hijacked. Live: "will god forgive me" → 1.
Matthew 18:21-22, "does god forgive me" → 2. Matthew 18:21-22.

**Change — three files, five edits, not "a single line".**
```yaml
# 1. ontology/concepts/forgiving-others.yaml — lexicon
lexicon:
  - forgive one another        # WAS: forgive others  (renamed)
  - forgive                    # NEW: the bare register, written bare
  - forgive as you have been forgiven
  - seventy times seven
  - forgiving one another
  - reconcile with your brother
```
```yaml
# 2. ontology/lexicon-inventory.yaml, `collapses:` (line 110) — DELETE
#    the whole 8-line entry. After the rename no forgiving-others phrase
#    is a multi-word phrase collapsing to one token, so the acknowledgment
#    is stale and collision.ts lexiconInventoryCheck fails on it
#    ("stale acknowledgment ... delete the entry").
#  - conceptId: forgiving-others
#    phrase: "forgive others"
#    token: forgive
#    ...
```
```yaml
# 3. ontology/lexicon-inventory.yaml, `concepts:` (line 1529) — KEEP the
#    row, rewrite its note. `admitted: [forgive]` still fires, because the
#    bare entry above IS a lexicon phrase normalizing to {forgive};
#    lexiconInventory.ts's admitted-does-not-fire check is satisfied by
#    construction rather than by accident.
  - id: forgiving-others
    # 2026-08-08 correction table: the verb belongs to this concept as
    # forgiveness-of-sins owns the noun. r2 (Phase A3.2): the bare word is
    # now an EXPLICIT lexicon entry rather than the accidental collapse of
    # "forgive others"; the register decision is unchanged, the accident
    # is gone. Whether forgiveness-of-sins should own bare `forgive`
    # instead remains OPEN — rulings ledger 2026-08-27 row 14 (J1) and
    # row 24 (the PR #33 deny-list flag, "`forgive`->forgiving-others:
    # the fix belongs to ranking/alias work").
    admitted: [forgive]
```
```yaml
# 4. ontology/lexicon-inventory.yaml, file header lines 26-28 — the J12
#    flag quotes `forgive others` by name and says it is "acknowledged to
#    stand as-is until that ruling". Rewrite to name the r2 state: the
#    collapse is gone, the bare admission is explicit, J1 is still open.
```
```yaml
# 5. ontology/concepts/forgiving-others.yaml header — record the rename
#    and cite ledger rows 14 and 24, so the next reader does not think

```
No anchor or `related:` change.

**Why this shape, and not the alternatives.** The critic is right that
deleting the register outright would remove coverage and add none (measured:
after a bare rename with no replacement, `forgive` and `how do i forgive
someone` reach **nothing**). The critic is also right that moving the bare
word to `forgiveness-of-sins` would *resolve J1 by fiat*. Writing the bare
word explicitly does neither: it removes the accident the inventory file
exists to catch, preserves the recorded routing decision exactly, and leaves
the ownership question where the ledger already put it — with Jesse.

**Tokenizer hazards (run).** `forgive one another` → `{forgive,another}`;
`forgiving one another` → `{forgiv,another}` (stemmed `-ing` form, a
different token string — both survive, collision-free);
`forgive as you have been forgiven` → `{forgive,forgiven}`;
bare `forgive` → `{forgive}` (one raw word, so `singleTokenCollapses` does
**not** fire — that check requires `phrase.split(/\s+/).length > 1`; verified
against `eval/src/gates/collision.ts:176`).

**Anchors.** No change.

**Guards.** `mustNotRank: Matthew 18:21-22` on the assurance fixture —
**non-vacuous, proven**: measured #1 for "will god forgive me" before this
change, and absent from the top 10 after (the pack still fires via the
1-token bare match, but the 1-token specificity discount puts it below
salvation's 2-token matches).

### A3.3 Felt distance and coming back — routed against the recorded register boundary

**What the asker is really asking.** "I feel far from God" is not a request
for seek-and-find commands. It is *is he still there, and will he take me
back?* Those are two different sentences and this item routes them to two
different packs, because `seeking-god.yaml`'s own header already drew the
line: *"the row's own register check verified: hunger-for-god owns
thirst/longing, **presence-of-god nearness**, prayer asking — none carries
seek/his-face vocabulary."*

r1 dropped nine anchors into `seeking-god` and never engaged that sentence.
Three things were wrong with it, all measurable:

1. `seeking-god`'s live tier is Jer 29:12-13 (1.0), Isa 55:6 (0.95), Ps 27:8
   (0.9), 1 Chr 16:10-11 (0.9), 2 Chr 7:14 (0.85), 1 Chr 28:9 (0.8), Deut
   4:29 (0.75). Every r1 addition was ≤0.7, so the top of the list stays
   seven consecutive imperatives to seek — to a person writing in to say
   seeking is what they cannot do. r1's "Acceptance: top-3 includes Luke
   15:11-24" was arithmetically unreachable.
2. r1's lead addition, **James 4:8 at 0.7, is already
   `presence-of-god`'s anchor at 0.95** (`grep`:
   `presence-of-god.yaml:20`). r1 called it new. So is Ps 139:7-12, whose
   near-identical `Psalms 139:7-10` is `presence-of-god`'s **1.0**. The
   right pack was already holding the right texts.
3. `why do i feel so distant from the lord` → `{feel,distant,lord}` does not
   contain `{feel,distant,god}`. Measured live: it fires only
   `guidance("the will of the lord")` and returns Prov 14:16 / Ezek 38:16 /
   Jer 31:10 / Ps 32:8 — career-guidance proof-texts to someone saying they
   feel far from God. That collapse is rulings-ledger **row 23/24**'s `lord`
   deny-list candidate, the MEASURED ph6-B cause.

**Tokenizer hazards (run).** `i feel far from god` → `{feel,far,god}`;
`i feel distant from god` → `{feel,distant,god}`; `i feel far from the lord`
→ `{feel,far,lord}`; `i feel distant from the lord` → `{feel,distant,lord}`
— **four separate entries, because `god` and `lord` are different tokens and
containment is one-directional**; the query `why do i feel so distant from
the lord` → `{feel,distant,lord}` is reached only by the fourth.
`coming back to god` → `{coming,back,god}` vs `how to come back to god` →
`{come,back,god}` — two token strings for one verb (`coming` does not stem:
the `-ing` rule needs a ≥4-char remainder and `com` is 3). Both kept
deliberately. `returning to god` → `{return,god}`, which is a subset of
`repentance`'s existing "return to the lord"? No — that is `{return,lord}`,
a different set; the new entry is genuinely new reach.

```ts
// Explanation tripwire (ruling row 19): scans EVERY returned result, not a
// window — a forbidden claim is a contract breach wherever it appears.
for (const substring of fixture.forbiddenReasonLabelSubstrings) {
  for (const entry of results) { ... }
}
```
— `corpusGolden.ts:1277-1296`. The gate's own call is `engine.research(query)`
with no options, which returns **25** results, and `Psalms 32:8` survives at
**rank 25** (r4 re-measure; r3 printed 24, before Psalms 42:1-5 was
anchored) carrying `Theme cue: God's guidance`:

```
from the lord" carries the reason 'Theme cue: God's guidance', which contains the
forbidden fragment 'God's guidance'.
```

The root cause is the `lord`-collapse of `guidance`'s "the will of the lord"
(rulings-ledger rows 23/24) — a J12 lexicon edit outside this section's
declared scope. Narrowing the substring is not available: the window is the
whole result set **by design**, and gaming it would be exactly the
"guardrail as decoration" CLAUDE.md forbids. So the guard is deleted and
replaced with one that says what this item actually achieved.

*Shipped: `mustNotRank: Psalms 32:8`.* `mustNotRank` carries no `withinTop`
field (`MUST_NOT_RANK_FIELDS` is `reference|ref|why`); it is measured inside
`measuredWindow` = max(expectedTop windows, `expectedWithinTop`) = **10**
here. MEASURED: Psalms 32:8 is **#4 before** this change for `why do i feel
so distant from the lord` (the career-guidance proof-text at the top of the
first screen) and **#25 after** — outside the window, so the guard passes,

exactly what this item fixed: the one guidance verse that was on the first
page. The remaining chip at rank 25 is disclosed in the fixture note rather
than hidden behind a substring guard that cannot hold.

```
"why would god let this happen"       1. Exodus 21:13  2. Daniel 3:17  3. Isaiah 7:7    (nothing fires)
"where is god in my pain"             1. Psalms 69:29  2. Revelation 16:11  3. 1 Peter 2:19
"is god punishing me"                 1. Job 31:28  2. 2 Thessalonians 1:8  3. Ezra 9:13
"why do i suffer"                     1. 1 Peter 4:12-16  2. Philippians 1:29  3. Romans 8:17  (suffering-for-christ's bare `suffering`)
```

**Ruling on bare `suffer` ownership (requested; unchanged from r1, now with
its consequence stated).** It stays with `suffering-for-christ`. Two concepts
sharing one admitted bare token needs a resolution rule this codebase lacks,
and reassigning it would break existing bare-`suffering` queries. The
consequence, which r1 hid by choosing a different fixture query: **"why do i
suffer" still leads with 1 Peter 4:12-16 (persecution) after this item, and
this item does not close that.** Stated in Acceptance, not buried.

**Change.**
```yaml
# ontology/concepts/why-god-allows-suffering.yaml — lexicon additions
lexicon:
  - where is god in my pain
  - is god punishing me
  - why did god let this happen to me
  - why would god let this happen
```
No anchor change — the four existing anchors are correct and, measured, they
lead.

**Tokenizer hazards (run).** `why did god let this happen to me` →
`{do,god,happen}` (`did` lemmas to `do`, which is deliberately not a
stopword; `let`/`would`/`why`/`this`/`to`/`me` all are).
`why would god let this happen` → `{god,happen}` — **the 2-token form r1
missed**; without it the commonest variant of the sentence reached nothing.
`why do i suffer` → `{suffer}` — rejected (owned).
`why is this happening to me` → `{happen}` — rejected (bare, generic).
`why me god` → `{god}` — rejected.
`where is god in my pain` → `{god,pain}`. `is god punishing me` →
`{god,punish}`.

**Breadth, judged honestly.** `{god,happen}` is broad: it also fires on "what
does god say about things that happen". That is the price of the tokenizer
treating `not`, `let` and `would` as stopwords, and it is paid deliberately
here, because the measured alternative is that a person asking the commonest
theodicy sentence in English gets Exodus 21:13 ("if he doesn't lie in wait,
but God delivers him into his hand"). The four anchors this admits —
Job 1:21, Romans 8:18, Genesis 50:20, John 9:2-3 — are safe answers to a
generic God-and-events question too.

**Anchors.** No change. Job 1:21 (1.0), Romans 8:18 (0.9), Genesis 50:20
(0.9), John 9:2-3 (0.8) — all re-read in WEB.

**Guards — both r1 guards deleted, with the measurement.**
- `mustNotLead: 1 Peter 4:12-16` — **deleted.** Measured: it does not appear
  in the top 10 of any of this fixture's four queries, before or after. It
  leads only the bare-`suffer` register, which this item deliberately does
  not touch. r1 asserted it on queries where it could never fire.
- `mustNotRank: Hebrews 12:5-11` — **deleted.** Measured: absent from the
  top 10 for every query here, before and after; it is anchored nowhere
  (grep: no `ref: Hebrews 12:5`). A ban on a text that cannot appear is the
  decoration CLAUDE.md names.
- Recorded instead in the fixture note, so the intent is not lost: *if bare
  `suffer` is ever reassigned (the open ruling), re-run and re-derive both
  guards from the measurement.*

**Fixture.**

### A3.5 "God isn't answering my prayers" — and the negation the tokenizer cannot see

**Measured gap** (live, before) — the exact defect
`unanswered-prayer.yaml`'s own header says the pack exists to close:
```
"god is not answering my prayers"
 1. Philippians 4:6  2. 1 Thessalonians 5:16-18  3. 2 Corinthians 1:11
 4. Matthew 6:9-13   5. Ephesians 6:18  6. 1 John 5:14-15  7. Matthew 6:6
 8. Psalms 86:5-7    9. Matthew 7:7    10. 1 Timothy 4:5
"god doesnt hear me"       1. Psalms 38:14  2. Job 27:9  3. Luke 6:49   (nothing fires)
"god is silent to my prayers"  fires prayer + wrestling-with-god
```
Someone who types that sentence is told "Ask, and it will be given you"
(Matt 7:7) and "if we ask anything according to his will, he hears us"
(1 John 5:14-15) — the ask-and-receive register, which the pack's header
calls *"the OPPOSITE of what the asker is living"*.

**The containment correction.** r1 wrote that the uncontracted form "still
matches (a subset)". It is the other way round: the **phrase** must be a
subset of the **query**. `god isnt answering my prayers` →
`{god,isnt,answer,prayer}`; the uncontracted query → `{god,answer,prayer}`;
the 4-token phrase is not contained, so it never matched. Verified by
simulation against the live compiled lexicon: the uncontracted query fired
only `prayer("prayer")`.

**Change.**
```yaml

lexicon:
  - god isnt answering my prayers        # {god,isnt,answer,prayer}
  - god is not answering my prayers      # {god,answer,prayer}  <- the fix
  - god is silent to my prayers          # {god,silent,prayer}
  - god doesnt hear me                   # {god,doesnt,hear}
  # ADDED IN r4 — the VERB-FRONTED INTERROGATIVE. Every phrase above
  # requires `prayer`/`prayers` or `hear`, and the commonest way a person
  # types this register carries neither. Measured before: "why wont god

  # argues with God, let him answer it") — the accusation this pack exists
  # to prevent, arriving through the door the pack left open.

  - why isnt god answering me            # {isnt,god,answer}
  # NOT ADDED, and the reason is a measurement rather than a judgment:
  # `why doesnt god answer me` -> {doesnt,god,answer} is ALREADY contained
  # by the pack's existing HEAD phrase "when god doesnt answer"
  # ({god,doesnt,answer}), and measured on HEAD it already returns
  # 2 Corinthians 12:8-9 at #1 (47.22). A phrase for it would be weight
  # without value (CLAUDE.md, "Adding data").
  #
  # ADDED IN r4 — the SHORT FORM. r3 counted `god is silent` as covered by

  - god is silent                        # {god,silent}
```

one, and it is booked below as a `pending` fixture rather than hidden.
Phase B2/B4 (query-side negation handling) is what actually finishes this.

### A3.6 NEW pack: `favor-of-god`

**What the asker is really asking.** "How do I get God's favor?" — a question
the prosperity teaching §3 excludes answers with a technique. The pack's
whole discipline is that its anchor set answers it with *grace*, not method.

**Measured gap** (live, before):
```
"favor of god"   1. Malachi 1:9 (40.00, exact_phrase)  2. Luke 2:52  3. Psalms 90:17  4. Luke 1:30  5. Acts 2:47
"favor" (bare)   1. Exodus 23:3  2. Luke 1:43  3. Genesis 6:8
"gods favor"     1. Jeremiah 16:13  2. Job 13:8  3. Job 33:26
```
WEB, **Malachi 1:9**: *"'Now, please entreat the favor of God, that he may be
gracious to us. With this, will he accept any of you?' says the LORD of
Armies."* — the prophet's sarcasm at priests offering blind and lame animals;
v10 continues *"I have no pleasure in you... neither will I accept an
offering at your hand."* It is the verbatim #1 answer to a sincere search
today. This is **rulings-ledger row 18 (J5)** by name: *"May the verbatim
rebuke Mal 1:9 stay #1 for 'favor of God', or should the catered answer
(Ps 90:17 / Prov 3:3-4) lead?"* — recommendation on file: catered answer
leads. This item applies that default provisionally and says so.

`favor` and `increase` are both on `ontology/flagged-pairings.yaml`'s
`materialFrameKeywords`, so this pack's id/label/lexicon is automatically in
scope for the G4 doctrinal pairing scan on every anchor. That is a hard
constraint, not a reason to skip minting it — the register is real and
currently unowned.

**Change.**

```yaml
  - { ref: Luke 1:30, sources: [editorial], weight: 0.85 }         # ledger: unanchored
```

**Deliberately dropped from r1.**
- `walking in favor` → `{walk,favor}`. Not a question anyone asks about
  Scripture; it is a phrase from the teaching §3 excludes ("walking in favor
  and increase"). r1 rejected `favor and increase` on the correct grounds
  and then kept its sibling from the same idiom. The G4 pairing scan is a
  lookup over anchors, not protection against vocabulary that recruits.
  `favor`, `favor of god`, `gods favor` and `find favor with god` cover the
  register and none of them is movement vocabulary.
- `Isaiah 61:1-2` (r1, 0.5). It is `god-of-all-comfort`'s at 0.7 and
  overlaps `pastoral-near-to-the-brokenhearted`'s Isaiah 61:1-3 at 0.8 —
  r1 called it new. The register there is anointing and comfort, not favor;
  no third home.

**Tokenizer hazards (run).** `favor of god` → `{favor,god}`; `gods favor` →
`{gods,favor}` (`gods` does not stem to `god` — a distinct token, so this is
genuine extra reach, measured); `find favor with god` → `{find,favor,god}`;
bare `favor` → `{favor}`. `favor and increase` / `increase my favor` →
`{favor,increase}` — both rejected: a second `materialFrameKeyword` doubles
the G4 scan surface for no reach.

**Two of r2's eleven "unanchored (grep)" warranties in this item were
false** (Titus 3:4-7, Exodus 33:12-17); both are corrected above from the
range ledger, and both duals now name the owner and the re-run.

Three of eleven carry a conduct condition in their own clause (Ps 84:11,
Prov 3:3-4, Ps 5:12). They are kept, weighted low, and read in context; the
reason they are safe is that Titus 3:4-7 sits second at 0.95 and, measured,
lands in the top 4 of every favor query.

**Guards.**
- `mustNotLead: Malachi 1:9, withinTop 1` — **non-vacuous, proven**:
  measured **#1 today at 40.00 by `exact_phrase`**; #5 after. Window 1, not
  3: `exact_phrase` is authoritative evidence and the verse is genuinely the
  verbatim match, so demoting it out of the lead is the whole claim; banning
  it from the top 3 would be suppressing a true exact-phrase hit. That is
  the J5 default, expressed as narrowly as it can be.
- `mustNotRank` on the four recruitment texts (Mal 3:10, Luke 6:38, Phil
  4:19, John 14:13-14). Measured: none appears in the top 10 for any favor
  query, before or after — but these are the *watchlist*, and the fixture's
  job is to keep them out as the pack grows. Recorded as what they are:
  **standing watchlist guards, not measured-firing guards.** This is the
  same posture as the ten shipped `prosperity-*.json` guard fixtures.

### A3.7 Prayer for a child — and the prodigal's parent, routed away from Proverbs 22:6

**What the asker is really asking.** "Praying for my prodigal child" is not a
parenting question. It is *will he come home, and does God see me waiting?*

**Measured gap** (live, before):
```
"prayer for my son"            1. 1 Thess 5:16-18  2. Philippians 4:6  3. Matthew 6:9-13   (only `prayer` fires)
"prayer for my daughter"       identical
"prayer for my kids"           identical
"praying for my prodigal child" 1. 1 Thess 5:16-18  2. Philippians 4:6  3. Matthew 6:9-13  (only prayer("how to pray"))
"prayer for my child"          1. Proverbs 22:6 (42.07)  2. Deuteronomy 6:6-7  3. Ephesians 6:4
```
The last line is the measurement that decides this item. WEB, **Proverbs
22:6**: *"Train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is old he
will not depart from it."* — the pack's 1.0 keystone, at rank 1. r1 proposed
adding `praying for my prodigal child` to `parenting` with **no guard**. A
parent whose adult child has walked away would type the sentence and receive,
at rank 1, a proverb that reads as a verdict on their parenting.
`parenting.yaml`'s own comment concedes the risk ("a wisdom-genre
generalization, not an unconditional guarantee") — which is an argument for
a guard, not against one.

**Change — (a) the noun variants stay in `parenting`.**
```yaml
# ontology/concepts/parenting.yaml — lexicon additions
lexicon:
  - prayer for my son
  - prayer for my daughter
  - prayer for my children
  - prayer for my kids
```
```yaml

  # "if your child left the faith, you trained him wrong", handed at rank 1
  # to a parent who typed a prayer request. r3's answer was that the query
  # is "general". The tokenizer cannot tell a worried parent from a curious
  # one; that is an argument for the guard, not against it.

  # WHY THIS ANCHOR AND NOT A GUARD ALONE: `mustNotLead` cannot displace
```

**Deliberately dropped from r1.** Philippians 1:9-11, Colossians 1:9-12 and
Ephesians 3:14-19. All three are Paul's intercessions **for congregations**.
Anchoring them to `parenting` is legal under CLAUDE.md #6 but it is the
weakest kind of editorial claim, and r1's own rationale ("Paul's model
prayer-for-another") conceded it. Measured, they were also unnecessary: the
three texts that ARE about a child being prayed for (1 Sam 1:27-28, Isa
54:13, 3 John 1:4) already land at #6, #8, #9 and the pack's own tier leads.

**Tokenizer hazards (run).** `prayer for my son` → `{prayer,son}`;
`prayer for my daughter` → `{prayer,daughter}`; `prayer for my children` →
`{prayer,children}` (**`children` does not stem to `child`** — that is why
`parenting`'s existing "prayer for my child" never fired these);
`prayer for my kids` → `{prayer,kids}`;
`praying for my prodigal child` → `{pray,prodigal,child}` — note `pray`, not
`prayer`, so `parenting`'s "prayer for my child" is **not** contained and
the prodigal query does not fire `parenting` at all (verified by simulation
and by the live run: only `family-reconciliation` fires).
`my child has walked away from god` → `{child,walk,away,god}`.
`prayer for parents` → `{prayer,parent}` — **rejected**, genuinely ambiguous
("pray for [aging] parents" vs "a parent's prayer"); left to
`caring-for-aging-parents.yaml`.

**Guards.**
- `mustNotLead: Proverbs 22:6, withinTop 1` on the **parenting** fixture —
  **new in r4, and the point of the item's re-weight.** Measured **#1
  (40.00) for all four "prayer for my …" forms before the re-weight**, #2
  after. `withinTop: 1` rather than 3 is deliberate and is the honest
  window: Proverbs 22:6 is the pack's own reviewed keystone and belongs in
  the window for a parenting query; what it must not do is answer a prayer
  request *first*. Non-vacuous by the before-run, not by hope.
- `mustNotLead: Proverbs 22:6, withinTop 3` on the prodigal fixture —
  **non-vacuous, proven by the sibling query**: Proverbs 22:6 is measured
  **#1 (42.07) for "prayer for my child"**, and it is what r1's routing would
  have produced for "praying for my prodigal child" verbatim. After routing
  to `family-reconciliation` it is absent from the result list entirely. The
  guard pins the routing: if anyone later adds a `prodigal` phrase to
  `parenting`, this fires.
- `mustNotRank: "Psalms 91"` on the parenting fixture — r1's prose said
  "Psalms 91 (any span)" while its fixture banned only `"Psalms 91:1"`, so
  Ps 91:2 or 91:11 would have passed the guard the prose claimed.
  `parseAnchorRef("Psalms 91")` resolves to 19091001–19091999, so the
  whole-chapter form is available; use it. Measured: absent from the top 10
  before and after — recorded as a **standing** guard (the pack's own header
  already excludes Ps 91 deliberately; this pins that decision), not as a
  measured-firing one.

**Rulings for Jesse.**
- **R1.** The routing: prodigal → `family-reconciliation`, not `parenting`.

### Named-passage items (A3.8–A3.15)

The reference parser (`engine/src/reference/reference.ts`) resolves literal
book/chapter citations only, never informal names, so every one of these
needs coverage somewhere. **Measurement moved two of them out of Phase A.**
The reason is structural and worth stating once: a named-passage query
answered by firing a whole thematic concept returns *the concept's keystone*,
not *the named passage*, unless the named passage is the keystone. That is
what B10's named-passage alias kind exists for — and B10's own worked example
is literally `name: The Beatitudes, range: Matthew 5:3-12`. **r4 moved a
third one out of `loving-others` for the same reason**: A3.8's parable now
ships as its own one-anchor pack, because measured, anchoring a named
passage inside a thematic pack made the pack's keystone answer the passage's
name at one weight and made the passage answer a *different* passage's name
at another. See the named-passage rule near the top of this section.

#### A3.8 "good samaritan" → NEW pack `parable-of-the-good-samaritan`

**This item was redesigned in r4, and the redesign is the answer to the r3
critique's one blocking objection (O-1).** r3 put Luke 10:25-37 into
`loving-others` at 1.0. Measured, that made a named-passage query for
*a different passage* return the parable:

```
"the golden rule"        r3 DESIGN                  HEAD (and r4)
  1.  Luke 10:25-37   40.00                         John 13:34-35   40.00
  2.  John 13:34-35   40.00                         Matthew 7:12    38.11
  3.  Matthew 7:12    38.11                         1 Cor 13:4-8    38.00
```

A person typing the popular name of Matthew 7:12 was handed the Good
Samaritan first and the verse they named third — the exact failure the
named-passage register exists to prevent, introduced by an item adding a
named passage. No fixture could see it: `eval/golden/loving-others.json`
pins `John 13:34-35` with `expectedWithinTop: 10` and no per-query rank, and
`corpusGolden.ts:867-871` is a `.some()` over the whole result set, so #1
versus #3 is invisible to a 549-fixture suite.

**Two designs were built and measured end to end** (plus r3's, kept as the
counterfactual), on the owner's instruction: the anchor at a lower weight
inside `loving-others`, and a small dedicated pack holding it at full weight
with the named phrases and a `related:` edge back to `loving-others`.

| | r3: anchor @1.0 in `loving-others` | (a) anchor @0.85 in `loving-others` | **(b) dedicated pack @1.0, related → `loving-others`** |
|---|---|---|---|
| `good samaritan` #1 | Luke 10:25-37 (40.00) ✓ | **John 13:34-35** ✗ — parable at **#5** (34.00) | **Luke 10:25-37 (40.00)** ✓ |
| `who is my neighbor parable` #1 | Luke 10:25-37 (41.94) ✓ | John 13:34-35 ✗ — parable at #5 | **Luke 10:25-37 (41.94)** ✓ |
| `the parable of the good samaritan` #1 | Luke 10:25-37 (22.86) ✓ | John 13:34-35 ✗ — parable at #5 | **Luke 10:25-37 (22.86)** ✓ |
| `the golden rule` #1 | **Luke 10:25-37** ✗ | John 13:34-35 ✓ (Matt 7:12 #2) | **John 13:34-35 ✓ (Matt 7:12 #2)** |
| new top-10 rows in existing active fixtures | **24 entries / 16 fixtures** | 6 entries / 5 fixtures, + 1 rank move | **0 entries / 0 fixtures** |
| chip on the parable | `Theme: Loving one another` | `Theme: Loving one another` | `Theme: The Good Samaritan` |

Design (b) is the only one that satisfies both halves of the owner's test —
the parable leads its own three names, and **nothing else moves anywhere**.
It is adopted. Design (a) fails the first half outright: at 0.85 the parable
cannot pass `loving-others`' own 1.0/0.95/0.9 tier on a two-token query, so
the name returns the pack's keystone and the parable sits at #5 — a
named-passage query answered by a theme, which is the structural defect this
whole item family exists to remove.

**The displacement measurement, in full.** Generated over all 998 active
existing-fixture queries by verse-range containment on Luke 10:25-37 (not by
reference string: the related-theme rows render as sub-runs such as
`Luke 10:25-27`, which is why a string match undercounts). For design (b)
the list is empty. For r3's design it is not, and the r3 disclosure named
**two** of these:

```

favoritism           "favoritism in the bible"                                 #7

love-your-enemies    "pray for those who persecute you"         Luke 10:25-37  #2
loving-others        "love one another"                         Luke 10:25-37  #7
loving-others        "the golden rule"                          Luke 10:25-37  #1   <- the blocking row
loving-others        "treat others the way you want to be..."   Luke 10:25-37  #2
popular-1-corinthians-13-4  "love is patient love is kind"      Luke 10:25-37  #3
servanthood          "servanthood in the bible"                                #7
```

**24 new top-10 rows plus one rank move, across 16 existing fixtures.** The
critique counted 23; the difference is one row on the counting basis (it
listed fixtures, and `the-lords-discipline`'s `Luke 10:27` row is a
containment hit rather than the parable range). Either way r3 disclosed two.

**One claim in the critique's O-1 does not reproduce, and it is recorded
rather than adopted.** O-1 states that r3's disclosed `"love your neighbor"`
cost is false — *"Luke 10:25-37 is absent from all 25 results for that
query"*. Re-run on **the critique's own artifact**
(`$SCRATCH/sim-A3-crit3/db/after.db`) and on this section's independently
built r3 state, both return:

```
"love your neighbor"   6. Luke 10:25-37  43.64  [Theme: Loving one another | ...]
```

Identical to the point on both harnesses. r3's disclosure of that one row
was correct; what was wrong with r3's disclosure is that it listed two rows
out of twenty-five, and that is the half of O-1 this item fixes. The rule
this section keeps is the one S-B keeps for the same class of disagreement:
a measurement is contested with the measurement, never by substituting a
different rule — so the `"love your neighbor"` sentence is not "corrected"
into something the corpus does not say.

**Measured gap** (live, before — unchanged from r3):
```
"good samaritan"                    1. Acts 8:25 (6.87)  2. Genesis 2:18  3. John 8:48-49 (1.80)
"who is my neighbor parable"        1. Luke 15:3 (4.10)  2. Luke 6:39  3. Galatians 5:14
"the parable of the good samaritan" 1. Acts 8:25 (5.92)  2. Matthew 13:24  3. John 8:48-49
```
WEB, **John 8:48**: *"Don't we say well that you are a Samaritan, and have a
demon?"* — at rank 3. `samaritan` occurs at word boundary in only four WEB
verses (Luke 10:33, 17:16, John 4:9, 8:48), so `passage_terms` treats it as
highly distinctive, which is exactly why the insult text ranks.

**Change (r4).**
```yaml
# ontology/concepts/parable-of-the-good-samaritan.yaml — NEW
# A one-anchor named-passage pack. It exists because the alternative
# designs were measured and both cost something this register cannot pay:
# at 1.0 inside loving-others the parable takes a DIFFERENT named passage's
# query (the golden rule) and enters 24 existing top-10s; at 0.85 inside
# loving-others it cannot lead its own name. A pack of its own is the only
# shape in which the name reaches the passage and nothing else moves.
# It is also the honest shape: "the Good Samaritan" is a passage, not a
# theme, and the chip should say so.
id: parable-of-the-good-samaritan
label: The Good Samaritan
lexicon:
  - good samaritan
  - who is my neighbor parable
anchors:
  # WEB: "But a certain Samaritan, as he traveled, came where he was. When
  # he saw him, he was moved with compassion" ... "'He who showed mercy on
  # him.' Then Jesus said to him, 'Go and do likewise.'"
  # RANGE LEDGER (generated, not grepped): UNANCHORED anywhere in the
  # compiled HEAD artifact. r1's one true "unanchored" claim, confirmed.
  - { ref: Luke 10:25-37, sources: [editorial], weight: 1.0 }
related:
  # The parable's own subject, and the pack a reader should reach next.
  # MEASURED: this edge puts `Related theme: Loving one another` chips at
  # #3-#5 of "good samaritan" (Matthew 5:45, John 13:34-35, 1 Cor 13:4-6),
  # so the register is still reachable from the name — the connection r3
  # bought by anchoring into the pack is kept, without the ordering cost.
  - loving-others
```
```yaml
# ontology/lexicon-inventory.yaml — NEW row under `concepts:` (line 722).
# No `collapses:` row: both phrases are written with >= 2 raw words.
  - id: parable-of-the-good-samaritan
    # 2026-09-04 Phase A3.8 (r4): authored with the pack (fixture-first,
    # named-passage-good-samaritan.json). Phrase-forms pack; no bare word
    # fires, and all four candidate bare words are refused with reasons.
    skipped:
      - token: samaritan
        reason: >-
          WEB John 8:48 "you are a Samaritan, and have a demon" — measured
          #3 for this query before the pack. The token is distinctive
          (four WEB verses) and a bare admission would hand the insult
          text a curated chip.
      - token: parable
        reason: Every parable in the corpus; it names no passage.
      - token: neighbor
        reason: >-
          `loving-others` records a `skipped: [love]` decision for exactly
          this class; bare `neighbor` is the same class, and it belongs to
          that pack's register rather than to one parable.
      - token: good
        reason: Generic.
```

**Tokenizer hazards (run).**
```
"good samaritan"                    -> {good,samaritan}
"who is my neighbor parable"        -> {neighbor,parable}   (who/is/my are stopwords)
"the parable of the good samaritan" -> {parable,good,samaritan}  ⊇ {good,samaritan} ✓
```
`{good,samaritan}` is not contained in `{neighbor,parable}`, so the second
lexicon entry is load-bearing rather than decorative — r1 asserted the
"who is my neighbor" query and shipped no phrase that could reach it. Bare
`who is my neighbor` → `{neighbor}` is **not** proposed; see the inventory
row.

**Guards.** `mustNotLead: John 8:48-49, withinTop 3` — non-vacuous, proven:
measured **#3 today** for this exact query; absent from the top 10 after.

**Rulings for Jesse.**
- **R1 (replaces r3's ruling, which rested on a two-item cost list).** Ship
  the Good Samaritan as a **dedicated one-anchor pack** rather than as an
  anchor inside `loving-others`. The cost of the pack is one more concept
  in the ontology (295 rather than 294) and one more inventory row; the
  measured benefit is that the parable leads its own three names with its
  own chip and **zero** existing top-10 lists move. Both alternatives are
  measured in the table above, and r3's — which you were previously asked to
  ratify on a two-item cost list — is measured at 24 entries across 16
  fixtures including a named-passage inversion.
- **R2 (new).** Adopt the **named-passage rule** for the whole section (see
  the rule block near the top): every named-passage query pins its own
  passage's rank explicitly, at 1 where an alias or a dedicated pack backs
  the name, and at the measured rank with a stated reason otherwise. This is
  what turns O-1 from a fixed bug into a defended register.

**Acceptance (measured, r4).** "good samaritan", "the parable of the good
samaritan" and "who is my neighbor parable" → Luke 10:25-37 at #1 (40.00 /
22.86 / 41.94) with `Theme: The Good Samaritan`; John 8:48-49 out of the top
10 for all three; `Related theme: Loving one another` present at #3-#5.
"the golden rule" byte-identical to HEAD. Generated displacement over 998
existing-fixture queries: zero.

**Effort.** S. No dependency.

#### A3.9 "the beatitudes" → `blessing`

**Measured gap.** `the beatitudes` → `{beatitud}`; live top-3 is Matthew 5:1,
5:6, 5:4 on `passage_terms` noise at ~1.9 points — the chapter, not the
passage, and no concept fires.

**Change.** `lexicon: + beatitudes` (bare). No anchor change (Matt 5:3-12
already anchored at 0.9).

`Acts 1:4-5` ("wait for the promise of the Father") wins a query that names
**Acts 2** because its `passage_terms` chip double-counts `acts` **and**
`pentecost` on the *preceding* passage. Bare `pentecost` is fine; the more
specific query is the one that breaks, which is the wrong direction for a
search engine to fail in.

**Why no data edit fixes it, measured.** Both verses are `holy-spirit`
anchors, so a lexicon phrase (`acts 2 pentecost`, say) multiplies the whole
pack equally and re-orders nothing — verified. Raising Acts 2:1-4 from 0.95
to 1.0 yields 14.21 against Acts 1:4-5's 15.18: still second, because the
gap is the `passage_terms` chip and not the weight. Making Acts 2:1-4 lead
requires demoting `holy-spirit`'s **1.0 keystone**, which
`eval/golden/holy-spirit.json` pins by name — a keystone re-order and a
Jesse ruling (R2), not a Phase-A data edit.

So the query leaves the main fixture's `additionalQueries` and gets **its
own active fixture asserting what is true**, because the critique's real
demand was not "drop it" but "do not leave it in without measuring it".

## Occasion packs (A3.16–A3.20)

All five are **new-pack or new-register** items, so all five carry the two
structural obligations r1 missed and the critique caught:

1. a row under `concepts:` in `ontology/lexicon-inventory.yaml`
   (`eval/src/gates/lexiconInventory.ts` emits `row-missing` for *every*
   compiled concept without one — three of r1's five packs had none, three
   G4 FAILs);
2. an active fixture whose `expectedTop` carries **both**
   `requiredReasonFamily: "concept_anchor"` **and**
   `requiredReasonLabel: "Theme: <the pack's compiled label>"`
   (`corpusGolden.ts:863-871` builds `` `Theme: ${concept.label}` `` and
   iterates **every** compiled concept, so a pack with no such fixture is a
   G3 FAIL on its own).

Both are mechanical and both are shown in full below, per pack.

---

### A3.16 Occasion: NEW pack `wedding-verses`

**What the asker is really asking.** "Wedding verses" is not a doctrinal
question about marriage. It is *which texts do people read at a wedding* —
a collection request, and the honest answer is a short, ordered list of the
passages that are actually read aloud.

**Measured gap** (live, before):
```
"wedding verses"                  1. Psalms 45:1 (4.44)  2. John 2:2  3. Mark 1:29 ... 10. Mark 1:27
                                     ranks 3-10 are pure `vers` stem noise ("reversed"-class)
"wedding verse"                   1. John 2:2 (2.09)  2. Matthew 5:40  3. Matthew 6:29   (`verse` != `vers`)
"bible verses for a wedding"      1. Psalms 45:1  2. Mark 1:29  3. Luke 6:32
"wedding scripture"               1. 1 Peter 2:6  2. James 2:23  3. James 2:8
"scripture for a wedding ceremony" 1. 1 Peter 2:6  2. James 2:23  3. James 2:8
"wedding readings"                1. John 2:2  2. Hebrews 4:2  3. Psalms 78:63
```
Six typed forms, six worthless answers. `godly-marriage` owns the teaching
register and is not reachable from any of them.

**Change — a new pack that is honestly an *occasion index*.** Four of its six
anchors are already anchored elsewhere, and that is the point rather than a
defect to be hidden: the texts read at weddings are owned by other packs for
their *doctrinal* register (`loving-others` owns 1 Cor 13 as the love
command; `friendship` owns Eccl 4 as companionship; `romantic-love-and-intimacy`
owns Song 8 as eros; `caring-for-aging-parents` owns Ruth 1 as covenant
loyalty to kin). This pack claims them in a *sixth* register — read aloud at
a wedding — and every dual is disclosed in both files, the convention this
repo already uses for `2 Chronicles 7:14`'s three-way note.

```yaml
  - scripture for a wedding ceremony
```
