**Two anchors r1 proposed and this revision refuses.**

*Genesis 2:24 — refused on recorded precedent.* r1 called it "unanchored
elsewhere"; it is `pastoral-marriage-divorce-teaching.yaml:36` (compiled id
`marriage-divorce-teaching`). More decisive: `godly-marriage.yaml:11` already
records the ruling in words — *"Genesis 2:24 is deliberately NOT re-anchored
here (it belongs to marriage-divorce-teaching); the cross-link is
related:."* A third pack re-anchoring the same verse a fortnight later would
be this section overruling a recorded decision by not reading it. The
cross-link is `related:`, exactly as `godly-marriage` did. The one-flesh
sentence is not lost — **Mark 10:6-9 quotes it**, and Mark 10 is unanchored
at HEAD (S-A2 A2.3 anchors the same span at 0.9 in its new
`marriage-in-crisis` pack; C10, disclosed in the fixture note below).

*Ephesians 5:25-33 — refused in r2 on a misreading of §4; **anchored in
r3**.* r2 wrote that "DOCTRINAL-BASIS §4 makes 'gender roles in church and
home' an explicit non-criterion, and selecting the husband-only half … is a
framing choice inside exactly that non-criterion", and refused any cut.

**§4 does not say that.** Its actual text: *"The following are **not**
admission criteria, and **no source may be rejected over them**."* Its three
stated reasons are all about **source admission** — the anchor congregations
differ, three consumer apps share the artifact, and an immersionist criterion
would retroactively impugn Matthew Henry. §4 exists to stop the guardrail
becoming a denominational filter. r2 used the anti-filter clause **as** a
filter — and, worse, used it in *opposite directions* in one section: A3.18
includes Acts 2:38 because baptism's mode is a §4 non-criterion (correct: a
non-criterion is not a reason to exclude), while A3.16 excluded Ephesians 5
on the same clause. One of those readings had to be wrong, and it was this
one.

**Measured cost of the refusal**, which r2 never ran: `"wedding verses"` had
**no Ephesians verse in the top 10** — Ephesians 5:25 sat at #11 (6.00) on a
bare `Related theme: Marriage` chip — for the passage that is, after
1 Corinthians 13, the one most read at Christian weddings.

r3 therefore anchored Ephesians 5 — and then defended the span it chose,
5:25-33, as *"the whole and uncut unit — we are not excerpting the husband's
half."* **That sentence is false on the verse numbers, and it is r2's
objection recurring inside r2's own remedy.** The unit is 5:22-33, governed
by 5:21; `5:25-33` **is** the husband half; and v33, the last verse r3 kept,
still reads *"let the wife see that she respects her husband"* — so the span
neither avoided the wives material nor included its own opening. The ruling
r3 put to Jesse was framed on the premise that the excerpting problem had
been solved. It had been renamed.

**r4 decides the span on the merits and says why: `Ephesians 5:21-33`.** The
reason is a wedding-reading reason, not a doctrinal one. Verse 21 —
*"subjecting yourselves to one another in the fear of Christ"* — is the
participial clause the whole household section depends on, and it is where
the passage is opened when it is read at a wedding. Keeping v33 while
dropping v21 is the cut; taking both halves and their own opening is not a
selection at all. The engine hands over what Paul wrote, in his order, and
adjudicates nothing — which is the only footing on which this section may
carry the passage (covenant #6). Measured, the widening costs nothing in
ordering: **#3 at 34.00 for all eight typed forms, identical to 5:25-33**,
behind 1 Corinthians 13:4-8 and Mark 10:6-9.

**Where the one-flesh sentence comes from, and where Ephesians sits relative
to it.** Genesis 2:24 is deliberately not anchored here (see below), and
measured it does not appear anywhere in this query family's result set. It
reaches the reader through **Mark 10:6-9 at #2**, which quotes it — so the
ordering the owner asked for holds as stated: 1 Corinthians 13:4-8 first,
the one-flesh text second, Ephesians third.

**Tokenizer hazards (run).**
```
"wedding verses"                   -> {wedd,vers}          "wedding verse"  -> {wedd,verse}
"bible verses for a wedding"       -> {bible,vers,wedd}    ⊇ {wedd,vers} ✓
"bible verse for a wedding"        -> {bible,verse,wedd}   ⊇ {wedd,verse} ✓
"verses for a wedding"             -> {vers,wedd}          ⊇ {wedd,vers} ✓ (set-equal)
"wedding scripture"                -> {wedd,scripture}
"scripture for a wedding ceremony" -> {scripture,wedd,ceremony} ⊇ {wedd,scripture} ✓
"wedding readings"                 -> {wedd,reading}
```
Every phrase is ≥2 significant tokens **written with ≥2 raw words**, so
`collision.ts`'s `singleTokenCollapses` (which fires only when
`tokens.length === 1 && rawWords > 1`) has nothing to acknowledge here.

**The `verses`/`verse` split.** `verses` → `-es` strip (6−2 = 4 ≥ 4) →
`vers`; `verse` ends in `e`, matches no rule → `verse`. Two different
tokens, so the plural-keyed phrase cannot answer the singular query. This
pack ships **both**, which is the general fix MAJOR 21 asked for; the same
split is handled by a *bare* admission in A3.15 (`easter`) and A3.19
(`christmas`), where the occasion's own name is safely bare.

**Bare `wedding` is deliberately NOT admitted — and the refusal is
measured.** With the phrase forms above and no bare word, `wedding feast`
still returns Matthew 22:2-4 / 25:10 / Luke 12:36 / 14:8 on `exact_phrase`
(40.00) and `the wedding at cana` still returns John 2:1-2 at #1 — both
untouched by this pack. A bare `wedding` admission would have handed both
narrative queries a list of ceremony readings. That measurement is the
`skipped:` reason below.

**Guards.** r1's `mustNotLead: Proverbs 21:9` is **deleted**. Measured: WEB
Prov 21:9 is *"It is better to dwell in the corner of the housetop than to
share a house with a contentious woman"* — it carries neither `wedd` nor
`vers` nor `scripture`, and it appears nowhere in the top 10 of any of the
eight typed forms, before or after. `guardVacuityFindings` would not catch
it (the ref resolves in corpus), which is exactly why CLAUDE.md's "never let
an unrun check report `pass`" applies: it would have shipped as decoration.

One guard **is** earned, from the after-run rather than from intuition
(**re-measured in r4; r3's prose printed #7 and its own fixture note printed
#8 — the fixture note was right**):
```
AFTER, "wedding scripture" / "scripture for a wedding ceremony":
   8. Matthew 19:7  (7.43)  [concept_lexicon: Related theme: Marriage and divorce | passage_terms: scripture]
AFTER, the other six forms:
   8. Matthew 19:3-5 (6.00) [concept_lexicon: Related theme: Marriage and divorce]
```
WEB Matt 19:7: *"Why then did Moses command us to give her a certificate of
divorce and divorce her?"* — reachable in this query family today, at #7,
through this pack's own `related:` edge, and the one verse in the window a
couple planning a wedding should not be handed near the top. A
`mustNotLead … withinTop: 3` is the right instrument, and its non-vacuity
claim is narrower than r3 wrote it. **r3 claimed the ref "demonstrably ranks
at #7 in six of eight measured forms". Measured, Matthew 19:7 ranks at #8 in
exactly two of the eight** — `wedding scripture` and `scripture for a
wedding ceremony`, the two forms carrying the token `scripture`, which is
what earns 19:7 its `passage_terms` component. The other six return
**Matthew 19:3-5** at #8, a different row whose head verse (19:3) the guard
does not match. So the guard is non-vacuous by rankability on two of eight
forms, not six, and that is what the fixture now says. It still ships green
and still becomes a tripwire the moment the `related:` weighting or a future
divorce-register anchor moves it. `mustNotRank` would be wrong — the window
is 10 and the verse is legitimately at #8.

**Fixture.**
```json
{
  "id": "occasion-wedding-verses",
  "query": "wedding verses",
  "status": "active",
  "note": [

'wedding verse' (singular) returned John 2:2 then eight Matthew verses on the `verse` term; 'wedding readings' returned John 2:2 / Hebrews 4:2; 'wedding scripture' returned 1 Peter 2:6 / James 2:23.",

### A3.17 Occasion: NEW pack `baby-dedication`

**What the asker is really asking.** *We are giving this child back to God in
front of the church on Sunday — what do we read?*

**Measured gap** (live, before):

"baby dedication verses"     1. 2 Chron 7:5  2. John 10:22  3. Mark 1:29
"baby dedication verse"      1. 2 Chron 7:5  2. John 10:22  3. 2 Chron 7:8

Solomon's temple, the Feast of Dedication, and a Levitical field-vow. Nothing
in the register.

**The adjacent register r3 did not type, added in r4 (O-14).** A dedication
pack that cannot answer the sentence a person types the week the baby is
born is a pack with a hole in it, and the hole returned something worse than
noise:
```

"verses for a newborn"        1. Mark 1:29 (`vers` noise)  2. Luke 6:32  3. 1 Peter 2:2

"newborn" (bare)              1. 1 Peter 2:2 — and it is the ONLY result
```
`John 11:35` at #1 for a query about a baby being born is the single result
in this item worth the item. It is pre-existing noise rather than anything
A3.17 caused, which is exactly why nothing caught it: no fixture in the repo
types the form. r4 types it.

**The Luke anchor is narrowed, on this repo's own precedent.** r1 anchored
Luke 2:22-40, nineteen verses containing v35: *"Yes, a sword will pierce
through your own soul, that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed."*
Honest Scripture, and wrong to hand new parents at rank 5 of a dedication
query. `hell.yaml` records the identical move in words — *"the anchor keeps
the whole saying (43-48) because v48 by itself is a dangling Isaiah
quotation … same narrowing-to-the-honest-unit move as
caught-up-together"* — so narrowing to the honest unit is the house rule,
not an invention. 2:22-32 is a complete unit: it opens on "to present him to
the Lord" and closes on Simeon's blessing.

**Tokenizer hazards (run).** This is the item r1 got wrong.
```
"dedicating my baby to god"  -> {dedicat,baby,god}    <- r1's own additionalQuery
"baby dedication"            -> {baby,dedication}     NOT contained in the above
"dedicating my baby"         -> {dedicat,baby}        ⊆ {dedicat,baby,god} ✓  <- the fix
"dedicating my child to god" -> {dedicat,child,god}
"baby dedication verses"     -> {baby,dedication,vers}
"baby dedication verse"      -> {baby,dedication,verse}
"child dedication ceremony"  -> {child,dedication,ceremony}
"bible verse for a newborn"  -> {bible,verse,newborn}  ⊇ {verse,newborn} ✓
"verses for a newborn"       -> {vers,newborn}         (set-equal)      ✓
"scripture for a newborn baby" -> {scripture,newborn,baby} ⊇ {newborn,baby} ✓
"newborn" (bare)             -> {newborn}              NOT admitted
```
`dedicating` → `-ing` strip (10−3 = 7 ≥ 4) → `dedicat`; `dedication` ends in
`n` and matches no suffix rule → `dedication`. Two tokens that never meet.
r1 shipped three `dedication`-keyed phrases and then asserted that a
`dedicat`-keyed query would reach them. Adding `dedicating my baby` and
`dedicating my child to god` closes it, measured below. Every phrase is
≥2 raw words → no `collapses:` row.

**Guards.** One, earned from the after-run:
```
AFTER (r4 re-measure; r3 printed #7/#6, one rank higher, before Psalms
139:13-14 was anchored):
       Proverbs 22:6 at #8 for "baby dedication", "baby dedication verses",
       "baby dedication verse", "dedicating my baby to god" and for all
       three newborn forms; at #7 for "child dedication ceremony"
       — via related: parenting (concept_lexicon chip).
```
WEB Prov 22:6: *"Train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is
old he will not depart from it."* This is the same verse A3.7 guards for the
prodigal's parent, reached here through this pack's `related:` edge, and the
same reasoning applies one notch more gently: a proverb of formation is not
what a dedication service reads, and it should never lead. Non-vacuous by
rankability — measured at #6/#7 across five of six forms.

**Two more guards, and r2's reason for omitting them was a false reading of
the gate.** r2 wrote that Hebrews 12:5 (#7) and 2 Samuel 12:16 (#8) are
"both outside any window a guard can honestly police". They are not.
`mustNotRank` is measured inside `measuredWindow` = max(expectedTop windows,
`expectedWithinTop`), and this fixture declares `expectedWithinTop: 10`, so
the window **is 10** and #7 and #8 are inside it. The claim was wrong in the
direction that excused doing nothing, which under this section's own gate
discipline is the thing that must not stand.

Measured on the r4 after-state, `dedicating my child to god` (r3 printed #7
and #8; the Psalms 139:13-14 addition pushes both down one):
```
  8. Hebrews 12:5     9.27  [translation_variant: child, god | passage_terms: child]
  9. 2 Samuel 12:16   8.75  [proximity | token_overlap: child, god]
```
WEB Hebrews 12:5-6: *"My son, don't take lightly the chastening of the Lord…
For whom the Lord loves, he chastens."* WEB 2 Samuel 12:16: David fasting
and lying all night on the ground for the infant who then dies. On the first
page of a baby-dedication query.

**The instrument is `mustNotLead … withinTop: 3`, not `mustNotRank`, and the
reason is stated rather than assumed.** `mustNotRank` would ban them from
the whole window of 10 — and both are honest Scripture reached by pure
`child`+`god` token noise that this pack cannot remove, because no lexicon
or anchor edit changes a `translation_variant` or `proximity` hit. Banning
them would fail the fixture and demand a fix that Phase A does not have; the
real fix is B1 (tokenizer/lemma work) and it is booked as that. What this
pack *can* honestly police is the lead, and both guards are non-vacuous by
rankability — measured at #8 and #9, inside the declared window of 10, on a
query in this fixture's own list.

`magnificat` is absent from `spelling_terms`, so the spelling corrector
rewrites it to `magnifical` before matching ever runs, and the query returns
**zero results even with the entry present** — verified on the simulated
after-state. The register is real and the fix is a curated alias (equality
on `normalizedPhrase`, which runs before correction), so "the magnificat"
moves to **A3.25**, where it is measured working: an alias row returns
Luke 1:46-55 at 40.00 with the chip carrying `(query corrected from
"magnificat")`. A lexicon entry here would have been a silent no-op.

`concepts:` admission below. r1 wrote `the magnificat` / `the nativity`
(2 raw words → 1 token), which are collapses and would have failed G4.

split (MAJOR 21) for this pack, the same way `easter` does in A3.15.

```
The last line is the whole diagnosis: `new-creation`'s existing `fresh
start` phrase already answers this register correctly. The gap is only that
the words people actually type — "new year", "new year's resolution" — reach
the Hebrew civil calendar instead.

**Change — lexicon only. No anchor.**
```yaml
# ontology/concepts/new-creation.yaml — lexicon additions
lexicon:
  - new year
  - new years resolution
```
```yaml
# ontology/concepts/new-creation.yaml — related: addition
related:
  - restoration        # NEW: Isaiah 43:18-19 lives there (restoration.yaml:42)
```

**Isaiah 43:18-19 is NOT anchored, and r1's reason for anchoring it was
false.** r1: *"the most-used New Year's text across topical sources,
unanchored anywhere in this ontology."* It is
`ontology/concepts/restoration.yaml:42`, identical range. Rather than
duplicate a range a neighbouring pack already owns for the same sense
("Behold, I will do a new thing"), this item adds `restoration` to
`new-creation`'s `related:` — one hop, the neighbour's own chip, no second
home for one verse. That is the cross-reference-rather-than-duplicate rule
applied where it plainly fits.

With that, A3.20 is what the critique said it should have been from the
start: **a pure lexicon extension**, and the measurement shows it is enough.

**Tokenizer hazards (run).**
```
"new year"                     -> {new,year}
"new years resolution"         -> {new,year,resolution}      ⊇ {new,year} ✓
"new year bible verse"         -> {new,year,bible,verse}     ⊇ {new,year} ✓
"fresh start for the new year" -> {fresh,start,new,year}     ⊇ {new,year} ✓ and ⊇ {fresh,start} ✓
```
Both entries are ≥2 raw words and ≥2 tokens → no `collapses:` row, and
`new-creation`'s existing inventory row needs no `admitted:` change (nothing
new fires bare). **The `verse`/`verses` split does not bite here**: `new
year bible verse` and `new year bible verses` both contain `{new,year}`.

**Guards.** None. Measured: the after-window for all four forms is
`new-creation`'s own anchor tier — 2 Corinthians 5:17, Psalms 51:10,
Acts 3:19, Galatians 6:15, Revelation 21:5, Ezekiel 36:26. Nothing in it is
a resolution-culture or prosperity reading; there is nothing to guard.
**No guard needed today; re-check after B1.**

`["blessing", "loving-others"]`; both compile, so neither would be

under `unproven` and reads as coverage this fixture does not provide.

**Note on the runner.** `presenceOnly` is **fail-closed**: a runner that
provides no limit-50 engine emits `G3_PRESENCE_NOT_MEASURED` rather than
skipping (`corpusGolden.ts:1199-1213`). r2 added a hedge — *"if the
gauntlet's corpus runner does not yet supply `presenceEngine`, this fixture
will report a measured failure"* — and that conditional is **false and was
never checked**: `eval/src/gauntlet.ts:847-853` constructs a
`rankOptions: { limit: 50 }` engine and passes it as `{ presenceEngine }`,
with a comment saying why. The hedge is deleted. This fixture **is**
measured, by the real runner, and the r3 harness supplies the same shape.

## Phase C — curated aliases (A3.24, A3.25). Nothing here ships before B10.

**Plainly: these two items are Phase C, and both are gated on Phase B10.**
r1 claimed one of their rows was "shippable today". It was not, and neither
is anything else in this family. Three facts, each verified against the
running code rather than argued:

**1. The live importer reads exactly one top-level key, and ignores the rest
in silence.** `pipeline/src/importers/aliasImporter.ts:20-33` declares
`HymnAliasPackSource { sourceId; hymns? }` and `:127` iterates
`parsed.hymns ?? []`. `ontology/aliases/hymn-lines.yaml` confirms the live
shape (`sourceId: hymn-aliases`, then `hymns:`). r1's two proposed files
both used **`entries:`**, so `parsed.hymns` would be `undefined`, the loop
would never run, **no error would be pushed**, and the build would stay
green with zero rows compiled. That is precisely the failure mode the
importer's own header says it exists to prevent — *"an alias row that
silently does nothing … is worse than one that loudly does not exist"* —
reintroduced by the plan that quoted the header. Every YAML block below now
uses B10's keys.

**2. Every alias chip says `Hymn:` today, whatever the row is.** Measured,
2026-09-04, by inserting four alias rows into a scratch copy of
`pipeline/output/fixture.db` and re-running the engine:
```
"the magnificat"        1. Luke 1:46-55   40.00  concept_anchor: Hymn: "The Magnificat" (query corrected from "magnificat")
"romans road"           1. Acts 16:30-31  40.00  concept_anchor: Hymn: "Romans Road" → Theme: Salvation
"sermon on the mount"   1. Matthew 5:1-7:29 42.43 concept_anchor: Hymn: "Sermon on the Mount"
"god helps those…"      1. Isaiah 41:10   47.23  concept_anchor: Hymn: "God helps those who help themselves — not in the Bible"
```
`engine/src/intents/concept.ts:246` and `:268` hardcode `Hymn: "…"` in both
alias arms. The last line is the argument in one image: a reader asking
about a proverb that is not in the Bible would be told it is a **hymn**.
CLAUDE.md #5 — "a result that ranks correctly but carries the wrong reason
is a G3 failure, not a cosmetic bug" — settles it. **No alias-shaped row
may ship until B10's per-kind labels land.**

**3. `curated_alias` is not a signal family.** r1's fixtures asserted
`requiredReasonFamily: "curated_alias"`. `SignalFamily`
(`engine/src/reasons/types.ts`) is `reference | exact_phrase |
concept_anchor | concept_lexicon | token_overlap | translation_variant |
proximity | passage_terms | cross_reference | co_citation`. Both alias arms
emit **`concept_anchor`** (measured above). Every fixture below is corrected.

**Owner ruling 17 owns the `saying` contract; this section copies it and
does not restate it.** The round-3 critique found four ways A3.24/A3.25 and
§B.10 contradicted each other while each cited the other's assent, which is
the failure mode a two-section spec has. Ruling 17 resolves all four in
§B.10's favour as the single owner, and r4 rewrote both items to it:

| conflict (r3) | ruling 17 |
|---|---|
| B.10: "saying + range = build error"; A3.24: five range-targeted rows | **`range:` XOR `concept:`, exactly like `hymn`.** The build-error rule is withdrawn. |
| B.10 chip `Saying: "…" — <note> → Theme: <label>`; A3.24 fixtures pinned `Saying: "…" (<note>)` | **Per arm.** Range: `Saying: "<title>" — <note> → <reference>`. Concept: `Saying: "<title>" — <note> → Theme: <label>`. A3.24's fixtures are re-pinned to the range form, character for character. |
| B.10's `ADMITTED_SAYING_NOTES` did not contain A3.24's notes | **The vocabulary is extended to the exact notes A3.24 uses**, which A3.24 now lists in one table so B.10 can copy them. One new value. |
| B.10: Romans Road ships as a `the-romans-road` concept; A3.25: "no alias row, no lexicon phrase, no pack" | **Neither.** The phrase `romans road` on the **existing `salvation` pack**, fixture-first — no new concept, no alias row. A3.1 carries the line; A3.25 carries the reasoning; A3.1's `named-passage-romans-road` carries the fixture. |

`forbiddenReasonLabelSubstrings: ["Theme:"]` is deleted from A3.24's fixture
in the same ruling.

**Five further B10 clarifications this section depends on (agreed with the
engine section, r3, and unchanged by ruling 17).** These are the points
A3.22/A3.24/A3.25 are written against, and each one changed a row or a
fixture here:

1. **`phrases:` is a LIST per row, and every typed variant gets its own
   entry.** `aliasImporter.ts:31` already accepts
   `phrases: [{ phrase, weight }]`, and `normalized_raw` uniqueness (`:230`)
   is per **key**, not per row — so multiple keys per row are legal today.
   §B.10 said neither, and r2 read the silence as one phrase per row.
   Measured cost of that reading, with r2's exact rows installed:
   `the sermon on the mount` → John 8:1 at 3.23; `lords prayer` →
   Matthew 6:9-13 at **#3**. Every row in A3.25 now ships every form.
2. **Presence is matched on the group's START verse id, so a
   `named-passage` row's `range:` is what a fixture must pin.**
   `hitInRange` reads `verseIdOf(entry.targetId)`
   (`corpusGolden.ts:809-812`). A3.22's `Matthew 5:3-12` pin against
   A3.25's `Matthew 5:1-7:29` row was unsatisfiable; the fixture now pins
   the row's range.
3. **Global `normalized_raw` uniqueness is kept, and is a KNOWN LIMIT:
   one phrase, one target.** "This too shall pass" therefore gets one lead
   verse (2 Cor 4:17-18) and not two. Recorded as a deliberate non-goal in
   §B.10 itself rather than left for A3.24 to discover.
4. **A named passage that is not a contiguous range is a LEXICON PHRASE on
   the owning concept, not an alias row.** `kind: named-passage` forbids a
   `concept:` target, so "Romans Road" (five verses across three chapters)
   has no alias home. Under ruling 17 it does not get a concept of its own
   either: the phrase goes on `salvation`, which already anchors the
   register. A3.13 proves the alternative works, and A3.7's one-line
   `prodigal son` fix proves it again, measured.
5. **`sourceLabel` gains `misquotes` and `named-passages`, and
   `pipeline/manifests/misquotes.json` / `named-passages.json` must be
   admitted before any Phase-C row ships.** This belongs in B's own
   dependency list, not only here.

**What B10 otherwise specifies** (read from
`$SCRATCH/plan/sections/S-B-engine-determinism.md` §B.10, not paraphrased):
per-file `kind: hymn | saying | named-passage`; `sayings:` rows carry
`text` / `origin` / `note` and keep the concept-XOR-range target (ruling
17); `passages:` rows carry `name` / `range` and a **concept target is
forbidden**; the compiled `title` is mapped per kind (`hymns[].title` /
`sayings[].text` / `passages[].name`); labels become
`Saying: "${title}" — ${note} → ${reference}` on the range arm,
`Saying: "${title}" — ${note} → Theme: ${label}` on the concept arm, and
`Passage: ${title}` for a named passage; `curated_aliases` gains `kind` and
`note` in schema v10. Kept for every kind: ≥2 raw words, global `normalizedRaw`
uniqueness, the double-chip guard, `weight` in (0, 1].

**Which live importer field blocks each proposed row TODAY** — the table the
owner asked for, re-derived, with the file key added because it is the field
that decides whether any row is read at all:

| row | blocked today by | resolved by B10? |
|---|---|---|
| *all rows, both files* | **file key.** `parsed.hymns ?? []` — an `entries:`/`sayings:`/`passages:` key compiles to nothing, silently (`:127`) | **yes** — `sayings:` / `passages:` are read |
| "god helps those who help themselves" | `year` must be an integer (`:138-141`); `author` must be a non-empty string (`:134-137`) — a folk proverb has neither honestly | **yes** — `kind: saying` requires `text`/`origin`/`note`, no author, no year |
| "this too shall pass" | same `author`/`year`; **and** `normalizedRaw` global uniqueness (`:230-237`) if both 2 Cor 4:17-18 and Psalms 30:5 are wanted | **partly** — the author/year block goes and ruling 17 unblocks the range target; **the uniqueness block remains**, because B10 keeps `:230` verbatim and ruling 17 does not touch it. One phrase, one target, still. |
| "god won't give you more than you can handle" | `year` (`:138-141`): no dateable origin exists | **yes** (range arm, ruling 17) |
| "cleanliness is next to godliness" | the `concept`/`range` **XOR** itself (`:150-156`): no way to express "correction only, no scriptural target" | **no** — B10 keeps the XOR. Stays skipped (recommended). |
| "money is the root of all evil" | `author` (`:134-137`) is asked to name a human source for a *Scripture* misquote | **yes** — `origin` is the honest field |
| "spare the rod, spoil the child" | nothing hard; `author`/`year` are honest here (Samuel Butler, *Hudibras*, 1664) | n/a — but the chip would still read `Hymn:` |
| "romans road" | `year` (`:138-141`) — r1's own row wrote `year: null` and `typeof null === 'object'`, a hard build error | **not applicable — it is no longer an alias row.** Owner ruling 17: it ships as the lexicon phrase `romans road` on the existing `salvation` pack, fixture-first. B10 still forbids a `concept:` target under `kind: named-passage` and the Romans Road is still not a contiguous range; what changed is that it needs neither. |
| "sermon on the mount" | `author`/`year` (`:134-141`); the range itself is fine — `parseAnchorRef("Matthew 5:1-7:29")` resolves to 40005001–40007029 (verified) | **yes** — `kind: named-passage` needs only `name` + `range` |
| "the magnificat" | `author`/`year`; otherwise clean | **yes** |

**G1 source manifest.** B10 extends `sourceLabel` for two new source ids, so
before any row ships, `pipeline/manifests/misquotes.json` and

### A3.24 Misquotes alias file — `ontology/aliases/misquotes.yaml` (Phase C, gated on B10)

**What changed in r4, and why the whole item was unbuildable before.** The
round-3 critique read §B.10 verbatim against this item and found that it did
not compile: B.10 said *"a saying with a range target is a build error"* and
**all five** rows here are range-targeted; B.10's chip form was
`Saying: "…" — <note> → Theme: <label>` and this item's fixtures pinned a
different string; B.10's `ADMITTED_SAYING_NOTES` did not contain the notes
this item shipped; and one fixture carried
`forbiddenReasonLabelSubstrings: ["Theme:"]`, which would have rejected the
only label B.10 permitted. Two sections of one plan gave an engineer
opposite instructions and each cited the other's assent.

**Owner ruling 17 settles it, and this item is now written to the settled
contract.** A `saying` row may carry **either** a `range:` **or** a
`concept:`, exactly like a `hymn` row, and the chip is chosen per arm:

| arm | chip |
|---|---|
| `saying` + `range:` | `Saying: "<title>" — <note> → <reference>` |
| `saying` + `concept:` | `Saying: "<title>" — <note> → Theme: <label>` |

`<reference>` is the row's declared `range:`, rendered canonically — the
same string a fixture's expectation carries. **All five rows below take the
range arm**, so every chip in this item is of the first form.

**The exact `note:` values this item uses**, so §B.10's
`ADMITTED_SAYING_NOTES` can copy them rather than guess:

| note | rows using it |
|---|---|
| `not in the Bible` | `god helps those who help themselves`, `this too shall pass`, `spare the rod spoil the child` |
| `a paraphrase, not a quotation` | `god wont give you more than you can handle` |
| `a misquotation of the verse it names` | `money is the root of all evil` |

Two of the three are already in B.10's vocabulary. **One value is new:
`a misquotation of the verse it names`** — and it is deliberately generic,
because the alternative r3 shipped (`the verse says "the love of money is a
root of all kinds of evil"`) embeds one passage's wording in a vocabulary
that is supposed to be reusable, and reads as the engine correcting the
reader rather than the pack stating a fact about a phrase. The verse itself
is on the chip already, as `→ 1 Timothy 6:10`. B.10's other two admitted
values (`not a Bible verse`, `often attributed to the Bible`) are unused
here and are not removed — B.10 keeps them marked `# reserved`, which is what
its own both-directions pipeline test admits for an entry no shipped row uses
(C6). B.10's admitted list is now exactly these three values plus those two,
and the two r3 strings it wrongly attributed to this item are gone.

**Measured gap.** No misquote/correction mechanism exists. Every phrase in
this family either collapses to a dangerous generic token under lexicon
containment matching, or hijacks unrelated queries even at two-plus tokens:
```
"god helps those who help themselves"      -> {god,help}       <- would fire on "please God help me"
"this too shall pass"                      -> {pass}           <- one token; a lexicon entry here is the F5 class
"money is the root of all evil"            -> {money,root,evil}
"spare the rod spoil the child"            -> {spare,rod,spoil,child}
"god wont give you more than you can handle"-> {god,wont,give,handle}
"cleanliness is next to godliness"         -> {cleanliness,next,godliness}
```
Alias matching is **equality on `normalizedPhrase`** (stopwords kept, no
stemming), never containment, so a row can only ever answer the exact line
it names. `"this too shall pass"` is four raw words even though its
significant form is the single dangerous token `{pass}` — which is the
whole reason this family is alias-shaped and not lexicon-shaped.

**Live baseline for all five rows** — re-run on `pipeline/output/fixture.db`,
unmodified. r3 measured two of the five and shipped three unmeasured
(MAJOR O-9); the three it skipped include the one query the item's own
"stated bar" names.
```
"god helps those who help themselves"
  1. Psalms 3:2  10.10   2. Psalms 46:5  10.09   3. 2 Chronicles 26:7  9.64   (`god`+`help` noise)

"spare the rod spoil the child"
  1. Proverbs 22:15  7.29  [proximity | token_overlap: child, rod]
  2. 1 Kings 16:11   6.00  [translation_variant: child, spare]
  3. Proverbs 23:13  5.96  [proximity | token_overlap: child, rod]
  4. Proverbs 29:15  5.64  [proximity | token_overlap: child, rod]
  (Proverbs 13:24 is ABSENT from all 25 results)

"this too shall pass"                                        <- UNMEASURED IN r3
  1. Deuteronomy 2:18  5.00  [token_overlap: pass]   ("You are to pass over through Ar")
  2. 2 Samuel 15:33  5.00   3. Psalms 37:36  5.00   4. Psalms 48:4  5.00
  (pure `pass` token noise, twenty-five rows deep, no curated claim anywhere in it)

"god wont give you more than you can handle"                 <- UNMEASURED IN r3
  1. Psalms 44:21  7.99   2. Exodus 3:19  7.72   3. Deuteronomy 13:12  7.43
  (1 Corinthians 10:13 absent from all 25)

"money is the root of all evil"                              <- UNMEASURED IN r3
  1. 1 Timothy 6:6-10  (the right passage already, uncorrected)  2. Philippians 4:11-13  3. Hebrews 13:5
```
r2 wrote, twice, that "Proverbs 13:24 already leads this query lexically" and
built the ship/no-ship rule on it — *"the alias's value here is the CHIP …
not the ranking."* **Proverbs 13:24 does not lead that query; it does not
rank at all.** The row's effect is not cosmetic: it replaces the #1 result.

And the true before-state is a better argument for the row than the false
one was. A parent typing this sentence is handed, today, on pure token noise
with no curated claim behind any of it: Proverbs 22:15 ("The rod of
correction drives [folly] far from him"), 1 Kings 16:11, Proverbs 23:13 ("If
you punish him with the rod, he will not die"), Proverbs 29:15. **Measured
after, with the row installed:** 1. Proverbs 13:24 (40.71, the alias chip),
then Proverbs 22:15 #2, 1 Kings 16:11 #3, Proverbs 23:13 #4, Proverbs 29:15
#5 — each pushed down exactly one rank, none suppressed. The correction
leads and the rod verses remain visible below it, which is the honest shape
for this family.

**`this too shall pass` is the row the item exists for, and r3 shipped it
with no fixture.** Its before-state is `Deuteronomy 2:18` — *"You are to
pass over through Ar"* — at 5.00, matched on the single token `pass`,
followed by twenty-four more rows of the same. A person typing the sentence
people say at funerals and in hospital corridors gets a border-crossing
itinerary. **Measured with the row installed: 1. 2 Corinthians 4:17-18
(40.00)**, *"our light affliction, which is for the moment, works for us
more and more exceedingly an eternal weight of glory"*, and the `pass`
noise falls to #2 and below, unsuppressed. It now has a fixture.

The ship/no-ship rule, with its premise repaired: **a misquote row ships
when it can name a real origin AND has an honest scriptural target to
correct toward.** "Spare the rod" has both (Butler, *Hudibras*, 1664;
Proverbs 13:24 is the verse people think they are quoting). "Cleanliness is
next to godliness" has the first and not the second, so it stays skipped.

**Change (B10 shape, ruling 17).**
```yaml
# ontology/aliases/misquotes.yaml — PROPOSED, PHASE C, BLOCKED ON B10
sourceId: misquotes
kind: saying
sayings:
  - text: god helps those who help themselves
    origin: >-
      Algernon Sidney, Discourses Concerning Government (1698); popularized
      in English by Franklin's Poor Richard's Almanack (1736).
    note: not in the Bible
    # RULING NEEDED — see below. B10's illustrative row targets
    # `concept: work-and-diligence`; this section proposes the range
    # instead, and says why. Under ruling 17 both arms compile, so this is
    # a judgment call and no longer a schema question.
    range: "Isaiah 41:10"
    phrases: [{ phrase: god helps those who help themselves, weight: 1.0 }]
    # CHIP: Saying: "god helps those who help themselves" — not in the Bible → Isaiah 41:10
  - text: this too shall pass
    origin: >-
      Persian/Sufi proverb (Attar of Nishapur, 12th c.), popularized in
      English by Edward FitzGerald.
    note: not in the Bible
    range: "2 Corinthians 4:17-18"
    # KNOWN LIMIT B10 DOES NOT CLOSE: a second row for Psalms 30:5 on this
    # SAME phrase is rejected by normalizedRaw uniqueness (aliasImporter
    # :230), which ruling 17 does not touch. One lead verse only.
    phrases: [{ phrase: this too shall pass, weight: 1.0 }]
    # CHIP: Saying: "this too shall pass" — not in the Bible → 2 Corinthians 4:17-18
  - text: god wont give you more than you can handle
    origin: Folk paraphrase of 1 Corinthians 10:13; no identifiable author.
    # `a paraphrase, not a quotation` is B10's OWN admitted value and it is
    # used verbatim. r3 shipped "a paraphrase — the verse is about
    # temptation, not hardship", which is a build error against the
    # vocabulary AND a reading of the verse rather than a fact about the
    # phrase. The reading belongs in the item, not on the chip: WEB
    # 1 Cor 10:13 is about `peirasmos` — testing/temptation — and the folk
    # form transfers it to bereavement and illness. The engine does not
    # say that; this file does, to its reviewers.
    note: a paraphrase, not a quotation
    range: "1 Corinthians 10:13"
    phrases: [{ phrase: god wont give you more than you can handle, weight: 1.0 }]
    # CHIP: Saying: "god wont give you more than you can handle" — a paraphrase, not a quotation → 1 Corinthians 10:13
  - text: money is the root of all evil
    origin: >-
      A misquotation of 1 Timothy 6:10 itself, not an external saying.
    note: a misquotation of the verse it names
    range: "1 Timothy 6:10"
    phrases: [{ phrase: money is the root of all evil, weight: 1.0 }]
    # CHIP: Saying: "money is the root of all evil" — a misquotation of the verse it names → 1 Timothy 6:10
    # MEASURED, AND IT CHANGES THE FIXTURE: the row's verse falls inside
    # contentment.yaml's 1 Timothy 6:6-10 anchor, so `collapseRuns`
    # (createEngine.ts:998) merges them and the RENDERED reference is
    # `1 Timothy 6:6-10`, carrying BOTH this chip and `Theme: Contentment`.
    # The fixture therefore pins `1 Timothy 6:6-10` — the row that exists —
    # while the chip still points at v10, which is the verse being
    # misquoted. This is the only row in either Phase-C file whose
    # rendered reference differs from its declared range, and it is the
    # kind of thing a fixture written from the YAML rather than from a run
    # gets wrong.
  - text: spare the rod spoil the child
    origin: Samuel Butler, Hudibras (1664) — satirical, not biblical.
    note: not in the Bible
    range: "Proverbs 13:24"
    phrases: [{ phrase: spare the rod spoil the child, weight: 1.0 }]
    # CHIP: Saying: "spare the rod spoil the child" — not in the Bible → Proverbs 13:24
  # "cleanliness is next to godliness" — SKIPPED, no row. The honest answer
  # is "not in the Bible, and no verse says this," and the concept/range XOR
  # has no way to express a correction with no scriptural target. Psalms
  # 51:10 was considered and rejected: it is moral, not physical, cleanness,
  # and forcing it would be the engine adjudicating (covenant 6). Ruling 17
  # does NOT unblock this row — it widens the target arms, and this row's
  # problem is that it wants no target at all.
```
Note what the `note:` field buys, and why it is not a verdict: it puts a
fact about the phrase's **origin** on the chip, stated by the pack. "Not in
the Bible" is a provenance claim, not the engine judging the sentiment,
which covenant #6 forbids. The two non-default values say the same kind of
thing: that a phrase is a paraphrase rather than a quotation, and that a
phrase misquotes the verse it is pointing at. Neither says whether the
saying is *true*.

**The `forbiddenReasonLabelSubstrings: ["Theme:"]` guard is DELETED**, on
the owner's ruling, and the measurement says the ruling is right twice over.
r3 put it on the "god helps those" fixture to stop the correction reading as
a list of supporting texts. (1) Under B.10's concept arm it forbade the only
label B.10 permitted — self-cancelling. (2) Under the range arm it would
still be wrong, and the sibling row proves it: `money is the root of all
evil` returns `1 Timothy 6:6-10` at #1 carrying **both** the saying chip and
`Theme: Contentment`, because the corrected verse is legitimately anchored
by a concept pack. A guard that forbids `Theme:` anywhere in the window

1. **`range: Isaiah 41:10` vs. B10's illustrative `concept: work-and-diligence`
   for "god helps those who help themselves"** — recommended: the range.
   Routing the query to a diligence pack half-endorses the saying: it answers
   *"yes, and here is the Bible on working hard"*, whereas the saying's
   actual defect is its account of **who helps whom**. WEB Isaiah 41:10:
   *"Don't you be afraid, for I am with you… I will strengthen you. Yes, I
   will help you."* Under ruling 17 both arms compile, so this is a judgment
   and not a constraint. (Checked: no `work-and-diligence` lexicon phrase's
   token set is contained in `{god,help}`, so the double-chip guard passes
   either way.)
2. **One new `note` value.** `a misquotation of the verse it names` joins
   `ADMITTED_SAYING_NOTES`. The other two values this file uses are already
   admitted. Confirm the value, or name a different generic phrasing —
   but not a verse-specific sentence, for the reason in the item.
3. **B10 does not close the multi-target gap.** `normalizedRaw` uniqueness
   is kept verbatim by ruling 17, so "this too shall pass" gets one lead
   verse (2 Cor 4:17-18) and not two. Accept one lead, or extend B10 to
   allow an ordered target list?
4. Confirm **"cleanliness is next to godliness" stays skipped** —
   recommended; ruling 17 widens the target arms and this row's problem is
   that it honestly wants no target at all.

### A3.25 Named-passages alias file — `ontology/aliases/named-passages.yaml` (Phase C, gated on B10)

**What changed in r4.** Two things, both because r3 and §B.10 contradicted
each other and each cited the other's agreement (the round-3 blocking
objection O-2):

1. **The Romans Road ruling is WITHDRAWN.** r3 ruled "no alias row, no
   lexicon phrase, no pack" and attributed the rule to B.10; B.10 said the
   Romans Road "ships as a small concept (`the-romans-road`) with those
   verses as weighted anchors and 'romans road' as a lexicon phrase". Owner
   ruling 17 settles it, and neither text was right: it ships as **the
   lexicon phrase `romans road` on the existing `salvation` pack** — no new
   pack, no alias row, fixture-first. The line lands in A3.1 (where the file
   is) and the fixture is `named-passage-romans-road`. The measurement and
   the limit are below.
2. **The Beatitudes row now exists**, closing r3's dangling cross-reference:
   A3.9 said the span decision was "Booked in A3.25", A3.25 had no such row,
   and §B.10 said the decision was "recorded in S-A3". It was recorded
   nowhere. It is recorded here, with the span and the reason.

**Measured gap.** Named passages a person types by name that the engine
cannot reach — and, in r3, the typed *variants* of each, because that is
where r2's one-key-per-row reading measurably failed:

"1 corinthians 13 love chapter" 1 Corinthians 13:4-8 absent from all 25

**"The magnificat" is the strongest case in this section for the alias
mechanism, and it is measured.** A lexicon entry cannot serve it: the token
`magnificat` is absent from `spelling_terms`, so the corrector rewrites the
query to `magnifical` before concept matching runs and the query returns
zero results **even with the entry present** (verified on the simulated
after-state — this is the defect that moved the register out of A3.19).
Alias matching keys on `normalizedPhrase` and survives the correction:
```
with a scratch alias row:  "the magnificat" -> 1. Luke 1:46-55  40.00
                              chip: Hymn: "The Magnificat" (query corrected from "magnificat")
```
Right passage, right score, wrong word — `Hymn:` — which is B10's job to fix
and the reason this row is `pending` rather than shipped.

**Change (B10 shape).**
```yaml
# ontology/aliases/named-passages.yaml — PROPOSED, PHASE C, BLOCKED ON B10
sourceId: named-passages
kind: named-passage
passages:
  # EVERY ROW CARRIES EVERY TYPED FORM (r3). `phrases:` is a list and
  # `normalized_raw` uniqueness (:230) is per KEY, not per row
  # (aliasImporter.ts:31), so this is a data choice and was always
  # available. r2 gave each row ONE key and, measured, one of the two forms
  # a person actually types missed on two of the three rows.
  - name: The Magnificat
    range: "Luke 1:46-55"
    # ONE key only, and the reason is measured rather than stylistic: bare
    # `magnificat` returns ZERO results whatever we do, because the token is
    # absent from spelling_terms and the corrector rewrites it to
    # `magnifical` before matching runs. A `magnificat` key would compile,
    # never fire, and read as coverage. Recorded as a known dead form.
    phrases: [{ phrase: the magnificat, weight: 1.0 }]
  - name: The Sermon on the Mount
    range: "Matthew 5:1-7:29"     # parseAnchorRef resolves this to 40005001-40007029 (verified)
    phrases:
      - { phrase: sermon on the mount, weight: 1.0 }
      - { phrase: the sermon on the mount, weight: 1.0 }
  - name: The Lord's Prayer
    range: "Matthew 6:9-13"
    phrases:
      - { phrase: the lords prayer, weight: 1.0 }
      - { phrase: lords prayer, weight: 1.0 }
  - name: The Love Chapter
    range: "1 Corinthians 13:4-8"
    # Range is 13:4-8 rather than 13:1-13: it is the range loving-others
    # already anchors and the unit actually read aloud, and A3.16 anchors
    # the same range for the wedding register.
    phrases:
      - { phrase: the love chapter, weight: 1.0 }
      - { phrase: love chapter, weight: 1.0 }
      - { phrase: 1 corinthians 13 love chapter, weight: 1.0 }
  # NEW ROW IN r4 — the row A3.9 has pointed at since r3 and §B.10 said was
  # "recorded in S-A3". See "The Beatitudes span decision" below.
  - name: The Beatitudes
    range: "Matthew 5:3-12"
    # ONE key. Bare `beatitudes` is one raw word and fails aliasImporter's
    # >= 2-raw-word floor (:194), so it CANNOT be an alias key at all; it
    # stays served by A3.9's lexicon entry at #3, which is what A3.9's
    # fixture pins.
    phrases: [{ phrase: the beatitudes, weight: 1.0 }]
  # "Romans Road" — NO ROW. Not a contiguous range, and `kind:
  # named-passage` forbids a concept target. It ships as a LEXICON PHRASE
  # on the existing salvation pack (A3.1), per owner ruling 17. See below.
```

**The Beatitudes span decision — recorded here, as §B.10 asks.** B.10's
worked example for the `named-passage` kind was originally the Beatitudes,
and B.10 moved it to the Lord's Prayer because of a real trap: an alias
row's presence is matched on the group's **start verse id**
(`corpusGolden.ts:809-812`, `hitInRange` over `verseIdOf(entry.targetId)`),
so two overlapping ranges cannot both be asserted against the same row —
and `Matthew 5:3` falls inside any Sermon-on-the-Mount range. B.10 asked
S-A3 to "pick one span, assert it, and do not admit the enclosing one".

The decision, and the honest version of the constraint:

- **The span is `Matthew 5:3-12`** — the blessings themselves, from "Blessed
  are the poor in spirit" to "for great is your reward in heaven". Not
  5:1-12 (5:1-2 is the narrator setting the scene) and not 5:3-16 (the salt
  and light sayings are a different unit). It is also the range `blessing`
  already anchors at 0.9, so the alias and the concept name the same text.
- **The enclosing Sermon range is admitted, under a different name, and that
  is not the trap B.10 named.** The trap is two overlapping expectations
  inside *one fixture* matching the same row. Here the two rows are reached
  by disjoint phrase keys — alias matching is equality on
  `normalizedPhrase`, so `the beatitudes` can never reach the Sermon row and
  `sermon on the mount` can never reach the Beatitudes row — and each
  fixture asserts exactly one range. **Measured**, with both rows installed:
  `the beatitudes` returns **Matthew 5:3-12 at 61.69**, and `sermon on the
  mount` returns **Matthew 5:1-7:29 at 42.43**; neither query returns the
  other's row. What S-A3 must *not* do is add a second key for the same
  passage under the enclosing range, or write a fixture that pins both — and
  it does neither.

**Measured, with all five rows installed on the r4 after-state:**
```
"the magnificat"                 1. Luke 1:46-55       40.00   [Hymn: "The Magnificat" (query corrected from "magnificat")]
"magnificat"                     (zero results — spelling corrector; known dead form)
"sermon on the mount"            1. Matthew 5:1-7:29   42.43   [Hymn: "The Sermon on the Mount"]
"the sermon on the mount"        1. Matthew 5:1-7:29   42.43   [same]      <- r2: John 8:1 at 3.23
"the lords prayer"               1. Matthew 6:9-13     81.36   [Hymn: "The Lord's Prayer" | Theme: Prayer]
"lords prayer"                   1. Matthew 6:9-13     81.36   [same]      <- r2: #3
"the love chapter"               1. 1 Corinthians 13:4-8  45.70 [Hymn: "The Love Chapter"]
"love chapter"                   1. 1 Corinthians 13:4-8  45.70 [same]
"1 corinthians 13 love chapter"  1. 1 Corinthians 13:4-8  40.00 [same]     <- r2: 1 Cor 13 absent from all 25
"the beatitudes"                 1. Matthew 5:3-12     61.69   [Hymn: "The Beatitudes" | Theme: Blessing]   <- NEW in r4; was #3
"beatitudes" (bare)              1. Ephesians 1:3, Matthew 5:3-12 at #3     <- unchanged; 1 raw word cannot be a key
```
Eleven typed forms, nine of them led by the named passage, and the two that
are not are blocked by the corrector (`magnificat`) and by the ≥2-raw-word
floor (`beatitudes`) rather than by this file. The only thing failing in all
nine is the word `Hymn:`.

**"romans road": the ruling r3 put to Jesse is WITHDRAWN, and the phrase
ships.** r3 ruled "no alias row, no lexicon phrase, no pack" on the ground
that a lexicon phrase would deliver `salvation`'s own order under the name
of a five-verse sequence. The reasoning is still true; the conclusion was
the wrong one, and §B.10 said the opposite in the same plan. Owner ruling 17
settles it as: **the lexicon phrase `romans road` on the existing
`salvation` pack — no new concept, no alias row, fixture-first.** Three
things stay true and are stated rather than shipped around:

1. **It is not an alias row.** `kind: named-passage` forbids a `concept:`
   target, and Rom 3:23 / 6:23 / 5:8 / 10:9-10 / 10:13 is not a contiguous
   range. r1's proposed row also wrote `year: null` against an integer
   check (`typeof null === 'object'`) and would not have compiled at all.
2. **It is not a new pack.** B.10's `the-romans-road` sketch would mint a
   concept whose five anchors duplicate `salvation`'s register under a
   second `Theme:` chip, for one query. Owner ruling 17 narrows it to the
   phrase, which is what A3.13 and A3.7 have already proved works.
3. **What it delivers, measured and disclosed.** With the one line on
   `salvation`: `"romans road"` → 1. Acts 16:30-31 (40.00) 2. Romans 10:9
   (38.00) 3. Ephesians 2:8 (38.00) 4. 1 John 1:9 5. John 14:6; Romans 10:13
   at #12, John 3:16 at #17. That is `salvation`'s anchor order under the
   name of a sequence — a good answer to *"how is a person saved"* and **not
   the Romans Road**. Two of the five sequence verses are in `salvation`'s
   anchor set at all, and neither leads. The before-state was
   `John 11:48 / Luke 19:36 / Isaiah 49:11` on `roman`/`road` token noise
   with no curated claim in the whole list, so the line is a large
   improvement over nothing and is still not the thing the name means. The
   real fix is a `sequence:` target — an ordered list of ranges under one
   name — which is a B10+ **schema** question, not a Phase-A data question,
   and it is booked as one.

The fixture (`named-passage-romans-road`, in A3.1 where the lexicon line
lands) pins what is true — the pack answers, with its own chip — and records
what is not. A fixture pinning Romans 3:23 at #1 would assert a state no
data edit in this section can produce.

**Interaction with A3.22 and with the Lord's-Prayer callout.** "Sermon on
the mount" has **three** candidate designs — a dedicated pack (A3.22's
pending fixture), a lexicon extension, and this `passages:` row — and they
must not all land, or one query gets two authoritative chips. The
`passages:` row is the cheapest and the most honest (a named passage IS a
range), and it is what this section recommends; A3.22's fixture stays
`pending` precisely so the measurement decides. Similarly the Lord's-Prayer
row here would answer *"the lords prayer"* at equality without touching
`prayer.yaml`'s internal ordering — related to the B6 callout but not a
substitute for it.

**Tokenizer / importer hazards (run).**
```
normalizedPhrase("the magnificat")               = "the magnificat"               2 raw words ✓
normalizedPhrase("sermon on the mount")          = "sermon on the mount"          4 raw words ✓
normalizedPhrase("the sermon on the mount")      = "the sermon on the mount"      5 raw words ✓
normalizedPhrase("the lords prayer")             = "the lords prayer"             3 raw words ✓
normalizedPhrase("lords prayer")                 = "lords prayer"                 2 raw words ✓
normalizedPhrase("the love chapter")             = "the love chapter"             3 raw words ✓
normalizedPhrase("love chapter")                 = "love chapter"                 2 raw words ✓
normalizedPhrase("1 corinthians 13 love chapter")= "1 corinthians 13 love chapter" 5 raw words ✓
normalizedPhrase("the beatitudes")               = "the beatitudes"               2 raw words ✓
normalizedPhrase("beatitudes")                   = "beatitudes"                   1 raw word  ✗ REJECTED (:194)
```
Nine of ten clear the ≥2-raw-word floor; the tenth is the reason bare

`aliasImporter.ts:209`'s double-chip guard does not apply (it runs only when
`conceptId !== null`). All nine keys are unique against `hymn-lines.yaml`
and against A3.24's five keys — checked pairwise, and compiled together in
the r4 harness without a uniqueness error.

**Anchors.** N/A. Ranges verified: Luke 1:46-55, Matthew 6:9-13,
1 Corinthians 13:4-8 and Matthew 5:3-12 resolve;
`parseAnchorRef("Matthew 5:1-7:29")` resolves to 40005001–40007029, and the
scratch run returns the grouped range `Matthew 5:1-7:29` as a single result
at 42.43.

**Guards.** None. Measured: with the rows in place, each query returns its
named passage at #1 and nothing else above the noise floor — there is
nothing in the window to protect against. **No guard needed today; re-check
after B10 lands and the labels change.**

## Critic responses

Three places where this revision does **not** simply comply. Each is a
measurement or a code reading, not an argument.

#### 1. MAJOR 15's alternative fix is not available — measured

The objection is correct: `mustNotRank: Proverbs 21:9` on a "wedding
verses" fixture is vacuous by rankability, and r2 deletes it. But the
objection offers two fixes — *"Delete the guard, **or** move it to a
`godly-marriage`-family fixture where it can be shown to fire"* — and the
second one cannot be done. Live engine, top 10, 2026-09-04:

```
"marriage"                   Proverbs 21:9 absent
"biblical marriage"          Proverbs 21:9 absent
"husbands love your wives"   Proverbs 21:9 absent
"godly wife"                 Proverbs 21:9 absent
"marriage problems"          Proverbs 21:9 absent
"contentious woman"          1. Proverbs 21:9  40.00  [exact_phrase]
```

Proverbs 21:9 is reachable **only** by quoting its own distinctive words. It
does not rank for any query in the `godly-marriage` family, so a guard moved
there would be exactly as vacuous as the one being removed — and `guardVacuity
Findings` would not catch it there either, for the same reason (the ref
resolves in corpus). The correct action is the objection's first option, and
r2 takes it. Recorded so the next reviewer does not re-open the second.

#### 2. BLOCKING 25's fix is stated as `every`; the gate reads `some`

The objection's fix line is *"Add `"requiredReasonLabel": "Theme: <exact
label>"` to **every** `expectedTop` entry whose concept appears in
`coversConcepts`."* The gate is:

```ts
(fixture.expectedTop ?? []).some(
  (expectation) =>
    expectation.requiredReasonFamily === 'concept_anchor' &&
    expectation.requiredReasonLabel === expectedLabel,
)
```
— `corpusGolden.ts:867-871`. **One** qualifying entry proves the coverage.
The distinction is not pedantry: applying the objection literally would be
wrong in three shapes this section actually ships. (a) A `presenceOnly`
entry cannot carry a rank and is a different assertion; A3.22's does not get
a label. (b) An `expectedTop` entry whose ref is anchored by a *neighbouring*
pack would carry that pack's `Theme:` label, and forcing this pack's label
onto it would assert something false. (c) A second entry pinned only for
ordering (`Mark 10:6-9 withinTop 3`) needs no coverage claim — though r2
labels those anyway where the ref genuinely is the pack's own anchor,
because a redundant true assertion is free and a missing one is not.

So r2 implements the **owner's** phrasing — *"`requiredReasonLabel` on at
least one `expectedTop` entry"* — which is what the code enforces.

#### 3. Two counts in the critique are low; both corrections favour the critique

Recorded because the critique's own headline arithmetic is the thing a
reader would check first, and because r2's method claim has to survive the
same scrutiny r1's did not.

- *"None of the section's **21** fixtures carries `requiredReasonLabel`."*
  r1 contains **24** fixture blocks (20 `active`, 4 `pending`) — `grep -c
  '"id": "' ` on the archived r1. The "21 new fixtures (18 active, 3
  pending)" figure comes from r1's own Summary table, which was itself
  wrong; the critique inherited it. The objection's scope is three fixtures
  larger than stated.
- *"**Three** false 'unanchored elsewhere' verifications in one item"*
  (A3.16). r1 made **four** such claims in that item — Genesis 2:24,
  Ecclesiastes 4:9-12, Ruth 1:16-17 **and** 1 John 4:7-12 — and the
  critique's own grep block lists all four as anchored (it files 1 John
  4:7-8 as "overlapping" and does not count it). Likewise MAJOR 13's "five
  other packs" for the Psalms 23:1-6 span: the grep returns **six**.

None of this changes a verdict. r2 ended this appendix by producing a tally
("the honest number… is fifteen"). **r3 withdraws the tally**, and not
because it was low — though it was; r2's own greps were wrong five more
times, which is what its critique found. A count of one's own false claims
is a rhetorical instrument, not a check: it moves every time someone counts
differently, and it invited exactly the arithmetic quarrel that occupies the
paragraphs above. What replaces it is the appendix's **Anchor overlap
ledger** — a generated table of all 62 proposed anchors against the compiled
HEAD artifact, which nobody has to count and nobody can miscount.

Each objection in `$SCRATCH/plan/critique/S-A3-r2.md` → what changed, and
where the run that proves it lives. The critique numbers restart per
severity (BLOCKING 1-5, MAJOR 1-8, MINOR 1-6), so each row is qualified by
severity. Every "measured" in this table means: run on the simulated
after-state described in the appendix, against the real gate.

**The one-line shape of r3.** r2 built a simulated corpus and did not run
the gates over it. r3 runs them. Three of this section's own fixtures failed
and two of the repo's existing fixtures regressed; all five are fixed **by
changing the design**, not by loosening the assertion — one anchor dropped,
two anchors re-weighted, one impossible guard replaced by two possible ones,
one span corrected, one honest second fixture added where the ordering
genuinely cannot be moved from Phase A.

## Revision log (r4)

Each objection in `$SCRATCH/plan/critique/S-A3-r3.md` → what changed, and the
run that proves it. r3's critique carried **2 BLOCKING, 7 MAJOR, 8 MINOR**.
Every "measured" below means: run on the r4 simulated after-state described
in the appendix, against the real gate, from the blocks printed in this file.

**The one-line shape of r4.** r3 measured its own changes and disclosed
their cost; r4 is the round where the *design* moved because the measurement
said so. Two anchors are gone (Isaiah 49:25, and Luke 10:25-37 out of
`loving-others` entirely), one anchor is re-spanned on the merits
(Ephesians 5:21-33), one weight is recalibrated with the ladder printed
(Matthew 1:18-25 0.7 → 0.6), one whole design is replaced by the alternative
that measured better (a dedicated Good Samaritan pack), Phase C is rewritten
onto owner ruling 17, and seven printed-vs-harness drifts are corrected to
the data rather than the data argued toward the prose. This is the last
revision round: what is unresolved is in **Known gaps**, not implied to be
finished.

### Defects r4 found that the critique did not

| Defect | Evidence |
|---|---|
| **The r3 Good Samaritan blast radius was larger than either side had counted.** | The critique counted 23 existing top-10 lists; a naive reference-string match in my first harness counted 7. Both are wrong for the same reason: the related-theme edge renders as sub-runs (`Luke 10:25-27`, `Luke 10:27`), so only verse-range containment sees them. Re-measured properly: **24 new entries + 1 rank move across 16 fixtures**. The measuring script was wrong before the design was, which is the argument for the redesign being adopted on numbers rather than on the objection's count. |
| **A `mustNotLead` cannot be pinned at an arbitrary rank, and the golden-rule fixture found it.** | `WITHIN_TOP_VALUES = [1,3,5,10]`. Matthew 7:12 is measured **#4** on `treat others the way you want to be treated` — it ties Matthew 5:44-45 at 36.00 and loses the tie on canonical order. The fixture pins `withinTop: 5`, the smallest legal window, with the tie written into the note, and the assertion that actually defends the register is the neighbouring `mustNotLead: Luke 10:25-37, withinTop 3`. |
| **`1 Timothy 6:10` is not what the money row returns.** | `collapseRuns` (`createEngine.ts:998`) merges member rows into one row keyed on the range head, so the row declared at `1 Timothy 6:10` renders as **`1 Timothy 6:6-10`**. A fixture pinning the declared reference would fail for a reason that has nothing to do with the alias layer. Disclosed in A3.24; the fixture pins the rendered reference. |
| **The named-passage rule was missing, and writing it exposed three unpinned names.** | New in the header: *every named-passage query pins its own passage's rank explicitly — `withinTop: 1` where an alias or a dedicated pack backs the name, otherwise the measured rank with a stated reason.* Applying it produced `named-passage-golden-rule`, `named-passage-romans-road` and `named-passage-beatitudes-alias`, none of which existed in r3. |
| **Two existing pending fixtures still flip to PASS, and one of this section's own does.** | `assurance-forgiveness-query` and `favor-of-god` go FAIL → PASS on the repo side; `named-passage-sermon-on-the-mount` passes on the section side. The gate prints all three by name. Carried forward from r3 and re-confirmed on the r4 corpus, because the r4 design changes could have taken them back. |

## Appendix — Simulated-gate results (r4)

Everything in this appendix is output, not prose. The fixtures the gate runs
are **extracted from this file** — `extract.mjs` pulls every fenced JSON
block carrying an `id` out of the markdown and hands the gate exactly those
46 objects — so a fixture that is wrong on the page is wrong in the run. That
is the structural answer to O-7: printed-vs-harness drift is now a gate
failure, not a proofreading exercise.

### The harness

| stage | what runs |
|---|---|
| ontology at HEAD | `git archive HEAD ontology/concepts` → 289 files (the working tree is **not** read, and nothing is written inside the repo) |
| compile | the **real** `compileOntology` from `pipeline/src/importers/ontologyImporter.ts`, before and after this section's edits — 0 errors both runs |
| diff → corpus | the compiled row sets are diffed and applied to a copy of `pipeline/output/fixture.db` (`concepts`, `concept_lexicon`, `concept_anchors`, `concept_related`) |
| aliases (Phase C) | inserted into `curated_aliases` the way `aliasImporter.ts` compiles them: `normalizedPhrase(raw)` → `normalized_raw`, **one row per phrase key** |
| spelling index | rebuilt with the real `pipeline/src/buildSpellingIndex.ts` (18 422 terms, 400 538 delete rows) |
| gates | `corpusGoldenGate`, `conceptCoverageGate` (`eval/src/gates/corpusGolden.ts`); `collisionGate`, `singleTokenCollapses`, collapse-acknowledgment (`collision.ts`); bare-word inventory (`lexiconInventory.ts`); doctrinal pairing (`doctrinalGuardrail.ts`) — imported unmodified |
| engines | `createEngine` + a `node:sqlite` `ContentQueryPort`, read-only; a second `rankOptions: { limit: 50 }` engine is supplied as `presenceEngine`, the shape `eval/src/gauntlet.ts:847-853` supplies |
| probes | 17 additional corpora built from the same pipeline at different parameter settings, so every weight and design choice in this section is a comparison and not a preference: `gsa` / `gsb` / `gsnone`, `xm05` / `xm06` / `xm085`, `isa0`, `eph21`, `ps127`, `nb2`, `hell` / `hellb`, `ffps42` |

### The Good Samaritan decision, measured three ways

Owner ruling: measure the anchor-at-a-lower-weight design against a small
dedicated pack, and adopt the one where `good samaritan` leads it with zero
unwanted displacement. Displacement is counted by **verse-range containment**
(any `Luke 10:n`, 25 ≤ n ≤ 37) over the top 10 of all 998 active
existing-fixture queries — a reference-string match undercounts it 24 → 7,
because the related-theme edge renders as sub-runs.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **r3** — `Luke 10:25-37 @1.0` added to `loving-others` | **#1** 40.00 | #1 | #1 | **#1 Luke 10:25-37** — takes the lead from John 13:34-35 | **24 new entries + 1 rank move across 16 fixtures** |
| **(a)** — same anchor at **@0.85** inside `loving-others` | **#5** — **John 13:34-35 leads** | #1 | #1 | #1 John 13:34-35 (safe) | 6 new entries + 1 rank move across 5 fixtures |
| **(b) ADOPTED** — dedicated pack `parable-of-the-good-samaritan` @1.0, `related: [loving-others]` | **#1** 40.00 `Theme: The Good Samaritan` | **#1** 41.94 | **#1** 22.86 | #1 John 13:34-35 — top 10 **byte-identical to HEAD** | **0** |

adopted, `ontology/concepts/loving-others.yaml` is untouched by this section,
and the register the objection was defending is now pinned by
`named-passage-golden-rule` rather than left to hold by luck.

### What this appendix does not measure

Stated so the next reviewer does not have to find it:

1. **G8 churn is listed, not judged.** 92 moved top-10s across 55 fixtures
   (94/56 with labels) is a real review load; this section shows them and
   does not claim they are all improvements. Two of them — the label-only
   rows — are argued; the other 92 are not.
2. **The Phase-C rows are simulated, not compiled from YAML.** The alias rows
   are inserted the way `aliasImporter.ts` would compile them, but the YAML
   files themselves are not run through that importer — they cannot be, until
   B10 ships owner ruling 17's `sayings:` shape with the either-range-or-
   concept target. The ten alias-label failures in the per-fixture table are
   exactly that gap and nothing else.
3. **No G1 / G2 / G5-G8 run.** Source-manifest admission, determinism
   fingerprints, latency and rank-metrics budgets are not exercised here;
   `ENGINE_VERSION` is untouched because this section changes no engine code,
   but the layer fingerprint moves and G2 will see it.
4. **`ontology/lexicon-inventory.yaml` was edited in the harness copy** to
   carry this section's six new rows and four modified ones; the bare-word
   and collapse gates run against that copy. The row texts in the items above
   are the shipping versions.
5. **Nothing was written inside the repository.** The whole harness reads
   `git archive HEAD` and writes only into the scratch tree; the working tree
   is clean at the commit this section was measured against.

## Known gaps

Recorded rather than closed, because this is the last revision round and an
unfinished thing that reads as finished is the failure mode this section's
own critique exists to punish.

1. **`christmas bible verses` cannot be inverted from Phase A.** Isaiah 9:6-7
   leads it at every legal weight for Matthew 1:18-25 and Luke 2:1-20,
   because `bible` contributes passage-term mass the Luke run does not carry.
   The recalibration to 0.6 fixes the other three christmas forms; this one
   is disclosed in A3.19 and pinned at what it actually does.
2. **R1b — the `{hell}` collapse.** All four hell forms reduce to one token
   and Mark 9:43-48 leads them. The fix is an edit inside `hell.yaml`, a pack
   this section does not own; `assurance-will-i-go-to-hell` is a pending
   fixture that fails on purpose and is the record.
3. **Bare `magnificat` is a dead form.** The alias importer's ≥2-raw-word
   floor (`aliasImporter.ts:194`) rejects it, so the row can only ship the
   key `the magnificat`, and the single most likely typed form reaches
   nothing. Same shape, same cause: bare `beatitudes` cannot be an alias key
   either, so the Beatitudes row ships `the beatitudes` alone and A3.9's
   concept arm is what catches the bare word.
4. **`god helps those who help themselves` returns noise at ranks 2-5.** The
   misquote row corrects rank 1, which is the row's whole job; the rest of
   that page is token scatter, and fixing it is a B1 scoring matter, not a
   data matter.
5. **92 churned top-10s are shown, not adjudicated.** Every one still passes
   its fixture. Nobody has read all 92 and said each is an improvement, and
   this section does not claim otherwise.
6. **Phase C is not compilable until B10.** A3.24 and A3.25 are written to
   owner ruling 17, and **§B.10's body now is too** — that divergence is
   closed. The engine section states the withdrawal in its own heading
   (*"`saying` takes the range arm, and 'saying + range is a build error' is
   WITHDRAWN"*), rules that *"a `saying` row carries **`range:` XOR
   `concept:`, the same rule as `hymn`**"*, and settles the Romans Road the
   way this section does: *"it ships as the **phrase `romans road` on the
   existing `salvation` pack**, fixture first — **no new concept**."* No
   sentence of pre-ruling text remains for A3.24 to route around.
   What remains is the dependency itself, unchanged and still hard: these
   two items are **Phase C and ship only after the B10 engine bundle** — the
   `sayings:` / `passages:` keys, the named-passage kind, the per-kind chip
   labels (every alias chip renders `Hymn:` today, measured on a scratch
   artifact), and the two `pipeline/manifests/` source rows G1 requires.
   Until that lands, A3.24's five fixtures and A3.25's four are `pending`
   and fail on the label alone.
7. **A3.21 (`honoring-parents`) is proposed and not built.** Its fixture
   `occasion-honoring-parents` fails four expectations by design, and the
   pack's Exodus 20:12 anchor would sit inside `the-ten-commandments`
   20:1-17 @1.0 — a dual-rule case nobody has ruled on.
8. **`prayer-positive-form-after-negation-fix` needs engine work.** The
   positive form of a negated query is a whole-query behaviour; no weight or
   phrase in this section reaches it. Pending, failing, and named as B-work.
