# Phase A4 — Deferred-anchor backfill, from-knowledge fixes, and fixture conventions

All verse text below was checked directly against the built corpus
(`pipeline/output/fixture.db`, `verses` table joined to `books`, run via
`node --experimental-sqlite`). That database already holds the full
31,098-verse WEB corpus (confirmed 2026-09-04: `select count(*) from verses`
returns 31098), so every ref this section calls "present" is present in the
corpus this plan will actually ship against, not the historical 5,726-verse
fixture subset most of the deferred comments were written against. Anything
marked **UNVERIFIED** below was not checked this way and must be before it
lands in a PR. No URLs appear in any YAML text proposed here.

## A4.0 Why

Two separate, unglamorous debts sit in the ontology today, both dating from
the same historical fact: most concept packs were authored against a small
pinned WEB subset (audit-era ~5,726 verses), and the corpus has since grown
to the full 31,098-verse Bible without anyone going back to redeem the
promises the pack authors made at the time.

**D3 — deferred anchors.** Pack authors routinely wrote a verse they knew
was the *right* answer, discovered it wasn't in the pinned subset, and left
a comment — "corpus-deferred to the re-pin payload (P4.15)", "corpus-blocked
(backlog.md)", "NOT in web-subset; re-check at re-pin" — instead of silently
dropping the point. That discipline is exactly right and exactly why this
backfill is now possible without re-deriving anything from scratch: the
comments are a checklist someone already wrote. Re-running that checklist
against the current full-Bible `fixture.db` (this plan's own audit,
`scratchpad/audit.py` + `scratchpad/out.txt`, cross-checked against
`concept_anchors` for every candidate) found **360 raw hits across 114
packs**, netting to **~314 genuine, DB-confirmed gaps across 109 packs**
after removing false positives, honest non-claims, and previously-rejected
rows (full accounting in A4.3). The headline losses are not marginal
riders — they are, in several cases, *the* verse the concept is named after:

| Pack | Missing today | What it costs a searcher |
|---|---|---|
| `justification-by-faith` | Romans 3:21-26 | the doctrine's own proof text is absent from its own pack |
| `incarnation` | Philippians 2:6-8 | the kenosis hymn — the single most-quoted incarnation text in print — is missing from a pack with only 3 anchors |
| `trinity` | 2 Corinthians 13:14 | the tri-personal benediction formula (also missing Matthew 3:16-17, the baptism scene) |
| `doubt` | Matthew 14:29-31, John 20:26-29 | Peter sinking and doubting Thomas — the two best-known doubt narratives in the Gospels — both absent from a 2-anchor pack |
| `caring-for-aging-parents` | Isaiah 46:4 | the pack's own header calls this "the register's true 1.0 per the worklist," and it is still not there |

**D5 — from-knowledge wording.** 25 packs carry anchors whose comment
quotes the WEB wording from the curator's memory rather than a live lookup
("WEB from knowledge" / "wording from knowledge" markers, 58 marked anchors
total). CLAUDE.md's covenant #5 — "explanations are part of the contract" —
makes a wrong quote a live liability the moment any user-facing snippet
generation starts copying comment text rather than the DB row, even though
today the mismatch is contained to a code comment. Diffing all 58 quotes
against the DB found 4 verbatim mismatches (A4.2); the other 54 are exact or
near-exact.

Both debts share one root cause and one fix: nobody re-ran the pack authors'
own checklists after the corpus grew. This phase runs them.

---

## A4.1 Tier-1 backfill PR (33 refs / 26 candidate packs)

**Tier 1** = the audit's highest-confidence class: a locus classicus (the
verse the doctrine or theme is *named after*), a ref the pack's own header
comment calls out as central, or a pack thin enough (≤3 live anchors) that
one more right verse materially changes what a searcher meets. Full pack
prose was read for the 6 packs quoted in A4.0 plus the 27 packs surfaced by
the ≤3-anchor rule; every ref below (this section, not just the 6 hand-read
packs) was independently checked against the live `verses` table AND against
the pack's own current YAML (not just against the comment) before being
listed as still open.

### A critical correction the ≤3-anchor rule alone would have missed

The audit's scan matches comment text ("corpus-blocked", "NOT in
web-subset", "re-check at re-pin") and reports a gap when no `- ref:` line
in the same file names that verse. That is a good filter, but it trusts the
comment's *age*, not the file's *current state* — a comment can go stale the
moment someone else re-pins the ref in a later PR and forgets to delete the
now-wrong sentence above it. Checking every candidate-pack file directly
(not just trusting the flagged-comment list) found **four packs where the
"deferred" ref is already a live anchor today**, with nothing wrong except
an obsolete comment:

| Pack | Ref flagged as deferred | Actual state | Fix needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `putting-god-first` | Haggai 1:2-11 | **Live anchor, weight 0.9**, line 72 of the file — sitting directly under a comment reading "(Haggai NOT in web-subset; re-check at re-pin.)" | Delete the stale parenthetical on both Haggai anchors (1:2-11 and 2:15-19). No data change. |
| `putting-god-first` | Haggai 2:15-19 | **Live anchor, weight 0.7**, line 78 | (same fix, same PR) |
| `famine-of-hearing-gods-word` | Amos 8:11-12 | **Live anchor**, line 45 | Delete the stale "corpus-blocked" comment. No data change. |
| `legalism` | Colossians 2:16-17 | **Live anchor**, line 45 | Delete the stale "CORPUS-BLOCKED ROSTER" header note — the pack now has both spans it was minted to eventually carry. |
| `legalism` | Colossians 2:20-23 | **Live anchor**, line 38 | (same fix, same PR) |
| `supporting-gospel-workers` | 1 Timothy 5:17-18 | **Live anchor**, line 62 | Delete the stale "corpus-blocked riders" mention of 5:17-18 specifically; 1 Cor 9:4-14 is still genuinely open (see batch 3). |
| `aging-and-old-age` (not itself a Tier-1 candidate; caught as a drive-by fix — this file is already opened and quoted at length below, for `caring-for-aging-parents`'s curator-ruling row) | Isaiah 46:4 | **Live anchor, weight 0.9**, lines 77-80 (the stale comment is line 77; `- ref: Isaiah 46:4` is line 78; `weight: 0.9` is line 80) — the ref sits directly under a comment reading "(Isaiah 46 NOT in web-subset; re-check at re-pin.)" | Delete the stale parenthetical. No data change. **Land it with S-A1 A1.13** (D3, cross-section): A1.13 rewrites this same file's HEAD lines 20-27 — the "Corpus-blocked riders" paragraph, which makes the identical stale claim about the identical anchor — so the two repairs are one file's header state and A1.13 owns it. Landing this line in the curator-ruling PR instead would leave the file contradicting itself for however long A1.13 waits. |
| `mortality` (not itself a Tier-1 candidate; caught the same way as `aging-and-old-age` above — this file is already opened and quoted elsewhere in this document, for `stewardship-of-days`'s Psalms 90:12 disclosure two sections below) | Psalms 90:3-12 | **Live anchor, weight 0.9**, line 123 (`weight: 0.9` on line 125) — sitting directly under a comment, lines 119-122, reading: `# "Teach us to number our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom"` / `# — the row's Psalter spine. (Psalm 90 NOT in web-subset; re-check at` / `# re-pin. Ps 90:2 is creation's / gods-unchanging-nature's; the` / `# mortality span 90:3-12 is disjoint.)`. The file's own top-of-header "CORPUS:" summary compounds it: line 30 reads "1 Cor 15:21-22, 1 Cor 15:26, Jas 4:13-14 in corpus. Ps 90:3-12," — naming 90:3-12 as corpus-blocked, also stale, also contradicted by the live anchor 93 lines below it in the same file. | Delete the stale parenthetical (lines 119-122) and the "Ps 90:3-12," clause from the CORPUS summary (line 30). No data change. Unlike the other seven rows, this one is not attached to any Tier-1 batch — `mortality` itself contributes zero anchors to this backfill (its own header declines the one ref this document did propose for it, 1 Corinthians 15:54-57, §A4.1's r3 correction) — so it rides whichever PR next touches `mortality.yaml`, or lands standalone. |

None of these eight need a new anchor, a new fixture assertion, or a
layerFingerprint-moving PR at all — they need a one-line comment deletion,
which is housekeeping, not curation, and can ride in the same PR as its
batch's real backfill with zero ranking risk. **Do not skip this check when
executing Tier 2/3** (A4.4): the same regex-scan-vs-live-file gap almost
certainly recurs at the ~109-pack scale, and the fix (`grep -n "^\s*- ref: <exact
candidate ref>$" <pack>.yaml` before touching anything) costs one command
per candidate.

Also corrected out of Tier-1 entirely: `mercy`'s two originally-flagged
refs. `mercy.yaml`'s own header states the span discipline in so many
words — "Lam 3:22-23 stays with gods-faithfulness" and "Eph 2:4-5... stays
with gods-love" — and both are in fact live there today (`gods-faithfulness.yaml`
line 16, weight 1.0; `gods-love.yaml` line 78, weight 0.8). The original
scan flagged them as `mercy` gaps because Micah 7:18/Psalms 103:8 (mercy's
*other* two flagged refs) really were false positives of the same shape
(§A4.3), and the scan's context window did not distinguish "this pack
declines the ref for itself" from "this pack wants the ref." Net effect:
**`mercy` contributes zero new anchors to this backfill.**

### r3 correction: exact-string matching cannot see a sub-span, a super-span, or a same-verse claim at a different weight — every ref was re-checked by range overlap, not by grep

The r2 pass above (`grep -n "^\s*- ref: <exact candidate ref>$"
ontology/concepts/*.yaml`, all 289 files) catches only a byte-identical
`- ref:` string. It cannot see a *sub*-span (a proposed 5-verse range whose
inner 2 verses are someone else's whole anchor), a *super*-span (the
reverse), or the same single verse claimed at a different weight under a
different locator string — exactly the shape three more errors turned out
to have, on top of the three r2 caught. This revision replaced the grep
with a mechanical range-overlap query against `concept_anchors`
(`pipeline/output/fixture.db`, the compiled ground truth, not the YAML
comments) for **every one of the 38 refs still in the tables after r2**,
not just a sample — script spec in §A4.5(i), so future backfills run the
same check instead of re-deriving it. The query found overlapping live
anchors for **9** of the 38 rows — `justification-by-faith`, `incarnation`,
`passover`, `salvation`, `mortality`, `the-name-of-god`, `doubt`,
`self-control`, `disputable-matters` — 7 of which were undisclosed at the
time (matching the critique's own count exactly), plus 2 the critique's
own review had not itself surfaced: `salvation` (already known to be a
drop from a different check, and confirmed independently by this query)
and `the-name-of-god` (not named by the critique at all — its overlap with
`prayer.yaml`'s full Matthew 6:9-13 span is real and structurally identical
to the other seven, just not caught in the critique's own pass). Reading
each hit's own pack header (not just the DB row) then surfaced 4 more
rows — beyond `complacency`/`temptation`/`head-coverings` — where the
*proposing* pack's own header, not just the sibling's, already and
explicitly declines the exact ref:

| Pack (as originally proposed) | Ref | Actually lives at / own header says | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| `complacency` | Revelation 3:17 | `self-deception.yaml:20`, weight 1.0 — and `complacency.yaml`'s **own** header names this exact verse and declines it: "(Rev 3:17 stays self-deception's; 3:19 the-lords-discipline's — disjoint by design.)" | Dropped from Tier-1 entirely (§A4.3) |
| `temptation` | 1 Corinthians 10:13 | `remembered-a-way-of-escape.yaml:35` (weight 1.0, its **only** anchor by deliberate one-anchor design) and `pastoral-freedom-from-bondage.yaml` (weight 0.8) — and `temptation.yaml`'s **own** header names this exact pack and declines it: "remembered-a-way-of-escape owns bare `temptation`/`tempted`... **and 1 Cor 10:13, which is NOT re-anchored here.**" | Dropped from Tier-1 entirely (§A4.3) |
| `head-coverings` | 1 Timothy 2:8-15 | `men-and-women-in-the-church.yaml`, split into three disjoint anchors (2:8-10 @0.85, 2:11-12 @1.0, 2:13-15 @0.75) — built out 2026-08-27, one day *after* `head-coverings.yaml` was minted (2026-08-26) and wrote "this row is entirely corpus-blocked and rides the re-pin, where its curator may still fold this row in." Every one of these seven drops (`salvation`, `mortality`, `passover`,
`the-name-of-god`, `shame`, plus the r2-caught `complacency`/`temptation`)
shares one tell worth naming for whoever runs Tier 2/3 next: **the
"deferred comment" quoted for the row was a short, generic phrase with no
verse-specific content** — "corpus-blocked.", "corpus-blocked; not in
web-subset; re-check at re-pin." — appearing identically across otherwise
unrelated rows, rather than the longer, ref-specific quotes most other rows
carry (e.g. `justification-by-faith`'s, which names the exact verse set and
a worklist rationale). Objection 1 of this document's r2 revision already
flagged this exact pattern ("a one- or two-word 'verbatim' quote with no
context is exactly where this slipped through undetected"); re-auditing
every row carrying one of these generic phrases against its own pack file,
per that objection's own prescribed fix, is what surfaced `mortality`,
`passover`, `the-name-of-god`, and `shame` in this pass — the range-overlap
query caught the first three as *overlaps*, but it was reading each hit's
own header, not the query result alone, that turned "undisclosed overlap"
into "actively declined." A future backfill should treat a generic,
non-ref-specific deferred-comment quote as a standing flag to read the
proposing pack's own header in full before drafting the row, not just
after a reviewer asks.

### Batching

26 candidate packs split into three batches, grouped by doctrinal cluster
(not rebalanced by count — see the note below), each shippable and
measurable on its own Admission Report, per CLAUDE.md's "NO MEASURABLE
EFFECT means don't merge" — a batch that moves nothing should be caught by
its own gauntlet run, not buried in one 33-ref PR where a single flat
category could hide inside an otherwise-real signal.

> Batch sizing note, told straight because the number moved four times:
> R7's own accounting states "32 packs total qualify for Tier 1." The first
> draft of this section re-verified the 14 anchor-count-triggered packs
> individually and raised that to 33, calling it "very likely an off-by-one
> in the earlier count" — but the 33rd pack was `complacency`, whose sole
> proposed ref turned out to be already claimed, by name, in its own
> header. That single error explains the entire 32-vs-33 gap: R7's original
> 32 was right. The next revision found one *more* pack of the same shape
> R7's 32 had never separated out either — `temptation`'s 1 Corinthians
> 10:13, likewise declined by name in its own header — bringing the count
> to 31. **This revision's full range-overlap audit (§A4.1's r3
> correction) then found four more of the identical shape**
> (`salvation`/John 3:36, `mortality`/1 Corinthians 15:54-57,
> `passover`/Luke 22:19-20, `the-name-of-god`/Matthew 6:9) plus one related
> but distinct case (`shame`/Romans 10:11, declined on textual-fidelity
> grounds rather than an overlap) — landing the true count at **26**. The
> lesson restated a third time, since it recurred after two prior
> corrections: recount from the tables and the live files every time, using
> a mechanical check (grep, then range-overlap, then each hit's own header
> read in full) rather than trusting the previous draft's arithmetic or a
> generic "corpus-blocked" comment at face value. Batches below total 26
> packs, 21 of which carry at least one genuine open ref (or a genuine
> span-widening edit) after the corrections above; the other 5 ride a
> batch's PR for housekeeping only and add no anchor. **Batch sizes are
> deliberately left uneven (7/9/10) rather than reshuffled to look even**:
> the doctrinal clusters (locators / pastoral-felt-need / practice-
> discipline) predate this count, six of the ten dropped-or-declined rows
> across this and the prior revision came out of what was Batch 1, and
> moving packs between batches now to restore evenness would touch more
> rows than the audit itself needed to and risk introducing exactly the
> kind of drive-by error this note keeps having to correct. Sizing was
> always secondary to "sized as close to even as the doctrinal groupings
> allow," not a target in its own right.

Every row below lists: pack id · ref · WEB text (verified against
`fixture.db` unless marked UNVERIFIED) · suggested weight · why · the exact
deferred comment it discharges (quoted verbatim) · the fixture action
needed.

**A note on the "Fixture" column, corrected after r3.** Every one of the 26
candidate packs already has an active `eval/golden/<id>.json` file today —
this backfill adds anchors to *existing* concept packs, not new concepts,
so it is structurally impossible for any row below to need a genuinely new
fixture file (an earlier draft of this table said "new fixture" for seven
rows; that was checked against `ontology/concepts/`, never against
`eval/golden/`, and was wrong — corrected in the r4 revision log). "Yes" in
this column always means *update the existing active fixture*; it varies
only in *what* gets added. For 12 of the 19 files touched, the file's
existing `expectedTop` entry already names the ref this batch widens, or
already satisfies G3-golden coverage (§A4.5h) for the concept and needs no
new entry at all. For the other 7 files — `spiritual-growth`,
`self-control`, `judgment-seat-of-christ`, `disputable-matters`,
`new-heaven-and-earth`, `the-lords-discipline`, `stewardship-of-days` — the
concept was already covered by a *different* pre-existing anchor before
this batch, so the fixture change here is not about closing a coverage gap
(it was already closed); it is a new `expectedTop` entry that proves the
*backfilled* anchor's own presence, added to the file's existing
`expectedTop` array. Per `corpusGolden.ts:969`
(`for (const query of [fixture.query, ...fixture.additionalQueries])`),
every `expectedTop` entry in a fixture is checked against **every** query
the fixture already defines — entries are not bound to one query each — so
a new entry needs no new `additionalQueries` probe. `withinTop: 10` (the
fixture's own `expectedWithinTop` fallback) is used for every new entry
below rather than a tighter window, the same loose-presence treatment
`eval/golden/gods-love.json`'s existing three-anchor fixture already gives
its own second and third entries (Romans 5:8 at `withinTop: 1`, John 3:16
and Romans 8:38-39 both at `withinTop: 10`) — this is a live, established
pattern for "more than one anchor of the same concept, one fixture," not a
new mechanism invented for this batch.

## A4.2 From-knowledge wording fixes

Four verbatim mismatches, found by diffing all 58 "WEB from knowledge" /
"wording from knowledge" comment quotes against the live DB text at the
same `ref:` locator. All four anchors are live today and serving queries —
this is a comment-text correction, not an anchor change, and moves no
fingerprint (comments are not compiled). Still worth its own PR per
CLAUDE.md #5, since a wrong quote is exactly the kind of thing that
propagates into user-facing snippet text the moment anyone builds a feature
that copies from pack comments instead of re-querying the DB.

**1. `nations-and-peoples`, Genesis 10:32**

Before (comment, as currently committed):
> "...Of these were the nations divided in the earth after the flood"

After (actual WEB text in `fixture.db`):
> "These are the families of the sons of Noah, by their generations,
> according to their nations. **The nations divided from these on the
> earth after the flood.**"

Different clause order and voice (active "the nations divided" vs. the
comment's passive "were... divided"). If this exact phrasing appears in any
user-facing explanation string, it is quoting the wrong edition and needs
its own follow-up check outside this ontology fix.

**2. `friendship`, Proverbs 18:24**

Before:
> "There are friends who destroy a man, but there is a friend who sticks
> closer than a brother."

After:
> "**A man of many companions may be ruined**, but there is a friend who
> sticks closer than a brother."

The first clause is substantially different — the committed comment reads
like a KJV/NIV blend, not the WEB text actually in the corpus.

**3. `hospitality`, Isaiah 58:7**

Before:
> "Isn't it to **share your bread with** the hungry..."

After:
> "Isn't it to **distribute your bread to** the hungry, and that you bring
> the poor who are cast out to your house? When you see the naked, that you
> cover him; and that you not hide yourself from your own flesh?"

Verb and preposition both differ ("share...with" vs. "distribute...to").

**4. `waiting-for-a-child`, Psalms 113:9**

Before:
> "...as a joyful mother of children. **Praise Yah!**"

After:
> "He settles the barren woman in her home as a joyful mother of children.
> **Praise the LORD!**"

This one is worth a repo-wide grep before closing it out — the "Praise
Yah!" vs. "Praise the LORD!" Hallelujah-refrain rendering is a
translation-edition question that plausibly recurs anywhere else a psalm
ending in הַלְלוּיָהּ is quoted in a comment from memory, not just here.

All four fixes: edit the comment text only, verify the anchor's `ref:` and
`weight:` are untouched, run `npm run gauntlet` to confirm zero findings
(comments don't compile, so this should be a no-op run), and land as a
single small PR separate from A4.1's data batches so its Admission Report
is trivially "nothing moved, as expected."

same-pack, textual-fidelity decline under `shame.yaml`'s own
"ANCHOR-ACCURACY DECISION," "checked and NOT anchored" because the WEB
wording doesn't contain the word "shame" at all. Net effect: `seeking-god`
contributes zero refs to this backfill despite six originally flagged, and
`shame` contributes zero refs despite the one originally flagged.

**Corrections added across this document's revisions, beyond R7's original
24** (R7 §(a): "Confirmed false positives... 24 refs across 12 packs").
These are genuinely this table's shape (a ref already live on a *different*
concept, not the one that flagged it) — found by checking the candidate

## A4.4 Tier-2/Tier-3 backfill as Phase C work

Tier 1 (A4.1) closes the highest-leverage ~10% of the debt. The remaining
~270 refs across the same 109 packs are real but lower-urgency, and
CLAUDE.md's own rule for this is explicit: **"Never add data because it
exists. Add it to close a measured gap"** — Tier 2/3 must not become a
mechanical sweep just because the refs are sitting there documented.

**Sequencing: thinnest packs first.** Computed directly against the live
ontology (`ontology/concepts/*.yaml`, 289 packs, 2026-09-04):

| Anchor count | Packs |
|---|---|
| exactly 1 anchor | 16 |
| ≤2 anchors | **31** |
| ≤3 anchors | 52 |

A pack with 1-2 anchors is a pack where the *next* anchor changes what a
searcher sees far more than the 30th anchor on an already-well-built pack
does. Cross-reference the 31 thinnest packs against the ~109 Tier-2/3
candidate list before scheduling: any pack that appears in both is next in
line, ahead of a well-built pack (like `slander-and-false-accusation`,
which already has a strong anchor ladder and whose 14 remaining Proverbs
riders are curator-pick-2-3, not a coverage emergency).

**Representative Tier-2 clusters** (full 360-row scan output remains in
`scratchpad/out.txt` for the executing PR's author to walk):

- **Christology cluster** — `deity-of-christ`, `christ-the-cornerstone`
  (already touched in Tier 1), `messianic-prophecy` share reviewers and
  overlapping proof-text registers; sequence together.
- **`slander-and-false-accusation`** — 14 Proverbs/Psalms riders on an
  already-strong pack; the pack's own comment calls this "the Proverbs
  block's held contingency" — curator picks 2-3, not all 14.
- **`discipleship`** — the "counting the cost" cluster (Matt 4:18-22,
  8:18-22, Mark 8:34-38, John 21:19-22, 1-2 Thessalonians, 2 Tim 3).
- **`governing-authorities`** — 6 flagged refs, but the pack's own note
  says its in-corpus Acts 4:19-20 anchor "carries the query family until
  the re-pin" — these are parallel/duplicate texts of marginal incremental
  value; a strong **NO MEASURABLE EFFECT candidate**, flag before drafting.
- **`occult-and-divination`** — the pack names Deuteronomy 18:9-14 as "the
  very ref the row's rationale says would complete the pack," but that ref
  itself was not in the original flagged list — check it directly; it may
  be the actual priority, not the six riders the scan caught.

**Tier-3 (marginal, or affirmatively contested) — do not backfill without
a curator's explicit yes**: `seeking-god`'s three rejected refs (already
tested and declined, §A4.1); `deity-of-christ`'s Psalms 82 / John 10:34 /
Matthew 2:5-6 (the pack's own doctrinal-scan language treats these as
"a-fortiori argument, not a retraction" — interpretively hedged by the pack
authors themselves); `messianic-prophecy`'s Zechariah 3 (low-information
single verse; the pack's own note suggests the real candidate may be a
wider span); `resisting-the-devil`'s Ezekiel 28 (already flagged as a
curator ruling in Tier 1, batch 3 — the same disputed-typology caution);
`governing-authorities` (see above); `judgment-seat-of-christ`'s Matthew
25:14-30 / Luke 19:11-27 (parables *about* judgment, softer fit than the
direct statements already anchored); `the-name-of-god`'s Proverbs 18:10 /
Exodus 34:6-7 (reinforcing, not new territory); `benediction`'s Revelation
22:21 (a generic closing-grace formula, weaker than the pack's two Tier-1
texts).

**The rule, restated for whoever executes Phase C**: fixture first (write
the query you'd type and what should surface, before touching the pack
YAML), run the gauntlet, read the Admission Report. If the Admission Report
comes back `NO_MEASURABLE_EFFECT`, that means the addition is weight
without value — don't merge, even though the ref is real, even though it's
already sitting in a comment waiting to be typed in. A pack passing through
Phase C with zero merged Tier-3 rows is not a failure of the phase; several
rows above are specifically documented candidates for staying out
permanently.

**Effort estimate**: ~109 packs touched across both tiers combined (Tier 1
+ Tier 2/3), ~314 genuine refs total, and — per CLAUDE.md's fixture-first
rule — a minimum of 109 fixture files/updates (one per touched pack), with
Tier-1-and-heavier packs (multiple new anchors in one PR) wanting a fixture
per new query surface plus a regression check against the pack's existing
fixture. Realistic range: **130-170 fixtures total** across the whole plan,
not 109 flat.

## A4.5 Fixture conventions for this whole plan

Binding for A1-A3 and every Phase-C item, not just this backfill.

**(a) Search-form matrix.** Every register item this plan ships carries a
fixture with `additionalQueries` covering, at minimum: first-person ("I
feel worthless"), bare noun ("worthlessness"), question ("why do I feel
worthless"), uncontracted ("I am worthless" vs. "I'm worthless"),
plural/singular where relevant, and the `-ing` variant where the concept has
one ("doubting" alongside "doubt"). A fixture that only asserts the curator's
own preferred phrasing has not measured the gap a real searcher hits.

**(b) `mustNotLead` requires `why`; `mustNotRank` is a total ban.**
`mustNotLead` (`eval/src/gates/corpusGolden.ts`'s `MustNotLead` type) demotes
a reference out of the lead window (rank 1, or top-3 with `withinTop: 3`)
without forbidding it outright — the validator makes `why` **required** here
("a leadership demotion is always a human ruling, and the finding must be
able to cite it"), unlike `mustNotRank`, where `why` stays legacy-optional.
Use `mustNotLead` for a verse that is an honest lexical result but must not
be the *first* thing a vulnerable searcher reads.
`eval/golden/day-of-the-lord.json`'s Psalms 32:8 guard is the working
example already in the ontology — confirmed by grepping every
`eval/golden/*.json` for the literal field name (20 files use it;
`day-of-the-lord.json` is one of them):
```json
"mustNotLead": [
  {
    "reference": "Psalms 32:8",
    "why": "guidance's acknowledged bare-`lord` collapse hijacked this query's window before the pack (Ps 32:8 at #2 with Theme: God's guidance); a named prophetic phrase must never be led by an instruction-psalm register mismatch"
  }
]
```
and the fixture's own `note` array confirms the guard is load-bearing, not
vacuous: "The mustNotLead guard is real, not vacuous: Ps 32:8 is in-corpus
and led the hijack window before the pack." (`doubt.json`, checked directly,
has **no** `mustNotLead` field — the James 1:5-6 vs. Mark 9:23-24 ordering
it actually achieves is a separate, correctly labeled precedent for the
*different* technique of demoting a verse through anchor **weight** rather
than a schema field: Mark 9:23-24 sits at weight 1.0 against James 1:5-6's
0.75 in `doubt.yaml`, backed by a plain `expectedTop` entry and James 1:5-6
listed only in `alsoAcceptable`. Cite `doubt` for the weight-based tone
technique; cite `day-of-the-lord` for `mustNotLead` itself.) Use
`mustNotRank` only for a verse that must **never** appear at
all — the suicide-narrative bans in `pastoral-suicide-word.json` are the
canonical example, and per that fixture's own note, "a mustNotRank against
an absent verse passes vacuously — protection that is decoration," so every
`mustNotRank` verse this plan adds must already be confirmed present in the
corpus before the assertion is written.

**(c) Bare-cue overrides in Phase A, upgrade in Phase C.** Where a bare cue
still fires today and the engine change that would let the ranking demote it
outright hasn't landed yet, use `mustNotLead` with `withinTop: 1` (or `3` if
the harm tolerates a wider miss window) as the Phase-A guard, and record in
the fixture's `note` array that this is a placeholder pending the Phase-C
engine change — then upgrade to `mustNotRank` once that change lands and the
verse can be measured as fully excluded rather than merely demoted. Do not
write `mustNotRank` against a bare-cue collision the current engine cannot
actually prevent; that is exactly the "decoration" corpusGolden.ts's own
vacuous-guard reporting exists to catch.

**(d) `status: pending` for Phase-B-dependent expectations.** A fixture
whose passing outcome depends on a Phase B engine change ships today as
`"status": "pending"`. Per `corpusGolden.ts`'s pending-fixture handling: it
runs on every gauntlet invocation like an active fixture, but its failures
never fail the build (they fold into a `warn`-status sub-result, "Pending
fixture status: N of M still failing" — which is what flips the verdict to
`ADMIT_WITH_WARNINGS`, never `REJECT`). If a pending fixture's run comes
back with zero findings, the gate reports it as a **promotion candidate**
(`GateResult.promotionCandidates`) rather than silently passing it — someone
still has to flip the JSON's `status` by hand. A pending fixture whose only
findings are vacuous guards (a `mustNotRank` ref absent from the running
corpus) is reported separately again ("N pending, M vacuous-guarded... none
failing") and is **not** a promotion candidate — promoting it would activate
a decoration, not a real assertion.

**(e) Pending-debt hygiene.** 15 fixtures in `eval/golden/` currently carry
`"status": "pending"` (534 are `active`, 549 total). `--pending-debt-ok` (a
`gauntletMachineReport.ts` flag, requires `--require-admit`) is the
maintainer-ruling exit-code relaxation that lets a CI run with *only*
pending-fixture-debt warnings still exit 0 — any other warning or failure
still blocks. The rule this plan commits to: **a Phase B merge that unlocks
a pending fixture must, in the same PR, either promote it to `active` or
delete it** — never leave a now-passing pending fixture sitting in the 15,
quietly accumulating debt the next person has to re-diagnose. `--pending-
debt-ok` exists to tolerate debt that a train did not itself cause, not to
excuse a train from cleaning up the debt it just resolved.

**(f) Fixture naming.** `pastoral-<register>-<slug>.json` for the pastoral-
care family (matching the existing `pastoral-suicide-word.json` /
`pastoral-despair-give-up.json` convention); a doctrinal-locator pack's
fixture keeps the pack's own id as the fixture id (`justification-by-
faith.json`, `trinity.json`) per the pattern already live in `eval/golden/`.

**(g) Gauntlet command sequence for a data PR, and identity consequences.**

`npm run gauntlet` with no target is a **fixture-only** run. Read literally
from `eval/src/gauntlet.ts`: `NO_MEASURABLE_EFFECT` detection is gated on an
explicit target (`target === null ? null : detectNoMeasurableEffect(...)`,
`gauntlet.ts:917`), and the file's own doc comment says why: "Fixture runs
are structurally out of scope: metrics need the battery" (`gauntlet.ts:914`).
The two commands an earlier draft of this section gave —
`npm run build:fixture --workspace pipeline` then bare `npm run gauntlet` /
`npm run gauntlet:report` — can **never** produce a `NO_MEASURABLE_EFFECT`
verdict, no matter how inert a batch is, because neither one passes a
target. A4.7's "no batch reports `NO_MEASURABLE_EFFECT`; full stop" is only
a real gate against the sequence below, which supplies one:

```
# 1. Build the real artifact this batch's YAML changes produce.
npm run build:artifact --workspace pipeline -- --out workbench/.artifact/content.db

# 2. Run the gauntlet against it as an explicit RELEASE target, which is
#    what actually turns on the G12 battery and NO_MEASURABLE_EFFECT
#    detection (gauntlet.ts:860, target !== null). This is the same
#    invocation shape the admission worktree's own release leg uses
#    (workbench/src/admission.ts:1690-1696) — not new machinery, the
#    existing CLI flag this plan's data PRs were not using.
npm run gauntlet -- --require-admit --json eval/.runs/gauntlet-report.json \
  --release-database workbench/.artifact/content.db
# Read the Admission Report in full — ADMIT / ADMIT_WITH_WARNINGS /
# NO_MEASURABLE_EFFECT / REJECT — before opening the PR, not just the
# top-line verdict.
```

`npm run build:fixture --workspace pipeline` still has a place — it is the
fast, no-target loop for iterating on lexicon/anchor changes and getting
G1-G11 feedback before a batch is ready — but it is a development step, not
the merge-gating check, and must not be presented as one.

**A precondition this plan must not paper over.** `detectNoMeasurableEffect`
fires only when all three of its named anchors compare cleanly
(`rank-metrics.ts:1355-1360`), and the first of those anchors is the
committed `eval/baselines/rank-metrics.json`. As of this writing that file
does **not exist** in the repository (`eval/baselines/` holds
`probes.json` / `probes.approval.json` / `ordering.snapshot.json` /
`ordering.snapshot.approval.json` only) — so today, running the release
sequence above reports anchor 1 as `skipped: anchor missing`, which makes
`evaluated: false` and therefore `fired: false` **regardless of what any
batch does**. Per CLAUDE.md's own gate discipline ("a gate that cannot run
reports not-applicable with a reason... never let an unrun check report
pass"), the honest status of A4.7's "no batch reports NO_MEASURABLE_EFFECT"
criterion, before A4.8 below lands, is **not-applicable — the baseline
anchor does not exist yet**, not a silent pass. See A4.8.

**(h) The one rule that decides whether a fixture counts as coverage at
all.** `eval/src/gates/corpusGolden.ts`'s `conceptCoverageGate` (G3-golden —
the actual enforcement behind CLAUDE.md's "a pack with no fixtures is
rejected structurally") does not accept a fixture that merely names the
right verse. A concept counts as covered **only** when an active fixture's
`expectedTop` carries an entry whose `requiredReasonFamily` is the exact
string `"concept_anchor"` **and** whose `requiredReasonLabel` is the exact
string `"Theme: <concept's label>"` — verbatim, including the capital `T`
in `Theme`, the colon-space, and the concept's own `label:` field value
byte-for-byte (`corpusGolden.ts:863`: `` `Theme: ${concept.label}` ``; the
match itself, `corpusGolden.ts:870-871`, requires both fields to hold
simultaneously). A fixture whose `expectedTop` entry gets the reference
right but omits these two fields, or misspells the label, or matches the
family without the label, does not count — G3-golden reports it as
"declared... but the assertion is incomplete" and the concept as
uncovered, and the failure message names the requirement
(`corpusGolden.ts:899`) but not the JSON shape needed to fix it. This is
the one rule every other clause in this section assumes; state it here so
a Phase-C engineer working from this section alone does not have to
discover it from a failed build.

**Worked example, already live and passing** — `eval/golden/
justification-by-faith.json`'s `expectedTop` entry:
```json
{
  "reference": "Romans 5:1",
  "withinTop": 5,
  "requiredReasonFamily": "concept_anchor",
  "requiredReasonLabel": "Theme: Justified by faith"
}
```
`"Theme: Justified by faith"` is not a free-standing string picked for this
fixture — it is `` `Theme: ${label}` `` applied to `justification-by-
faith.yaml`'s own `label: Justified by faith` (line 36). Change the pack's
`label:` field without updating every fixture's `requiredReasonLabel` to
match, and every one of them silently stops counting as coverage — the
gate does not cross-reference the two live, it only compares the fixture's
committed string against the concept's committed string at gate time, so a
drifted label is a G3-golden failure waiting for the next build, not
something caught at label-edit time.

**(i) Mechanical overlap check — run before every batch, not just this
one.** This backfill found that an exact-string grep against every pack's
`- ref:` lines (A4.1's original check) and even that same grep run against
*every* pack rather than just the target's own (A4.1's r2 correction, superseded by the r3 range-overlap correction below) both
miss a sub-span, a super-span, or the same verse claimed at a different
weight under a different locator string — the shape that produced 9 of
this document's undisclosed-or-declined rows (§A4.1's r3 correction). The
fix is a five-line range-overlap query against the compiled
`concept_anchors` table (`pipeline/output/fixture.db`), not a new tool:

```sql
-- Given a candidate ref's start_verse_id/end_verse_id (looked up from the
-- verses table the same way this document did throughout), list every
-- OTHER pack's anchor whose range overlaps it at all:
SELECT concept_id, start_verse_id, end_verse_id, weight, locator
FROM concept_anchors
WHERE end_verse_id >= :candidateStartVerseId
  AND start_verse_id <= :candidateEndVerseId
  AND concept_id != :candidatePackId
ORDER BY concept_id;
```
A hit does not by itself mean drop the row — it means **read that pack's
own header before drafting the Why cell**, per this document's own
worst-recurring failure: of the 9 hits this pass found, 5 were a
legitimate Romans 8:1-style dual claim (disclose and keep), and 4 were the
proposing pack's own header explicitly declining the ref in the sibling's
favor (drop entirely, same disposition as a stale-comment false positive).
The query only surfaces the candidates; the header read is what tells them
apart, and skipping it is exactly how `mortality`, `passover`, and
`the-name-of-god` almost shipped as clean adds in an earlier draft of this
section.

---

Every Tier-1/2/3 batch in this plan is a **data train**: it moves
`layerFingerprint` (the curated `- ref:` list changed) while leaving
`corpusFingerprint` (the WEB text itself, untouched) and `ENGINE_VERSION`
(no ranking-formula, tokenizer, cap, or tie-break change) fixed. Per the
project's standing **merge-first-sign-once** rule (the J39 baseline
ordering, stated in `docs/plans/2026-08-27-votes-to-engine-plan.md` §5.5:
"every data train moves the layer fingerprint and therefore owes one
post-merge re-approval by an independent person... approvals are authored
**after** the train's PR merges, against the settled identity") — every
merge in this backfill re-enters the signing cycle, and the independent
reviewer signs J39 **once**, after the *last* identity-moving merge in the
batch sequence, not once per PR. Signing after every individual PR would
both multiply the reviewer's workload for no safety benefit and contradict
the ordering's own stated purpose (avoiding "a spiral where the sign-once
target never stops moving"). Sequence the three Tier-1 batches (and any
Tier-2/3 batches that follow in the same signing window) to land close
together, then sign once.

## A4.6 Lexicon-inventory rules for bare words

`ontology/lexicon-inventory.yaml`'s `concepts:` section requires exactly one
row per compiled concept — `{ id, admitted?: string[], skipped?: {token,
reason}[] }` — and gate G4 (`eval/src/gates/lexiconInventory.ts`) fails a
build that: (1) has a compiled concept with no row at all; (2) has a row
naming a concept that no longer exists; (3) has an `admitted` token that
does **not** actually fire the concept under `significantWords()`
containment matching; (4) has a `skipped` token that **does** fire (the
2026-08-08 accident class this whole mechanism exists to prevent — bare
`god`/`work` firing concepts nobody intended); or (5) has a skip whose
`reason` is empty (rejected at parse time, before G4 even runs). A firing
bare token with no `admitted` entry at all is report-only — surfaced as
"behaviour without a recorded decision," but does not fail the build on its
own.

Every bare word this plan proposes anywhere (A1-A5, collected from the
underlying felt-need/crisis/doctrine research) needs a WEB-safety check —
`SELECT document_count FROM token_stats WHERE token=?` plus a direct grep of
verse text for that token — before it can get an `admitted` row. Checked
directly against `fixture.db` (2026-09-04, full 31,098-verse corpus):

| Token | `document_count` | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `suicide` | 0 | **SAFE** | absent from WEB; the word IS the concept (§1.6d precedent, already admitted elsewhere) |
| `suicidal` | 0 | **SAFE** | absent |
| `depression` | 0 | **SAFE** | absent |
| `depressed` | 0 | **SAFE** | absent |
| `funeral` | 0 | **SAFE** | absent; same class as `hospice`/`bereavement`/`sorrow`, already admitted |
| `widower` | 0 | **SAFE** | absent |
| `dementia` | 0 | **SAFE** | absent |
| `alzheimer's` | 0 (checked as `alzheimer`) | **SAFE** | absent; note the apostrophe — the token this actually needs to admit is the stemmed/normalized form the tokenizer produces from "alzheimer's," verify at admission time, not the bare string `alzheimers` |
| `caregiver` | 0 | **SAFE** | absent |
| `panic` | **2** | **UNSAFE** | both occurrences (1 Samuel 5:11, "there was a deadly panic throughout all the city"; Zechariah 14:13, "a great panic from the LORD") are divine-judgment/battle-terror uses, not personal anxiety — a bare admission risks pulling judgment text into `token_overlap` scoring for an anxiety-attack query; same caution class as the rejected bare `bereaved` (R2's own finding). Recommend multi-word phrases only ("panic attack," "feeling panicked") |
| `numb` | 0 | **SAFE** | absent |
| `unemployed` | 0 | **SAFE** | absent |
| `surgery` | 0 | **SAFE** | absent |
| `diagnosis` | 0 (as bare token; stems to `diagnosi`, also 0) | **SAFE** | absent under either the raw or stemmed form; `diagnosed` stems separately to `diagnos` (also 0) — both need their own `admitted` row, they do not share a stem |
| `chronic` | 1 | **SAFE, low-risk** | the single occurrence is Leviticus 13:11, "it is a **chronic** leprosy in the skin of his body" — a benign, on-topic use (a real chronic-illness text), not a misfire risk; note for the record but no `skipped` entry needed |
| `retirement` | 0 | **SAFE** | absent |
| `favor` | **111** | **UNSAFE — and doctrinally flagged** | far too common for a bare admission on frequency alone (111 documents), and separately, `favor` is one of `ontology/flagged-pairings.yaml`'s 10 `materialFrameKeywords` (prosperity-gospel watchlist) — any concept whose id/label/lexicon contains it is automatically in scope for the doctrinal-guardrail pairing scan on every anchor it carries (confirmed: `favor`, `increase`, `prosperity`, `wealth`, `success`, `money`, `breakthrough`, `abundance`, `promotion`, `financial`). A `favor-of-god` locator pack is a legitimate future concept (R5's own recommendation, built doctrinally clean from day one, zero watchlisted anchors), but the bare token itself must stay a `skipped` entry everywhere else, and any pack that does admit it needs its lexicon and every anchor re-verified against the watchlist before every future edit, not just at minting |
| `pentecost` | 3 | **SAFE** | occurs 3 times, all the named event itself (Acts 2 and its cross-references) — precedented alongside `hell`/`benediction`/`identity` bare-word admissions |
| `easter` | 0 | **SAFE** | absent — the WEB text uses "Passover," not the KJV's Acts 12:4 "Easter" rendering |
| `beatitudes` | 0 | **SAFE** | absent; the word never occurs, it is a post-biblical name for Matthew 5:3-12 — same class as `pentecost`/`hell` |
| `kill` | **493** | **RULING — not a mechanical SAFE** | 493 documents is not a "distinctive modern word absent from WEB" case at all — it's core, high-frequency WEB vocabulary (commandments, war narratives, sacrificial law). The concrete proposal in the underlying research (R1) is **not** a bare `kill` lexicon entry but the phrases `"kill myself"` / `"want to kill myself"`, which strip to the bare token `{kill}` / `{want, kill}` under the one tokenizer — functionally a single-token collapse needing its own `lexicon-inventory.yaml` row regardless of the multi-word spelling. Recommend: admit narrowly, scoped to the first-person self-harm phrase only (not bare `kill` as a standalone lexicon entry), and add a `mustNotLead`/`mustNotRank` guard fixture naming the specific WEB "kill" verses this collapse could misfire against (e.g., the Cities-of-Refuge and war-narrative clusters) before merging — this is a curator ruling, not a checkbox |
| `worthless` | **16** | **VERIFY — recommend against bare admission** | 16 occurrences, and they are exactly the wrong register for a self-worth query: "worthless fellows"/"worthless men" (1 Sam 10:27, 25:17, 25:25, 30:22; 2 Chr 13:7 — all about wicked *people*, not self-perception), "worthless shepherd" (Zech 11:17, a judgment oracle), "worthless thing" (Hosea 8:8, 12:11, national judgment), plus a few closer hits (2 Sam 6:22, "I will be... worthless in my own sight" — self-deprecating but about undignified dancing, not despair; 1 Cor 3:20, "the reasoning of the wise... is worthless"; James 1:26, "this man's religion is worthless"). R1's own live-query test already showed "I'm worthless" returning exactly this scatter (1 Cor 3:20, 2 Sam 6:22, Prov 6:12, Acts 4:11) — the gap R1 measured is real, but a **bare** `worthless` admission would trade an empty result for a wrong one. Recommend a `mustNotRank`-guarded multi-word phrase ("I feel worthless," "I'm worthless") anchored to `identity-in-christ`, not a bare-token admission |
| `failure` | 0 | **SAFE** | absent from WEB entirely — confirmed live (`engine.research("I'm a failure")` returns an empty result set today); the starkest gap in the whole crisis-register research, and the cleanest §1.6d case in this table: the word IS the concept, nothing to misfire against |

Three of these twenty-three (`kill`, `worthless`, `panic`) do not clear a
mechanical SAFE/UNSAFE check and need a named curator ruling before an
`admitted` row is written — write the ruling into the `lexicon-
inventory.yaml` row's own governance the same way `abide`'s
`reviewedBy: pending-J12` precedent already does, rather than silently
admitting or silently dropping them.

## A4.7 Acceptance and effort

**Acceptance, per batch:**
- Fixture(s) committed and failing (or, for the doc-only cleanup rows,
  no fixture change and a clean `git diff` limited to comment text) before
  the corresponding pack YAML changes land, per CLAUDE.md's "Adding data"
  discipline.
- `npm run gauntlet` run locally, Admission Report read in full — not just
  the top-line verdict — before opening the PR.
- `npm run gauntlet:report` green (`ADMIT` or `ADMIT_WITH_WARNINGS` with
  only pending-fixture-debt warnings covered by `--pending-debt-ok`) in CI
  on both OS legs (gate G2's cross-platform determinism check).
- The batch's **release-target** run (A4.5(g)'s second command — the one
  that actually can produce a `NO_MEASURABLE_EFFECT` verdict, once the
  pre-Tier-1 rank-metrics baseline exists) does not report it; if it does,
  that batch does not merge, full stop, regardless of how well-sourced the
  ref is. That baseline is D2's mechanism (§C.4/D2 in the measurement
  section), not this document's — see A4.8, now a cross-reference, not a
  duplicate protocol. **Until D2's Step 0 clears and the baseline lands,
  this criterion is honestly `not-applicable`** (A4.5(g)), not a silent
  pass, and the batch reviewer reads two things instead: (1) **G3-golden's
  own per-fixture pass/fail**, in the same Admission Report — the fixture
  committed failing before the anchor lands and passing after is the
  actual fixture-first evidence CLAUDE.md's "Adding data" section asks for,
  and it does not depend on the rank-metrics baseline at all; (2) the
  release-target run's absolute `rankMetrics` numbers (nDCG@10, MRR@10,
  good-or-better@3, recall@50), which the Admission Report prints even
  with no baseline to diff against (`report.ts`'s `rankMetricsRow`) — worth
  quoting in the PR body for later comparison once D2's baseline exists,
  even though nothing compares against them today. There is **no**
  ordering-snapshot diff to lean on in the meantime: verified directly
  against `gauntlet.ts:826-841` — the ordering-snapshot gate's `observed`
  comparison runs only when `target === null` (a fixture-only invocation);
  an explicit `--release-database`/`--candidate-*` run passes `observed:
  null` and gets document-integrity and tripwire checks only, per the
  code's own comment ("only document integrity and the tripwire apply on
  those runs, and the fixture-based CI legs keep enforcing the orderings
  themselves") — so a PR description must not claim an ordering-snapshot
  comparison it did not actually get.
- The three curator-ruling bare words (`kill`, `worthless`, `panic`) and
  the two curator-call refs (`resisting-the-devil`'s Isaiah 14/Ezekiel 28,
  `caring-for-aging-parents`'s Isaiah 46:4 — comfort-lead placement AND a
  duplicate anchor at `aging-and-old-age`, §A4.1's r3 correction) are
  resolved by a named human decision recorded in the PR body, not
  defaulted either way by an implementer.
- `layerFingerprint` moved for every batch that added a live anchor;
  `corpusFingerprint` and `ENGINE_VERSION` unchanged for all of them; J39
  signed once, after the last identity-moving merge in the sequence.

**Effort, this phase (A4 only, i.e. Tier 1 plus the wording/false-positive
cleanup — Tier 2/3 effort is carried separately under A4.4/Phase C):**

## A4.8 Rank-metrics baseline — owned by D2, not this document

An earlier draft of this section specified its own protocol for
establishing `eval/baselines/rank-metrics.json`. That was a defect, not a
convenience: `S-C-search-forms-and-measurement.md` §C.4/D2 already owns
this exact mechanism end to end (the same file, the same
`--update-rank-baseline` flag, the same hand-authored approval), and a
second, independently-drafted copy of "how to establish this file" in a
second document is exactly how the two copies drift — which they already
had, since D2's protocol carries a hard precondition this section's
original A4.8 never mentioned at all.

**The one fact this document adds, that D2 does not need to repeat: A4
depends on D2, and D2's own Step 0 is not clear today.** D2 requires,
before any of its four steps may run, that main's standing G2/G8 approval
debt be zero (`docs/governance/probe-baseline-review.md`: "Steps 1-4
cannot begin while main's standing G2/G8 approval debt is open — a rank
baseline minted now would chain from an unratified identity"). D2 itself
verifies, against live `HEAD`, that this debt is open today (the last
signed baseline's `layerFingerprint` no longer matches a fresh build's,
per a data-changing commit that landed after the 2026-08-29 sign-off). D2
also requires **≥3 ADMIT runs against a real artifact** to accumulate
before `--update-rank-baseline` writes anything — not the single build an
earlier draft of this A4.8 proposed.

**Precondition for Batch 1, stated once, here:** the pre-Tier-1
rank-metrics baseline must be established, per D2's own protocol, before
any Tier-1 batch in this document can turn A4.7's "no batch reports
NO_MEASURABLE_EFFECT" criterion into a real, enforceable gate. That
requires D2's Step 0 (G2/G8 approval debt) closed first, then D2's
≥3-ADMIT-runs accumulation, then the baseline-and-approval flow. None of
that is scheduled or owned by this document; it is scheduled and owned by
D2, and A4 merely inherits its state. **Until then**, A4.5(g) and A4.7
already state the honest interim position: the criterion reports
`not-applicable — the baseline anchor does not exist yet`, and the batch
reviewer reads G3-golden's fixture pass/fail plus the release-target run's
absolute `rankMetrics` numbers instead (A4.7's acceptance bullet, in
full).

This section does not re-specify D2's protocol, re-run its ≥3-ADMIT-runs
requirement early, or attempt to establish the baseline off a single build
before Batch 1 — doing so would produce exactly the unratified-identity
baseline D2's own governance citation warns against, on this exact repo,
today. Whoever sequences Batch 1's merge should confirm D2's Step 0 has
cleared (or is scheduled and owned) before treating A4.7's release-target
criterion as more than `not-applicable`; that confirmation belongs in the
PR sequencing this document's own maintainers do at merge time, not in a
duplicated protocol here.

## B.0 Why one bundle, and the covenant checklist

Ten engine changes ship as **one** version bump — `ENGINE_VERSION`
`0.14.0 → 0.15.0`, `TOKENIZER_VERSION` `1.0.0 → 2.0.0`, `SCHEMA_VERSION`
`9 → 10` — because every one of them alters ordering and CLAUDE.md #2 plus
gate G2 (`eval/src/gates/orderingSnapshot.ts`, rule 5:
`ordering-changed-without-version-bump`) require an `ENGINE_VERSION` bump per
ordering change. Ten bumps would mean ten ordering-snapshot regenerations,
ten probe-baseline regenerations, ten independent reviews under
`docs/governance/probe-baseline-review.md`, and ten consumer re-pins across
Maskil, LH Worship Setlist and Versed. One bundle means:

- **one** `ENGINE_VERSION` bump (0.15.0) and **one** `TOKENIZER_VERSION` bump
  (2.0.0) in the final baseline commit of the branch;
- **one** regeneration each of `eval/baselines/ordering.snapshot.json`
  (G2), `eval/baselines/probes.json` (G8) and, on the minted full artifact,
  `eval/baselines/rank-metrics.json` (G12, thresholds stay `null`);
- **one** independent-review packet and **one** set of approvals
  (`ordering.snapshot.approval.json` v2 with `priorProvenance`,
  `probes.approval.json`, and a dated `docs/reviews/` record);
- **one** consumer re-pin: `(0.15.0, new descriptor)`. Because tokenizer
  2.0.0 refuses every 1.0.0 artifact at `createEngine.ts:161`, the engine
  and artifact halves of the pin move together by construction.

The bundle is developed on one branch with one commit per item (B.11), and
the version constants are bumped only in the final baseline commit so that
intermediate commits do not each need snapshot regeneration. The G2 rule
"orderings changed while the identity triple did not" therefore fires on the
branch's intermediate CI runs and is expected to; the branch merges only
after the baseline commit lands and CI is green on both OS legs.

### Covenant checklist (each item tagged against CLAUDE.md #1–#6)

| Item | #1 No AI at runtime | #2 Determinism | #3 No I/O in engine | #4 One tokenizer | #5 Explanations are contract | #6 No theology scores |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B1 Tokenizer v2 | Tables are reviewed data, derived mechanically from vocabularies; no model | Rules and tables only; whole-vocabulary snapshot + BIDIRECTIONAL invariant (mustMerge, mustNotMerge, morphological and register reports), all cross-platform | Untouched | **This is #4's whole point**: one module, one call site (`index.ts:166`), pipeline imports it | Labels unchanged here (B9 fixes surface forms) | n/a |
| B2 Sole-evidence predicate | n/a | New constant mirrored (G6); the ceiling is ASSIGNED exactly, so no capped tie is decided by floating-point noise | Untouched | n/a | Labels untouched; points admit the cap via `uncappedPoints` | Uses `isAuthoritative`, an evidence class, not a doctrine |
| B3 Query frames | Reviewed phrase list | List mirrored (G6); deterministic left-to-right longest-first, and the protected-token set is an order-independent union over a fixed table | Frames live in `engine/src/config/`, a constant, not a file read; the protection lookup goes through `ContentQueryPort` like every other corpus read | Applied to `rawWords` output before `significantWords`, never a second tokenizer | Frame words never appeared in chips (they are frame, not evidence); a frame word a curated phrase needs is now KEPT, so the curated chip survives | n/a |
| B4 Parity dominance | n/a | Thresholds mirrored (G6) | Untouched | n/a | Demoted cue keeps its `Theme cue:` label | Prefers the wider curated phrase — recorded curation, not doctrine |
| B5 Ordered phrases | n/a | Contiguity check is a pure function of an ordered array | Column read through `ContentQueryPort` | Uses the same significant-token order both sides | `matchedPhrase` still names the phrase that fired | Pack author decides which phrases are order-bound; engine adjudicates nothing |
| B6 Curated-order guard | n/a | Scale constant mirrored (G6); step 4b iterates the live array, so it is order-independent | Untouched | n/a | Add-on chips stay, with `uncappedPoints`; a chip whose verbatim text covers the WHOLE query (`complete`) is never scaled | Pack weights (a named source's prior) decide; engine adds no score |
| B7 Precision floor | n/a | Constant mirrored (G6) | Untouched | n/a | Label unchanged | n/a |
| B8 Contract fields | Derived from reason families | Pure function of ranked reasons | `care` flag ships in the artifact, read via the port | n/a | `evidenceTier` is a *summary* of the chips, never a replacement | `care` says "a reviewed care list names this concept", nothing more |
| B9 Surface-word labels | n/a | Surface = first raw word per token, deterministic | Untouched | Uses `significantWordsWithSurface`, the existing pairing | **This item is #5 work**: chips quote what the user typed | n/a |
| B10 Alias kinds | Rows are reviewed data | Sorted insert order kept | Untouched | Uses `normalizedPhrase` as today | Chip names the kind and the source ("not in the Bible" is provenance, not judgment) | Honesty note is a fact about origin, not a verdict |

## Owner rulings applied (1–9 in r3, 10–17 in r4)

Seventeen rulings closed the decisions r2 and r3 left open. Each is applied
exactly as stated; where a ruling has a measured consequence the owner may not
have had in front of them, the consequence is recorded here and carried into
the approval packet (B.11) rather than argued away.

| # | Decision | Option chosen | Why (as ruled), and what it costs |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `myself` | **(b) stays a STOPWORD in 0.15.0**; revisit in Phase C, fixture first | At df 140 / IDF **5.408** (re-measured, §B.1) `myself` would *lead* a suicide query with Job 42:6 "Therefore I abhor myself" — the highest-IDF token in "i will kill myself" pointing at self-loathing with no pack behind it. Cost, stated: `"kill myself"` continues to tokenize to `[kill]` and therefore continues to rely on the **bare `kill` admission ruling in S-A1** (**S-A1 §A1.1** — the `kill myself` entry with its `collapses:` row, `admitted: [kill]` and twelve `mustNotRank` guards; r3 cited a §"bare cue admissions" heading S-A1 does not have) for its pastoral answer; B.1 changes nothing about that path. Phase C removes the stopword in the same artifact as the `kill myself` / `hate myself` / `cutting myself` phrases, with `pastoral-kill-myself.json` written first. |
| 2 | B.2 `uncappedScore` tie-break | **Ship, GATED to capped rows** | Uncapped rows keep the documented stable-ID tie-break (`docs/implementation-plan.md:31`, `rank.ts:50-56`), so §5's contract is untouched for every result the ceiling did not rewrite. Gate is on a new `soleCapped` marker — "the score was ASSIGNED the ceiling" — not on `capped`, which four other steps also set. Removes objection 8's interaction with B.6 entirely: an anchored row is never sole-capped, so B.6's post-guard totals can never be re-ordered by pre-guard ones. |
| 3 | B.6 scale | **0.10**, with the verbatim exemption **narrowed to the `complete` case** | 0.10 is the only measured scale at which pack weight decides order in both inversions (§B.6). The exemption is now exactly `lexical.ts:76-82` with `complete === true` (label `Exact phrase`) — the branch where the verbatim text covers the WHOLE query — which is what the engine's own comment at `:71-77` allows and what r2's wider marker did not. Measured incidence of the exemption: **3 of 1,211 anchored rows (0.25 %)** over 229 distinct queries. |
| 4 | B.4 wide bare-cue threshold | **Ship as designed** | The consequence is a 0.3 factor on one chip. The ruling is re-attached to the assertions it actually inverts — `engine/test/concept.test.ts:78` and `:92-94` — and **not** to `:90`, which is unchanged at share 0.5. |
| 5 | `SignalBudgets` breaking type change | **Ship under the verified precedent** | `COMPATIBILITY.md:82` (0.8.0 breaking ordering change in a minor) and `:38`/`:88` (0.14.0 internal-surface removal). The **tie-break change of ruling 2 travels in the same COMPATIBILITY note**, so consumers read one paragraph, not two. |
| 6 | B.3 frames | **New design: runtime protected tokens** (replaces r2's static-admissibility idea) | Concept-phrase matching runs on the UNSTRIPPED significant tokens first; every token participating in any matched lexicon phrase is protected; stripping then removes only unprotected frame tokens, and if stripping would leave zero significant tokens nothing is stripped. Measured: every parity anchor the critic found destroyed is **preserved** under the rule, and stripping still fires on framed queries with no phrase match (§B.3). (r3 said all four were byte-identical; under ruling 12 three are, and `"help me with my unbelief"` keeps its 40.000 anchor while the page improves — corrected in B.3.) |
| 7 | `cutting myself` | **(b) delete the phrase and its `collapses` row** | Its v2 collapse token would be `cut` (df **364**, measured), an unsafe bare cue: a one-word query `"cut"` is never demoted (`concept.ts:211` requires `queryTokenCount > 1`) and would fire the hope-in-despair anchor set authoritatively. Recorded in the B.1 data-ripple table as a DELETE, not a re-derivation. Phase C restores the phrase once `myself` is retained (ruling 1). |
| 8 | `news` | **Identity row — `news` stays `news`** | Plus a **bidirectional** invariant: a reviewed `mustNotMerge` list AND a reviewed `mustMerge` list, both tested, and a reviewed exception row for every bad merge the critic found, each with a merge-or-split ruling and a one-line reason (§B.1, "The bidirectional invariant"). |
| 9 | `gods` | **Keep DISTINCT from `god`** (identity lemma `gods`) | Idols and God must not merge. **Measured consequence, named in the approval packet:** of the 609 WEB occurrences of the surface form `gods`, **374 are the possessive "God's"** (apostrophe stripping folds `God's → gods` at `tokenizer/index.ts:148`), so the ruling as written would divert "God's love" away from `god`. The ruling therefore ships with a **required companion**: the raw-word stage folds a trailing possessive `'s` before apostrophes are removed (§B.1, "Possessive folding"). With the companion, `gods` carries **235** occurrences — the idol plurals — and `god`'s document frequency rises 3,553 → 3,862 instead of falling. Without the companion the ruling is a regression, and that is the alternative the packet names. |
| 10 | Contractions | **Direction REVERSED: canonicalize TOWARD the contracted WEB token** | The negation contractions are no longer expanded into stopwords; the raw-word stage folds the multi-word forms INTO them (`do not → dont`, `can not`/`cannot → cant`, `will not → wont`, …, **13 rows**), and `dont`/`cant`/`wont` remain significant tokens because they are real WEB tokens (v1 df **1,209 / 187 / 237**, verified against `token_stats`; §B.1 "Negation folding" lists all 13 with df before and after). Pronoun contractions are NOT folded, and `im`/`ive`/`youre`/`theyre` join `STOPWORDS` (their expansions are stopwords), so `TOKENIZER_STOPWORD_COUNT` moves **173 → 177**. Measured consequences: `dont give up` compiles to **`dont give`** (2 tokens) — the r3 rule's df-1,946 bare `give` cue **cannot arise**, which is what made the round-3 objection blocking; **five** lexicon phrases stop collapsing to a bare cue (`afraid`, `lie`, `anxiou`, `fret`, `worry`); and today's split between `"i cant go on anymore"` (token scatter, measured) and `"i cannot go on anymore"` (the despair pack at 40.000, measured) closes, because both sides now land on `cant anymore`. One correction, with proof: the ruling's example `cant go on → {cant, go}` is `{cant}` in fact — `go` is two letters and the surface floor drops it (`index.ts` `raw.length < 3`), the same floor the section already cites for `going → going`. `not` stays a stopword; the "fear not" case is out of scope and noted in B.1. |
| 11 | Bad merges | **SPLIT `divine`; ACCEPT `bow`/`arm`/`sow`** | `divined`/`divines`/`divining` → **`divin`** (the `divin` row is a reviewed REMOVAL from the derived `E_RESTORE`, plus one lemma row `divines → divin` because step 1a would otherwise give `divine`), so 2 Peter 1:3-4's *divine nature* and Deuteronomy 18:10's *divining* stay apart — the `occult-and-divination` pack's own subject. `divine/divin` joins `mustNotMerge` (**27** pairs). `bow` (204 occ), `arm` (138) and `sow` (74) are accepted as homograph collisions of the class v1 already carries, and `acceptedCollisions` becomes a reviewed list **with a reason column** (**9** rows). A fifth generated report is added — *new families touching lexicon / `docs/DOCTRINAL-BASIS.md` vocabulary since v1*, **252** families on this run — signed once by the reviewer and pinned, so the next `bow` fails a test instead of waiting for a critic. |
| 12 | B.3 measurement basis | **Phrase step on the STRIPPED sequence; protection from the UNSTRIPPED tokens** | `phraseEvidence` (exact phrase / `complete` / coverage denominator) runs on the stripped word sequence; the protected-token set is computed from concept matches on the unstripped tokens; final concept matching runs on the stripped tokens with protected tokens retained. Consequences, all measured (§B.3): `"bible verses about the lord is my shepherd"` gains **`Exact phrase` 40.000** (53.236 → 86.710) where r3 left it at `Contains …` 20.000; B.6's `complete` verbatim exemption is **alive** on framed queries instead of dead; and the r3 claim that all four parity queries stay byte-identical is **corrected** — three do, and `"help me with my unbelief"` improves (52.177 → 82.477) because the phrase step finally sees the quotation the user typed.
