## B.1 … B.10 — one item each

### B.1 Tokenizer v2

**Measured defect.** The 1.0.0 stemmer at `engine/src/tokenizer/index.ts:132-142`
is five suffix rules with a 4-character residual floor:

```ts
/** Light suffix stemming: -ing, -ies, -ed, -es, -s. Stem must stay >= 4 chars. */
function stem(word: string): string {
  if (word.endsWith('ing') && word.length - 3 >= 4) return word.slice(0, -3);
  if (word.endsWith('ies') && word.length - 3 >= 4) return `${word.slice(0, -3)}y`;
  if (word.endsWith('ed') && word.length - 2 >= 4) return word.slice(0, -2);
  if (word.endsWith('es') && word.length - 2 >= 4) return word.slice(0, -2);
  if (word.endsWith('s') && !word.endsWith('ss') && word.length - 1 >= 4) {
    return word.slice(0, -1);
  }
  return word;
}
```

Seven defect classes, all measured against `pipeline/output/fixture.db`:

1. **No e-restoration.** `verse_terms` holds **483** `stem | stem+e` pairs
   under the definition *"distinct terms `t` for which `t+'e'` is also a
   term"* (**478** under the narrower definition r2 used, which additionally
   required `t` not to end in `e`; the five it excludes are the `-ee` bases
   `agre|agree`, `decre|decree`, `degre|degree`, `pharise|pharisee`,
   `zebede|zebedee`). Top rows: `apostl/apostle 82/239`,
   `sacrific/sacrifice 76/110`, `judg/judge 60/118`, `believ/believe 97/77`,
   `promis/promise 91/82`, `receiv/receive 82/64`, `prais/praise 43/80`.
   `token_stats` shows the same class from the scripture text
   (`believ 120 / believe 148`, `forgiv 6 / forgive 52`,
   `prais 73 / praise 196`, `agre 9 / agree 8`). **161** distinct
   `concept_lexicon` tokens sit on one side of such a pair (re-counted: 161
   of the 1,254 distinct lexicon tokens), so a query typed with the other
   inflection misses the lexicon phrase (R6 E1).
2. **`-ies` on six-letter words falls through to `-es`.** `bodies → bodi`
   (`bodi 58 / body 218`), `cities → citi` (`393 / 762`), `armies → armi`
   (`319 / 225`), `ladies → ladi`, `duties → duti`.
3. **`-ied` never restores `y`.** `sanctifi 44 / sanctify 62`,
   `justifi 36 / justify 15`, `crucifi 37 / crucify 12`,
   `glorifi 45 / glorify 30`, `carri 150 / carry 128`, `buri 103 / bury 41`.
4. **`-s` stripped from `-us`/`-ous` words.** 191 `token_stats` tokens end
   in `u` (`SELECT count(*) FROM token_stats WHERE token LIKE '%u'` → 191):
   `jesu 940` (there is no `jesus` token at all), `mose 793`, `juda 29`,
   `thoma 11`, `titu 12`, `lazaru 15`, and every `-ous` adjective —
   `anxiou 16` (battery query fn1 "I'm anxious" tokenizes to `anxiou`),
   `courageou`, `consciou`, `covetou`, `blasphemou`.
5. **The 4-char floor strands common pastoral verbs.** `loved 88` beside
   `love 374`, `saved 109` beside `save 189`, `died 213` beside `die 266`,
   `dying 15`, `lying 67`; `crying`, `giving` likewise never reach their
   base (`giving` is rescued only because `gives/gave/given` are in
   `IRREGULAR_LEMMAS`, `giving` is not).
6. **A negation has two spellings and the index treats them as two
   vocabularies.** Apostrophes are stripped at `index.ts:148`, so
   `don't/can't/won't` become the tokens `dont 1374 / cant 202 / wont 270`
   (occurrences over `verses.text`; the `token_stats` figures r2 quoted —
   1,209 / 187 / 237 — are *document* frequencies, and both are verified in
   the df tables below), while the multi-word spelling of the same negation
   dissolves into stopwords (`do`, `not`, `can`, `will`). Measured live at
   HEAD, this is not cosmetic:

   ```
   "i cannot go on anymore"  -> 1. 2 Corinthians 1:8-10  40.000  Theme: Hope in despair
                                2. 1 Kings 19:4-7        38.000  3. Matthew 11:28-29 37.600
   "i can't go on anymore"   -> 1. Job 23:8   1.655  [token_overlap] Shared word: cant
                                2. Romans 8:8 1.655  3. Psalms 91:1 1.590 (passage_terms: cant)
   ```

   The pack's phrase is `cannot go on anymore`, which compiles to
   `cannot anymore`; the apostrophe spelling gives `[cant, anymore]` and
   reaches nothing. **Owner ruling 10** closes it by folding the multi-word
   form into the contracted token rather than the other way round
   (§"Negation folding"). The same apostrophe pass turns every possessive
   into a plural-shaped word: **3,706 possessive occurrences over 290
   distinct bases**, of which `lord's` is 1,213 and `god's` is 374. Today the
   `-s` rule accidentally repairs most of them (`lords → lord`);
   §"Possessive folding" below shows why that accident is not good enough
   once identity lemmas exist.
7. **`myself` is a stopword** (`index.ts:27`). "kill myself", "hate myself",
   "cutting myself" collapse to one token: measured live today,
   `"I hate myself"` → #1 John 15:23 ("He who hates me, hates my Father
   also", 7.500 `Shared word: hate`), #4 Revelation 2:6 6.000, #3
   Psalms 139:22 (imprecatory); `"I want to kill myself"` → #1 Acts 7:28
   ("Do you want to kill me…", 11.167). **Owner ruling 1: it stays a
   stopword in 0.15.0** — see the ruling table and the note at the end of
   this item.

**How the r3 rule set was derived.** r1 seeded `E_RESTORE` from residuals the
**v1** stemmer produced, which is circular; r2 derived it from the **v1→v2
regression list**, which the round-2 review proved is structurally incapable
of finding the defect the item exists to fix (a family both stemmers split
never enters a regression list, and 113 e-families inside the WEB stayed
split). r3 derives every table from **vocabularies**, not from either
stemmer's output:

Let **A** = the attested *surface* vocabulary — the WEB surface word types
(12,298 under the v2 raw-word stage, below) ∪ every word of every
`concept_lexicon.phrase` (**1,553** types) ∪ every word of every curated alias
title and key (54 types) = **12,511 types**. (r3 published 12,282 / 1,551 /
12,499; the round-3 review showed the phrase side had been tokenized with the
*v1* raw stage and got 1,547 / 12,495 under the r3 rules. Under ruling 10 the
phrase side gains `dont, cant, wont, isnt, doesnt, didnt, arent` and loses
`cannot` — net +6 on the critic's figure — and the corpus side keeps the 16
contraction forms. All three numbers here come from the one r4 run.) Layer B's exposition source
text is NOT in the artifact (only its distilled `verse_terms` stems, which
are v1 stems and therefore not surface words — putting `believ` into A would
poison the derivation), so A is what the artifact can attest, and the
acceptance section reports the residual measured *against* `verse_terms`
rather than pretending it was derived from it.

Let **A⁺** = A ∪ { `step1a(w)` : w ∈ A } (**13,161** types) — A closed under
the plural rule, so a base form attested only in its `-s` inflection
(`determines`, `carves`, `injures`, `exposes`) still counts as attested.

1. **`E_RESTORE`** (residuals of `-ed`/`-ing` that take a trailing `e`).
   For every w ∈ A whose step-1b residual `r` is not already handled by the
   doubling, `at|bl|iz` or CVC rules: `r` joins `E_RESTORE` iff
   **`r ∉ A⁺` and `r+'e' ∈ A⁺`**. The `r ∉ A⁺` clause is the safety
   property — the rule can never grow a residual that is *itself* a word,
   so it cannot merge two lexemes. Clean rows: **226** (re-derived under the
   r4 raw stage: the identical 226 rows).
   Residuals where **both** `r` and `r+'e'` are attested are not decided
   mechanically; there are exactly **7**, and each is a reviewed ruling with
   its evidence (table below). Two of the seven restore, five do not.
   **Owner ruling 11 adds the first reviewed REMOVAL from the clean set:**
   `divin` is derived-clean (`divin ∉ A⁺`, `divine ∈ A⁺`) and is taken out,
   because restoring it merges *divining* into *divine* — see the ruling row
   in the bad-merge table. Total `E_RESTORE` = 226 − 1 + 2 = **227**.
2. **`E_BLOCK`** (residuals the `at|bl|iz` rule wrongly grows). Derived
   half: `r` ends `at|bl|iz`, `r ∈ A⁺`, `r+'e' ∉ A⁺` → **11** rows
   (`beat coat defeat eat entreat float gloat heat mistreat seat treat`).
   Blocking can only *prevent* a merge, never create one, so its reviewed
   half may draw on vocabulary A cannot attest — the closed class of English
   base words ending `-at`/`-eat`/`-oat` that are not `-ate` verbs — **7**
   rows, each with its evidence (table below). Total **18**.
3. **`IDENTITY_LEMMAS`.** Derived stream: a word ending `-s` whose
   non-verse-initial occurrences are ≥ 95 % capitalised (**408** candidates
   under the v2 raw-word stage) is a word whose final `-s` is not a plural
   inflection; it becomes an identity row only when the row is
   **load-bearing and safe**:

   ```ts
   const identityCandidate = (w: string): boolean =>
     endsWithS(w) && nonInitialCapRatio(w) >= 0.95;   // 408
   const identityRow = (w: string): boolean =>
     identityCandidate(w) && stem2(w) !== w && !attestedWEB.has(stem2(w));  // 233
   ```

   `stem2(w) !== w` drops the 175 candidates the stemmer already leaves
   alone (`jesus`, `titus`, `festus` and every `-us` name; `jewess`,
   `carmelitess` and every `-ss` name) — a row that changes nothing is
   decoration, and G6 mirrors a count, so decoration is a maintenance
   hazard. `!attestedWEB.has(stem2(w))` drops the candidates whose stem is
   a real word — which is **exactly the `holies` row the round-2 review
   asked about**: `stem2('holies') = 'holy'`, `holy` is attested 676 times,
   so `holies` is NOT an identity row and `holy{holies, holy}` (677
   occurrences) stays in the win list, as the section's own table says.
   Same clause keeps `philistines → philistine`, `lords → lord`,
   `sabbaths → sabbath` out.
   Then **8 reviewed removals** — candidates whose `-s` IS a plural and
   whose capitalisation is an artifact of quoted or headline text
   (`maggots`, `outlaws`, `assassins`, `taverns`, `rays`, `hellenists`,
   `libertines`, `asiarchs`; r2's ninth, `chidons`, is no longer a candidate
   because it is a possessive and the possessive fold removes it) — and
   **8 reviewed additions** (`goes`, `shemed`, `meres`, `mered`, `news`,
   `gods`, `cunning`, `rugged`; the last five are the ruling-8/9 exception
   rows). **233 rows**, enumerated below in full.
4. **`IRREGULAR_LEMMAS`** gains **23** rows (38 → **61**): the sub-floor
   irregulars, the `-the`/`-th` families, the `-ie` family the round-2
   review flagged, one plural-of-`calf` correction, and the three r4 rows —
   `divines → divin` (ruling 11), `using → use` (ruling 15) and
   `unties → untie` (an r4 self-correction: `-ies` fires at length ≥ 5, so
   `unties → unty`, which r3's `mustMerge` line claimed merged and does not;
   re-running the assertion is what found it). r3's `esaus → esau` row is
   **deleted** as decoration — see the note after the list.

The scratch implementation, the vocabulary extract and the classifier live
only in the session scratchpad; nothing was written into the repository. The
implementation commit ports the final rule set below and commits the tables
as reviewed data, together with the derivation script, so a reviewer can
re-run it.

**Design.** One module, one ordered algorithm, four reviewed tables.
`normalizeToken` keeps its shape; the raw-word stage gains **possessive
folding** and **negation folding** (ruling 10, replacing r3's contraction
expansion), `stem` becomes `stem2`, and `STOPWORDS` gains exactly the four
pronoun-contraction forms ruling 10 names — `im`, `ive`, `youre`, `theyre` —
while `myself` stays under ruling 1, so `TOKENIZER_STOPWORD_COUNT` moves
**173 → 177**. Nothing takes an option (CLAUDE.md #4).

**Final rule set, stated exactly.** Order inside `normalizeToken` is
unchanged except for one added lookup: stopword → `ARCHAIC_FORMS` →
`IRREGULAR_LEMMAS` (surface lookup, wins outright) → `IDENTITY_LEMMAS`
(surface lookup, wins outright, and **is consulted after `IRREGULAR_LEMMAS`
and before the length floor**) → surface length floor (< 3 → null) →
`stem2` → stopword check on the result. An identity hit does **not** bypass
the trailing stopword check (no identity row is a stopword today; the check
is kept so that a future row cannot smuggle one in). `stem2` is
Porter-shaped: step 1a runs, and **its output feeds step 1b**
(`givings → giving → give`).

```ts
// engine/src/tokenizer/index.ts (v2). Replaces lines 132-142 (the `stem`
// doc comment and function) and the body of rawWords (145-152).

const MIN_RESIDUAL = 3;                       // was 4
const DOUBLING_EXEMPT = new Set(['l', 's', 'z', 'f']);   // f added: scoffed -> scoff
const SIBILANT_E = ['ch', 'sh', 'x'] as const;           // NOT 's', NOT 'z'

const VOWELS = new Set(['a', 'e', 'i', 'o', 'u']);
/** Porter's vowel test: y is a vowel only after a consonant. */
function isVowel(s: string, i: number): boolean {
  return VOWELS.has(s[i]!) || (s[i] === 'y' && i > 0 && !VOWELS.has(s[i - 1]!));
}
function hasVowel(s: string): boolean {
  for (let i = 0; i < s.length; i += 1) if (isVowel(s, i)) return true;
  return false;
}
/**
 * Porter's m, written out rather than cited (round-2 review): the number of
 * VC sequences in [C](VC)^m[V].
 */
function measure(s: string): number {
  let m = 0;
  let i = 0;
  while (i < s.length && !isVowel(s, i)) i += 1;      // leading [C]
  while (i < s.length) {
    while (i < s.length && isVowel(s, i)) i += 1;     // V…
    if (i >= s.length) return m;                     // trailing [V]: not a VC
    while (i < s.length && !isVowel(s, i)) i += 1;    // …C
    m += 1;
  }
  return m;
}
/** Porter's *o: ends consonant-vowel-consonant, last not w/x/y. */
function endsCVC(s: string): boolean {
  const n = s.length;
  if (n < 3) return false;
  if (isVowel(s, n - 1) || !isVowel(s, n - 2) || isVowel(s, n - 3)) return false;
  return !['w', 'x', 'y'].includes(s[n - 1]!);
}

/** Step 1a — plurals and bare -s. NEVER strips -es as a unit. */
function step1a(word: string): string {
  if (word.endsWith('sses')) return word.slice(0, -2);              // blesses -> bless
  if (word.endsWith('ies') && word.length >= 5) {                   // cries -> cry, bodies -> body,
    return `${word.slice(0, -3)}y`;                                 // cities -> city; ties (4) falls through
  }
  if (word.endsWith('ss')) return word;                             // bless, cross unchanged
  if (word.endsWith('us')) return word;                             // never strip -s after u
  if (word.endsWith('s') && word.length - 1 >= MIN_RESIDUAL) {
    return afterSCleanup(word.slice(0, -1));                        // comes->come, hates->hate,
  }                                                                 // makes->make, times->time, ties->tie
  return word;
}
/** The epenthetic e of -ches/-shes/-xes. Measured: 40 WEB families need it. */
function afterSCleanup(r: string): string {
  if (r.endsWith('e') && r.length >= 4) {
    const base = r.slice(0, -1);
    for (const s of SIBILANT_E) if (base.endsWith(s)) return base;  // searches->search, bushes->bush
  }                                                                 // houses->house (s excluded),
  return r;                                                         // baptizes->baptize (z excluded)
}

/** Step 1b — -eed guard, -ied, -ed, -ing. */
function step1b(word: string): string {
  if (word.endsWith('eed')) return word;             // proceed/proceeded/proceeds all -> proceed;
                                                     // need/seed/feed/indeed untouched
  if (word.endsWith('ied') && word.length >= 5) {
    return `${word.slice(0, -3)}y`;                  // cried->cry, carried->carry, sanctified->sanctify
  }
  if (word.endsWith('ed')) {
    const r = word.slice(0, -2);
    return r.length >= MIN_RESIDUAL && hasVowel(r) ? afterStrip(r) : word;
  }
  if (word.endsWith('ing')) {
    const r = word.slice(0, -3);
    return r.length >= MIN_RESIDUAL && hasVowel(r) ? afterStrip(r) : word;
  }
  return word;
}
export function stem2(word: string): string { return step1b(step1a(word)); }

/** Porter 1b clean-up, in fixed order. */
function afterStrip(r: string): string {
  const last = r[r.length - 1]!;
  if (r.length >= 4 && last === r[r.length - 2] && !VOWELS.has(last) && !DOUBLING_EXEMPT.has(last)) {
    return r.slice(0, -1);                          // stopped->stop, sinned->sin, putting->put;
  }                                                 // filled/blessed/buzzed/scoffed untouched
  if (r.endsWith('at') || r.endsWith('bl') || r.endsWith('iz')) return addE(r);
  if (measure(r) === 1 && endsCVC(r)) return addE(r);   // loved->love, saved->save, hoping->hope
  return E_RESTORE.has(r) ? `${r}e` : r;               // believ->believe, judg->judge, prais->praise
}
function addE(r: string): string { return E_BLOCK.has(r) ? r : `${r}e`; }
```

The vowel guard on `-ed`/`-ing` is what saves the `-ing` nouns r1 broke:
`spring → spr` has no vowel-bearing residual → the rule refuses to strip, so
**`spring → spring`**, and identically `thing`, `king`, `bring`, `sing`,
`wing`, `string` (all verified in the whole-vocabulary run). `springs →
spring` via 1a. `MIN_RESIDUAL = 3` on `-ing`/`-ed` keeps `going → going`
(residual `go` is 2), so v2 never mints a `go` token that the word `go`
itself — two letters, below the surface floor — cannot produce.

**Possessive folding (owner ruling 9's required companion).** The raw-word
stage folds a trailing possessive before apostrophes are removed:

```ts
function rawWords(text: string): string[] {
  return foldNegations(                              // ruling 10, AFTER the passes below
    text
      .toLowerCase()
      .normalize('NFKC')
      .replace(/['‘’‛ʼ]s(?![\p{L}\p{N}])/gu, '')   // possessive: god's -> god  (0.15.0/B1)
      .replace(/['‘’‛ʼ]/g, '')                       // don't -> dont, can't -> cant
      .replace(/[^\p{L}\p{N}\s]/gu, ' ')
      .split(/\s+/)
      .filter(Boolean),
  );
}
```

Order matters and is fixed: the possessive fold runs **before** apostrophe
removal (or `god's` would already be `gods`), apostrophe removal produces the
contracted forms `dont`/`cant`/`wont`, and negation folding then pulls the
multi-word spellings onto those same forms — so all three spellings of one
negation converge on one token in one pass, with no second tokenizer and no
option (CLAUDE.md #4).

Measured over all 31,098 verses: the fold moves **3,706 occurrences** across
**290 bases**; **284** of those bases (3,695 occurrences) are already
attested as bare words, so the fold merely reaches the token the `-s` rule
was reaching by accident, and **6** bases (11 occurrences) are newly
reachable (`fuller`, `chidon`, `spider`, `barber`, `needle`, `chloe`). What
it *fixes* is the class identity lemmas create: with `gods` an identity row
(ruling 9) and no fold, all 374 occurrences of "God's" would tokenize to
`gods` and never meet `god`. With the fold, `gods` carries **235**
occurrences — the idol plurals — and `god`'s document frequency rises
**3,553 → 3,862** while `gods` falls **566 → 208**. `let's`/`it's`/`he's`
fold to `let`/`it`/`he`, all stopwords, so the contraction question does not
arise for them. Deterministic: one regex, no locale, applied before every
other pass.

| `E_RESTORE` | **227** | 226 clean (`r ∉ A⁺ ∧ r+'e' ∈ A⁺`) − 1 reviewed removal (`divin`, ruling 11) + 2 reviewed conflict rulings | `eRestoreCount` |
| `E_BLOCK` | **18** | 11 derived (`r ∈ A⁺ ∧ r+'e' ∉ A⁺`) + 7 reviewed | `eBlockCount` |
| `IDENTITY_LEMMAS` | **233** | 408 capitalisation candidates → 233 load-bearing-and-safe → − 8 reviewed removals + 8 reviewed additions | `identityLemmaCount` |
| `IRREGULAR_LEMMAS` additions | **23** (38 → 61) | shape-C survivors, sub-floor irregulars, `-the`/`-th` families, `-ie` family, `calves`, and rulings 11/15 + the `unties` correction | `lemmaCount` (mirrors `TOKENIZER_LEMMA_COUNT`, which exists) |

The **7 conflict rulings** (both `r` and `r+'e'` attested), with the
evidence the ruling was made on:

| residual | `r` occ | `r+e` occ | forms | Ruling |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pleas` | 1 (`pleas`, plural of *plea*) | 240 (`please`) | pleased 55, pleasing 23 | **RESTORE.** The plural *pleas* tokenizes to `plea` under step 1a, so nothing occupies `pleas`; without the row v1's single `pleas` family splits into `pleas`/`please` (99 occurrences), a regression. |
| `unit` | 3 (`unit`) | 1 (`unite`) | united 3 | **RESTORE.** *Unite* and *unit* are different words; `unit` itself is untouched (no suffix), only `united` moves. Accepted split, listed in the regression table. |
| `cloth` | 23 | 27 (`clothe`) | clothed 71, clothing 109 | **NO restore**, and `clothe → cloth` is added to `IRREGULAR_LEMMAS` so the whole family (cloth, cloths, clothe, clothed, clothes, clothing) lands on `cloth`. One lexeme, one token. |
| `breath` | 56 | 2 (`breathe`) | breathed 10, breathing 1 | **NO restore**; `breathe → breath` lemma row, matching the existing `breathes → breath`. |
| `bath` | 6 | 26 (`bathe`) | bathed 1, bathing 1 | **NO restore**; `bathe → bath` lemma row, matching the existing `bathes → bath`. |
| `sever` | 1 | 24 (`severe`) | severed 1 | **NO restore.** *Severed* is from *sever*; merging it into *severe* would be a lexeme error. |
| `rout` | 1 | 2 (`route`) | routed 1 | **NO restore.** *Routed* is from *rout* (defeat), not *route*. |

`E_BLOCK` (18): derived —
`beat coat defeat eat entreat float gloat heat mistreat seat treat`;
reviewed —

| row | Why it must block, with evidence |
|---|---|
| `cheat` | `cheated`/`cheating` are ontology lexicon vocabulary (the marriage-crisis phrases B.5 is built on) and `cheat` is a live `verse_terms` term. Without the row `cheated → cheate` while a query `"my wife cheats"` gives `cheat` — a split in exactly the vocabulary B.5 turns on. **This is a defect r2's rule set shipped and no WEB-only test could see** (`cheat` has 0 WEB occurrences). |
| `repeat` | `verse_terms` holds 53 rows with term `repeat`; without the row `repeated → repeate` reaches none of them (the round-2 review's objection 18). |
| `retreat` | `retreat` occurs twice in the WEB; `retreated`/`retreating` would grow to `retreate`. |
| `sweat` | `sweat` occurs 3 times (Luke 22:44); `sweating` would grow. |
| `combat` | live `verse_terms` term; `combated`/`combating` would grow. |
| `bleat` | the WEB has `bleating` (1 Samuel 15:14) but not the base; `bleate` is not a word. |
| `sibl` | `sibling(s)` is ontology vocabulary; `sible` is not a word. |

Read the list against the round-2 review's four questions: `holies` is
**out** (its stem `holy` is a word — see the derivation), `hades` is **in**
(`hade` is not), `alas` is **in** (its `-s` is not a plural; without the row
it becomes the non-word `ala`), `jewess` is **out** (`stem2` already leaves
it alone — the row would change nothing). `jesus` is likewise **out and
correct**: the `-us` rule already yields `jesus`, and the acceptance list
asserts the *behaviour*, not the table membership.

`IRREGULAR_LEMMAS` additions (23):

```
died→die  dies→die  dying→die  lying→lie  lied→lie  tying→tie
tied→tie  untied→untie  untying→untie  unties→untie   # the -ie family
                                                      # (round-2 obj 17; `unties` is r4's)
agreed→agree  freed→free  decreed→decree

bathes→bath  bathe→bath

forgiven→forgive
divines→divin                                   # ruling 11: the divination verb, not `divine`

**`unties` — an r4 self-correction, found by re-running the assertion.**
r3 listed `tie/ties/tying/tied + untie/unties/untied/untying` on one
`mustMerge` line and the round-3 review verified that "each lands on one
token". It does not: `-ies` fires at length ≥ 5, so `unties → unty`, a string
no other word produces. The r4 run fails that assertion (`{untie, unty}`) and
the fix is the lemma row above. `unties` has **0** WEB occurrences, so the row
changes no corpus number — it is a query-side row, and the `mustMerge` family
carries `corpusAbsent: true` for `unty` accordingly. This is the strongest
evidence available that the bidirectional invariant is load-bearing rather
than decorative: it caught a defect two reviews missed.

**`esaus → esau` is DELETED (round-3 minor 14).** `esaus` has 12 I1
occurrences and **0** in I2 — it is the possessive "Esau's", which the fold
sends to `esau` before any lemma lookup — so the row cannot fire on corpus
text, and the section's own exclusion rule ("a row that changes nothing is
decoration, and G6 mirrors a count, so decoration is a maintenance hazard")
excluded 175 identity candidates on exactly that ground. The cost is stated
rather than hidden: **on the I1 control** (not on anything that ships) the
regression list grows a tenth family, `esau{esau}` vs `esaus{esaus}`, 263
occurrences — vacuous over I2 exactly like the `mered` row, and the
acceptance list asserts I2. `calfs` (1 occurrence) is the same shape and is
not a row either; `calves → calf` is load-bearing and stays.

`ties` is **not** a lemma: `-ies` needs `word.length >= 5`, so `ties` falls to
the bare `-s` rule and yields `tie`. This *changes* the existing assertion
`engine/test/tokenizer.test.ts:41` `expect(normalizeToken('ties')).toBe('ties')`.
`tied`, `untied` and `untying` are lemma rows for the same family, because
the rules alone give `tied → tied` (residual `ti` is below the floor) and
`untied → unty` (`-ied` with length ≥ 5) — the ruling is **merge**: a user
who types "tied" means the verb.

`scar`/`scare` behaves as the owner ruled, and by rule, not by table:
`scar → scar`, `scars → scar` (bare `-s`), `scared → scare` (residual `scar`
is m=1 and ends CVC → `+e`). `scar` is **not** in `E_RESTORE`. The
`scar`/`scare` split is on the reviewed `mustNotMerge` list below.

**Definitions for every published count.** The round-2 review's central
finding was that r2's headline numbers came from more than one run. Every
number below comes from **one** run, and each carries the definition it
uses. Two inventories exist and they are not the same thing:

- **I1** — the surface word types v1's `rawWords` produces over
  `verses.text`: **12,477 types / 757,240 occurrences**.
- **I2** — the surface word types v2's `rawWords` produces (possessive
  folding + negation folding): **12,298 types / 755,646 occurrences**.
  **185** I1 types disappear — 184 possessive forms (`davids` 142,
  `pharaohs` 53, `armiess` …) plus `cannot` (12), which ruling 10 folds into
  `cant` — **6** appear (`fuller`, `chidon`, `spider`, `barber`, `needle`,
  `chloe`), and **413** types change occurrence count. The largest movers,
  each verified in the run: `not` 3,341 → **1,747** (the multi-word negations
  fold away), `lord` 6,758 → 7,971 and `gods` 609 → 235 (the possessive
  fold), `wont` 270 → **920**, `havent` 98 → **317**, `isnt` 168 → **436**,
  `dont` 1,374 → **1,415**. Under r3's expansion rule this line read 12,282 /
  760,762 with 201 types disappearing; ruling 10 reverses the sign of the
  contraction half, which is why every number in this paragraph moved.

The **stemmer** comparison below holds the raw-word stage constant and runs
both `normalizeToken`s over **I1**, so it isolates the change under test;
the raw-word stage is reported separately, above. r2's row claiming "12,477
types under both v1 and v2" was wrong, and this is the correction.

| Quantity | Definition | v1 (1.0.0) | v2 (2.0.0) |
|---|---|---|---|
| surface word types / occurrences | I1 | 12,477 / 757,240 | (I2: 12,298 / 755,646) |
| distinct index tokens | distinct non-null `normalizeToken` values over I1 | **9,570** (= `SELECT count(*) FROM token_stats`) | **8,721** |
| distinct index tokens, actual | the same over I2 | — | **8,718** |
| word types → `null` | over I1 | 170 | **176** |
| families v1 merges that v2 **splits** | a v1 token whose I1 members take > 1 distinct v2 value | — | **10** (263 occurrences) over I1, **8** over I2 — every one a reviewed desired split, two of them (`mered`, `esau`) vacuous once possessives fold |
| families v2 merges that v1 **split** | a v2 token with ≥ 2 I1 members taking > 1 distinct v1 value | — | **767** |
| ↳ occurrences | sum of those members' I1 occurrences | — | **80,334** |
| surface types whose token changes | `v1(t) !== v2(t)` over I1, `null` counting as a value | — | **1,742** (25,950 occurrences, **3.427 %** of the token stream) |
| newly-deleted types | `v1(t) !== null && v2(t) === null` | — | **6** (348 occurrences) |
| `verse_tokens` rows | **non-null token OCCURRENCES** over 31,098 verses — one row per `(verse_row_id, token, position)`, which is what the table stores | 318,012 (= the shipped table exactly) | **319,240** |
| ↳ distinct token per verse | the same rebuild, deduplicated per verse (NOT what `verse_tokens` holds) | 292,353 | **292,343** |

The last two rows are the round-3 minor 9 correction: r3 labelled 318,012 /
315,352 "distinct token per verse". The numbers were right for v1 and for the
r3 rule; the **unit** was wrong. Under ruling 10 the v2 figure *rises* above
v1 (319,240) rather than falling, because `dont`/`cant`/`wont` are now tokens
where r3's expansion turned them into stopwords — one more reason the unit had
to be named before the number moved.

**Where r2's numbers were wrong, and by how much.** r2 published 693 merge
families over 523,250 occurrences and 1,644 changed types over 26,094
occurrences. The round-2 review reproduced 692/83,674 and 1,645/26,141 and
could not reproduce 523,250 under any definition. r4's run reproduces
neither r2's figure nor the review's, because the tables differ (a larger,
vocabulary-derived `E_RESTORE` closes more families): **767 / 80,334** and
**1,742 / 25,950**. (r3 published 768 / 80,338 and 1,743 / 25,936 and the
round-3 critic reproduced them exactly; rulings 11 and 15 and the `esaus`
deletion move each by a handful of types.) The specific corrections:

- **523,250 was wrong by roughly 6×** and is withdrawn. It is not a
  member-occurrence sum under any grouping. For calibration from the r3
  run: total corpus occurrences 757,240; non-null under v1 318,012; the
  occurrences of ALL v2 groups with ≥ 2 members (not only the ones v1 split)
  is **224,402**. The merge-family member-occurrence sum is **80,334**.
- **The three headline numbers come from one table.** 8,721 distinct
  tokens, 767 merge families and 1,742 changed types are the same run over
  I1 with the 233-row identity table above; the file that produced them is
  committed with the implementation commit.
- **8,705 is withdrawn** (round-3 objection 2). It never reproduced: the
  round-3 critic re-derived **8,703** for the r3 rule set, and the r3 prose's
  own "201 I1 types disappear (16 contraction forms …)" put the ceiling at
  8,704 before the possessive class was counted. Under ruling 10 the actual
  figure is **8,718** — the I1-controlled 8,721 minus exactly two tokens that
  no I2 surface word can produce: `armiess` (a possessive the fold removes)
  and `cannot` (folded to `cant`). The set difference is printed by the run,
  which is how the two are named rather than inferred.

`god{god,gods}` — r2's largest single family at 4,664 occurrences — is
**absent by ruling 9**: `gods` is an identity row, `god` and `gods` stay
distinct, and the possessive fold sends "God's" to `god` rather than to
either of them.

Six word types are newly deleted from the index (v1 token → v2 `null`),
because the merged form is a stopword: `lets` 196, `ones` 144, `owns` 3,
`letting` 2, `owned` 2, `arts` 1 — **348 occurrences, 0.046 % of the token
stream**. This is a *ruling*, not an accident: `let`, `one` and `own` are
already stopwords. The pastoral phrase "loved one(s)" is carried by `love`,
whose document frequency rises from 374 to 616 in the same change.

**The bidirectional invariant (round-2 objection 2).** "No family v1 merges
may v2 split" constrains one direction only, and nothing in r2 constrained
v2 from merging two different lemmas — which it did, eleven times. r3 ships
four acceptance artifacts, two reviewed and two generated, and all four run
over the whole vocabulary on both OS legs:

**(1) Reviewed `mustNotMerge`** — pairs that must land on different tokens.
All **27** verified distinct in the r4 run:

```
plan/plane   strip/stripe  twin/twine   shin/shine   shem/shemed  scar/scare
unit/unite   mere/mered    mere/meres   sin/sine     man/mane     hat/hate
gat/gate     mal/male      born/borne   sin/sing     pray/prey    live/liver
holy/holi    sever/severe  rout/route   cheat/cheate
new/news     god/gods      cun/cunning  rug/rugged
divine/divin                                    # owner ruling 11
```

`new/news`, `god/gods`, `cun/cunning`, `rug/rugged` are owner rulings 8 and 9
plus their siblings; `divine/divin` is ruling 11; the `cheat/cheate` row pins
the `E_BLOCK` defect r2 would have shipped.

**What each row can and cannot prove (round-3 minor 20).** Seven of the
strings in this list are **not producible** by the v2 rules from any WEB
surface word: `cheat`, `cheate`, `gat`, `hat`, `holi`, `mal`, `sine`. A pair
containing one of them can only ever pass, which is the "guardrail as
decoration" shape CLAUDE.md's gate discipline warns about — so they are
labelled for what they are: **regression pins against a previous rule set**
(r1's and r2's, which did produce `cheate`, `holi` and friends), kept so that
re-introducing those rules fails a test rather than a review. The producible
rows are the live half. Two corrections to the round-3 review's version of
this list, both from the run: `mane` **is** producible — the WEB attests the
surface word once, Job 39:19 *"clothed his neck with a quivering mane"* — and
`cheat` itself is not, because the base has **0** WEB occurrences (which is
exactly why `cheat/cheate` had to be a reviewed `E_BLOCK` row in the first
place). Same count, different membership.

**(2) Reviewed `mustMerge`** — families that must land on one token, each
asserting (i) one stem for all members, (ii) that the stem is the declared
canonical form, (iii) the stem is present in `token_stats` after
`npm run build:fixture` or the family carries `corpusAbsent: true`, so the
test cannot pass vacuously.

**The counting rule, written down (round-3 minor 15).** A *family* is **one
canonical token**. `tie/ties/tying/tied` and `untie/unties/untied/untying`
land on `tie` and `untie`, so they are **two** families and are printed on two
lines. A single word with no inflections (`jesus`, `anxious`) is a family of
one: assertion (i) is vacuous for it, but (ii) and (iii) are not — they pin
that the word survives as itself and is present in `token_stats`, which is the
behaviour the acceptance list cares about. Under that rule the list is
**41** families, all verified in the r4 run:

The nine families after `spring/springs` are the ones the round-2 review

that the lexicon phrase `cant stop using` recompiles to **`cant stop use`**,
so the surface word "use" reaches it — the round-3 minor 17 case. **Residual,
stated and not smuggled:** `used` (35 occurrences, df 35) still lands on
`used`, because its `-ed` residual is the same sub-floor `us`. Closing it is a
second lemma row (`used → use`) that ruling 15 did not ask for; it is recorded
as an open item in the approval packet with its measurement, not added here.

**(3) Generated: the morphological report.** For every v2 family with ≥ 2
members, each member must be a declared inflection of the family's canonical
form (`c`, `c+s/es/ed/d/ing/ings/er/ers`, the `y→ies/ied` forms, the
`e`-dropping forms, the consonant-doubled forms) or a key of
`ARCHAIC_FORMS`/`IRREGULAR_LEMMAS`. Residual on the r4 run over I2 —
**identical to r3's, which the round-3 review reproduced independently** —
**1 family**:

```
628  hundr{hundred,hundreds}   # `hundreds` is hundr+eds, not hundr+s. v1 has the
                               # same token; accepted.
```

**(4) Generated: the register report.** No v2 family may contain both a
proper-noun-shaped member (≥ 95 % capitalised in non-verse-initial position)
and a common-word member. This is the check that catches the collisions
morphology cannot see — `cun`/`cunning` and `mere`/`mered` are both
morphologically legal and both wrong. Residual on the r3 run: **22
families**, each an enumerated reviewed exception:

```

meet{meet,meeting*,meets}        ascent{ascent,ascents*}     twin{twin*,twins}

antichrist{antichrist*,antichrists}   deity{deities,deity*}   haven{haven,havens*}
dispersion{dispersion*,dispersions}   vindicate{vindicate*,vindicated}
chisel{chisel*,chiseled,chiseling}    fix{fix*,fixed}   hoist{hoisted,hoisting*}
hush{hush*,hushed}   repairer{repairer*,repairers}   tuck{tuck*,tucked}

Re-run under the r4 rules the residual is the **same 22 families, the same
members** (the run prints them with occurrence counts: `lord` 8,011, `holy`
677, `christ` 563, `meet` 270, `ascent` 38 … `hoist` 2). (`*` marks the member
the capitalisation rule flags.) Every one is a
sentence-position or title-case artifact — "Tent of **Meeting**", "the
**Ascent** of Adummim", "**Lord**'s" — not a name/word collision; the
exception list is reviewed data and adding to it is a reviewed diff. Run
against the r2 rule set **without** the ruling-8/9 exception rows, this same
report prints `cun{cun*,cunning}`, `mere{mere,mered*,mereds*,meres*}` and
`new{new,news*}` — i.e. it is the check that would have caught the round-2
review's list before the reviewer did.

**(5) Generated: new families touching reviewed vocabulary (owner ruling 11).**
The two reports above cannot see a homograph collision whose members are all
legal inflections of common words — which is exactly what `bow`, `arm` and
`sow` are, and why the round-3 review found them by reading the merge list by
hand. The fifth report makes that reading a build artifact instead of a
favour: for every v2 family of ≥ 2 members whose canonical token appears in
the **reviewed vocabulary** — the tokens of every `concept_lexicon.phrase`
plus every token of `docs/DOCTRINAL-BASIS.md`, **1,507** tokens on this run —
it prints the family, its members and their occurrence counts, and marks the
ones that are **new** (v1 split them). Measured: **680** families touch the
reviewed vocabulary, **252** of them new, and **250** of the 252 have a
canonical form that is itself an attested WEB surface word (the round-3
review's proposed candidate rule — it does not narrow the set usefully, which
is stated here rather than discovered by the next reviewer).

The report is **signed once**: it is committed as
`engine/test/fixtures/new-families-review.json` with `reviewedBy`, `date` and
the family list, and `engine/test/tokenizer-new-families.test.ts` regenerates
it and fails when the generated set differs from the signed one — naming every
family that entered. Adding a family to the signed file is a reviewed-data
diff, so the next `bow` fails a test in the commit that creates it. The
report is a *review artifact with a stated scope*, not a filter: it cannot
decide which of the 252 are homographs (that needs word senses, which the
runtime has none of and CLAUDE.md #1 forbids importing), and the scope it does
guarantee is "no family touching curated or doctrinal vocabulary enters
unreviewed".

**`myself` — owner ruling 1 (option b).** It **stays a stopword** in

Deuteronomy 32:39 — capped at 6.000 by B2, carrying no authority, and
answering nothing. The consequence to state plainly: **`"kill myself"`
continues to tokenize to `[kill]`, and therefore continues to depend on the
bare `kill` admission ruling in S-A1** — that ruling, not this item, is what
makes the suicide query safe in 0.15.0. Phase C removes the stopword in the

phrases, fixture first (`pastoral-kill-myself.json`), and re-measures.

(`im, ive, youre, theyre`), not from anything `myself` decides. The two
rulings touch the same constant and are independent, which is stated here
because a reader checking `stopwordCount` against ruling 1 alone would find
it wrong.

**Negation folding (owner ruling 10 — the direction is REVERSED).** r3
expanded the contracted forms into their words (`dont → do, not`), which put
the whole weight of a negation phrase onto whatever content word survived —
the mechanism that turned `dont give up` into the bare token `give` (df
1,946). Ruling 10 folds the other way: the **multi-word** spelling is
canonicalized onto the **contracted WEB token**, which already exists in the
index and is already significant.

```ts
/**
 * Negation folding (0.15.0/B1, owner ruling 10). Applied to the raw word
 * sequence AFTER the possessive fold and apostrophe removal, so `can't` has
 * already become `cant` and only the multi-word spellings remain. Two-word
 * keys are tried before one-word keys, left to right, non-overlapping.
 * 13 rows; mirrored as tokenizer.negationFoldRows.
 */
const NEGATION_FOLDS_2: ReadonlyMap<string, string> = new Map([
  ['can not',    'cant'],      ['do not',     'dont'],
  ['will not',   'wont'],      ['is not',     'isnt'],
  ['does not',   'doesnt'],    ['did not',    'didnt'],
  ['could not',  'couldnt'],   ['would not',  'wouldnt'],
  ['should not', 'shouldnt'],  ['are not',    'arent'],
  ['was not',    'wasnt'],     ['have not',   'havent'],
]);
const NEGATION_FOLDS_1: ReadonlyMap<string, string> = new Map([
  ['cannot', 'cant'],          // one word in the WEB 12 times; same lexeme
]);

function foldNegations(words: readonly string[]): string[] {
  const out: string[] = [];
  let i = 0;
  while (i < words.length) {
    const two = i + 1 < words.length
      ? NEGATION_FOLDS_2.get(`${words[i]!} ${words[i + 1]!}`)
      : undefined;
    if (two !== undefined) { out.push(two); i += 2; continue; }
    const one = NEGATION_FOLDS_1.get(words[i]!);
    if (one !== undefined) { out.push(one); i += 1; continue; }
    out.push(words[i]!); i += 1;
  }
  return out;
}
```

`dont`, `cant`, `wont`, `isnt`, `doesnt`, `didnt`, `couldnt`, `wouldnt`,
`shouldnt`, `arent`, `wasnt`, `havent` all survive `normalizeToken`
unchanged — none is a stopword, none matches a suffix rule — so each is a
significant token carrying its negation. Their df before and after the fold
is the table above; every one of them is a **real WEB token today**, which is
the ruling's premise and is verified rather than assumed.

**What the reversal buys, measured on the live 0.14.0 engine.**

| query | today (HEAD) | under ruling 10 | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `"i cannot go on anymore"` | 2 Corinthians 1:8-10 **40.000** `Theme: Hope in despair`, 1 Kings 19:4-7 38.000, Matthew 11:28-29 37.600 | unchanged | phrase `cannot go on anymore` compiles to `cannot anymore` today, `cant anymore` under r4; the query lands on the same tokens either way |
| `"i can't go on anymore"` | Job 23:8 **1.655** `Shared word: cant`, Romans 8:8 1.655, Psalms 91:1 1.590 — **the pack is not reached** | **the same page as "cannot"** — both sides are `[cant, anymore]` | the apostrophe spelling and the written-out spelling stop being two vocabularies |
| `"dont give up"` | Galatians 6:9 **49.636** = anchor 40.000 + proximity 6.000 + `Shared words: dont, give` 3.636 | **byte-identical** (phrase `dont give`, query `[dont, give]`) | the r3 rule would have compiled the phrase to bare `give` |
| `"do not give up"` | Genesis 25:5 6.000 `Shared word: give` — token scatter, **no concept chip** | **the Galatians 6:9 page above** | "do not" folds to `dont`, so the written-out form reaches the pack for the first time |
| `"give"` (one word) | Genesis 25:5 6.000, Genesis 30:28 5.000 — token scatter, no concept chip | unchanged | under the **r3** rule this query would have fired the `do-not-lose-heart` anchor set authoritatively (`isBareWordConceptCue` requires `queryTokenCount > 1`, `concept.ts:211`) — the round-3 BLOCKING hazard, now structurally impossible |

**Pronoun contractions are NOT folded** (ruling 10), and the four whose
expansions are entirely stopwords join `STOPWORDS`:

| form | ruling | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `im` | **STOPWORD** | "I'm" → `i am`, both stopwords. 16 WEB occurrences (Genesis 31:35 "I'm having my period", 2 Samuel 18:14, Matthew 8:8, …). Observationally a no-op today — `im` is two letters and the surface floor already drops it — so the row is *intent made explicit*, not a behaviour change. |

| `hes`, `shes`, `its`, `id`, `ill`, `well`, `were`, `wed` | **untouched** | each collides with a real word (`ill`, `well`, `wed` are live pastoral and marriage vocabulary; `were` is a narrative verb; `its` is a possessive), and the possessive fold already reduces `he's`/`she's` to stopwords. Expanding any of them would rewrite text the author wrote. |
| `youve`, `theyve` | **untouched, and it costs nothing** | `youve` is a token **today** (df 3) and stays one; `theyve` has 0 occurrences. The ruling does not name them, so they keep v1's behaviour exactly — this is stated because r3 *expanded* them and a reader comparing the two versions would otherwise see an unexplained difference. |

`TOKENIZER_STOPWORD_COUNT` is therefore **173 → 177**. `myself` is untouched
(ruling 1).

**Two residuals, stated rather than closed by the author.**

1. **OWNER-DESIGN CONCERN — the fold list is not closed under its own rule.**
   Ruling 10 enumerates twelve two-word folds. Three negations whose
   contracted form is a live WEB token have **no** multi-word row:
   `werent` ("were not", 28 df), `hasnt` ("has not", 49) and `hadnt` ("had
   not", 6). Their apostrophe spellings fold to the token; their written-out
   spellings still dissolve into stopwords — i.e. the exact asymmetry ruling
   10 exists to remove, surviving in three rows. Applied as ruled (twelve
   rows + `cannot`); the three-row extension is offered in the approval
   packet with these figures and is a one-line reviewed-data diff if the
   owner wants it.
2. **`not` stays a stopword, so "fear not" is out of scope.** The ruling says
   so explicitly. `"fear not"` therefore still tokenizes to `[fear]`, exactly
   as today; the negation is carried only where a *contracted* form exists.
   Noted here so the next reader does not read the fold table as a general
   negation feature. It is not one.

**One correction to the ruling's worked example, with proof.** Ruling 10
gives the consequence `cant go on` ≡ `cannot go on` ≡ `can't go on` →
`{cant, go}`. The token set is **`{cant}`**: `go` is two letters and dies on
the surface length floor (`raw.length < 3 → null`, `index.ts`), the same
floor this item already invokes for `going → going` ("v2 never mints a `go`
token that the word `go` itself cannot produce"). The three spellings do
converge, which is the ruling's substance, and they converge on one token
rather than two. Nothing else in the ruling depends on it, and no lexicon
phrase collapses to a bare `cant` (the two `cant …` phrases compile to
`cant stop drink` and `cant stop use`; `cannot go on anymore` compiles to
`cant anymore`), so the widening the ruling-7 class worries about does not
arise here — verified over all 1,654 rows.

**Locale and Unicode invariance.** `toLowerCase()` with no locale argument
(ECMAScript default case mapping is locale-independent; the Turkish-i hazard
exists only in `toLocaleLowerCase`), `normalize('NFKC')` before the
possessive/apostrophe/punctuation passes so composed and decomposed input
reach one form, and the `\p{L}\p{N}` classes as today. No `Intl`, no `Date`,
no `Math.random`, no Map-iteration-order dependence (tables are looked up,
never iterated).

**Ordering impact.** Everything moves; this is why the bundle exists.
Specifically: (a) inflection families merge, so `token_overlap` coverage
rises for queries whose inflection differed from the verse ("sanctify" now
reaches "sanctified"); (b) IDF for every merged token falls (df sums — see
the table above), so its share of `queryIdfTotal` shifts; (c) lexicon
phrases whose `normalized` form changes (**288 of 1,654 rows**, measured)
re-match; (d) `verses → verse` merges — and, stated honestly, this makes the
Layer B `verse` scatter **larger**, not smaller: `verse` occurs once in
scripture text but 401 times in `verse_terms`, and today's query `verses`
reaches only the 30 rows under `vers`. What removes it is B.3, and only for
queries where no curated phrase needs the token: under B.3's protected-token
rule `"verses for a funeral"` strips it (no phrase match) while
`"bible verses for widows"` keeps it (the compiled phrase `bible vers widow`
needs it) — which is the correct behaviour in both cases, and the residual
is stated in B.3's table rather than claimed away; (e) `anxiou → anxious`,
`jesu → jesus` change spelling-correction vocabulary and therefore which OOV
corrections fire (`spelling_terms` rebuilds); (f) the possessive fold moves
3,706 occurrences to their base word; (g) negation folding moves 1,594
occurrences off `not` and onto twelve negation tokens, and adds
`verse_tokens` rows rather than removing them (318,012 → 319,240). The
`verse_translation_tokens` index (307,923 rows) re-stems too, so
`translation_variant` matches move. The measured size of the stemmer move is
**1,742 word types / 25,950 occurrences / 3.427 %** of the token stream, and
**849 fewer** distinct index tokens over the I1 control (**852 fewer** on the
inventory that ships: 9,570 → 8,718).

**Determinism proof.** `stem2` is a total function of its input string over
fixed tables; no table is iterated; all comparisons are code-unit string
comparisons. The pipeline imports the same module
(`pipeline/src/importers/ontologyImporter.ts:18`, `aliasImporter.ts:17`,
`tskImporter.ts:46`, `buildCorpus.ts:13`), so both vocabularies are produced
by one function. `TOKENIZER_VERSION = '2.0.0'`
(`engine/src/config/engineVersion.ts:66`) is stamped into `meta`
(`buildCorpus.ts:209`) and checked at `createEngine.ts:161`; a 1.0.0
artifact cannot be opened by a 2.0.0 engine, so mismatched vocabularies
cannot compare.

**Mirror keys.** `MIN_RESIDUAL` and the table contents change the ordering of
every query, and `eval/budgets.json signalBudgets.$comment` states the
doctrine plainly: "a constant cannot be retuned in code without this
reviewed-data change travelling in the same commit". B1 therefore registers a
**top-level `tokenizer` block** in `eval/budgets.json`, and — owner ruling 13
— **a gate call that reads it**, because r3's version registered eleven keys
that no gate could ever have read (round-3 objection 5: the G6 half receives
only the parsed `signalBudgets` block, so a stale tokenizer count and a
missing one would both have passed). Keys inside the block are **flat**, which
is the shape the gate's `Record<string, unknown>` walk (`:391`) and
`canonicalConstant` (`:452-461`) actually compare — r3's dotted
`tokenizer.minStemResidual` matched neither.

| Mirror key (inside the `tokenizer` block) | Engine export | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `minStemResidual` | `MIN_STEM_RESIDUAL` | 3 |
| `doublingExempt` | `TOKENIZER_DOUBLING_EXEMPT` (array, code-unit sorted) | `["f","l","s","z"]` |
| `sibilantE` | `TOKENIZER_SIBILANT_E` (array) | `["ch","sh","x"]` |
| `stopwordCount` | `TOKENIZER_STOPWORD_COUNT` (`index.ts:244`) | 173 → **177** (ruling 10's four pronoun forms; `myself` stays under ruling 1) |
| `archaicFormCount` | `TOKENIZER_ARCHAIC_FORM_COUNT` (`:245`) | 39, unchanged |
| `lemmaCount` | `TOKENIZER_LEMMA_COUNT` (`:246`) | 38 → **61** (+23) |
| `identityLemmaCount` | `TOKENIZER_IDENTITY_LEMMA_COUNT` (new) | **233** |
| `eRestoreCount` | `TOKENIZER_E_RESTORE_COUNT` (new) | **227** |
| `eBlockCount` | `TOKENIZER_E_BLOCK_COUNT` (new) | **18** |
| `negationFoldRows` | `TOKENIZER_NEGATION_FOLD_ROWS` (new) | **13** (`NEGATION_FOLDS_2.size + NEGATION_FOLDS_1.size`) |
| `possessiveFold` | `TOKENIZER_POSSESSIVE_FOLD` (new, boolean) | `true` |

today takes one argument — the mirror — and hard-codes its gate id, its label
and its `engineValues` registry (`eval/src/gates/budgetsProperty.ts:370-449`).
It is generalized to take the registry first, exactly as the ruling states the
call:

export function reviewedConstantsCheck(

The `mergeGateResults` row stays one roster row (the same pattern G2 and G3
use), so the gate count does not change. Both halves keep the existing
both-directions behaviour: a mirror key the registry does not know is
`unknown-constant` (`:403-408`), a registry key the mirror lacks is
`unmirrored-constant` (`:426-432`), and an absent block is
**not-applicable with a reason** (`:371-377`) rather than a pass — gate
discipline, and now with a second reason string naming the `tokenizer` block.

**The test that fails when a constant drifts** (round-3 objection 5 asked for
the mirror to be shown red once):

```ts
// eval/test/budgets-property.test.ts — new cases beside the existing eight,
// which all gain the registry argument (`reviewedConstantsCheck(signalConstants, …)`).
const committedTokenizerMirror = () =>
  (JSON.parse(readFileSync(new URL('../budgets.json', import.meta.url), 'utf8')) as
    { tokenizer?: unknown }).tokenizer;

it('passes when the committed tokenizer mirror equals the engine tables', () => {
  const result = reviewedConstantsCheck(tokenizerConstants, committedTokenizerMirror());
  expect(result.status).toBe('pass');
  expect(result.summary).toContain('identityLemmaCount');
});

it('rings on a drifted table: identityLemmaCount 232 against a 233-row table fails', () => {
  const result = reviewedConstantsCheck(tokenizerConstants, {
    ...(committedTokenizerMirror() as Record<string, unknown>),
    identityLemmaCount: 232,
  });
  expect(result.status).toBe('fail');
  expect((result.findings ?? []).some((f) => f.categoryCode === 'mirror-mismatch')).toBe(true);
});

it('rings on a deleted mirror key: dropping eRestoreCount is unmirrored-constant', () => {
  const mirror = { ...(committedTokenizerMirror() as Record<string, unknown>) };
  delete mirror.eRestoreCount;
  const result = reviewedConstantsCheck(tokenizerConstants, mirror);
  expect(result.status).toBe('fail');
  expect((result.findings ?? []).some((f) => f.categoryCode === 'unmirrored-constant')).toBe(true);
});

it('reports not-applicable with the reason when the tokenizer block is absent', () => {
  const result = reviewedConstantsCheck(tokenizerConstants);
  expect(result.status).toBe('not-applicable');
  expect(result.summary).toContain('tokenizer');
});
```

The first drift test is the one that makes the mirror argument true rather
than plausible: with `TOKENIZER_IDENTITY_LEMMA_COUNT` asserted against
`IDENTITY_LEMMAS.size` in the engine and mirrored here, a table edit that does
not travel with its reviewed-data diff is a red `budgets-property` run naming
the key. **Cost, stated:** generalizing the signature touches the eight
existing call sites in `eval/test/budgets-property.test.ts:119-174` and the
one in `gauntlet.ts:1148`; they are mechanical edits in the B1 commit.

Arrays mirror directly: `canonicalConstant`
(`eval/src/gates/budgetsProperty.ts:452-461`) routes arrays through
`JSON.stringify`, so ordered JSON is the canonical form — no SHA hedge is
needed anywhere in this bundle. A count mirror that disagrees with the
engine export is a `budgets-property` failure, which is what caught
r2's 20-vs-21 contraction error; the acceptance list below asserts every
count against `.size`/`.length` rather than a literal.

New tests. **The idempotence property test from r1 is DROPPED**, and it is
worth saying why so nobody re-adds it: Porter-shaped stemmers are not
idempotent (`proceeded → proceed`, and a second application of a rule set
without the `-eed` guard gives `procee`), so `stem2(stem2(x)) === stem2(x)`
is the wrong invariant. The real invariant is that `stem` is applied
**exactly once per surface token**, which is structural, not algebraic.
Six tests replace it:

- **(a) single-application invariant.** `stem2` is called from exactly one
  place, `normalizeToken` (`engine/src/tokenizer/index.ts:166`), and
  `normalizeToken` is the only path into a token on both sides: runtime
  `significantWords`/`significantWordsWithSurface`/`tokenStream`
  (`index.ts:175-203, 234-241`) call it once per raw word, and the pipeline
  reaches tokens only through the same module.
  `engine/test/tokenizer-single-application.test.ts` asserts it mechanically:
  a source-level check that `stem2(` appears exactly once outside its own
  definition, plus a spy-based test that
  `significantWords('proceeded proceeds proceed')` calls the stemmer three

### B.2 Sole-evidence predicate

**Measured defect.** `engine/src/ranking/budgets.ts:201-226` (step 5; the
code begins at `:207`):

```ts
  const soleCaps = budgets.soleEvidenceMaxPoints;
  if (soleCaps && reasons.length > 0) {
    const memberCaps = reasons.map((reason) => soleCaps[reason.family]);
    if (memberCaps.every((cap) => cap !== undefined)) {
      const soleCap = Math.min(...(memberCaps as number[]));
```

"Sole" means "every surviving reason's family is a key of
`soleEvidenceMaxPoints`", and that map has one key (`translation_variant:
6`, line 88). One `passage_terms` chip worth 1.018 points disables the step.
Measured live: `"I'm having a panic attack"` → #1 2 Samuel 17:9 at
**15.018** = `translation_variant 14.000` + `passage_terms 1.018` ("Behold,
he is now hidden in some pit…", a battle narrative), #2 2 Samuel 17:2
14.986, while #3/#4 (Judges 4:15, 1 Samuel 7:10) — lone variants — are
correctly capped at 6.000. The corroboration that lifts #1 above the floor
is a single homiletical term, `attack`.

**Design.** Sole = no authoritative reason survived. Replace the per-family
map with one scalar.

```ts
// budgets.ts — SignalBudgets (replaces lines 48-57, the soleEvidenceMaxPoints
// doc block and declaration)
  /**
   * Sole-evidence ceiling (0.15.0/B2): when NO surviving reason is
   * authoritative (reference / exact_phrase / concept_anchor), the result
   * rests on hints, and its total is capped here — below token_overlap's
   * own 10 — so accumulated hints never impersonate a match. Ordering
   * among capped results is preserved by rank()'s uncapped-total tie-break.
   */
  readonly soleEvidenceCeiling: number;

// DEFAULT_BUDGETS (replaces line 88, `soleEvidenceMaxPoints: { translation_variant: 6 },`)
  soleEvidenceCeiling: 6,

// applyBudgets step 5 (replaces lines 201-226)
  // 5: sole-evidence ceiling. No authoritative family survived: the whole
  // result rests on weak/hint evidence, so the total is capped. Labels are
  // untouched; uncappedPoints records what the hint would have claimed.
  const uncappedTotal = reasons.reduce(
    (sum, reason) => sum + (reason.uncappedPoints ?? reason.points), 0,
  );
  let soleCapApplied = false;
  if (reasons.length > 0 && !reasons.some((reason) => isAuthoritative(reason.family))) {
    const soleCap = budgets.soleEvidenceCeiling;
    const total = reasons.reduce((sum, reason) => sum + reason.points, 0);
    if (total > soleCap && total > 0) {
      capped = true;
      soleCapApplied = true;
      const scale = soleCap / total;
      for (let index = 0; index < reasons.length; index += 1) {
        const member = reasons[index]!;
        reasons[index] = { ...member, points: member.points * scale,
                           uncappedPoints: member.uncappedPoints ?? member.points };
      }
    }
  }
  // ... and at the end of applyBudgets (replaces line 235):
  //   REQUIRED: assign the ceiling EXACTLY; do not re-sum the scaled parts.
  const score = soleCapApplied
    ? budgets.soleEvidenceCeiling
    : ordered.reduce((sum, reason) => sum + reason.points, 0);
  return { score, reasons: ordered, capped, soleCapped: soleCapApplied,
           uncappedScore: uncappedTotal };
  // BudgetedScore and RankedResult both gain `readonly uncappedScore: number`
  // AND `readonly soleCapped: boolean` in the SAME commit, or rank() reads
  // undefined. `soleCapped` is NOT `capped`: four other steps set `capped`,
  // and the tie-break below must fire only on rows whose score was ASSIGNED
  // the ceiling (owner ruling 2).
```

**The composition of steps 4, 4b and 5, in one place** (round-2 objection
19: B2 and B6 were written independently and their composition was never
shown). Final order inside `applyBudgets`, with the line each hunk replaces:

```ts
  // 3  correlation groups                       budgets.ts:167-181  (unchanged)
  // 4  weakAggregateCap 30                      budgets.ts:184-198  (unchanged)
  // 4b curated-order guard (B6)                 INSERTED after :199
  //      iterates the LIVE `reasons` array by index — step 4 replaced its
  //      entries, so the `weak` array captured at :186 must NOT be reused.
  //      Writes uncappedPoints only if not already set.
  // 5  sole-evidence ceiling (B2)               REPLACES :201-226
  //      `uncappedTotal` is computed HERE, i.e. AFTER 4b, so on an anchored
  //      row it is the post-guard total. That is harmless and now provably
  //      so: 4b only runs when a concept_anchor is present, step 5 only runs
  //      when none is, and `soleCapped` gates the tie-break — so no row can
  //      ever be ordered by a pre-guard total. (This is the interaction
  //      objection 8 named; ruling 2's gate closes it rather than documents
  //      it.)
  // -- presentation sort                        budgets.ts:229-233  (unchanged)
  // -- score                                    REPLACES :235
  //      soleCapped ? budgets.soleEvidenceCeiling : sum(ordered.points)
```

**The exact-assignment rule is not decoration — measured.** With the
ceiling reached by proportional scaling and the score re-summed, the total
lands within one ULP of 6 but not on it, and `compareResults`'s first line
(`if (b.score !== a.score) return b.score - a.score;`, `rank.ts:58`) then
orders capped rows by floating-point noise and the `uncappedScore`
tie-break never runs. Measured on the patched build, `"I'm having a panic
attack"`, scores printed at 20 significant digits:

```
re-summed:   2 Sam 17:2  6.0000000000000008882   2 Sam 17:9  5.9999999999999991118
             -> page order 17:2, Judges 4:15, 1 Sam 7:10, 17:9   (today's order is 17:9 first)
assigned:    2 Sam 17:2  6.0000000000000000000   2 Sam 17:9  6.0000000000000000000
             -> uncappedScore 15.018 > 14.986 > 14 > 14
             -> page order 17:9, 17:2, Judges 4:15, 1 Sam 7:10  (today's order, restored)
```

That is also a cross-platform determinism hazard of exactly the kind G2
exists to catch, so the assignment is mandatory, not an optimisation. The
same re-summing pattern exists today for `weakAggregateCap` and the
correlation-group cap; it is currently unreachable on this corpus (0 rows in
the measurement below) and is recorded as a follow-up, not fixed here.

**OWNER-DESIGN CONCERN (kept as designed, with a required companion).** A
hard cap makes every capped result score exactly 6.000. Today that already
produces the flat tie visible at #3/#4 above; under the new predicate it
would flatten *every* lexical-only query — for
`"do justly love mercy walk humbly"` Micah 6:8 (13.123), Ephesians 2:4-5
(11.236) and Genesis 32:10 (6.000) would all read 6.000 and `compareResults`
(`rank.ts:57-77`) would fall through to `targetId`, putting **Genesis 32:10
first** by canonical order. That is an ordering regression, not a safety
improvement. The companion that makes the owner's design sound without
changing its scores: `compareResults` gains one tie-break.

**Placement, precisely.** The new comparison goes **after** the
authoritative-first rule (`rank.ts:59-61`) and **after** the
`concept_anchor` curated tie-break (`rank.ts:71-75`), and **immediately
before** the `targetId` return (`rank.ts:76`) — i.e. it is inserted as a new
line between the closing brace of the `if (aAuth && bAuth)` block at `:75`
and the `return a.targetId …` at `:76`:

```ts
// rank.ts — inserted between :75 and :76
  // Owner ruling 2: GATED to sole-capped rows. Two rows whose scores were
  // both ASSIGNED the ceiling carry no information in `score` at all, so
  // ordering them by what they would have scored is the only honest choice.
  // Every other exact tie keeps the documented stable-ID tie-break
  // (docs/implementation-plan.md:31, rank.ts:50-56) — §5 is untouched for
  // them, and an anchored row (which can never be sole-capped) can never be
  // ordered by a pre-B6-guard total.
  if (a.soleCapped && b.soleCapped && b.uncappedScore !== a.uncappedScore) {
    return b.uncappedScore - a.uncappedScore;
  }
  return a.targetId < b.targetId ? -1 : a.targetId > b.targetId ? 1 : 0;
```

Placing it any earlier — directly after `score` — would let a weak-only row
with a 13.1 uncapped total outrank a genuine 6.000 authoritative row at an
exact tie, inverting the very rule B2 exists to enforce. The gate is what
keeps the change inside its blast radius: **the comparison is unreachable
for any row the sole-evidence ceiling did not rewrite**, which is every
anchored row and every row scoring below the ceiling.

`RankedResult` carries `uncappedScore` and `soleCapped` (internal types, not
on `DiscoveryResult`; `RankedResult` is exported **only** from
`engine/src/internal.ts:119` — the `./internal` subpath in
`engine/package.json` — never from `engine/src/index.ts`, and
`eval/test/public-surface.test.ts` pins `Candidate` as unreachable, so nothing
in the consumer contract moves). **Owner ruling 14: `soleCapped` stays
internal** — it is not added to `DiscoveryResult`, and the tests that observe
it do so through the engine-internal surface, not the public one:
`engine/test/rank.test.ts` and `engine/test/budgets.test.ts` already import
`../src/ranking/rank.js` and `../src/ranking/budgets.js` directly, so the flag
is assertable without widening anything a consumer can see. The consequence
for B.12's risk list — that a consumer cannot observe which tie-break produced
an order — is real and is recorded there as an accepted cost rather than
mitigated away. The
comparator remains a total order (`targetId` is unique, and it is still the
final comparison on every path). **The behaviour change is nevertheless a §5
matter and is carried in the consumer note** (B.11) in the same paragraph as
the `SignalBudgets` break, per owner ruling 5: *at an exact tie between two
sole-capped results the order is now decided by the uncapped total rather
than by `targetId`; every other tie is unchanged.*

**Measured, on the patched build** (`"do justly love mercy walk humbly"`,
with the exact-assignment rule above):

| Rank | Passage | today | B2 score | `uncappedScore` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Micah 6:8 | 13.123 | 6.000 | 13.123 |
| 2 | Ephesians 2:4-5 | 11.236 | 6.000 | 11.236 |
| 3 | Colossians 3:14 | 9.181 | 6.000 | 9.181 |
| 4 | Ephesians 5:2 | 8.562 | 6.000 | 8.562 |
| 5 | Galatians 6:16 | 8.066 | 6.000 | 8.066 |
| 6 | Jude 1:2 | 7.375 | 6.000 | 7.375 |

Order preserved exactly; every score is 6.000.

**Where `uncappedScore` does NOT reproduce today's order — stated plainly,
and accepted (now bounded by the gate).** The class below can only be
reached by a row that is *also* sole-capped, since the tie-break no longer
fires anywhere else. `uncappedPoints` is written by whichever cap fires *first*
and is never overwritten (`member.uncappedPoints ?? member.points`,
`budgets.ts:196` and `:221`). So for a result whose weak total already
exceeded `weakAggregateCap 30` at step 4, `uncappedScore` is the
**pre-step-4** total, not today's post-step-4 score. Two weak-only results
at raw 40 and 35 tie at 30.000 today and are separated by `targetId`; under
the companion they are separated by 40 vs 35. That is deterministic and
arguably better, but it **is** a behaviour change and it is named here, in
the changelog and in the approval packet. `ENGINE_VERSION` bumps for this
bundle regardless.

Measured incidence, re-run for r3 over **229 distinct queries** (the
84-query battery, the 50-query second battery, the 25 probes and nine
half-remembered-phrase queries, deduped): the engine returned **4,180
weak-only rows**, of which **0** had a weak total above `weakAggregateCap
30`. (r2 measured 3,140 of 175 queries and the round-2 review 3,046 of 152;
all three runs agree on the number that matters, which is zero.) The class
is reachable in principle (anchor-free `translation_variant 14 +
token_overlap 10 + proximity 6 + passage_terms 8 = 38`) but is empty on
today's corpus, so the expected probe churn from this specific consequence
is zero.

Ordering of steps: step 5 runs after step 4 (`weakAggregateCap` 30), so a
weak-only result is scaled twice when its raw weak total exceeds 30; both
scalings are proportional and commute, so the result is identical to a
single scaling to 6. Step 4 is kept because it also governs results that
DO carry an authoritative reason.

**Ordering impact — re-derived from the battery, not from the family caps.**
Every result with no `reference`/`exact_phrase`/`concept_anchor` reason is
capped at 6. r1 read this class off the per-family `maxPoints` table and got
one row wrong; the corrected list is measured:

| Weak-only shape | today | B2 | measured example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `token_overlap`-led lexical | ≤ 10 | 6.000 | John 15:23 on "I hate myself" 7.500 → 6.000 |
| `translation_variant` + `passage_terms` | ≤ 15 | 6.000 | 2 Samuel 17:9 on "panic attack" 15.018 → 6.000 |
| lone `translation_variant` | 6 (already capped) | 6.000 | Judges 4:15, unchanged |
| **`concept_lexicon`-only "Related theme" rows** | **up to 12** (`maxPoints 12, maxReasons 2`) — **not 6** | 6.000 | **1 John 1:9 on "unpardonable sin" 11.100 → 6.000** (two chips: `Related theme: Repentance` 5.700 + `Related theme: God's forgiveness` 5.400) |
| `concept_lexicon` + `passage_terms` | ≤ 20 | 6.000 | Psalms 51:3 6.283 → 6.000; Isaiah 43:25 6.073 → 6.000 |
| `passage_terms`-only | < 6 | unchanged | Matthew 11:17 on "verses for a funeral" 1.776 |
| any row with an authoritative chip | — | untouched | Matthew 12:31-32 40.000, unchanged |

r1 stated "`concept_lexicon`-only rows (6 → 6, unchanged)". That is wrong:
`concept_lexicon` has `maxPoints 12, maxReasons 2`, so a two-chip
"Related theme" row reaches 12, and 1 John 1:9 measurably drops 11.100 →
6.000. The corrected row is above and the approval packet carries it.

Consequence for the pastoral battery: 2 Samuel 17:9 and 17:2 drop to 6.000
on "panic attack" and tie with the other variants; with the companion
tie-break and the exact-assignment rule they stay in today's order (17:9,
17:2, Judges 4:15, 1 Samuel 7:10) but behind any anchor a Phase C anxiety
phrase provides.

**Determinism proof.** Pure arithmetic on the reasons array; `isAuthoritative`
is a fixed list (`reasons/types.ts:34-42`). New constant
`DEFAULT_BUDGETS.soleEvidenceCeiling = 6` is registered in
`eval/src/gates/budgetsProperty.ts:383-389` as mirror key
**`soleEvidenceCeiling`**, and `soleEvidenceMaxPoints` is REMOVED from the
registry and from `eval/budgets.json:216` in the same commit (the registry
and mirror must match in both directions; a stale key is an
`unknown-constant` failure, `budgets-property.test.ts:162-169`).
`SignalBudgets` is a public type (`engine/src/index.ts:30`): removing the
optional `soleEvidenceMaxPoints` and adding the required
`soleEvidenceCeiling` breaks any consumer that *constructs* a budgets
object. **Resolved, not deferred:** nothing in `docs/COMPATIBILITY.md` or
§5 forbids a breaking type change pre-1.0, and there is precedent in this
package's own history — 0.8.0 shipped a breaking ordering change in a minor,
and 0.14.0 removed the internal surface from the root entry. The tokenizer
bump (B1) forces every consumer to re-pin `(engine, artifact)` in this
release anyway, so the change costs no additional migration. It ships as a
breaking type change (owner ruling 5), documented in `docs/COMPATIBILITY.md`
and the changelog, with the removed key recorded as a `$comment` tombstone
in `eval/budgets.json` (see B.11 step 4). **The same COMPATIBILITY note
carries the tie-break behaviour change** (ruling 2): one paragraph naming
both, so a consumer reads the type change and the ordering change together
rather than discovering the second from a snapshot diff. No `soleEvidenceMaxPoints?: never`
tombstone is added to the TypeScript type: a removed optional key that no
consumer can set is better expressed by the changelog entry than by a
permanent phantom field.

**Tests.** Existing:
- `engine/test/budgets.test.ts:86-138` — `:89` reads
