### B.10 Alias importer generalization

**Measured defect.** `pipeline/src/importers/aliasImporter.ts` is
hymn-shaped: `HymnAliasPackSource.hymns[]` (`:20-33`) requires
`title/author/year/provenance` (`:128-145`), the row's `locator` is
`Author, "Title" (year)` (`:256`), and — the part that matters most for
Phase C — **every alias chip the engine renders today says `Hymn:`**. There
are exactly two label sites, and both hard-code the word:

```
engine/src/intents/concept.ts:246   aliasConceptEvidence  → `Hymn: "${alias.title}" → Theme: ${anchor.conceptLabel}`
engine/src/intents/concept.ts:268   aliasPassageEvidence  → `Hymn: "${alias.title}"`
```

So a misquote ("God helps those who help themselves") or a named passage
("the Lord's Prayer") cannot be expressed without the chip calling it a
hymn — a covenant-#5 failure (the explanation is the contract) before it is
a schema problem. The Phase C data plan (S-A3) needs both kinds.

**Design.** `kind` per file (top-level default) or per row; provenance
fields validated per kind; the three admission rules kept verbatim; **the
chip label chosen per kind**.

```yaml
# ontology/aliases/misquotes.yaml (Phase C data)
sourceId: misquotes
kind: saying
sayings:
  - text: god helps those who help themselves
    origin: Algernon Sidney, Discourses Concerning Government (1698); popularized by Franklin's Poor Richard's Almanack (1736)
    note: not in the Bible                # admitted vocabulary, below
    concept: work-and-diligence           # XOR range, as today
    phrases:                              # a LIST per row (aliasImporter.ts:31);
      - phrase: god helps those who help themselves   # each entry is its own
        weight: 1.0                                   # curated_aliases key
      - phrase: does the bible say god helps those who help themselves
        weight: 1.0
# ontology/aliases/named-passages.yaml
sourceId: named-passages
kind: named-passage
passages:
  - name: The Lord's Prayer
    range: Matthew 6:9-13
    phrases: [{ phrase: the lords prayer, weight: 1.0 }]
```

```ts
// aliasImporter.ts
+export type AliasKind = 'hymn' | 'saying' | 'named-passage';
 export interface AliasPackSource { sourceId: string; kind?: AliasKind;
   hymns?: HymnRow[]; sayings?: SayingRow[]; passages?: NamedPassageRow[] }
 // Per-kind required fields (build errors, same style as :128-145):
 //   hymn: title, author, integer year, provenance      (unchanged)
 //   saying: text, origin, note (from the admitted vocabulary below); the
 //           concept/range XOR is the SAME as hymn's — owner ruling 17
 //   named-passage: name, range (concept target forbidden: a named passage IS a range)
 // Kept for every kind: >= 2 raw words (:194), global normalized_raw uniqueness
 //   (:79 seenKeys, :230 check, :246 insert), the double-chip guard (:209-229),
 //   weight in (0, 1] (:238-245).
 export interface CompiledAliasRow { ...; readonly kind: AliasKind; readonly note: string | null }

// pipeline/src/schema.ts curated_aliases (schema v10):
//   + kind TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'hymn', + note TEXT, + range_ref TEXT
// engine/src/corpus/repository.ts CuratedAliasRow: + kind, + note, + rangeRef
```

**The label, per kind — the two sites above, rewritten.** `title` is mapped
per kind first (`hymns[].title` / `sayings[].text` / `passages[].name`), and
then the chip text is chosen by `kind`, not by source id:

| kind | concept arm (`concept.ts:246`) | range arm (`concept.ts:268`) |
|---|---|---|
| `hymn` | `Hymn: "${title}" → Theme: ${conceptLabel}` (unchanged) | `Hymn: "${title}"` (unchanged) |
| `saying` | `Saying: "${title}" — ${note} → Theme: ${conceptLabel}`, e.g. `Saying: "god helps those who help themselves" — not in the Bible → Theme: Work and diligence` | `Saying: "${title}" — ${note} → ${reference}`, e.g. `Saying: "this too shall pass" — not in the Bible → 2 Corinthians 4:17-18` |

**Owner ruling 17 — `saying` takes the range arm, and "saying + range is a
build error" is WITHDRAWN.** r3 forbade it on the reasoning that "the honesty
note has no passage to attach to". That reasoning is wrong on the data: **all
five misquote rows in S-A3 A3.24 are range-targeted** (`range: Isaiah 41:10`,
`2 Corinthians 4:17-18`, `1 Corinthians 10:13`, `1 Timothy 6:10`,
`Proverbs 13:24`), and the note is *more* useful on that arm, not less — it is
exactly how a correction reads: the saying, the fact about its origin, and the
verse it should have been. So a `saying` row carries **`range:` XOR
`concept:`, the same rule as `hymn`** (`aliasImporter.ts:209`'s
`if (conceptId !== null)` guard already branches on precisely this), and the
per-arm chip text is the row above. Had r3's rule shipped, every row A3.24
plans would have been a build error — which is the measurable cost of the
withdrawn rule and the reason it is recorded here rather than quietly edited.
`named-passage` keeps its one-arm restriction (`concept:` forbidden — a named
passage IS a range); only `saying` changes.
| `named-passage` | (forbidden: `concept:` is rejected for this kind) | `Passage: ${title}`, e.g. `Passage: The Lord's Prayer` |

`locator` per kind: hymn `Author, "Title" (year)` (`:256`, unchanged);
saying `origin`; named-passage `${name} (${range})`. `sourceLabel`
(`concept.ts:461-529`) gains `'misquotes' → 'LH editorial (common sayings
index)'` and `'named-passages' → 'LH editorial (named-passage index)'`.

The `note` rides the chip because covenant #5 says the explanation is the
contract and covenant #6 says the engine names sources, never verdicts:
"not in the Bible" is a fact about the phrase's origin, stated by the pack.
To keep it a fact rather than a verdict, `note` is **not free text**: it is
an admitted vocabulary, validated by the importer, and extending it is a
reviewed data change like adding a source:

```ts
// pipeline/src/importers/aliasImporter.ts
// The THREE notes S-A3 A3.24's five shipped rows actually use, copied from
// that item verbatim (owner ruling 17), plus two general forms kept for
// reuse and marked `# reserved` so the both-directions test below admits
// them. A note outside this list is a build error.
const ADMITTED_SAYING_NOTES = [
  'not in the Bible',                          // A3.24 x3
  'a paraphrase, not a quotation',             // A3.24 x1
  'a misquotation of the verse it names',      // A3.24 x1 (new; A3.24.R2)
  'not a Bible verse',                         // reserved
  'often attributed to the Bible',             // reserved
] as const;
```

**Corrected against A3.24's final vocabulary (C6, cross-section).** r3 listed
two further strings — `a paraphrase — the verse is about temptation, not
hardship` and `the verse says "the love of money is a root of all kinds of
evil"` — and asserted that they were "the exact strings A3.24's `god wont give
you more than you can handle` and `money is the root of all evil` rows carry".
**A3.24 withdrew both**, for a reason this item agrees with: a note that
embeds one passage's wording is the engine correcting the reader rather than
the pack stating a fact about a phrase, and the verse is already on the chip
as `→ 1 Timothy 6:10`. A3.24's shipped vocabulary is the three values above,
and the third, `a misquotation of the verse it names`, is new (A3.24 ruling
R2). Against this item's own both-directions pipeline test the r3 list failed
in **both** directions at once — one unadmitted note, two unused entries — so
the list is now exactly A3.24's three, plus the two general forms marked
`# reserved`, which is what the test's second clause admits. An admitted
vocabulary that does not admit the data it was written for is a build error
waiting in Phase C; so is one that admits strings nothing uses.

**Where this list lives, and where it does NOT (round-3 minor 18).** r3 said
it is "mirrored as `signalBudgets.admittedSayingNotes`". That is wrong in both
directions and the claim is **deleted**: G6's registry
(`budgetsProperty.ts:383-408`) mirrors **engine** exports, and
`ADMITTED_SAYING_NOTES` is a *pipeline* constant, so a `signalBudgets` key
naming it fails as `unknown-constant`; and the key is absent from B.11 step
4's enumerated `signalBudgets` list, so the both-directions rule fails from
the other side too. The engine never reads the vocabulary — it renders
whatever `note` the compiled row carries — so moving the constant into
`engine/` to earn a mirror would be inventing an engine dependency to satisfy
a gate. The home is the **pipeline**, and the guard is the pair that actually
runs there: the importer's build error (a note outside the list refuses the
pack, `aliasImporter.ts`'s per-kind validation) and a new pipeline test
`aliasImporter.test.ts` "every `note` in every shipped alias pack is in
`ADMITTED_SAYING_NOTES`, and every entry of `ADMITTED_SAYING_NOTES` is used by
some shipped row or carries a `# reserved` comment" — which is the
both-directions property, enforced where the constant lives. It is listed in
B.11's dependency table as reviewed data, not in the budgets mirror.

**Known limit, stated rather than discovered: one key, one claim.**
`normalized_raw` uniqueness is enforced **globally across every alias file**
(`aliasImporter.ts:79` builds one `seenKeys` map for the whole import;
`:230` rejects a duplicate with "one key, one claim"). Two consequences the
Phase C data plan must design around, and neither is changed here:

1. **No multi-target aliases.** One typed phrase can name exactly one
   target — one concept, or one range. A saying that ought to point at two
   concepts ("god helps those who help themselves" → *work and diligence*
   AND *grace, not works*) cannot be expressed as two rows; it must pick the
   single concept whose pack answers the query, and the second connection
   belongs in that concept's own `related` edges. Lifting the constraint is
   a schema change with an evidence-hierarchy consequence (two authoritative
   chips on one typed phrase) and is explicitly **not** in this bundle.
2. **Uniqueness is per key, not per row.** Because `phrases:` is a list, one
   saying may carry several keys ("god helps those who help themselves" and
   "does the bible say god helps those who help themselves"); each key must
   be globally unique, and each becomes its own `curated_aliases` row with
   the same title, note, target and locator.

**A named passage that is not a contiguous range ships as a lexicon phrase,
not an alias row (owner ruling 17).** The schema's range target is a single
`start_verse_id`–`end_verse_id` span, so "the Romans Road" (Romans 3:23,
6:23, 5:8, 10:9, 10:13) has no representation here: the `named-passage` kind
forbids `concept:` (rule above), and the passage is not a range. **Rule for
Phase C: a named passage whose text is not one contiguous range is a
concept-lexicon phrase on a concept that anchors its verses, never an alias
row.**

Ruling 17 narrows what that means for the Romans Road specifically: it ships
as the **phrase `romans road` on the existing `salvation` pack**, fixture
first — **no new concept**. r3 proposed a new `the-romans-road` concept; the
ruling declines it, and the reason is one this section can measure: the
`salvation` pack already anchors Romans 3:23, 6:23, 5:8 and 10:9, so a new
concept would duplicate four of five anchors and split one query class across
two packs, which is the parity-dominance hazard B.4 exists to arbitrate.
`romans road` is two raw words, so it clears the lexicon floor; it is a
2-token phrase (`roman road` after stemming — neither token is a stopword and
neither is bare-cue material on its own), so it is not the F5 single-token
class. The fixture is written first, per CLAUDE.md's "adding data" rule, and
the `NO MEASURABLE EFFECT` verdict decides whether it merges. That work is
Phase C data and is named here only so the rule above has a worked case
attached to it.

**How a range row is asserted in a fixture — and what cannot be asserted.**
The range arm emits one equal-strength `aliasPassageEvidence` row per verse
in the range (`createEngine.ts:576-591`), so every member scores identically
and `compareResults` falls through to the `targetId` tie-break; the run then
collapses (`collapseRuns`, `:998`) into one row whose `targetId` is the
head — i.e. **the range's first verse**. G3 matches an expectation to a row
by verse-id containment on that targetId (`eval/src/gates/corpusGolden.ts:809-812`,
`hitInRange`). So:

- a fixture asserts a named-passage row with ONE expectation whose reference
  range contains the row's start verse, e.g.
  `{ "reference": "Matthew 6:9-13", "withinTop": 1,
     "requiredReasonLabel": "Passage: The Lord's Prayer" }`;
- **two overlapping ranges cannot both be asserted against the same row.**
  r2's example, "The Beatitudes" → Matthew 5:3-12, is exactly this trap: its
  start verse (Matthew 5:3) also falls inside any Sermon-on-the-Mount range
  a pericope or another alias might claim (Matthew 5:1-7:29), so the two
  expectations match the same row and the fixture cannot tell which
  produced it. The example is changed to **The Lord's Prayer (Matthew
  6:9-13)** — a range no other admitted row contains — and the Beatitudes
  case is recorded in S-A3 as a data decision (pick one span, assert it,
  and do not admit the enclosing one).

**Source manifest (G1).** `sourceLabel` is being extended for two new ids,
so both must be **admitted in the source manifest before any row ships**:
`pipeline/manifests/misquotes.json` and `pipeline/manifests/named-passages.json`
are added with the same shape as `pipeline/manifests/hymn-aliases.json`
(`id`, `label` — which must equal the `sourceLabel` string exactly —
`rightsClass: "editorial"`, `licenseRecord`, `maxTier`, `attributionNote`),
and `aliasImporter`'s `citedSourceIds` (`:247`) carries them into G1's
admission check exactly as it does for the hymn pack. A `sourceLabel` case
with no manifest entry is a G1 failure, which is the correct outcome — the
two lines in `concept.ts:461-529` are not sufficient on their own. **This
dependency is carried in B.11's dependency list**, because the manifest
files are the gating artifact, not the importer change.

**Ordering impact.** None until Phase C rows exist (the QR-6 equality match
is untouched); a new row can only answer its exact key.

**Determinism proof.** Rows stay code-unit sorted by `normalizedRaw`
(`:264`); `aliasLayerFingerprint` feeds every field including `kind` and
`note` (extend `pipeline/test/aliasImporter.test.ts:368-386` "every row
field individually moves the fingerprint"). No constants.

**Tests.** Existing `aliasImporter.test.ts:54-330` — the hymn cases pass
unchanged (`kind` defaults to `hymn`); add per-kind missing-field
rejections, `named-passage` with `concept` rejected, `saying` with **both**
`concept` and `range` rejected and with **neither** rejected (the XOR, owner
ruling 17 — and a positive case for **each** arm asserting the two chip
strings in the table above), `note` outside the admitted vocabulary rejected,
the both-directions `ADMITTED_SAYING_NOTES` test above, cross-kind key
uniqueness (a saying and a hymn claiming the same normalized key is a build
error with the "one key, one claim" message), and a two-key saying compiling
to two rows with one title. Engine: `concept.test.ts` label cases per kind,
asserting the exact chip strings in the table above;
`eval/test/hymn-alias*.test.ts` unchanged (they pin `Hymn:` and must stay
green).

**Data rebuild.** Schema v10 (bundle). Phase C ships `misquotes.yaml` and
`named-passages.yaml` with fixtures first.

**Rollback.** Revert importer/schema/label hunks; rows are data.

**Acceptance.** Importer accepts the two Phase C file shapes in a unit test
with a scratch pack; the QR-6 pack compiles byte-identically except for the
three new columns; every existing `Hymn:` chip is unchanged; a
**range-targeted** `saying` row renders `Saying: "this too shall pass" — not
in the Bible → 2 Corinthians 4:17-18` (owner ruling 17), a concept-targeted
one renders `Saying: "…" — not in the Bible → Theme: …`, and a
`named-passage` row renders `Passage: …`. Gauntlet green; G2 both OS.

**Effort.** M.

## B.12 Risks and rollback for the bundle

- **One bump hides ten causes.** Mitigation: one commit per item with its
  own e2e fixture, and the packet tags every churned probe with the item
  responsible; G8 `maxTop10ChurnRatio 0.4` is expected to be EXCEEDED on
  this bundle (tokenizer rebuild moves almost everything) — the approval
  is the reviewed override, not a budget edit.
- **B2 ships the tie-break, GATED to capped rows** (owner ruling 2 —
  r2 left this open; it is now decided). The residual risk is no longer
  "flat ties if rejected" but the narrower one the gate creates: two
  ordering rules now coexist, `uncappedScore` for `soleCapped && soleCapped`
  pairs and stable-ID for everything else, and a reader comparing two pages
  cannot tell which rule produced an order by looking. Mitigations — **two,
  not three** (round-3 objection 6, owner ruling 14): the gate condition is
  one clause in `compareResults` with all three branches unit-tested (a
  capped/capped pair, a capped/uncapped pair, an uncapped/uncapped pair);
  and the COMPATIBILITY note (ruling 5) states the condition in words.

  **The third mitigation r3 claimed is DELETED, because it was false in both
  halves.** r3 wrote "`capped` is already a public field on `RankedResult`,
  so the condition is observable by a consumer rather than hidden". Verified
  against the tree: `RankedResult` appears only in
  `engine/src/internal.ts:119` and is **not** exported from
  `engine/src/index.ts` (which exports `Evidence`, `Provenance`, `Reason`,
  `SignalFamily`, `ReferenceSuggestion`, `FamilyBudget`, `SignalBudgets`,
  `RankOptions` and nothing else type-wise); and `DiscoveryResult`
  (`types.ts:126-143`) is `{targetId, reference, excerpt, score, reasons,
  verses?, grouping?}` — no `capped`, no `soleCapped`. B.2 said as much four
  pages earlier, so the section also contradicted itself. Owner ruling 14
  keeps `soleCapped` **internal** and declines the alternative (a fourth
  additive `DiscoveryResult` field beside B.8's three). **The residual that
  leaves, stated rather than mitigated away: a consumer cannot observe the
  condition at all.** What is true is narrower and is what the risk register
  now claims — the condition is observable in `engine/test/*`, which import
  `../src/ranking/rank.js` and `../src/internal.js` directly, so the branch
  is pinned by tests inside this repository; and it is stated in words in the
  COMPATIBILITY note, which is what a consumer actually reads. Ruling 2's
  justification ("the change is bounded and legible") therefore rests on the
  bound plus the note, not on introspection. The tie-break additionally requires the **exact-ceiling
  assignment** — measured, a re-summed proportional cap lands one ULP off 6
  and `compareResults`'s first line then orders capped rows by
  floating-point noise, defeating the tie-break and creating a
  cross-platform hazard. Both halves ship or neither does.
- **B3 is now runtime protected-tokens, not static admissibility** (owner
  ruling 6). The `prayer for` hazard r2 solved by deleting two frames is
  solved structurally instead: `"prayer for healing"` matches a concept
  lexicon phrase on the UNSTRIPPED significant tokens, so both `prayer` and
  `healing` are protected and no frame can remove them — measured
  byte-identical, along with four of the other five parity queries. (Under
  ruling 12 the sixth, `"help me with my unbelief"`, is **not**
  byte-identical: it keeps its 40.000 `Theme: Doubt` anchor and rises
  52.177 → 82.477 because the phrase step now reads the stripped string. r3
  claimed all four of its parity set were unchanged; that claim is corrected
  in B.3 rather than left standing.) The frames
  therefore stay in the list and still help where nothing is protected
  (`"verses for a funeral"`, where no lexicon phrase matches).
  Two NEW risks this design introduces, both stated rather than hidden:
  **(a) B3 is artifact-dependent.** Whether a token is protected depends on
  the compiled concept lexicon, so the SAME query can strip differently
  against two artifacts. That is not a determinism failure — the identity
  triple already carries `layerFingerprint`, and a lexicon edit moves it —
  but it does mean a frame's behaviour can no longer be reasoned about from
  the frame list alone. Mitigation: all **eighteen** measured queries ship as
  fixtures — the twelve of r3 plus the six added under round-3 minor 21 — so
  a lexicon edit that silently changes stripping fails G3 with the query
  named. **(b) A future frame added without the guard in mind.**
  The zero-significant-token fallback and the protection rule are both
  unconditional and table-driven-tested, and the frame list stays reviewed
  data mirrored into `budgets.json`, so a new frame arrives as a
  reviewed-data diff with the eighteen fixtures re-run beside it.
- **B6 scale is 0.10, not 0.25** (B.6 ruling): both measured inversions are
  resolved at 0.10 and neither is at 0.25. The residual is the recorded
  cost — on an anchored row a `translation_variant` chip is worth ≤ 1.4 and
  an ordinary `token_overlap` chip ≤ 1.0 — bounded by the `verbatim`
  exemption, which under owner ruling 3 is now narrowed to the `complete`
  case only (the chip's verbatim text covers the WHOLE query). The residual
  risk that narrowing creates: a NEAR-complete verbatim chip (five of six
  significant words, say) is now scaled to ≤ 1.0 on an anchored row where
  r2's wider marker would have kept it at 10. Measured incidence of the
  exemption itself is 3 of 1,211 anchored rows (0.25 %) over 229 distinct
  queries, so the class is small and enumerable; the acceptance test pins
  `"the truth"` at 32.000, the one live case where it decides anything.
- **B7 named verses are not B7's class** (B.7 note): 2 Samuel 17:9 is B2's,
  Matthew 11:17 is B3's + Phase C data.
- **`myself` stays a STOPWORD in 0.15.0** (owner ruling 1, option (b)).
  Re-measured, `myself` is df 140, IDF **5.408** — *above* `kill`'s 4.160 —
  which is precisely why scoring it now is the risk rather than the fix: a
  high-IDF `myself` would lead `"i will kill myself"` with Job 42:6 ("I
  abhor myself"), Deuteronomy 32:39 and Job 9:21, i.e. a suicide query
  answered by self-loathing and divine killing, on a weak-only page capped
  at 6.000. The one-line `STOPWORDS` edit is held until Phase C lands the
  phrases, fixture-first, and both ship in one artifact — which costs
  nothing, because both are gated behind one re-mint. Everything else in B1
  is identical under this choice. `tokenizer.stopwordCount` moves
  173 → **177** in this bundle, but **not** because of this ruling — the four
  additions are ruling 10's pronoun contractions, and ruling 1 removes
  nothing.
  **The residual risk this leaves, stated as a cross-reference:** with
  `myself` unscored, `"kill myself"` tokenizes to the bare `[kill]`, so the
  query's entire behaviour rests on the bare-`kill` admission ruling
  recorded in **S-A1**. That ruling, not this section, is what makes the
  query safe; if S-A1's ruling changes, this decision must be revisited in
  the same commit. Section B carries no independent protection for it.
- **`ontology/lexicon-inventory.yaml` needs deletions, not only
  re-derivation.** Under owner ruling 7 (option (b)) the **`cutting myself`
  phrase and its `collapses` row are both DELETED** in the B1 commit. The
  reason is measured, not editorial: v2 collapses the phrase to the bare
  cue `cut`, whose df is **364** — a bare-word trigger on an ordinary
  English verb, exactly what the thin-cue rules exist to refuse. (`cutt`,
  the v1 token, has df 11; the collapse is what makes it unsafe.) Phase C
  restores the phrase, fixture-first, with phrases that do not collapse to
  a bare cue. Beyond that row, any phrase whose only surviving token was a
  now-merged inflection may newly collapse and need a NEW row. 68 `collapses` rows,
  285 `admitted` and 241 `skipped` bare tokens are all re-derived
  mechanically and reviewed by the file's named owner in the B1 commit;
  missing any one fails G4.
- **Reviewed-data ripples** B1 forces (`sensitive-categories.json`'s 28
  `tokens` arrays, alias keys through contraction expansion): all
  mechanical, all diff-reviewed in the B1 commit; missing any one ships a
  stale telemetry matcher.
- **The tokenizer tables are now ordering-bearing reviewed constants**, so
  they carry G6 mirrors (`tokenizer.*`, B.1). Without them a table edit
  could change every query's ordering with no reviewed-data diff travelling
  in the commit — the exact failure `signalBudgets.$comment` forbids.
- **Schema v10 with three column additions** (B5 `concept_lexicon.ordered`,
  B8 `concepts.care`, B10 `curated_aliases.kind/note`): one bump; G10 size
  budgets (`budgets.json:64-83`) have ample headroom (each table ≤ 4 MiB
  budgeted, columns are integers/short text).
- **Cross-platform floating point**: no new transcendental function is
  introduced (B1–B10 use `Math.max`, multiplication, division); `Math.log`
  in IDF and `Math.exp`-free scaling remain as today, already proven
  byte-identical across the two OS legs by G2.
- **New in r3: the possessive fold is a corpus-wide change riding in on a
  two-token ruling.** Ruling 9 (`gods` kept distinct from `god`) is safe
  only with `possessiveFold: true`, and that fold touches **3,706
  occurrences across 290 distinct bases** — far beyond the two tokens the
  ruling names. `god` df 3,553 → 3,862 and `gods` df 566 → 208 are the two
  largest movers, but every possessive in the corpus re-files. The risk is
  that it gets reviewed as a footnote to a lemma decision. Mitigations: it
  is a named mirror key (`tokenizer.possessiveFold`) with its own G6 row;
  it appears in the approval packet as its own measurement rather than
  inside ruling 9's paragraph; and the whole-vocabulary snapshot, checked
  on both OS legs, makes each of the 290 bases a reviewable diff line.
- **New in r4: negation folding is a corpus-wide rewrite riding in on a
  contraction ruling** (ruling 10). Measured at the raw-word stage: **413**
  surface types change occurrence count, the stream drops **1,594**
  occurrences net (757,240 → 755,646), and `not` alone falls 3,341 → 1,747.
  Twelve written-out negations that previously dissolved into stopwords now
  carry a significant token, so `wont`'s document frequency goes 237 → 827,
  `isnt` 159 → 418 and `havent` 87 → 293. Every query containing "do not",
  "will not", "cannot" or "is not" therefore re-ranks. Two specific risks. **(a)
  The fold list is not closed under its own rule** — `werent`, `hasnt` and
  `hadnt` are live WEB tokens with no multi-word row, so "were not"
  dissolves while "weren't" folds, which is the exact asymmetry the ruling
  exists to remove, surviving in three rows. Applied as ruled; the extension
  is offered in the packet with its figures. **(b) `not` is still a
  stopword**, so "fear not" is unchanged and out of scope — stated because a
  reader who sees negation folding land will reasonably assume the whole
  negation problem was addressed, and it was not. Mitigation for both: the
  34-row phrase enumeration, the five un-collapse rulings and the two
  collapse deletions are all committed reviewed data, and every one of the
  five phrases that stops collapsing is either re-pointed (keeping today's
  behaviour exactly) or deleted with the sibling phrase that already covers
  the token named — measured, not assumed.
- **New in r4: the accepted-collision class is a review artifact, and its
  scope is a promise about a sweep** (ruling 11). `divine/divin` is split and
  `bow`, `arm` and `sow` are accepted, but the honest statement is that
  `acceptedCollisions` is not derivable — "more than one dictionary sense"
  is not computable from the corpus, and the runtime has no word senses by
  covenant #1. The mitigation is the fifth generated report (every new v2
  family touching curated-lexicon or `docs/DOCTRINAL-BASIS.md` vocabulary,
  **252** families on this run), signed once and pinned, so the *next*
  homograph arrives as a failing test rather than as a critique. The residual
  risk, stated plainly: the report's scope is the reviewed vocabulary, so a
  bad merge on a word no pack currently names is still invisible until a pack
  names it — at which point the report fires, which is the correct time.
- **New in r4: the phrase step and the token step now read the same string**
  (ruling 12), which fixes an incoherence and creates one risk. `phraseEvidence`
  runs on the **stripped** sequence, so `complete` and the coverage
  denominator are computed over the query the engine actually ranks. The risk
  is that a frame word which is part of a verse's own wording is now stripped
  before the phrase step sees it, so a query quoting a verse that *contains*
  a frame word could lose an exact-phrase hit it has today. Measured across
  the eighteen B.3 queries: no row loses a phrase chip and one gains one
  (Psalms 23:1, `Contains …` 20.000 → `Exact phrase` 40.000). The class is
  bounded by the protection rule — a frame word inside a matched lexicon
  phrase is never stripped — but it is not empty by construction, and the
  eighteen fixtures are what would catch it.
- **New in r4: `used` is left split** (ruling 15's stated residual). `use`
  and `uses` merge to `use`, `using` merges by lemma row, and `used` (35
  occurrences) still lands on `used` because its residual `us` is below the
  floor. A second lemma row would close it; the owner has not been asked, so
  it ships split and is listed as an open item rather than smuggled in with
  the ruling that named the other three.
- **Rollback of the whole bundle.** r2 wrote "regenerate nothing", which is
  true of the *repository* and false of everything downstream. The
  corrected procedure has three parts, in order:
  1. **Repository.** Revert the branch merge. The pre-bundle baselines,
     approvals, ordering snapshot and `eval/budgets.json` come back with
     it, so nothing is regenerated in-tree — that much of r2's sentence
     stands.
  2. **Artifact.** A 0.15.0 artifact was minted and may have been
     published; reverting code does not unpublish it, and anyone holding
     its descriptor can still open it. The 0.15.0 **descriptor must be
     withdrawn** — marked superseded in the release index, with the reason
     recorded — and the existing 0.14.0/1.0.0 descriptor remains current.
     Do NOT re-mint a fresh 0.14.0 artifact: the existing one is still
     valid, and re-minting would produce a second artifact with the same
     engine version and a different `corpusFingerprint`, which is precisely
     the ambiguity the identity triple exists to prevent.
  3. **Consumers.** Maskil, LH Worship Setlist and Versed pin
     `(engine semver, artifact descriptor)` (§5). Any consumer that
     re-pinned to `(0.15.0, <new descriptor>)` must be told to **re-pin
     back to `(0.14.0, <the 0.14.0 descriptor>)`**, and the withdrawal note
     must name all three apps. A consumer left on the withdrawn pair is not
     broken — the artifact still opens — but it is then running an engine
     the project has repudiated, which is worse than a hard failure because
     it is silent. Consumers that never re-pinned are unaffected
     throughout.

  A **partial** rollback of one item is a code revert plus a NEW
  `ENGINE_VERSION`, a fresh baseline regeneration and review, and a new
  descriptor with its own consumer re-pin — there are no feature flags
  anywhere in this bundle, by design (CLAUDE.md #2 and #4).

Two further changes r2 makes that the round-1 review did not raise, both
found by re-running the examples on a patched build:

- **B.2 — the sole-evidence ceiling must be ASSIGNED, not re-summed.** With
  proportional scaling and a re-sum, capped totals land within one ULP of 6
  (`6.0000000000000008882` vs `5.9999999999999991118`), `compareResults`'s
  `b.score !== a.score` guard fires on the noise, the `uncappedScore`
  tie-break never runs, and page order is decided by floating point — a
  cross-platform hazard. The fix and the before/after page order are in B.2.
- **B.6 — the 0.10 scale needs the `verbatim` exemption to be safe.** The
  review's own analysis of the hole is adopted: `phraseEvidence` marks the
  `token_overlap` chips it creates from verbatim text, step 4b skips them,

  `Exact phrase` chip at 10.000 while its ordinary chip scales to 0.273.

## Revision log (r4)

Round-3 verdict: **FAIL** — 1 blocking, 6 major, 14 minor. All twenty-one are
answered below. **Eight owner rulings (10–17) arrived with the critique** and
are applied exactly, recorded in "Owner rulings applied (1–9 in r3, 10–17 in
r4)" near the top. Ruling 10 answers the blocking objection by **reversing**
r3's contraction direction rather than by ruling on the hazard r3's direction
created, which is why the blocking row below reads as a design change and not
as a patch.

Every number republished here comes from **one re-run of the round-3 critic's
own reference implementation** with rulings 10, 11 and 15 applied
(`$SCRATCH/b-r4/`). Using the critic's harness rather than a fresh one is
deliberate: the critic reproduced almost every r3 figure from it, so a
disagreement between r3 and r4 can only be the rule change, never the
instrument. Where r4 and the critic's r3 figures differ, the difference is
named with its cause.

This is the last revision round; there is no further critic pass. What is
still open is listed under "Known gaps (r4)" below rather than left for a
reader to discover.

|---|---|---|---|

### Known gaps (r4)

This is the last revision round, so what is not closed is listed rather than
implied. None of these is a number in dispute; each is a decision that has not
been made or a guard whose scope is narrower than the claim it supports.

1. **The negation-fold list is not closed under its own rule.** `werent`,
   `hasnt` and `hadnt` are live WEB tokens (df 28 / 49 / 6) with no
   multi-word row, so "weren't" folds and "were not" still dissolves. Applied
   as ruled (12 two-word rows + `cannot`); the three-row extension is a
   one-line reviewed-data diff offered in the approval packet with its
   figures. **Owner decision, not an implementation gap.**
2. **`used` stays split from `use`** (ruling 15's residual). 35 occurrences; a
   second lemma row would close it and has not been ruled on.
3. **`not` is still a stopword**, so "fear not" is out of scope. Ruling 10
   addresses negated *contractions*, not negation generally, and a reader who
   sees the fold land will reasonably assume more was fixed than was.
4. **`acceptedCollisions` is a review artifact, not a derivation.** The fifth
   generated report bounds it to the reviewed vocabulary (252 families this
   run), so a bad merge on a word no pack names is invisible until a pack
   names it. That is the correct trigger, but it is not the same as a proof.
5. **`E_BLOCK` is fitted to the WEB, and the runtime sees more than the
   WEB.** The eleven derived rows come from the corpus; the seven reviewed
   rows exist precisely for words the corpus does not attest (`repeat`,
   `relapse`, `cheat`, …). A Layer B or query word outside both lists can
   still be mis-stemmed. Standing risk, carried from r3, unchanged by r4.
6. **`soleCapped` is not observable by a consumer** (ruling 14). The
   condition is pinned by engine-internal tests and described in the
   COMPATIBILITY note; there is no runtime way for Maskil, LH Worship Setlist
   or Versed to tell which tie-break produced an order.
7. **B.3 is artifact-dependent by construction.** Whether a token is
   protected depends on the compiled lexicon, so the same query can strip
   differently against two artifacts. The identity triple covers it
   (`layerFingerprint` moves), and the eighteen fixtures catch a silent
   change, but a frame's behaviour can no longer be reasoned about from the
   frame list alone.
8. **Two irregular e-family splits are left open** (`hid/hide`, `mad/made`).
   A lemma row would close each; both are recorded as Phase C candidates
   rather than added here, because neither has a fixture behind it.
9. **The r4 numbers come from a reference implementation, not from the
   shipped pipeline.** It reproduces `token_stats` (9,570) and `verse_tokens`
   (318,012) exactly under v1, which is the strongest available check, but
   the first real confirmation is the B1 commit's own
   `npm run build:fixture` — and the section says so rather than implying the
   pipeline has already been run.
10. **`docs/COMPATIBILITY.md` carries one note for two changes** (ruling 5).
    That is as ruled and it is the right call for a reader, but it does mean
    a consumer skimming for "type change" may not read as far as the ordering
    half.

## Critic responses

**Round 3's objections are accepted in full: r4 contests none of the
twenty-one, and the round-3 review's own reference implementation is the
instrument every republished number comes from.** Three of its *incidental*
figures are contested with the measurement, and only those three — each is
recorded at the place it matters and listed here so nothing is contested
silently:

1. **Ruling 10's worked example, `cant go on → {cant, go}`.** It is `{cant}`:
   `go` is two letters and the raw-word surface floor drops it
   (`index.ts`, `raw.length < 3`), the same floor the section already cites
   for `going → going`. Contested against the **ruling**, not the review, and
   the ruling is applied as written everywhere else (§B.1, "Negation
   folding").
2. **The review's member-occurrence splits for `bow` and `divining`.** The
   review gives `bow` as 171/25/4/4 and `divining` as 3; counted over
   `verses.text`, they are 101/83/2/18 and **1** (Ezekiel 22:28). The
   **totals agree exactly** (204 and 9), so the disagreement is in
   attribution, not in what merges, and both readings support ruling 11
   (§B.1, the bad-merge table).
3. **r3's own `mustMerge` line for `unties`.** The review verified and
   reproduced r3's claim that `untie/unties/untied/untying` all merge;
   re-running the assertion shows `unties` needs a lemma row of its own
   (`-ies` would give `unty`). The row is added. This is r4 contesting r3,
   with the review's agreement as the thing that made it easy to miss.

**Round 2's rulings are accepted in full. r3 contests nothing that round 2
ruled on.** The two entries below record what happened to r2's own contested
items, because a section that quietly deletes a rebuttal it lost is harder
to audit than one that says so.

**1. "212 lexicon collisions" — r2's rebuttal is WITHDRAWN. The critic is
right.**

r2 wrote: *"It is not reproducible against `pipeline/output/fixture.db` at
HEAD under any definition I could construct … None is 212"*, and then framed
the outcome as "the reviewer reproduced what the section asserted; the
assertion was the problem". Both sentences are wrong and both are retracted.

Re-run at HEAD, the five definitions give:

| Definition | r3's run |
|---|---|
| `concept_lexicon` rows with `token_count = 2` having a token that is a `token_count = 1` entry of a **different** concept | **202** |
| the same, deduplicated by `normalized` | **198** |
| the same, counted as **(row, colliding token) incidence pairs** | **212** ← r1's number |
| rows with `token_count >= 2` having such a token | **347** (380 incidence pairs) |
| distinct (phrase-concept, bare-concept, token) triples over all widths | **269** |

r2 printed 208 for the third row because it deduplicated by `normalized`
*before* counting pairs, which is a fourth definition, not the one stated.
Counting incidence over rows — the natural reading of "collisions", and the
one r1 used — gives exactly **212**. The headline stays **202** (distinct
rows with at least one collision, the number a reviewer acts on), the
incidence count is published beside it as **212** with its definition, and
the "not reproducible" claim is deleted from the section. The general lesson
is recorded in B.1's counting discipline: **every count in this section now
names its unit** (types, occurrences, rows, families, or incidence pairs),
because four of the five numbers here differ only in their unit.

**2. `forbiddenReasonLabelSubstrings` — settled in r2's favour by round 2,
kept here for the record.** The round-1 critique's closing sentence ("a
supported field that no fixture currently uses") was false — exactly one
fixture uses it, `eval/golden/spelling-archaic-guard.json`, with
`["(corrected from"]` — and round 2 ruled for the section. The substantive
argument stands and is stated in B.9 rather than assumed: the fixture forbids
a *correction citation* on `loveth`, and B9 changes only which surface word a
chip quotes, never whether `(corrected from …)` is emitted, which remains
governed by `correctionCitations` (`lexical.ts:193-196`) with `ARCHAIC_FORMS`
folding before correction runs. B.9 adds the ordering assertion that pins it.

**3. Two things r3 corrects that no critique caught**, recorded here so they
are not mistaken for silent edits:

- **Ruling 9 has a hidden companion cost.** Keeping `gods` distinct from
  `god` is safe only with the possessive fold, because **374 of the 609
  `gods` occurrences are the possessive "God's"** — without the fold, the
  ruling would file "God's" under `gods` and hand a reader the wrong lemma
  on the most common word in the corpus. The fold is therefore specified,
  measured (3,706 occurrences / 290 bases) and mirrored as
  `tokenizer.possessiveFold`, and it is called out in the approval packet as
  its own measurement rather than as a footnote to the ruling.
- **`cheat` was mis-stemmed** by the derived `E_BLOCK` (the WEB does not
  attest the base), found while deriving objection 18's reviewed tail. It is
  now a reviewed `E_BLOCK` row with the other six.

Sources for this section: `battery-results.md` (202 queries, format
`### query [intent: X; total: N]`), `battery2-results.md` (crisis/grief/topic
battery, format `## [category] "query"`), `queries.txt` / `queries2.txt` (the
query lists that produced them), `research-R6-engine.md` (engine ladder and
tokenizer defects E1–E9), `research-R8-schemas.md` (fixture schema, gate
roster, NO_MEASURABLE_EFFECT, baseline-approval protocol), `eval/budgets.json`,
and eleven queries run live against `pipeline/output/fixture.db` in this
session via `engine/dist/index.js` + `node --experimental-sqlite` (the same
technique `runBattery.ts` uses), because the matrix needs several search
forms — numerals, reference-glued forms, contractions, inflections, named
passages without a curated phrase, negated pairs — that neither committed
battery file happens to cover verbatim. Every live-run result below is
labelled **(live, this session)** and reports `engineVersion=0.14.0`,
`corpusFingerprint=6450b7d7…`, `layerFingerprint=f202502951c8…` — the same
identity triple stamped in both battery files, so the two evidence sources
are directly comparable. Nothing here modifies the repository.

## C.0 What "deterministic with various forms of searches" means here

CLAUDE.md's determinism covenant is stated per-query:
`(engineVersion, corpusFingerprint, layerFingerprint, query)` → identical
ordering. That covenant is already satisfied today, byte-for-byte, for any
single fixed query string — G2 enforces it. It says nothing about what
happens when a person means the same pastoral need but *types* it
differently. That is a second, harder property this plan section is about,
and it is not yet named anywhere in the gate roster:

> **Search-form determinism**: for a fixed pastoral need `N` and a fixed
> `(engineVersion, corpusFingerprint, layerFingerprint)`, the set of
> "reasonable surface forms" a person would use to ask for `N` — bare word,
> topic phrase, first-person statement, question, framed request, prayer
> request, contraction/typo variant, inflected variant, half-remembered
> phrase, named-passage title, reference shorthand, partial quote, a form
> carrying a small numeral, a multi-need conjunction, and a form whose token
> set is shared with its semantic opposite — should each independently
> resolve to a **top-3 result set that overlaps** (ideally: is identical to)
> the top-3 the plainest form of that need returns, **and each result's
> reasons should be phrased so a reader can see their own words reflected
> back** (CLAUDE.md non-negotiable #5, "explanations are part of the
> contract").

This is not one property but three, and the matrix below (C.1) exists to
keep them from being conflated:

1. **Coverage** — does the form surface the *intended* passages at all,
   anywhere in the top 10? (What the golden-fixture `expectedWithinTop`
   machinery already measures, per form, once a fixture's
   `additionalQueries` actually contains that form — see C.2.)
2. **Rank stability across forms** — does the form put the intended passage
   in the *same relative position* another form of the identical need would?
   This is the property most of the matrix rows below fail today, because
   different forms trip different ladder rungs (exact_phrase vs.
   concept_anchor vs. bare token_overlap) that are weighted incommensurably
   by design (`applyBudgets`'s per-family caps, R6 §E2).
3. **Explanation fidelity** — does the reason chip use words the *user*
   typed, or words a curator typed? A query like `"forgiving"` that falls
   through to `token_overlap(Shared word: forgiv)` (§C.1 row 8, live-run
   evidence below) shows the surface word ("forgiving") and the index token
   ("forgiv") diverging — the chip is technically honest but reads as a
   typo to the person who typed a perfectly good English word.

None of these three is "make every form rank identically" — that would
require collapsing genuinely different queries (a question is not a bare
word) into one signal, which is exactly the "hidden second ranking system"
CLAUDE.md and R6's E3 note both reject. The target is narrower: **within one
search form family, inflection and phrasing noise that a person does not
perceive as a different question should not be visible in the ranking
either.** A theological question ("why did God let my mom die") legitimately
ranking differently from a bare topic word ("grief") is not a determinism
bug. "Forgive" and "forgiving" landing on completely different evidence
families *is* one, because a person typing either believes they asked the
same thing.

### Row 10 reconciliation — the mechanism each named passage actually ships with

r1 proposed `curated_aliases` for four passages. r2 replaced that with a
reconciliation against S-A3's then-current text. **S-A3's final revision moved
again — it adopted an explicit named-passage rule and audited the top-1 result
for every name it touches — so this table is rebuilt a second time, against
that audit, and three of r2's rows were wrong.** The rule S-A3 now ships,
verbatim:

> **Every named-passage query pins its own passage's rank explicitly.** An
> alias-backed name pins `withinTop: 1`. A name served only by a lexicon
> phrase pins the rank the harness measures and states in the fixture note
> why it is not 1.

That second sentence is the part this chapter cares about: a named-passage
fixture that pins only presence cannot see its own passage being displaced by
another parable, which is the defect (`loving-others.json`'s `.some()` over
the whole result set) S-A3's rule exists to close. It is the same discipline
C.2's form-coverage rule asks for, arrived at independently.

## C.2 Per-form conventions (binding)

Three binding rules follow directly from the matrix above, because writing
"the fixture should cover more forms" as prose has already failed once in
this codebase's history — the matrix exists precisely because most fixtures
today pin one form (`query`) and treat `additionalQueries` as optional
enrichment rather than a coverage requirement.

**1. Minimum form coverage per register fixture.** Every fixture attached to
a pastoral-register concept (crisis, bereavement, marriage-crisis, abuse,
illness — the same five registers D1's `eval/registers.json` names) must have
`additionalQueries` containing at least one query recognizable as each of
forms **1 (bare word), 2 (topic phrase), 3 (first-person statement), 4
(question), 5 (framed request), 7 (contraction/typo pair), and 8
(inflection set)** where the underlying need can be phrased that way — a
few needs (e.g. a named-passage row like "prodigal son") cannot take a
first-person form and are exempt from that one requirement, but the
exemption must be explicit (a `note` entry), not silent, so the coverage
checker (below) can distinguish "not applicable" from "not written."

**2. `pipeline/scripts/expandForms.ts` (spec, Phase D, no AI).** r1 named
the home `eval/scripts/` and D4 leaned on that as precedent; **that
directory does not exist anywhere in the repository** (`find . -type d
-iname scripts` returns only `pipeline/scripts`, `sweep/scripts`,
`conformance/scripts`, `.github/scripts` — confirmed this revision, critique
MAJOR-2). The real, already-established home for exactly this kind of
authoring-time, no-AI, deterministic tool is `pipeline/scripts/` — where
`mineSearchLog.ts` (D4) already lives. Fixed here; every `eval/scripts/`
reference below and in D4 is now `pipeline/scripts/`.

A fixture author should not have to hand-type eight variants of every query
and personally catch every stemmer trap R6's E1 dossier catalogues (161
lexicon tokens on one side or the other of a "+e"/"-ies" split alone). Spec:

```
Input:  { query: string, register?: RegisterId }
Output: readonly string[]   // deterministic, order-stable, DE-DUPLICATED
                             // BY TOKEN SET: two templates that happen to
                             // significant-word-tokenize to the same set
                             // (e.g. a stopword-only prefix change) emit
                             // only the first form in template order — a
                             // fixture gains nothing from two additionalQueries
                             // strings that exercise the identical token
                             // set, and a coverage report (D5) counting
                             // "forms covered" must count DISTINCT token
                             // sets, not distinct strings, or it inflates
                             // coverage on exactly this template list.

Deterministic string templates only — no model call, no fuzzing, no corpus
lookup (CLAUDE.md #1: nothing AI-generated reaches the artifact; this tool
runs at authoring time and its OUTPUT is reviewed like any other data, but
the tool itself must be auditable as pure string transforms, not a black box
whose output changes between runs):

  - bare-word forms:        identity (if query is already <=2 significant
                             words, emit as-is)
  - topic-phrase forms:     "dealing with " + query, "overcoming " + query
                             (only for queries whose head is a noun the
                             template list already recognizes — a small,
                             reviewed noun list, not a POS tagger)
  - first-person forms:     query with a small reviewed template — but the
                             two templates are NOT equivalent in kind, and
                             the spec must say so explicitly (critique
                             MINOR-2, confirmed live this revision against
                             `engine/src/tokenizer/index.ts`):
                               * "my " + query — `"my"` IS a STOPWORD
                                 (`STOPWORDS` line 27), so this is a true
                                 tokenizer no-op, exactly like the review
                                 brief's own "adding 'I' changes nothing"
                                 example (`"i"` is also a stopword, same
                                 line). It is safe by construction for
                                 EVERY register, including ones where the
                                 possessive reads oddly ("my prodigal son"),
                                 because the token set is unchanged either
                                 way — it exists only to make the string
                                 read as first-person to a human reviewer,
                                 not to change what the engine sees.
                               * "I feel " + query — `"feel"` is NOT a
                                 stopword and is not in `ARCHAIC_FORMS`/
                                 `IRREGULAR_LEMMAS`; it adds a real,
                                 scoreable content token to every generated
                                 variant (confirmed live, this revision:
                                 `"anxiety"`/`"grief"` held their top-3 set
                                 with diluted scores, matching row 2's
                                 "dealing with"/"overcoming" pattern, but
                                 the template is NOT guaranteed neutral the
                                 way "my " is). Emit it only for
                                 emotion/felt-need registers where "I feel
                                 X" is a sentence a person would actually
                                 type (crisis, bereavement, loneliness,
                                 illness) — it makes NO SENSE, and must be
                                 skipped by the template's own register
                                 gate, for named-passage rows ("I feel the
                                 prodigal son"), doctrinal/occasion rows
                                 ("I feel pentecost"), and reference-shaped
                                 queries. Explicitly DOES NOT attempt to
                                 conjugate a verb-phrase query into first
                                 person for either template; that is exactly
                                 the kind of "hidden second ranking system"
                                 CLAUDE.md and R6's E3 both warn against
                                 baking into a tool with no reviewed ceiling
                                 on what it can emit, so unsupported inputs
                                 simply emit nothing for that form rather
                                 than guessing.
  - framed-request forms:   "bible verses about " + query,
                             "what does the bible say about " + query
  - prayer-request forms:   "prayer for " + query — the r2 hedge here is
                             RETIRED. S-B's **B.3 Query-frame stripping**
                             was redesigned under owner rulings 6 and 12
                             (runtime protected tokens), and `"prayer for"`
                             / `"prayers for"` are NOT in the shipped frame
                             list — B.3's own acceptance asserts
                             `"prayer for my son"` byte-identical to today.
                             So the template emits normally and its output
                             fixture may assert rank, not merely presence.
                             Where the need is a parent's prayer, the
                             assertion belongs in S-A3 A3.7's active
                             `prayer-for-my-son-daughter-children` fixture
                             rather than in a new one.
  - named-passage forms:    "the " + query, for named-passage rows only —
                             NEW, and the reason is row 16: `"armor of
                             god"` scores 41.87 on `exact_phrase` while
                             `"the armor of god"` scores 11.21 with no
                             exact_phrase chip at all, because the verbatim
                             step matches raw phrases and `the` is a
                             token-stage stopword, not a raw-word one. A
                             named-passage fixture that omits the articled
                             form passes while the form people say fails.
  - contraction/typo forms: run the REVIEWED contraction map — now a real,
                             numbered artifact rather than a hypothetical:
                             **B.1 Tokenizer v2's 13-row negation-fold
                             table** (`do not → dont`, `can not`/`cannot →
                             cant`, `will not → wont`, …, owner ruling 10).
                             This script CONSUMES that table; it does not
                             invent a second one, and it must not fold in
                             the opposite direction (r2 proposed `cant →
                             cannot`; the ruling canonicalizes toward the
                             contracted WEB token, the direction with
                             document frequency behind it)
  - inflection forms:       for each significant word in query with an
                             entry in a REVIEWED irregular/derivation table
                             (extending IRREGULAR_LEMMAS's existing shape,
                             not a generative rule — same "reviewed table,
                             not a stripping rule" discipline R6's
                             ARCHAIC_FORMS comment already states as the
                             reason that table isn't generative), emit the
                             base, -ing, and third-person -s forms.

The important property: expandForms.ts is deterministic and reviewable data
transformation, checked into `pipeline/scripts/`, never a runtime dependency
of the engine and never a call to a model. Its own test suite is a fixture
in the ordinary sense: given input query X, expandForms(X) == [fixed list]
forever, until a reviewed edit — including the token-set de-duplication
above, which the test suite pins with a case whose two templates collide on
purpose (e.g. a query already containing "my") and asserts only one survives.
```

**3. Fixture-validator coverage warning (spec, Phase D).** The existing
fixture validator (`eval/src/gates/corpusGolden.ts`, R8 §3e) already emits a
closed vocabulary of `G3_FIXTURE_*` finding codes for schema violations.
Add one new **warning-level** (never `fail`-level — this is a coverage
nudge, not a correctness assertion, and per CLAUDE.md gate discipline a
check that cannot yet run for every fixture must not silently read as more
than it is) finding: `G3_FIXTURE_FORM_COVERAGE_THIN` — fires when a fixture
tagged with a pastoral register has fewer than the forms-1/2/3/4/5/7/8
minimum in its `additionalQueries` (rule 1 above) *and* no `note` entry
recorded as an explicit exemption. It folds into the same `warn`-status
mechanism `PENDING_STILL_FAILING_CATEGORY` already uses (R8 §3f) — it should
never by itself move a verdict from `ADMIT` to `REJECT`, only to
`ADMIT_WITH_WARNINGS`, exactly like pending-fixture debt, and it should be
reported the same honest way: "N of M register fixtures below form-coverage
floor" rather than folded silently into G3's existing pass/fail count.

## C.3 Numerals and references

**What "40 days" does today (measured live, this session).** The tokenizer's
`rawWords()` (`engine/src/tokenizer/index.ts`) preserves `\p{N}` characters,
so digit strings survive the initial split — `"40"` and `"12"` are extracted
as raw words. But `normalizeToken()` then applies the same 3-character floor
that protects short words like `"do"` from stemming into noise
(`if (raw.length < 3) return null;`, R6 §E1/E6), and **that floor has no
numeral-aware exception**: any 1-or-2-digit numeral is silently discarded,
identically to a stopword, with no trace in `Reason`, no `SpellingCorrection`,
nothing. Measured:

| Query | Kind | Top result | Score | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `"40 days"` | discovery | Exodus 20:9 ("You shall labor six days…") | 6.35 | `token_overlap(5,Shared word: days)` + `passage_terms(1.35)` |
| `"forty days"` | discovery | 1 Kings 19:8 (Elijah, 40 days to Horeb) | 42.56 | `exact_phrase(40,Exact phrase)` + `passage_terms(2.56,…forty)` |
| `"12 disciples"` | discovery | Matthew 17:16 ("could not cure him") | 7.61 | `token_overlap(6,Shared word: discipl)` + `passage_terms(1.61)` |
| `"twelve disciples"` | discovery | Matthew 10:1 ("his twelve disciples") | 40.00 | `exact_phrase(40,Exact phrase)` |
| `"psalm 23"` | **reference** | Psalms 23 (6 verses) | — | Step 1 reference grammar |
| `"jn 3 16"` | **reference** | John 3:16 | — | Step 1 reference grammar |

(All rows measured live, this session, via `node --experimental-sqlite`
against `pipeline/output/fixture.db` and `engine/dist/index.js`, replicating
`runBattery.ts`'s own read-only technique — no tracked file modified.
`queries.txt`/`queries2.txt` do not contain these exact numeral-vs-word
pairs verbatim, so `battery-results.md`/`battery2-results.md` do not cover
this comparison; it was UNRUN before this session and is now measured.)

The pattern is exact and total: any query whose *only* distinguishing
content word is a small digit gets that digit deleted before ranking even
starts, and falls back to whatever generic noun sits next to it. This is
strictly worse than dropping the numeral *and* falling back gracefully to a
concept match, because there usually is no concept keyed to "days" or
"disciples" alone — the result is a low-score, semantically empty
`token_overlap` hit on the single surviving noun. Meanwhile the exact same
number, spelled as a word (because that is how WEB actually renders
Numbers/Kings/Matthew — `"forty days and forty nights"`, `"his twelve
disciples"`), matches `exact_phrase` cleanly at the ceiling score. The two
query strings name the identical scriptural fact and receive opposite
treatment.

Two genuinely separate defects hide inside this one observation, and they
want two different fixes:

### Reference-grammar placeholder — not needed, evidence checked and closed

(r1 labelled this **"B11"**; renamed here to plain prose, since S-B's
roster stops at B.10 and its own §B.11/§B.12 headings are non-fix
bundle-sequencing sections, not fix items — reusing "B11" for a new, unvetted
proposal would collide with that numbering even though it is not itself a
fix. If this item is ever scheduled it gets whatever number S-B's owner
assigns next, not "B11".)

This is explicitly **not** what's broken in `"40 days"` — row 11 of the
matrix (C.1) already showed the reference parser handles digits fine
(`"jn3:16"`, `"1cor13"`, `"romans 3 23"` all resolve correctly). `"40 days"`
and `"12 disciples"` are not malformed references; they are ordinary
discovery queries that happen to contain a small number, and Step 1 never
claims them (correctly — `"40 days"` is not a `book chapter[:verse]`
pattern). So there is nothing for a reference-grammar fix to do *for these
two queries specifically*, and — corrected here per critique MINOR-1 — this
placeholder currently has **zero** supporting evidence of its own, not
merely untested evidence: both candidate gaps r1 named were tested live this
revision (`node --experimental-sqlite` against `pipeline/output/fixture.db`
+ `engine/dist/index.js`) and **both already work**: `"ps23"` (glued, no
separator) → `kind: reference`, resolves to Psalms 23; `"first corinthians
13"` (ordinal book name) → `kind: reference`, resolves to 1 Corinthians 13.
Recorded here only as a placeholder so the numeral fix below is not mistaken
for a reference-grammar fix — it should not be scheduled on the strength of
anything measured so far.

### The actual fix — numeral floor in discovery-mode tokenization

- **Measured defect**: `normalizeToken()`'s `raw.length < 3` floor
  (`engine/src/tokenizer/index.ts`, R6 §E1/E6 code excerpt) applies
  uniformly to alphabetic and numeric raw words, silently discarding any
  1–2 digit numeral token before ranking. Independently, digit numerals and
  their spelled-out word forms (`"40"` vs `"forty"`) are disjoint
  vocabularies with no bridge at all — even a 3+-digit numeral like a future
  `"144000"` query would tokenize to `"144000"` but never match a corpus
  verse that spells it `"one hundred forty-four thousand"`.
- **Design**: two independent, separately reviewable changes, because they
  have different blast radii:
  1. *Stop dropping numerals under the length floor.* The 3-character floor
     exists to protect the stemmer from over-aggressive short-word
     stripping (R6 §E1); it has no defensible reason to apply to a token
     that is entirely `\p{N}` — a 2-digit number is not at risk of the
     `-ing`/`-es`/`-s` stemming rules a floor is meant to guard against
     (`stem()` never fires on an all-digit string in any of its five
     branches). The minimal fix is a one-line guard in `normalizeToken`:
     numeral tokens (`/^\d+$/`) skip the length floor entirely and are
     returned as-is.
     (**Confirmed against S-B's final B.1 this pass: Tokenizer v2 keeps
     this floor.** B.1 cites it twice as a live constraint — `go` dropped
     from `cant go on`, `im` a no-op — and mirrors `minStemResidual: 3` in
     `budgets.json`'s new `tokenizer` block under owner ruling 13. So no
     B-item closes the numeral gap, and this stays this chapter's own
     engine item.)
  2. *Bridge digit and word forms where the corpus actually spells the
     number as a word* (a REVIEWED, small, closed table — same discipline
     as `ARCHAIC_FORMS`/`IRREGULAR_LEMMAS` — mapping digit strings to their
     word forms for the small, closed set of numbers scripture actually
     uses spelled out: one through twelve, forty, seventy, etc. Not a
     generative number-to-words function — CLAUDE.md's "no theology
     scores" sibling principle for the tokenizer is "no generative rules
     where a reviewed table suffices," R6's own justification for why
     `ARCHAIC_FORMS` is a table and not a suffix rule).
- **Ordering impact**: real and intentional — `"40 days"` should stop
  matching Exodus 20:9 as its #1 (that match is pure accident, `days`
  appearing near an unrelated numeral) and start reaching Genesis 7:4/7:12,
  1 Kings 19:8 the way `"forty days"` already does. ENGINE_VERSION bump
  required (CLAUDE.md #2) since both sub-fixes touch ordering; if landed
  together with B1 (E1's stemmer fix), a single version bump can cover both
  (R6 already flags that a tokenizer change is likely to want an
  `ENGINE_VERSION` bump alongside `TOKENIZER_VERSION`).
- **Determinism proof**: both fixes are pure functions of the raw word
  string (no locale, no corpus lookup at tokenize time for fix 1; a static
  reviewed table for fix 2) — the same
  `(engineVersion, corpusFingerprint, layerFingerprint, query)` proof
  obligation G2 already enforces for every tokenizer change applies
  unchanged.
- **Tests**: `engine/test/tokenizer.test.ts` gains cases for 1/2/3-digit
  numerals surviving `normalizeToken`; a new fixture pair per C.2's
  "digit/word equivalence" convention for `"40 days"`/`"forty days"` and
  `"12 disciples"`/`"twelve disciples"`, asserting they now resolve to
  overlapping top-3 sets (not necessarily identical — `"forty days"`'s
  `exact_phrase` win is legitimately stronger evidence than a bridged
  `"40 days"` token match, but both should out-rank the current Exodus
  20:9/Matthew 17:16 misses).
- **Data rebuild**: full pipeline rebuild (`token_stats`, `verse_terms`,
  `spelling_terms`/`spelling_deletes`, `concept_lexicon.normalized`) exactly
  as R6's "how a tokenizer change propagates" describes for any tokenizer
  edit — this is a tokenizer edit.
- **Rollback**: revert the `normalizeToken` guard and the numeral-word
  bridge table in one commit, re-run `build:fixture`/the full mint, revert
  `TOKENIZER_VERSION`/`ENGINE_VERSION` together (an already-shipped artifact
  minted under the new tokenizer becomes unusable by a reverted engine per
  the hard compatibility check at `createEngine.ts:161`, R6 §E1 — rollback
  of a shipped artifact is a re-mint, not a flag flip).
- **Acceptance**: the two new fixture pairs above pass; G3-golden's existing
  battery is unchanged (no currently-passing fixture depends on a 1–2 digit
  numeral being silently dropped — a search across `eval/golden` for
  `\b\d{1,2}\b` inside `query`/`additionalQueries` values should confirm
  this as a pre-flight check, since a fixture that accidentally depends on
  today's drop-numeral behavior would need updating in the same PR).
- **Effort**: small (fix 1 is a one-line tokenizer guard; fix 2 is a small
  reviewed table plus one extra lookup at index-build time and at query
  time) — the bulk of the cost is the mandatory full corpus/lexicon rebuild
  and gauntlet re-run any tokenizer change carries, not the code itself.
