## C.4 Phase D — measurement and gates

### D1 — Pastoral battery as a maintained gate (G13)

**r1's design duplicated reviewed data — redesigned here (critique
BLOCKING-5).** r1 proposed seeding a new `eval/battery/pastoral.json`
file's `denyList: string[]` "directly from the `mustNotRank` lists already
reviewed and committed" in the golden fixtures — i.e., hand-copying the same
reference strings into a second file, in a different shape
(`mustNotRank: { ref, why }[]`, resolved through `parseAnchorRef`/
`hitInRange` range matching in `eval/src/gates/corpusGolden.ts:141,194,582`,
versus a bare string list with an unspecified resolution mechanism of its
own). Two committed copies of the same pastoral-harm data, in two shapes,
with two resolution mechanisms and no update-propagation between them, is
exactly the drift CLAUDE.md's gate-discipline principle exists to prevent —
a curator who tightens a `mustNotRank` guard in a fixture (adding a range,
fixing a typo) has no reason to remember a second, differently-shaped file
needs the identical edit, and nothing catches the gap when they don't.

**Redesigned G13: no new battery file. G13 reads the SAME fixtures G3
already validates**, adding one thing G3 does not guarantee today — a
mandatory, fail-level, fixed top-10 scan, regardless of what window a
fixture's own author configured — via one new reviewed data file that
answers a question the fixtures themselves cannot answer on their own:
*which concepts belong to which pastoral register.*

- **New file, `eval/registers.json`** (reviewed data, like `eval/budgets.json`
  — committed, PR-reviewed, not generated): a register → concept-id map,
  e.g. `{ "crisis": ["hope-in-despair", "identity-in-christ", ...],
  "bereavement": ["grief-and-loss", "pregnancy-and-child-loss", ...],
  "marriage-crisis": ["betrayal-and-marriage-crisis",
  "infidelity-and-temptation", ...], "abuse": [], "illness":
  ["serious-illness-and-dying"] }`. `"abuse"` is deliberately shown empty
  above — per **B.8 Additive contract fields** (`ontology/care-concepts.yaml`,
  whose five ids are `hope-in-despair, grief-and-loss,
  pregnancy-and-child-loss, betrayal-and-marriage-crisis,
  serious-illness-and-dying`), no
  `abuse`-register concept exists in `ontology/concepts/` today; that is a
  Phase C data gap, not a G13 bug, and the gate spec below says so rather
  than papering over it with an empty pass.
- **No `denyList` file. At gauntlet-run time**, for each register in
  `eval/registers.json`, G13 collects every `"status": "active"` fixture
  whose `coversConcepts` (the field G3's own concept-coverage check already
  reads, `corpusGolden.ts:855-857`) intersects that register's concept-id
  set, and unions those fixtures' own `mustNotRank` reference ranges — the
  SAME normalized ranges G3 already parses via `parseAnchorRef`, reused, not
  re-derived. This is the register's deny-list, computed fresh every run;
  it cannot drift from the fixtures because it IS the fixtures.
- **Check**: for every fixture collected into a register this way, run
  `research()` on **every one of `[fixture.query, ...fixture.additionalQueries]`**
  ("the additional top-10-across-all-additionalQueries check" the critique
  asked for) and scan the **fixed top 10** — not `measuredWindow(fixture)`,
  which G3 uses and which can be narrower than 10 when a fixture's own
  `expectedWithinTop`/`expectedTop[].withinTop` are set below it — for any
  reference in that register's unioned deny-list. G13's top-10 floor is
  strictly stricter than G3's per-fixture window in exactly the case that
  matters: a harmful reference sitting at rank 6-10 of a fixture configured
  with `expectedWithinTop: 5` passes G3 silently today and must not pass
  G13. Any hit is a **FAIL**, named by fixture id, query, register, and
  offending reference — never `warn`; CLAUDE.md's non-negotiables carry no
  "soft" tier for pastoral harm.
  **Short result sets are not a failure** (the one clause r2's spec left to
  "natural reading"): when a query's `totalCount` is below 10, the scan
  covers whatever the query actually returns and the row still reports a
  real result, not `not-applicable` — a register query that returns four
  results and none of them harmful has passed, and a fail-level pastoral
  gate must say which of those two it means rather than leave an engineer
  to infer it.
- **Determinism**: identical to every other gate — same
  `(engineVersion, corpusFingerprint, layerFingerprint)` triple, same
  in-process replay discipline as G2.
- **`not-applicable` with reason** (three independent cases, each named):
  (a) `eval/registers.json` absent → `not-applicable — register map not
  found at eval/registers.json`; (b) a register present in the map but with
  zero matching active fixtures (today's `"abuse": []`) →
  `not-applicable — no active fixture's coversConcepts names an "abuse"
  concept`; (c) a register with matching fixtures but none carrying a
  `mustNotRank` guard → `not-applicable — no <register> fixture declares a
  mustNotRank guard to check`. Never silently `pass` in any of the three.
- **`eval/budgets.json` key**: new top-level `pastoralHarm` block —
  `{ "$comment": [...], "registers": ["crisis","bereavement","marriage-crisis","abuse","illness"], "registerMapPath": "eval/registers.json" }`
  — deliberately **no numeric threshold to make null**: this is a
  structural pass/fail (any deny-listed reference in top 10 fails, zero is
  the only acceptable count), and the only reviewed data is now
  `eval/registers.json` itself plus the fixtures' own `mustNotRank` entries
  — nothing new to duplicate in budgets.json.
- **G6 mirror**: not applicable — G13 introduces no new engine-side ranking
  constant, so there is nothing for the `signalBudgets` reviewed-constants
  mirror to track (unchanged from r1's own conclusion here). (Distinguish
  from G12, which DOES need `rankQuality` entries, D2 below.)
- **Roster placement**: a 14th row alongside G12, for the same reason R6's
  Appendix gives for G12 being its own row rather than merged into G3 —
  "merging G13 into G3 would let `mergeGateResults` swallow a not-applicable
  battery beside passing sub-results into a green row," and pastoral harm
  is exactly the kind of check that must never be swallowed.

**Dependency this redesign makes explicit**: G13 cannot report anything but
`not-applicable` for a register until (a) `eval/registers.json` exists and
names that register's concepts, and (b) at least one active fixture in that
register carries a `mustNotRank` guard. Today, per A1-A4 (S-A1/S-A2/S-A3),
crisis/bereavement/marriage-crisis/illness already have multiple qualifying
fixtures (e.g. A1.1's `pastoral-kill-myself`, A1.3's
`pastoral-god-is-angry-with-me`, A2.1's `betrayal-and-marriage-crisis`
fixture, A3.1's `fear-of-judgment-am-i-going-to-hell`); abuse does not, per
B8's own statement that no abuse concept exists yet.

### D2 — Rank-quality threshold flip protocol

**Step 0 — G2/G8 approval debt must be zero before any of the four steps
below may start (critique BLOCKING-4, added here — r1 omitted this
precondition entirely).** `docs/governance/probe-baseline-review.md` states
it explicitly: "Steps 1–4 cannot begin while main's standing G2/G8 approval
debt is open — a rank baseline minted now would chain from an unratified
identity." **How to check it**: compare the `layerFingerprint` bound in the
last signed `eval/baselines/probes.approval.json` against the
`layerFingerprint` a live build of the current `HEAD` actually produces
(`node --experimental-sqlite` against a freshly built `pipeline/output/
fixture.db` + `engine/dist/index.js`, the same technique this whole
document uses) — if they differ, the debt is open, full stop, regardless of
what any gate reports (no gate currently fails on this by itself; it is a
governance check, not a G-numbered one).

**Verified on today's `HEAD` for this revision**: they differ. The last
signed baseline (`eval/baselines/probes.approval.json`, `reviewedAt:
"2026-08-29"`, commit `1acf565` "Sign the probe baseline and ordering
snapshot (J39)") binds `engineVersion: "0.14.0"`, `corpusFingerprint:
"6450b7d79c8c7e6254384c628efd63b3baed91fe49f351049f336ac2e782db33"`,
`layerFingerprint:
"9a11fd56edd7511bc7139db642dee26c19e5d4ce4456ed11bdc99b8bf181b8c5"`. `HEAD`
is now `528afdd` ("Execute supplement §2: distinct virgin-birth concept
pack, fixtures-first (#80)") — a data-changing commit landed two commits
after the signing — and a live build measured this revision reports
`layerFingerprint:
"f202502951c8bb03d757b407f95c9e2768f0a99477628ce813b46b5054cda549"` (same
`engineVersion`, same `corpusFingerprint` prefix `6450b7d7…`, **different
`layerFingerprint`**). By the governance doc's own definition this **is**
open G2/G8 approval debt, today, independent of anything this plan does —
so D2's own sequencing (C.6) is missing a real, currently-active blocking
dependency, and the first execution of D2's protocol is, by the governance
doc's own words, necessarily a later PR after a fresh sign-off closes this
debt — not something that can start once B1/B5/B8 land, as r1's C.6 implied.

The exact, already-enforced four-step protocol that may run only after Step
0 clears (`eval/budgets.json` `rankQuality.$comment`,
`docs/governance/probe-baseline-review.md`, R8 §5):

1. **≥3 ADMIT runs** accumulate real measurements against a real built
   artifact (never the fixture corpus — `--update-rank-baseline` structurally
   requires an explicit `--release-database`/`--candidate-*` target, R8
   §4b).
2. **`--update-rank-baseline`** writes the *candidate* baseline to
   `eval/baselines/rank-metrics.json` — "the machine never writes
   approvals" (R8 §4d) — this step alone cannot flip anything.
3. An **independent reviewer** — not the author of the change, not Jesse
   acting alone, designated by Jesse per-review (no standing role) —
   hand-authors `eval/baselines/rank-metrics.approval.json`, binding exact
   digests plus their identity and an independence attestation.
4. The **same PR** that lands the approval also flips the chosen null
   threshold(s) in `eval/budgets.json`, quoting the run history in the
   commit/PR description.

This is enforced structurally, not by convention: `parseThresholdMicro`
takes a `deps.rankBaselineEstablished` boolean, and a non-null threshold
with no matching approved baseline is **silently coerced back to null** and
raises a `rank-quality-premature-threshold` finding that fails G12 (R8 §5)
— a value literally cannot take effect by editing the JSON alone.

**Which metrics get thresholds first, and why:**

- **Top-1 hit rate on crisis registers = 100% required, first.** This is
  not one of the twelve existing `rankQuality` surfaces (nDCG@10 overall +
  9 per-category, MRR@10, good-or-better@3) — it is a new, narrower
  surface this plan proposes adding to `rankQuality` specifically because
  D1's G13 checks *presence in top 10*, a much weaker bar than "the very
  first result is right." For a crisis-register query, a person in crisis
  should not have to read past a mediocre #1 to find comfort at #3. A
  guessed threshold below 100% here would be exactly the "guessed
  threshold that never fires... worse than an absent one" CLAUDE.md warns
  against, because *any* number under 100% concedes that some fraction of
  people in crisis can be shown the wrong thing first and still call it
  passing — that concession needs to be a deliberate, dated ruling by
  Jesse (per J-numbered sign-off precedent throughout `eval/budgets.json`'s
  comments), not a statistically-convenient default.
- **Top-3 on all registers ≥ 90%, second.** This maps directly onto the
  existing `goodOrBetterTop3Rate` surface (already defined, currently
  `null`) — no new schema needed, just the baseline-and-approval flow
  above, run against the *full* battery (all nine `BatteryCategory` values,
  R8 §5), not only the crisis-adjacent five D1 covers.
- **Why these two, in this order, and not nDCG@10 or MRR@10 first**:
  nDCG@10/MRR@10 are the right metrics for *tuning* (comparing two
  candidate ranking changes against each other), but they are graded,
  continuous, and easy to satisfy on average while still failing badly on
  the tail — exactly the crisis queries this plan's matrix (row 15,
  bare-word row-adjacent evidence) shows are furthest from good today. A
  99th-percentile-friendly overall nDCG@10 threshold could pass while
  `"I hate God"` still surfaces nothing useful, per this session's own live
  measurement. Top-1-crisis and top-3-all are binary, register-scoped, and
  cannot be satisfied by averaging over queries that don't need the help.

**Who owns the first mint of `eval/baselines/rank-metrics.json` — D2 does,
and this is the statement S-A4 defers to.** Two chapters used to specify the
same four-step protocol against the same two files. That is resolved, in the
direction the critique recommended, and both halves are now recorded in one
place so neither chapter has to re-derive the other's:

- **S-A4's A4.8 no longer carries a protocol.** Its final text is titled
  "Rank-metrics baseline — owned by D2, not this document", states that a
  second independently-drafted copy "is exactly how the two copies drift —
  which they already had", and keeps exactly one fact of its own: *A4 depends
  on D2*. It does not run `--update-rank-baseline`, does not schedule a
  single-build mint before Batch 1, and does not attempt its own approval
  cycle.
- **D2 therefore owns the first execution, and its Step 0 is the gate on
  A4's whole Tier-1 sequence.** A4.7's acceptance criterion "no batch
  reports `NO_MEASURABLE_EFFECT`" cannot be enforced until this baseline
  exists, because `NO_MEASURABLE_EFFECT` is a comparison; until then A4.5(g)
  and A4.7 report it honestly as `not-applicable — the baseline anchor does
  not exist yet` and the batch reviewer reads G3-golden's per-fixture
  pass/fail plus the release-target run's absolute `rankMetrics` numbers
  instead. That interim position is A4's, stated in A4's own text, and this
  chapter does not weaken it.
- **The ordering that follows**: Step 0 (a fresh signed
  `probes.approval.json` whose `layerFingerprint` matches the artifact under
  test) → ≥3 ADMIT runs against a real artifact → `--update-rank-baseline`
  writes the candidate → an independent reviewer hand-authors
  `rank-metrics.approval.json` → the same PR flips the chosen nulls. A
  Tier-1 batch may merge before any of that (it always could — its evidence
  is fixture-first, not baseline-first); what it may not do is claim the
  `NO_MEASURABLE_EFFECT` criterion is being enforced while the anchor is
  missing.
- **What is left for the owner** is one scheduling question, not a design
  one: whether Step 0's re-signing happens as its own PR now (recommended —
  it is a governance signature, blocks nothing else, and unblocks a
  criterion three chapters lean on) or is folded into the first B-item
  merge. That is register 1.

### D3 — Pending-fixture debt burn-down

Measured this session (R8 §3f, `grep -n '"pending"' eval/golden`, first-run
count): **15 fixtures at `"status": "pending"`** out of 549 fixture files
(534 active). **Composed figure, for the end state this plan actually
produces: 30 pending out of 635 files (605 active)** — the 15 above plus
S-A2's one deliberate residual and S-A3's 14 B.10-gated alias and misquote
records; of the 15 existing, **two already pass on the composed build**
(`assurance-forgiveness-query` and `favor-of-god`, both promotion candidates
the gate names itself), so the debt this rule has to burn down is **28**, not
15. Of the 549/635, `corpusGolden` loads 546/632 as corpus fixtures — the
difference is three files that carry no `query` (`lords-supper-verbatim.json`
is the pending one), which is why the gate line and the file count never
match. Full run in *Composed verification* at the end of this chapter. Named examples: `lords-supper-verbatim.json`,
`no-other-gospel-another-jesus.json`, `assurance-bare.json`. Rule: Phase B
(the engine-fix phase, since several pending fixtures plausibly encode
exactly the kind of stemmer/order-blindness/frame-word behavior B1–B9 fix)
must **promote or delete every one of the 15**, not merely re-run them —
`corpusGoldenGate` already reports a pending fixture that now passes fully
as a **promotion candidate** in its headline (R8 §3f: "PENDING FIXTURES NOW
PASSING, promote to active") and one that is only vacuously passing
(`mustNotRank`/`mustNotLead` refs that resolve to no verse in the running
corpus) as neither a promotion candidate nor a failure but its own counted
category (`vacuousOnlyPending`) — "promoting it would activate a
decoration." Each of the 15 needs one of three dispositions, recorded in the
same PR that lands its promotion/deletion: **(a) promote** (all findings
resolved, non-vacuously), **(b) delete** (the fixture encoded a need this
plan has since decided is out of scope — a Jesse-level ruling, not a
default), or **(c) re-scope** (the need is real but the fixture's assertions
were wrong — rewrite and re-file, still counted against the debt). The
`--pending-debt-ok` flag (R8 §3f, PR #76) exists specifically so ordinary CI
runs aren't blocked by *known, tracked* pending debt while Phase B is in
flight; retire the flag itself (remove it from `parseGauntletOptions`,
CLAUDE.md-style — a maintainer-ruling escape hatch that's still wired up
after its debt hits zero is exactly the kind of decoration gate discipline
forbids) once the count reaches 0, in the same PR that promotes/deletes the
last of the 15.

### D4 — Gap mining

**r1 proposed building a new script that already exists, built, and
approved — corrected here (critique MAJOR-1).** r1's D4 proposed a
from-scratch `eval/scripts/gapMine.ts` (also citing the fabricated
`eval/scripts/` home corrected in C.2, critique MAJOR-2) with a design
weaker than what is already shipped. Reading `docs/telemetry-and-gap-
mining.md` in full (dated 2026-07-31, "**Status: APPROVED by Jesse**...
This repo's half (schemas, category list, distillation reference, miner) is
**built**") and `pipeline/scripts/mineSearchLog.ts` (read in full, 128
lines) this revision: the miner is real, working, and already does
everything r1's sketch wanted plus considerably more —

- validates every distillate against a reviewed schema, refusing mixed
  versions;
- **replays** each distinct query against a pinned artifact matched by the
  full `(engineVersion, corpusFingerprint, layerFingerprint)` identity
  triple (`pipeline/src/telemetry/mine.ts:48-78`, the same replay discipline
  this document uses throughout), flagging any conversion whose logged rank
  doesn't reproduce rather than half-trusting it;
- clusters by the shared tokenizer's normalized token signature (non-
  negotiable #4 — one tokenizer, so "plans to prosper" and "plans to
  prosper you" cluster as one gap);
- merges device-mined reformulation pairs into RENAMED verdicts;
- applies the reviewed `minDistinctDevices`/`weakConvertedRank` thresholds
  already sitting in `eval/budgets.json`'s `telemetry` block (this part of
  r1's citation was correct) to emit four other verdicts — MISS, WEAK,
  SATISFIED, SUPPRESSED — as a **Gap Report**, shaped like the Admission
  Report, with a **suggested move** column that is a suggestion only: "the
  report never writes YAML... the distance between 'the report suggests'
  and 'a human decides, fixtures first' is the entire safety argument";
- updates a committed **master analyzed record** across audits (§6b), so
  wording nuance accumulates across years rather than resetting per export.

This is real design maturity r1's from-scratch sketch did not have
(reformulation-pair mining, a five-verdict taxonomy, a master record with
cross-audit memory) built on a stronger privacy argument (§2's structural
no-hurt case, §4's consent/retention commitments, §8's permanent non-goals
including "no click-trained ranking" and "no popularity evidence"). Building
a second, weaker, differently-located tool alongside this one would not
close a measured gap — it would be exactly the "weight without value"
CLAUDE.md's "Adding data" section forbids, applied to tooling instead of
content.

**The actual delta D4 should scope, once B8 (Additive contract fields)
lands** — checked against `pipeline/src/telemetry/mine.ts` directly, which
has no `evidenceTier`/`confidence`/`care` awareness today because those
fields do not exist yet (**B.8 Additive contract fields**):

1. **Surface `evidenceTier`/`confidence` in the report.** `mine.ts`'s
   `replay()` (`:48-78`) already holds each replayed query's full
   `DiscoveryResult[]` (it reads `result.results[index]` per row today, just
   for rank/reference); once B8 ships, that same object carries
   `result.results[0]?.evidenceTier` and `result.confidence` for free — no
   new replay logic, only reading two fields already on the row. Add them to
   the conversion record the report already builds
   (`mine.ts:178-190`'s `conversions` map) and surface a `confidence` column
   on **SATISFIED** rows specifically: today's verdict logic
   (`mine.ts:264-271`) calls a cluster SATISFIED purely from
   `bestRank <= weakConvertedRank`, which cannot distinguish "converts at
   rank 1 via an authoritative `concept_anchor`" from "converts at rank 3
   via lexical scatter that happens to clear the rank floor" — the second
   case is exactly a query a curator should still look at, and today's
   report calls it "none — do not touch." This is a genuine, measurable
   delta: it changes what SATISFIED means, not just what it displays.
2. **Register tagging.** Once `eval/registers.json` exists (D1's redesigned
   G13, above), the report can tag each Gap Report cluster with the
   register(s) its converted target's `coversConcepts` belongs to (a pure
   join against data D1 already introduces — no new file), so a curator
   triaging a Gap Report can filter for "gaps inside a pastoral register"
   without re-deriving that mapping by hand each audit.
3. **No other delta identified.** The suppression rule, category exclusion,
   replay determinism, and reformulation-pair mining are already built and
   tested (`docs/telemetry-and-gap-mining.md` §7's T2/T3 rows, "✅ built
   2026-07-31, tested against synthetic distillates and the fixture
   artifact") — this document found nothing else to add.

Both deltas are small, additive extensions to `pipeline/src/telemetry/
mine.ts` (not a new script, not a new location), gated on B8 landing for
item 1 and on D1's `eval/registers.json` for item 2, each specced with a
fixture-shaped test the same way `docs/telemetry-and-gap-mining.md` §6b's
own rules are ("No below-threshold query string is ever emitted... the test
feeds it single-device events and asserts the string appears nowhere") — a
new test asserting `evidenceTier`/`confidence` appear only after B8's fields
exist on the replayed result, and a new test asserting a register tag never
appears for a query whose target has no `coversConcepts` entry in
`eval/registers.json`.

### D5 — Register coverage report

An extension of `npm run gauntlet:report` (R8 §4b) — or a sibling script if
`gauntlet:report`'s existing shape doesn't accommodate a non-gate report —
that, per register (crisis, bereavement, marriage-crisis, abuse, illness,
and the nine `BatteryCategory` values `rankQuality.battery.categoryFloors`
already names: adversarial, felt-need, misspelling, multi-concept,
reference-adjacent, remembered-phrase, single-word, theological-term,
worship-leader), counts: (a) lexicon phrases in `concept_lexicon` tagged to
that register's concepts, (b) concept anchors, (c) active golden fixtures,
and (d) **forms covered** per C.2's rule 1 — the same
`G3_FIXTURE_FORM_COVERAGE_THIN` signal, aggregated rather than per-fixture.
This is a report, not a gate (nothing here should be able to fail a build on
its own; it exists so a human reviewing register health before a release
doesn't have to grep five files by hand) — output format: plain text table
to stdout, matching the existing Admission Report's style, with an optional
`--json` mirror for tooling, same convention as the gauntlet's own
`--json <path>` flag.

**Signing convention** (J39-style, per CLAUDE.md's determinism covenant):
data-only changes (every A-item and C-item row above) move `layerFingerprint`
only — sign once after the last data-moving merge of a batch, not once per
fixture. Engine changes (every B-item) move both `engineVersion` and, for
tokenizer edits specifically, `TOKENIZER_VERSION` too — sign once after the
last engine-moving merge of a cycle, and if a tokenizer edit (B1, the
numeral fix) and a non-tokenizer engine edit (B5, B4, …) are batched into
one squash-merge cycle (R6's own precedent: "0.10.0: ranking fixes, staged
on one branch and landed as one squash"), sign once for the whole squash,
not per stage. Never sign an A-item batch and a B-item batch together under
one version bump — CLAUDE.md's three-identity model exists specifically so
a reviewer can tell from the version numbers alone whether a ranking change
came from curated data or from code. **D2's Step 0 is independent of this
convention** — it closes debt against the *current*, already-merged
identity; it is not itself a merge and needs no new sign-once rule beyond
the governance doc's own procedure.

## C.7 Risks and rollback (top 8)

1. **Batching B.1 Tokenizer v2 with the numeral fix risks a bigger,
   harder-to-bisect rebuild.** Both require the full pipeline rebuild
   (`token_stats`, `verse_terms`, `concept_lexicon.normalized`,
   `spelling_terms`/`spelling_deletes`); batching saves one rebuild but
   means a G3-golden regression after the squash can't be attributed to
   stemming vs. numerals without re-running each independently.
   **Rollback**: keep both changes on separate commits within one PR (not
   one commit) so `git bisect` still works inside the squash's history even
   if the merge itself is one version bump.
2. **The row-5 aging-parents/grief collision fix could over-correct** and
   make the eldercare concept require language so specific ("aging",
   "elderly") that genuinely eldercare-only queries stop matching it.
   **Rollback**: land the fix behind its own fixture pair (row 5's) so a
   regression shows up as a G3 fixture failure, not a silent quality drop.
3. **B.5 Ordered phrases could break currently-passing fixtures that
   accidentally rely on order-blindness** — e.g. a lexicon phrase written in one word order that
   a fixture's `query` happens to type in a different order today, silently
   working because `matchConcepts` doesn't check order. **Rollback**: run
   the full G3-golden suite against the fixture corpus before and after B.5
   lands, diff the two runs explicitly (not just pass/fail counts), since a
   same-pass-count run could still hide a different failing set.
4. **The redesigned pastoral G13 gate (D1) shipping with only
   crisis/bereavement/marriage-crisis/illness populated** (abuse has no
   Phase C concept yet, per **B.8**'s own grep of `ontology/concepts/`) **could read as "pastoral harm
   checked" when one of five registers is structurally unable to be
   checked.** **Rollback/mitigation**: G13 must report abuse's check as
   `not-applicable — no active fixture's coversConcepts names an "abuse"
   concept` explicitly (per the gate spec in D1), never silently omitted,
   so the Admission Report itself discloses the gap. This risk is smaller
   under the redesign than r1's version — three of the four previously
   "UNVERIFIED" registers (bereavement, marriage-crisis, illness) already
   have qualifying fixtures via A1/A2/A3, verified in this revision, leaving
   only abuse genuinely open.
5. **`expandForms.ts` (C.2) becoming a de facto second tokenizer** if its
   template list grows organically without review — the same "hidden
   second ranking system" risk CLAUDE.md's tokenizer covenant (#4) and R6's
   E3 both name, just at authoring time instead of query time.
   **Rollback**: cap its scope explicitly to the spec in C.2 (fixed
   templates, reviewed tables only, no fuzzing/generation) and require any
   template addition to go through the same PR review as a lexicon change.
6. **D2's crisis-top-1 threshold (proposed at 100%) could be unreachable
   given the corpus's actual coverage**, forcing an uncomfortable choice
   between shipping a 100% target that never flips from null (decoration by
   omission) or a Jesse-ruled lower number that concedes some crisis
   queries won't lead correctly. **Rollback**: this is a ruling item for
   the owner, not an engineering rollback — `plan/rulings-register.md`
   **row 38**.
7. **`--pending-debt-ok` retirement (D3) landing before all 15 fixtures are
   actually resolved** would re-block ordinary CI for unrelated PRs.
   **Rollback**: retirement is gated explicitly on the debt count reaching
   0, verified by the same PR that removes the flag (C.5 item 10) — never
   remove the flag speculatively ahead of the count.
8. **G13's `eval/registers.json` and B8's `ontology/care-concepts.yaml`
   naming overlapping-but-different concept lists could drift apart** —
   they answer related but distinct questions (which concepts belong to a
   pastoral *register*, for G13's harm check, vs. which concepts carry the
   reviewed *care* flag, for B8's consumer-facing crisis-resource card) and
   nothing today ties them together, so a future concept added to one list
   and not the other reads as "someone forgot," not as a deliberate scope
   difference. **Rollback/mitigation**: a presence-check (like G1's
   provenance-record presence check, R8 §7) that every concept id in
   `ontology/care-concepts.yaml` also appears in at least one
   `eval/registers.json` register (the reverse is not required — a register
   can legitimately have concepts the care flag doesn't cover) — not
   proposed as a new gate, but as a lint step in whichever CI job builds
   both files. (r1's version of this risk named `eval/battery/pastoral.json`
   vs. `eval/battery/queries.json` drift; that risk no longer applies under
   the redesign, since G13 has no second battery file to drift.)

consolidated list that lives inside one of six chapters is a list five
chapters cannot see.** Every decision awaiting the owner — from all six
chapters, deduplicated, grouped by theme, with the six that genuinely block

S-A2, ~5,956 of S-A3 and ~4,877 of S-B, which is to say a reader who wants to
know what the plan does *not* do must find four separate lists at the bottom
of four long documents. They are gathered here, verbatim in substance, each
tagged with the chapter that owns it. **Nothing in this list is new work this
chapter is proposing** — it is a table of contents for what is already
disclosed, plus this chapter's own five.

Each chapter measured its own side against HEAD, where the other's entry did not exist. It is a **pin that was measured before its sibling existed** | **Open, and it needs one decision.** Three closures, none mechanical: **(a)** split the query into its own active fixture with the composed ladder as its pin (costs one new fixture id nobody has written, and concedes that the two queries answer differently); **(b)** relax Acts 16:30-31 to `withinTop: 10` for the whole fixture (costs the "gospel at rank 1–3 for a frightened asker" claim on `am i going to hell`, which is A3.1's whole argument — rejected here, recorded so it is not re-proposed); **(c)** drop `too far gone` from `forgiveness-of-sins` (costs S-A1's `pastoral-too-far-gone` its primary route — that fixture's own query `im too far gone` normalizes to the same `{far, gone}`, so there is nothing to narrow *to*: **narrowing the phrase is a no-op the consistency report proposed and this run falsified**). Recommendation: **(a)**, taken by whoever owns A3.1, with the pin re-derived from the composed run rather than re-asserted |

**One theme runs through six of these.** KG-A1-3, KG-A1-6, KG-A2-5, KG-A3-3,
KG-C-5 and, in its own way, KG-A1-5 are all cases where **the assertion format
cannot express the honest claim** — `withinTop` accepts only 1/3/5/10, a bare
one-word key cannot be an alias, a pack's eleventh anchor silently disables a
`preferredOrder` pin, and no fixture can assert that two queries differ. That
is a fixture-schema observation, not a data one, and it is the strongest
candidate for a Phase D schema item that no chapter currently owns.

## Appendix — Composed verification (all chapters applied together)

Every number the six chapters print was measured **per chapter, against
HEAD**. This appendix is the first run of the data chapters **composed**: S-A1,
S-A2 and S-A3 applied to one tree, with the fourteen cross-chapter findings
resolved, compiled by the real compiler and judged by the real gates. It
exists because three of those findings were cases where two chapters each
measured a true number and the pair was false, and no per-chapter run could
have seen it.

**How the build was made.** Base: `ontology/concepts` at HEAD `528afdd` (289
packs) and the same fixture corpus the chapters' own harnesses use. Each
chapter's final tree (S-A1 `onto-r4`, S-A2's ops-applied tree, S-A3 `onto-r4`)
was merged file-by-file with a three-way merge against that base. Fifty-three
files are touched; **six are touched by more than one chapter** and needed the
merge to be resolved by hand: `caring-for-aging-parents`,
`family-reconciliation`, `forgiveness-of-sins`, `pastoral-hope-in-despair`,
`pastoral-serious-illness`, `presence-of-god`. Five of the six were adjacent
list additions and are unions. The sixth was **C2 itself** — the same
`Isaiah 46:4` anchor at two weights — resolved as ruled: one row, 0.95.
`lexicon-inventory.yaml` was composed record-by-record rather than by text
merge, applying each chapter's *delta* against the base row (which is what
C5 and D1 make the chapters' printed text do). The fixture set is
`eval/golden` at HEAD with the chapters' 86 new files and their amendments
overlaid by fixture id.

**What is not in it, stated plainly.** **S-A4's Tier-1 backfill** (33 refs /
26 packs) — that chapter has no simulator, ships as three separate PRs, and
its own measurements are against HEAD; its refs intersect the data chapters
in exactly one place, `Isaiah 46:4` (C2), which this build already carries
once. **S-B's engine bundle** — 0.15.0 is code, and this run is on the HEAD
0.14.0 engine; nothing below is evidence about tokenizer v2, ordered phrases
or the alias importer. **Phase-C alias data** — the misquote and named-passage
files are B.10-gated, which is why S-A3's 14 alias/misquote fixtures are
`pending` here and fail exactly as their chapter says they will.

### Compile and identity

```
composed/onto   concepts 305  lexicon 2017  anchors 2006  related 840  errors 0
spelling index  terms 18446   deletes 401453
```

### Gate results

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| **G3 corpus golden** (`corpusGoldenGate`, 635 fixtures) | **fail** — `1 corpus fixture expectation(s) failed`: `fear-of-judgment-am-i-going-to-hell`, Acts 16:30-31 not within top 3 for `"too far gone for god"` (**KG-C-7**, the one composed-only failure) |
| G3 corpus golden, with that single query isolated | `warn` — `603 corpus fixture(s) hold; 29 pending — PENDING FIXTURES NOW PASSING, promote to active: assurance-forgiveness-query, favor-of-god`; `Pending fixture status: 27 of 29 still failing` |

and `pipeline/src/importers/ontologyImporter.ts`, invoked exactly as each
chapter's appendix invokes them. The repository itself was not modified
(`git status --porcelain` empty).

# Rulings register — every decision waiting on the owner

**What this is.** One list, gathered from all six chapters of the plan
(`S-A1` crisis and bereavement, `S-A2` marriage and life events, `S-A3`
doctrine, named passages and occasions, `S-A4` backfill and fixture
conventions, `S-B` engine determinism, `S-C` search forms and measurement).
Every decision those chapters leave to you appears here **once**, in plain
language, whether it was written there as a "Ruling for Jesse", a `J-A2-n`, a
row of S-A3's 51-row rulings index, a curator-ruling cell in a backfill table,
or a line in a known-gaps list. Decisions the chapters already *took* are not
here; neither are S-B's seventeen owner rulings, which you have already made
and which are applied in its text.

**How to answer.** Every row is numbered and phrased so a one-word answer is
unambiguous. Replying **"1 yes, 2 no, 3 your call"** is enough — "yes" means
take the recommendation as written, "no" means take the stated alternative,
"your call" hands it back and it will be decided by whoever writes the PR and
recorded in the PR body as your delegation. Where a row bundles several
same-shaped decisions, "yes" accepts the whole list; name any member you want
pulled out and it becomes its own row.

**Reading the columns.** *Gates* names the chapter and item that cannot merge
(or cannot be trusted) until you answer. *Recommendation* is what the chapter
that owns the question recommends, with its one-line reason. *Cost either way*
is what it costs to say yes and what it costs to say no — because several of
these have a real price on both sides, and a recommendation that hides the
alternative is not a decision you can make.

Rows **1–6** genuinely block Phase A. The rest can be answered in any order,
and several can be answered "your call" without slowing anything down.

## If you answer nothing else

Rows **1**, **2**, **4**, **10** and **22** are the five where doing nothing
has a cost that is already being paid: an unratified identity underneath every
measurement, a live self-harm query returning the wrong verse, a hard funeral
text inside thirteen illness pages, a bereaved child reading eldercare
passages, and a confessing spouse reading the wounded spouse's comfort. The
rest can wait without anyone being harmed by the wait.
